The book of the birth of Y'shua the Mashiyach, the son of Dawid, the son of Avraham.
Avraham fathered Yitz'chak. Yitz'chak fathered Ya'akov. Ya'akov fathered Yehuda and his brothers.
Yehuda fathered Perets and Zarach from Tamar. Perets fathered Chetsron. Chetsron fathered Aram.
Aram fathered Aminadab. Aminadab fathered Nachshon. Nachshon fathered Salmon.
Salmon fathered Boaz from Rachab. Boaz fathered Obed from Ra'ut. Obed fathered Ishai.
Ishai fathered Dawid the king. Dawid fathered Shlemun from the wife of Uriya.
Shlemun fathered Rechav'am. Rechav'am fathered Aviya. Aviya fathered Asa.
Asa fathered Yehoshaphat. Yehoshaphat fathered Yoram. Yoram fathered Uziya.
Uziya fathered Yotam. Yotam fathered Achaz. Achaz fathered Chizqiya.
Chizqiya fathered Menasha. Menasha fathered Amon. Amon fathered Yoshiya.
Yoshiya fathered Yokaniya and his brothers in the captivity of Bavel.
And after the captivity of Bavel, Yokaniya fathered Shelatiel. Shelatiel fathered Zurbavel.
Zerubbabel fathered Abiud; Abiud fathered Eliakim; Eliakim fathered Azor.
Azor fathered Zadok; Zadok fathered Achim; Achim fathered Eliud.
Eliud fathered Eleazar; Eleazar fathered Matthan; Matthan fathered Ya'akov.
Ya'akov fathered Yosip, the husband of Maryam, from whom was born Y'shua who is called the Mashiyach.

So all the generations from Avraham to Dawid are fourteen generations, and from Dawid to the captivity of Bavel fourteen generations, and from the captivity of Bavel to the Mashiyach fourteen generations.
Now the birth of Y'shua the Mashiyach was like this. When his mother Maryam was betrothed to Yosip, before they came together, she was found to be with child from the Ruach haKodesh.
Yosip her husband was a just man and did not want to expose her, and he was minded to put her away secretly.

And while he was thinking these things, a messenger of Master YHWH appeared to him in a dream and said to him, Yosip son of Dawid, do not fear to take Maryam your wife, for that which is begotten in her is from the Ruach haKodesh.
She will bear a son, and she will call his name Y'shua, for he will give life to his people from their sins.
Now all this that happened was so that what was spoken by Master YHWH through the prophet might be fulfilled:
A virgin will conceive and will bear a son, and they will call his name Ammanu'el, which is interpreted, Our Elohim with us.
And when Yosip rose from his sleep, he did as the messenger of Master YHWH commanded him, and took his wife.
And he did not know her until she had borne her firstborn son, and she called his name Y'shua.
Now when Y'shua was born in Beth-Lekhem of Yehuda, in the days of Herodes the king, Magi came from the east to Urishlim,
and say: Where is the king of the Yehudeans who has been born? For we have seen his star in the east, and have come to worship him.
And Herodes the king heard, and he was disturbed, and all Urishlim with him.
And he assembled all the chief priests and scribes of the people, and was inquiring of them where the Mashiyach is born.
And they said: In Beth-Lekhem of Yehuda; for thus it is written in the prophet:
Also you, Beth-Lekhem of Yehuda, are not the least among the kings of Yehuda, for from you will go out a king who will shepherd my people Yisrael.
Then Herodes secretly called the Magi and learned from them at what time the star appeared to them.
And he sent them to Beth-Lekhem and said to them, Go, search carefully for the child; and when you have found him, come ‹and› show me, that I also may go ‹and› worship him.
And they, when they heard from the king, went; and the star they had seen in the east went before them until it came ‹and› stood over where the child was.
And when they saw the star, they rejoiced with very great joy.
And they entered the house and saw the child with Maryam his mother, and they fell down ‹and› worshipped him; and they opened their treasures and offered him gifts, gold and myrrh and frankincense.
And it was shown to them in a dream that they should not return to Herodes. And by another road they went to their country.

And when they had gone, a messenger of Master YHWH appeared in a dream to Yosip and said to him, Get up, take the child and his mother and flee to Mitsrayin, and stay there until I tell you, for Herodes is about to seek the child to destroy him.
Then Yosip got up, took the child and his mother by night, and fled to Mitsrayin.
And he was there until the death of Herodes, that what was spoken by Master YHWH through the prophet might be fulfilled, who said, From Mitsrayin I have called my son.

Then Herodes, when he saw that he had been mocked by the Magushi, became very angry, and he sent and killed all the boys in Beth-Lekhem and in all its borders, from two years old and under, according to the time he had carefully learned from the Magushi.
Then was fulfilled what was spoken through Armaya the prophet, who said,
A voice was heard in Ramtha, weeping and much wailing; Rakhyl weeping for her children, and she is not willing to be comforted, because they are no more.
But when king Herodes died, a messenger of Master YHWH appeared in a dream to Yosip in Mitsrayin,
and said to him, Rise, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Yisrael; for they have died who were seeking the life of the child.
And Yosip rose, took the child and his mother, and came to the land of Yisrael.
But when he heard that Archelaus was king in Yehuda in place of his father Herodes, he feared to go there. And it was shown to him in a dream that he should go to the region of Galila.
And he came and dwelt in the city that is called Natsrath, so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled, that he would be called a Natsraya.
And in those days Yochanan the Immerser came, and he was proclaiming in the wilderness of Yehuda,
and said, Repent, the kingdom of heaven has come near.
For this is he who was spoken of by the hand of Eshaya the prophet: A voice calling in the wilderness, Prepare the way of Master YHWH, and make his paths straight.
Now this Yochanan had clothing of camel's hair and a leather belt on his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
Then Urishlim went out to him, and all Yehuda, and all the region around the Yordanan,
and they were immersed by him in the Yordanan river while confessing their sins.
But when he saw many from the Pharisees and from the Sadducees who were coming to be immersed, he said to them: Offspring of vipers, who has shown you to flee from the wrath that is coming?
Produce therefore fruits that are worthy of repentance.
And do not think and say within yourselves, We have Avraham as father: for I say to you that Elohim is able from these stones to raise up children for Avraham.
Look, the axe is laid at the root of the trees. Every tree therefore that does not produce good fruit is cut down and falls into the fire.
I immerse you with water for repentance; but he who comes after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will immerse you with the Ruach haKodesh and with fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hand, and he will clean his threshing-floor. He will gather the wheat into his storehouse, and the chaff he will burn with fire that is not quenched.
Then Y'shua came from Galila to the Yordanan to Yochanan, to be immersed by him.
But Yochanan was refusing him and said, I need to be immersed by you, and have you come to me?
But Y'shua answered and said to him, Allow it now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness. Then he allowed him.
And when Y'shua was immersed, he went up at once from the water, and the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Ruach of Elohim descending like a dove and coming upon him.
And a voice from heaven that said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
Then Y'shua was led by the Ruach haKodesh into the desert, to be tested by the Accuser.
And he fasted forty days and forty nights, and afterward he was hungry.
And the Tempter came near and said to him: If you are the Son of Elohim, say that these stones should become bread.
But he answered and said: It is written that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that goes out from the mouth of Elohim.
Then the Accuser took him to the holy city and set him on a pinnacle of the temple,

and said to him: If you are the Son of Elohim, throw yourself down; for it is written that he will give his messengers charge over you, and on their hands they will lift you up, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.
Y'shua said to him, It is also written that you shall not tempt Master YHWH your Elohim.
Again the Calumniator took him to a mountain that was very high and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory;
and said to him, All these I will give you if you will fall down and worship me.
Then Y'shua said to him, Go away, Satana, for it is written that you shall worship Master YHWH your Elohim, and him only shall you serve.
Then the Calumniator left him, and messengers came and were ministering to him.
Now when Y'shua heard that Yochanan was delivered up, he withdrew to Galila.
And he left Natsrath and came ‹and› lived in Kfar-Nachum beside the sea, in the borders of Zebulun and of Naphtali.
so that what was spoken by the hand of Eshaya the prophet might be fulfilled, who said:
The land of Zebulun, the land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Yordanan, Galila of the peoples;
the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light; and those who sat in the place and in the shadow of death, light has dawned for them.
From then Y'shua began to proclaim and to say, Turn back, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.
And while he walked beside the sea of Galila, he saw two brothers, Shimon who was called Keefa, and Andraos his brother, casting nets into the sea; for they were fishermen.
And Y'shua said to them, Come after me, and I will make you fishers of the sons of men.
And at once they left their nets and went after him.
And when he passed on from there, he saw two other brothers, Ya'akov son of Zabdai and Yochanan his brother, in the boat with Zabdai their father, mending their nets. And he called them.
And at once they left the boat and their father and went after him.
And Y'shua went about in all Galila, and he taught in their synagogues and proclaimed the good news of the kingdom, and healed every pain and disease among the people.

And his fame was heard in all Syria, and they brought to him all who were badly afflicted with various diseases, and those tormented with pains, and demoniacs, and lunatics, and paralytics, and he healed them.
And great crowds went after him from Galila, and from the Ten Cities, and from Urishlim, and from Yehuda, and from beyond the Yordanan.
And when Y'shua saw the crowds, he went up the mountain; and when he sat down, his disciples drew near to him:
And he opened his mouth and taught them, and said:
Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven!
Blessed are the mourners, for they will be comforted!
Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth!
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied!
Blessed are the merciful, for mercies will be upon them.
Blessed are those who are pure in their heart, for they will see Elohim.
Blessed are the makers of peace, for they will be called sons of Elohim.
Blessed are those who are persecuted on account of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are you when they revile you and persecute you and say every evil word against you falsely on my account.
Then rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven. For so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be seasoned? It is good for nothing except to be thrown outside and trampled by people.
You are the light of the world. A city built on a mountain cannot be hidden.
And they do not light a lamp and set it under a basket, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house.
So let your light shine before people, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
Do not suppose that I have come to loosen the law or the prophets: ‹I have come› not to loosen, but to fulfill.
For amen I say to you, that until heaven and earth pass away, one yodh or one stroke will not pass from the law until all is fulfilled.

Therefore whoever breaks one of these small commandments and teaches people this way will be called little in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does and teaches ‹them› will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
For I say to you that unless your righteousness abounds more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to the ancients, Do not kill; and whoever kills is liable to judgment.

But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother without cause is liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, Raka, is liable to the council; and whoever says, Fool, is liable to Gehenna of fire.
If therefore you bring your offering to the altar, and there remember that your brother holds something against you,
leave your offering there before the altar, and go first be reconciled with your brother, and then come and present your offering.

Be in agreement with your adversary quickly while you are with him on the way, lest your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and you fall into the house of prisoners.
Amen I say to you, you will not come out from there until you have paid the last farthing.
You have heard that it was said, Do not commit adultery.
But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman so as to desire her has at once committed adultery with her in his heart.
And if your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it from you, for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body fall into Gehenna.
And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it from you, for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body fall into Gehenna.
It has been said that whoever puts away his wife must give her a writing of divorcement.
But I say to you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the word of fornication, makes her commit adultery, and whoever takes a divorced woman commits adultery.
Again you have heard that it was said to the ancients, Do not be false in your oaths, but fulfill your oaths to Master YHWH.
But I say to you, Do not swear at all: not by heaven, for it is the throne of Elohim,
and not by the earth, for it is the footstool under his feet, nor by Urishlim, for it is the city of the great king.
Nor swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair in it black or white.
But let your word be yes, yes, and no, no; anything more than these is from the evil one.
You have heard that it was said: An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.
But I say to you: Do not stand against the evil one; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.
And whoever wants to sue you and take your tunic, leave him also your cloak.
Whoever forces you one mile, go with him two.
Whoever asks of you, give to him, and whoever wants to borrow from you, do not refuse him.
You have heard that it was said: Love your neighbor, and hate your enemy.
But I say to you: Love your enemies, and bless whoever curses you, and do good to whoever hates you, and pray for those who lead you by force and persecute you:
so that you may be the children of your Father who is in heaven, who makes his sun rise on the good and on the bad, and sends down his rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do this?
And if you greet your brothers only, what more are you doing? Do not even the tax collectors do this?
Be therefore perfect, just as your Father who is in heaven is perfect.
Watch then your alms, that you do not do them before the sons of men so that you may be seen by them. Otherwise you have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.

So when you do alms, do not sound a trumpet before you as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be praised by the sons of men. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you do alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your alms may be in secret. And your Father who sees in secret will repay you openly.

And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, who love to stand in the synagogues and at the corners of the streets to pray so that they may be seen by the sons of men. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you pray, go into your inner room and shut your door and pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will repay you openly.
And when you pray, do not be garrulous like the heathen; for they expect to be heard for their abundance of words.
Therefore do not be like them; for your Father knows what is needful for you before you ask him.
In this manner, therefore, pray: Our Father who is in heaven, hallowed be your name.
Your kingdom come. Your will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
Give us our needful bread this day.
And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
And do not bring us into trial, but deliver us from the evil one, because yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever and ever.
For if you forgive the children of men their faults, your Father who is in heaven will also forgive you.
But if you do not forgive the children of men, neither will your Father forgive you your faults.
And when you fast, do not be gloomy like the face-takers, for they disfigure their faces so they may be seen by the children of men as fasting. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you fast, wash your face and anoint your head,
so that you may not be seen by the children of men as fasting, but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on the earth, where moth and rust spoil, and where thieves dig through and steal.
But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where no moth and no rust spoil, and where thieves do not dig through and do not steal.
For where your treasure is, there your heart is also.
The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body also is luminous.
But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. If then the light that is in you is darkness, how great will your darkness be!
No one can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will honor the one and neglect the other. You cannot serve Elohim and mammon.

Because of this I say to you, do not be anxious for your life, what you will eat and what you will drink, nor for your body, what you will wear. Is not the life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Look at the birds of heaven, that do not sow and do not reap and do not gather into storehouses, and your Father who is in heaven feeds them. Are you not more ‹important› than they?
And who of you by being anxious is able to add one cubit to his stature?
And about clothing, why are you anxious? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they do not toil and they do not spin.
But I say to you that not even Shlemun in all his glory was clothed like one of them.
And if Elohim so clothes the grass of the field, which today is and tomorrow falls into the oven, will he not much more ‹clothe› you, you of little faith?
Therefore do not be anxious or say, What will we eat, or what will we drink, or what will we wear?
For all these the nations seek. But your Father who is in heaven knows that all these are needed for you too.
But seek first the kingdom of Elohim and his righteousness, and all these will be added to you.
Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for its own. Sufficient for the day is its evil.
Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.
For with the judgment that you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure that you measure, it will be measured to you.
And why do you see the straw in your brother's eye, and do not notice the beam that is in your own eye?
Or how do you say to your brother, Let me take the straw out of your eye; and look, the beam is in your eye.
You hypocrite; first take the beam out of your eye, and then it will be clear for you to take the straw out of your brother's eye.
Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls before swine, so that they will not trample them under their feet and turn and tear you.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it is opened.
Or who is the man among you whose son will ask him for bread—will he hand him a stone?
And if he asks him for a fish, will he hand him a serpent?
If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him?
Everything that you want people to do to you, so also do to them, for this is the law and the prophets.
Enter by the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who go in it.
How narrow is the gate and constricted the way that leads to life, and few are those who find it!
Beware of false prophets who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are rapacious wolves.
From their fruits you will know them. Do they gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
So every good tree produces good fruit, but a bad tree produces bad fruit.
A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot produce good fruit.
Every tree that does not make good fruit is cut down and falls into the fire.
So then, from their fruits you will know them.
Not everyone who says to me, my Master, my Master, enters the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
Many will say to me in that day, my Master, my Master, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many works of power?
And then I will declare to them, I never knew you. Depart from me, you workers of iniquity.
Everyone therefore who hears these my words and does them will be likened to a wise man who built his house on the rock.
And the rain came down, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat against that house, and it did not fall, for its foundations were laid on rock.
And everyone who hears these my words and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
And the rain came down, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat against that house, and it fell, and its fall was great.
And it was that when Y'shua finished these words, the crowds were astonished at his teaching,
for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes and Pharisees.
And when he came down from the mountain, many crowds followed him.
And a leper came, bowed to him, and said: my Master, if you will, you can cleanse me.
And Y'shua stretched out his hand, touched him, and said: I will; be cleansed. And in that hour his leprosy was cleansed.
And Y'shua said to him: See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the offering as Moshe commanded, for their testimony.
And when Y'shua entered Kfar-Nachum, a centurion came to him and was requesting from him,
and said: my Master, my boy is lying in the house paralyzed, and is badly tormented.
Y'shua said to him, I will come and heal him.
That centurion answered and said, my Master, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word and my boy will be healed.
For I also am a man under authority, and there are soldiers under my hand, and I say to this one, Go, and he goes, and to another, Come, and he comes, and to my servant, Do this, and he does ‹it›.
And when Y'shua heard ‹this›, he marveled and said to those who came with him, Truly I say to you, that not even in Yisrael have I found faith like this.
And I say to you that many will come from the east and from the west and will recline with Avraham and Yitz'chak and Ya'akov in the kingdom of heaven;
but the children of the kingdom will go out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
And Y'shua said to the centurion, Go; as you have believed, it will be for you. And his child was healed in that hour.
And Y'shua came to the house of Shimon and saw his wife's mother lying down, and a fever had hold of her.
And he drew near to her hand, and the fever left her, and she rose and was serving him.
And when it was evening, they brought before him many demoniacs, and he cast out their demons by a word, and all who were badly afflicted he healed.
so that it might be fulfilled what was spoken by Esha'ya the prophet, who said, He will take our pains, and our diseases he will bear.
And when Y'shua saw great crowds surrounding him, he ordered that they go to the other side.
And a scribe came near and said to him, Rabbi, I will follow you to the place where you go.
Y'shua said to him, Foxes have dens, and the birds of heaven have shelters, but the Son of man has nowhere he may lay his head.
And another of his disciples said to him, my Master, allow me first to go bury my father.
But Y'shua said to him, Come after me, and leave the dead to bury their dead.
And when Y'shua went up into the boat, his disciples went up with him.
And a great quake arose in the sea, so that the ship was covered by the waves. But he, Y'shua, was asleep.
And his disciples came near and woke him, and said to him, Our Master, deliver us; we are perishing!
Y'shua said to them, Why are you afraid, you of little faith? Then he rose and rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
And the men were amazed, and said, Who is this, that the winds and the sea obey him?
And when Y'shua came to the other side, to the place of the Gadarenes, two demoniacs met him who came out from the tombs, very fierce, so that no one could pass by that road.
And they cried out and said, What have we to do with you, Y'shua, Son of Elohim? Have you come here before the time to torment us?
And at a distance from them there was a herd of many swine feeding.
But those demons were begging from him and saying, If you cast us out, allow us to go into the herd of swine.
Y'shua said to them, Go. And at once they went out and entered into the swine, and that whole herd rushed straight up to the precipice and fell into the sea and died in the waters.
But those who were herding fled and went to the city and showed everything that had happened and about those demoniacs.
And the whole city went out to meet Y'shua, and when they saw him they begged him to depart from their borders.
And he went up into the boat and crossed over and came to his city.
And they brought to him a paralytic lying on a bed. And Y'shua saw their faith and said to the paralytic, Take heart, my son; your sins are forgiven you.
But some of the scribes said in themselves, This one blasphemes.
But Y'shua knew their thoughts and said to them, Why are you thinking evil ‹things› in your heart?
For which is easier, to say, Your sins are forgiven you, or to say, Get up and walk?
But so that you may know that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins, he said to the paralytic, Get up, take up your bed, and go to your house.
And he got up and went to his house.
And when those crowds saw ‹it›, they were afraid, and they praised Elohim, who had given authority like this to the sons of men.
And as Y'shua passed on from there, he saw a man sitting at the tax house, whose name was Matai. And he said to him, Come after me: and he got up and went after him.
And as they were reclining in the house, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined with Y'shua and with his disciples.
And when the Pharisees saw ‹it›, they say to his disciples, Why does your master eat with tax collectors and sinners?
But Y'shua, when he heard, said to them: The healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are badly off.
Go and learn what this is: I seek compassion, and not sacrifice. For I did not come to call the righteous, but the sinful.
Then the disciples of Yochanan came near to him and say: Why do we and the Pharisees fast much, and your disciples do not fast?
Y'shua said to them: Can the sons of the bridal chamber fast as long as the bridegroom is with them? But days are coming when the bridegroom will be taken from them, and then they will fast.
No one puts a new patch on an old garment, lest its fullness tear away from that garment, and the tear become worse.
And they do not put new wine into old wineskins, lest the wineskins burst, and the wine is poured out, and the wineskins are ruined. But they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.
And while he was speaking these things with them, a certain ruler came, drew near, bowed to him and said: My daughter has just now died, but come, lay your hand on her, and she will live.
And Y'shua rose, and his disciples, and they went after him.
And look, a woman whose blood had been flowing twelve years came from behind him and touched the edge of his garment.
for she was saying in herself, If I only touch his clothes, I will be healed.
But Y'shua turned, saw her, and said to her, Take heart, my daughter; your faith has given you life. And that woman was healed from that hour.
And Y'shua came to the house of the ruler, and he saw the pipers and a crowd making an uproar.
And he said to them, Go away; for the girl has not died, but is sleeping. And they were laughing at him.
And when he had put out the crowd, he went in, took her by the hand, and the girl rose up.
And the fame of this ‹thing› went out in all that land.
And when Y'shua had passed from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying, Have mercy on us, son of Dawid!
And when he came to the house, those blind men drew near to him. Y'shua said to them, Do you believe that I am able to do this? They said to him, Yes, our Master.
Then he touched their eyes and said, As you have believed, it will be to you.
And at once their eyes were opened. And Y'shua charged them and said, See that no one knows ‹of it›.
But they went out and made him known in all that land.
And when Y'shua went out, they brought to him a mute man who had a demon on him.
And when the demon went out, the mute man spoke. And the crowds were amazed and said, Never has it been seen like this in Yisrael.
But the Pharisees were saying, By the head of demons he drives out demons.
And Y'shua was going around in all the cities and in the villages, and he was teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every pain.
And when Y'shua saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were weary and scattered like sheep that have no shepherd.
And he said to his disciples, The harvest is great, and the laborers are few.
Ask, therefore, of the master of the harvest, that he send laborers into his harvest.
And he called his twelve disciples ‹to him›, and gave them authority over unclean spirits to cast them out, and to heal every pain and disease.
And the names of those twelve apostles are these: The first of them, Shimon who is called Keefa, and Andrawos his brother; and Ya'akov the son of Zabdai, and Yochanan his brother;
and Philipos, and Bar-Tulmai, and Toma, and Matai the tax collector; and Ya'akov the son of Chalpai, and Levi who was named Tadai;
and Shimon the Qananya, and Yehuda Skaryota, he who handed him over.
These twelve Y'shua sent out, and he commanded them and said: Do not go on the road of the Gentiles, and do not enter the cities of the Samaritans.
But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yisrael.
And as you go, proclaim and say that the kingdom of heaven has approached.
Heal the sick, cleanse the leprous, ‹raise the dead,› and cast out demons. Freely you have received; freely give.
Do not provide gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses;
nor a wallet for the journey, nor two coats, nor shoes, nor a staff. For the laborer is worthy of his food.
And into whatever city or town you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and stay there until you depart.
And when you enter a house, ask for the peace of the house.
And if the house is worthy, your peace will come upon it; but if it is not worthy, your peace will return upon you.
And whoever will not receive you and will not hear your words, when you go out from the house or from that town, shake off the dust from your feet.
And truly I say to you that it will be more comfortable for the land of Sodom and of Amora in the day of judgment than for that city.
See, I am sending you as sheep among wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents and pure as doves.
But beware of people, for they will hand you over to the house of judgment, and in their assemblies they will scourge you.
And they will bring you before governors and kings because of me, for a testimony to them and to the peoples.
But when they hand you over, do not be anxious how or what you will speak, for it is given to you in that hour what you will speak.
For it is not you who speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaks in you.
And a brother will hand over his brother to death, and a father his son, and children will rise up against their parents and put them to death.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name. But the one who endures to the end, he will have life.
But when they persecute you in this city, flee to another. For amen I say to you, you will not finish all the cities of the house of Yisrael until the Son of man comes.
There is no disciple greater than his rabbi, and no servant greater than his master.
It is enough for the disciple that he be like his rabbi, and for the servant like his master. If they call the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more the children of his house?
So do not be afraid of them, for there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not be known.
What I say to you in the dark, speak in the light, and what you hear in your ears, proclaim on the housetops.
And do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Fear rather the one who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion? Yet not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father.
But as for you, even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
So do not be afraid: you are better than many sparrows.
So everyone who confesses me before the sons of men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven.
But whoever denies me before the sons of men, I will also deny him before my Father who is in heaven.
Do not think that I have come to cast peace on the earth: I have not come to cast peace, but a sword.
For I have come to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
And a man's enemies are the members of his household.
Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
And everyone who does not take up his cross and come after me is not worthy of me.
Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.
Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.
And everyone who gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold ‹water› to drink in the name of a disciple, truly I say to you, he will not lose his reward.
And it was that when Y'shua finished instructing his twelve disciples, he moved from there to teach and to proclaim in their cities.
Now Yochanan, when he heard in the house of prisoners the works of the Mashiyach, sent by the hand of his disciples,
and said to him: Are you the one who is coming, or are we waiting for another?
Y'shua answered and said to them: Go, tell Yochanan the things that you hear and see:
the blind see, and the lame walk, and the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, and the dead rise, and the poor are given good news:
and blessed is the one who is not stumbled in me.
And when they went, Y'shua began to say to the crowds about Yochanan: What did you go out to the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
And if not, what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Look, those who wear soft ‹robes› are in the houses of kings.
And if not, what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
For this is he of whom it is written: Look, I send my messenger before your face, that he may prepare the way before you.
Amen I say to you, among those born of women there has not arisen a greater than Yochanan the Immerser; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
And from the days of Yochanan the Immerser until now, the kingdom of heaven is driven by force, and the forceful seize it.
For all the prophets and the Torah prophesied until Yochanan.
And if you are willing, receive that this is Eliyahu who was about to come.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children who sit in the marketplace and call to their companions,
and say, We sang to you, and you did not dance; we wailed to you, and you did not lament.
For Yochanan came, not eating and not drinking, and they say, A demon is in him.
The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Look, a gluttonous man and a wine drinker, and a friend of tax collectors and sinners. And wisdom is justified by her works.
Then Y'shua began to reproach the cities in which his many mighty works were done, and they did not repent.

And he was saying, Woe to you, Korazin! Woe to you, Beth-Tsayda! For if the mighty works that were done in you had been done in Tsur and Tsidon, they would long ago have repented in sackcloth and ashes.
But I say to you, that for Tsur and Tsidon it will be more comfortable in the day of judgment than for you.
And you, Kfar-Nachum, who were lifted up to heaven, will be brought down to Sheol. For if the mighty works that were done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have stood to this day.
But I say to you, that for the land of Sodom it will be more comfortable in the day of judgment than for you.
At that time Y'shua answered and said: I thank you, my Father, Master of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and the knowing, and revealed them to little children.
Yes, my Father, for so was the will before you.
Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. And no one knows the Son except the Father. Also no one knows the Father except the Son, and the one to whom the Son wills to reveal ‹him›.
Come to me, all you who are weary and carrying heavy loads, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, that I am gentle and humble in my heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
for my yoke is pleasant and my burden is light.
At that time Y'shua was walking on the Sabbath in the grain fields, and his disciples were hungry and began to pluck the ears and eat.
But when the Pharisees saw them, they said to him, Look, your disciples are doing something that is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.
But he said to them, Have you not read what Dawid did when he was hungry, and those who were with him?
How he entered the house of Elohim and ate the bread of the table of Master YHWH, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, but only for the priests?
Or have you not read in the Torah that the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are without fault?
But I say to you that one greater than the temple is here.
And if you had known what that is, I desire mercy and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned those who are without fault.
For the Son of man is master of the Sabbath.
And Y'shua moved from there and came to their synagogue.
And a certain man was there whose hand was withered. And they were asking him and saying, Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath? so that they might accuse him.
But he said to them, Who among you is a man who has one sheep, and if it falls into a pit on the day of the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and raise it up?
How much then is a human being better than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful on the Sabbath to do what is good.
Then he said to that man, Stretch out your hand. And he stretched out his hand, and it was restored like its fellow.
And the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, that they might destroy him.
But Y'shua knew ‹it›, and he withdrew from there. And great crowds went after him, and he healed all of them.
And he charged them that they should not make him known,
that what was spoken by the hand of Yesha'ya the prophet might be fulfilled, who said:
Here is my servant in whom I am well pleased, my beloved in whom my soul delights. I will put my spirit upon him, and he will proclaim judgment to the peoples.
He will not contend, and he will not cry out, and no one will hear his voice in the marketplace.
A crushed reed he will not break, and a flickering lamp he will not extinguish, until he brings forth judgment to victory.
And in his name the peoples will hope.
Then they brought to him a demoniac who was mute and blind, and he healed him, so that the mute and blind man spoke and saw.
And all the crowds were amazed and said, Is this the son of Dawid?
But the Pharisees, when they heard ‹it›, said, This one does not cast out demons except by Beelzebub the head of the demons.
But Y'shua knew their thoughts, and said to them: Every kingdom that is divided against itself will be ruined, and every house and city that is divided against itself will not stand.
And if Satana casts out Satana, he is divided against himself; how then does his kingdom stand?
And if I by Baalzebub cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast them out? Because of this they will be judges for you.
And if by the Ruach of Elohim I cast out demons, the kingdom of Elohim has come near upon you.
Or how can a man enter the house of a strong man and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? And then he will plunder his house.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
Because of this I say to you that all sins and blasphemies will be forgiven to the sons of men, but the blasphemy that is against the Ruach will not be forgiven to the sons of men.

And everyone who will say a word against the Son of man, it will be forgiven him; but everyone who will say against the Ruach haKodesh, it will not be forgiven him, not in this world and not in the world that is coming.
Either make the tree good and its fruits good, or make the tree bad and its fruits bad; for from its fruits the tree is known.
Offspring of vipers, how are you able to speak good things, you who are evil? For from the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.
A good man from a good treasure brings out good things, and a bad man from a bad treasure brings out bad things.
For I say to you that every idle word that the sons of men will say, they will give its answer in the day of judgment.
For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.
Then some from the scribes and from the Pharisees answered and said to him, Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.
But he answered and said to them, A wicked and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and a sign will not be given to it except the sign of Yonan the prophet.
For as Yonan was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights, so will the Son of man be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
The men of Nineveh will rise in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Yonan, and a greater than Yonan is here.
The queen of the south will rise in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Shlemun, and a greater than Shlemun is here.
And when an unclean spirit goes out of a person, it wanders in places where there is no water, and seeks rest and does not find ‹it›.
Then it says: I will return to my house from which I came out. And it comes and finds it empty and swept and set in order.
Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits worse than itself, and they enter and dwell in it; and the end of that man is worse than his beginning. So it will be for this evil generation.
And while he was speaking to the crowds, his mother and his brothers came and stood outside and sought to speak with him.
And a person said to him: Look, your mother and your brothers stand outside and seek to speak with you.
But he answered and said to the one who told him: Who is my mother? and who are my brothers?
And he stretched out his hand toward his disciples and said: Here is my mother, and here are my brothers!
For everyone who does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother and my sister and my mother.
And on that day Y'shua went out from the house and sat by the side of the sea.
And great crowds assembled to him, so that he went up and sat in a boat, and all the crowd was standing on the shore of the sea.
And he spoke much with them in parables, and said, A sower went out to sow.
And as he sowed, some ‹seed› fell on the side of the path, and the birds came and ate it.
And other ‹seed› fell on rock where there was not much soil, and at once it sprang up because there was no depth of earth.
But when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it dried up.
And other ‹seed› fell among thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it.
And other ‹seed› fell on good earth and gave fruit, some a hundred, and some sixty, and some thirty.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
And his disciples came near and say to him, Why do you speak with them in parables?
But he answered and said to them, To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.
For to whoever has, it will be given to him and it will increase for him.

And from him who has nothing, even what he has will be taken away. Because of this I speak with them in parables, because they see and do not see, and they hear and do not hear, and they do not understand.
And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Eshaya who said, Hearing you will hear and not understand, and seeing you will see and not know.

For the heart of this people has grown fat, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I should heal them.
But happy are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.
For truly I say to you that many prophets and righteous ‹men› longed to see what you see and did not see ‹it›, and to hear what you hear and did not hear ‹it›.
But you hear the parable of the seed.
Everyone who hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away the word sown in his heart. This is what was sown by the side of the path.
But that which was sown on the rock is he who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.
Yet he has no root in him, but is only for a time, and when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he soon stumbles.
But that which was sown among thorns is he who hears the word, and the care of this world and the deceit of riches choke the word, and it becomes without fruit.
But that which was sown on good ground is he who hears my word and understands, and gives fruit and yields, some a hundredfold, some sixty, and some thirty.
He set another parable before them and said: The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
And while people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went away.
And when the grass sprouted and made fruit, then the tares also appeared.
And the servants of the master of the house came near and said to him, Our master, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where are the tares in it?
And he said to them, An enemy man has done this. His servants say to him, Do you want us to go gather them?
And he said to them, ‹No,› lest while you gather the tares you also uproot the wheat with them.

Leave them; let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather the tares first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my storehouse.
He set another parable before them and said: The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field.
And it is the smallest of all seeds; but when it has grown, it is greater than all the herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the bird of heaven comes and nests in its branches.
He spoke another parable to them: The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and buried in three measures of meal, until the whole was leavened.
All these things Y'shua spoke in parables to the crowd, and without a parable he did not speak with them.
so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled, who said: I will open my mouth in parables, and I will utter things hidden from before the foundation of the world.
Then Y'shua left the crowd and came into the house. And his disciples came to him and said to him: Explain to us the parable of the tares and of the field.
But he answered and said to them: He who sows the good seed is the Son of man.
And the field is the world. And the good seed are the sons of the kingdom, but the tares are the sons of the evil one.
And the enemy who sowed them is Satana. And the harvest is the end of the world, and the reapers are the messengers.
Just as the tares are gathered and burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of this world.
The Son of man will send his messengers, and they will gather out of his kingdom all the stumbling blocks and all the doers of iniquity,
and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid, and from his joy he went and sold all that he has and bought that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant who was seeking good pearls:
and when he found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was cast into the sea and gathered ‹fishes› of every kind.
And when it was full, they drew it up to the shore of the sea, and sat down and sorted: and the good they put into vessels, and the bad they threw outside.
So it will be at the completion of the world. The messengers will go out and separate the evil from among the righteous.
And they will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Y'shua said to them, Have you understood all these things? They say to him, Yes, our Master.
He said to them, Because of this, every scribe who is discipled for the kingdom of heaven is like a man, master of a house, who brings out from his treasure things new and old.
And it was that when Y'shua finished these parables, he moved from there.
And he came to his city and was teaching them in their assemblies, so that they were amazed and said, From where does this one have this wisdom and ‹these› powers?
Is this not the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Maryam, and his brothers Ya'akov and Yosa and Shimon and Yehuda?
And all his sisters, are they not with us? From where then does this man have all these things?
And they were stumbling at him. But Y'shua said to them: There is no prophet who is little, except in his city and in his house.
And he did not do many works of power there, because of their unbelief.
Now at that time Herodes the tetrarch heard the fame of Y'shua.
And he said to his servants: This is Yochanan the Immerser; he has risen from the house of the dead; because of this, powers are worked in him.
For this Herodes had seized Yochanan and bound him and cast him into prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philipos his brother.
For Yochanan had said to him: It is not lawful for you to have her as wife.
And he wanted to kill him, but he was afraid of the people, because they held him as a prophet.
But when Herodes’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced before the guests, and she pleased Herodes.
Because of this he swore to her with an oath that he would give her whatever she would ask.
And she, because she had been instructed by her mother, said, Give me here on a dish the head of Yochanan the Immerser.
And it grieved the king; yet because of the oath and the guests he commanded that it be given to her.
And he sent and cut off the head of Yochanan in the prison.
And his head was brought on a dish and given to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
And his disciples came and took away the corpse and buried ‹it›, and they came and told Y'shua.
And Y'shua, when he heard ‹it›, withdrew from there in a boat to a desert place by himself. And when the crowds heard ‹of it›, they went after him by land from the cities.
And Y'shua went out and saw a great crowd, and he had compassion on them, and he healed their sick.

And when it was evening, his disciples came to him and said to him: This is a desert place, and the time has passed; send the crowds away so that people may go to the villages and buy food for themselves.
But he said to them: They do not need to go; you give them ‹something› to eat.
But they said to him: We have nothing here except five cakes and two fish.
Y'shua said to them: Bring them here to me.

And he commanded the crowds to recline on the ground, and he took those five loaves and two fish, and looked to heaven and blessed and broke and gave to his disciples, and those disciples set them before the crowds.
And they all ate and were satisfied, and they took up the leftover fragments, twelve baskets full.
And those men who had eaten were five thousand, besides women and children.
And immediately he compelled his disciples to get into the boat and go before him to the other side, while he dismissed the crowds.
And when he had dismissed the crowds, he went up the mountain alone to pray. And when it grew dark, he was there alone.
And the boat was far from the land many stadia, while it was being tossed much by the waves, for the wind was against it.
And in the fourth watch of the night Y'shua came to them, walking on the water.
And his disciples saw him walking on the water, and they were shaken, and they were saying, It is a false vision; and from their fear they cried out.
But Y'shua at once spoke with them and said, Take heart; it is I; do not be afraid.
And Keefa answered and said to him, My Master, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water.
And Y'shua said to him, Come. And Keefa went down from the boat and walked on the water to come to Y'shua.
And when he saw the wind was strong, he was afraid and began to sink; and he raised his voice and said, My Master, rescue me.
And immediately our Master stretched out his hand and took hold of him, and said to him, Little of faith, why did you doubt?
And when they went up into the boat, the wind ceased.
And those who were in the boat came and bowed down to him, and said, Truly you are the Son of Elohim.
And they crossed over and came to the land of Gennesar.
And the men of that place recognized him, and they sent to all the villages around them, and they brought to him all who were very badly afflicted;
and they were asking of him that they might touch even only the fringe of his garment. And those who touched were healed.
Then Pharisees and scribes from Urishlim came near to Y'shua and said:
Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders, and do not wash their hands when they eat bread?
Y'shua answered and said to them: Why do you also transgress the commandment of Elohim on account of your tradition?
For Elohim said: Honor your father and your mother; and whoever reviles his father or his mother will surely die.
But you say: Anyone who says to a father or to a mother, My offering is whatever you would gain from me, then he need not honor his father or his mother.
And ‹thus› you make void the word of Elohim for the sake of your tradition.
You hypocrites, well did Eshaya prophesy about you, and say:
This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
And in vain they revere me, while they teach teachings that are the commandments of the sons of men.
And he called the crowd and said to them, Hear and understand.
It is not what enters the mouth that defiles a man, but what comes out from the mouth—that defiles a man.
Then his disciples came near and said to him, Do you know that the Pharisees who heard this word were offended?
But he answered and said to them: Every plant that my Father who is in heaven has not planted will be uprooted.
Leave them alone. They are blind guides of the blind. And if a blind person leads a blind person, both of them will fall into a pit.
And Shimon Keefa answered and said to him: My Master, explain this parable to us.
But he said to them: Are you also still without understanding even until now?
Do you not know that whatever enters the mouth goes into the belly, and from there is cast out in the latrine?
But what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart, and that is what defiles a person.
For from the heart come out evil thoughts, adultery, murder, whoredom, theft, false testimony, reviling.
These are what defile a person. But if a person eats while his hands are not washed, he is not defiled.
And Y'shua went out from there and came to the borders of Tsur and Tsidon.
And a Canaanite woman from those borders came out, crying out and saying, Have compassion on me, my Master, son of Dawid; my daughter is grievously tormented by a demon.
But he did not answer her a word. And his disciples came near, asked him, and said, Send her away, for she is crying after us.
But he answered and said to them, I was not sent except to the sheep that have strayed from the house of Yisrael.
But she came and bowed to him and said, “My Master, help me.”
He said to her, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
But she said, “Yes, my Master; even the dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table and live.”
Then Y'shua said to her, “O woman, great is your faith; let it be for you as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.
And Y'shua left from there and came beside the sea of Galila, and he went up the mountain and sat there.
And great crowds came to him, and with them were the lame and the blind and the mute and the maimed and many others, and they laid them at the feet of Y'shua, and he healed them.
so that those crowds were amazed who saw the mute speaking, and the maimed being healed, and the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they praised the Elohim of Yisrael.

Then Y'shua called his disciples and said to them: I have compassion on this crowd, for look, three days they have stayed with me and they have nothing to eat; and I am not willing to send them away fasting, lest they faint on the way.
His disciples say to him: From where for us in the wilderness bread to satisfy all this crowd?
Y'shua said to them: How many loaves do you have? They say to him: Seven, and a few small fish.
And he commanded the crowd to recline on the ground.
And he took these seven loaves and the fish and gave thanks and broke and gave to his disciples, and the disciples gave to the crowd.
And they all ate and were satisfied. And they took up the remains of the fragments, seven full baskets.
And those who had eaten were four thousand men, besides women and children.
And when he sent the crowds away, he went up into the boat and came to the borders of Magdu.
And Pharisees and Sadducees came near, testing him, and asking him for a sign from heaven that he would show them.
But he answered and said to them: When it is evening you say, It is fair weather; for the heavens are red.
And in the morning you say, Today there is a storm; for the heavens are red and gloomy. You know how to discern the face of the heavens, but the signs of this time you do not know how to discern.
A wicked and adulterous generation seeks a sign; and no sign is given to it except the sign of Yonah the prophet. And he left them and went.
And when his disciples came to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread with them.
And he said to them: Look, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.
But they were reasoning among themselves and saying, ‹it was› because they had taken no bread.
But Y'shua knew ‹it› and said to them, Why are you reasoning among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have taken no bread?
Do you not yet understand? Do you not remember those five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
Nor those seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
How is it that you do not understand that it was not about bread that I spoke to you, but that you should beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees?
Then they understood that he did not say to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.
And when Y'shua came to the place of Qasarya of Philippos, he was asking his disciples and said, Who do people say about me, that I am the Son of man?
And they said, Some say that ‹you are› Yochanan the Immerser; but others, Eliyahu; and others, Armiya, or one of the prophets.
He said to them, But who do you yourselves say that I am?
Shimon Keefa answered and said, You are the Mashiyach, the Son of the living Elohim.
Y'shua answered and said to him, Blessed are you, Shimon son of Yonah, for flesh and blood have not revealed ‹it› to you, but my Father who is in heaven.
Also I say to you that you are Keefa, and on this rock I will build my assembly, and the gates of Sheol will not prevail against it.
I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
Then he commanded his disciples that they should tell no one that he is the Mashiyach.
And from then Y'shua began to show his disciples that he is about to go to Urishlim and suffer much from the elders and from the chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day rise.
And Keefa took him and began to rebuke him and said, Far be it from you, my Master, that this should be to you.
But he turned and said to Keefa, Go behind me, Satana. You are a stumbling block to me, for you do not think the things of Elohim but of the sons of men.
Then Y'shua said to his disciples, Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and come after me.
For whoever wants to keep his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
For what does a man profit if he gains the whole world and loses his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?
For the Son of man is about to come in the glory of his Father with his holy messengers, and then he will repay each one according to his deeds.
Truly I say to you, there are people standing here who will not taste death until they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
And after six days Y'shua took Keefa and Ya'akov and Yochanan his brother and led them up a high mountain by themselves.
And Y'shua was changed before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white like the light.
And Moshe and Eliyahu appeared to them, speaking with him.
Then Keefa answered and said to Y'shua, my Master, it is good for us to be here; and if you want, we will make three shelters here, one for you and one for Moshe and one for Eliyahu.
And while he was still speaking, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice came from the cloud that said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.
And when the disciples heard ‹it›, they fell on their faces and were very afraid.
And Y'shua came near to them and touched them and said, Get up, do not be afraid.
And they lifted their eyes and saw no one except Y'shua alone.
And as they were going down from the mountain, Y'shua commanded them and said to them, Do not tell this vision to anyone until the Son of man rises from the dead.
And his disciples asked him and said to him, Why then do the scribes say that Eliyahu must come first?
Y'shua answered and said, Eliyahu comes first so that he may fulfill everything.
But I say to you that Eliyahu has come, and they did not know him, and they did to him whatever they wanted. In the same way also the Son of man is about to suffer from them.
Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them of Yochanan the Immerser.
And when they came to the crowd, a man approached him and knelt on his knees,
and said to him, My Master, have compassion on me. I have a son who is a lunatic and is badly afflicted; for often he falls into the fire, and often into the water.
And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not heal him.
Y'shua answered and said, O unbelieving and twisted generation! How long will I be with you, and how long will I bear with you? Bring him here to me.
And Y'shua rebuked the demon, and it went out from him, and the boy was healed from that hour.
Then the disciples came near to Y'shua by himself and said to him, Why could we not heal him?

Y'shua said to them, Because of your unbelief. For truly I say to you, that if there is in you faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, Move from here, and it will move, and nothing will be too hard for you.
But this kind does not go out except by fasting and by prayer.
And while they were going about in Galila, Y'shua said to them, The Son of man is about to be delivered into the hands of men,
and they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise. And it grieved them greatly.
And when they came to Kfar-Nachum, those who collect the two zuz of the head-tax came to Keefa and said to him, Does your master not give his two zuz?

He said to them, Yes. And when Keefa entered the house, Y'shua went before him and said to him, How does it appear to you, Shimon? The kings of the earth, from whom do they take tribute and head-money? from their children, or from foreigners?
Shimon said to him, From foreigners. Y'shua said to him, Then the children are free.
But so that we do not cause them to stumble, go to the sea and cast a hook, and the first fish that comes up, open its mouth and you will find a stater; take that and give for me and for you.
In that hour the disciples came near to Y'shua and say, Who then is great in the kingdom of heaven?
And Y'shua called a child and set him in their midst,
and said, Amen, I say to you, that unless you turn and become like children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
Whoever then humbles himself like this child, he will be great in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever receives one like this child in my name receives me.
And everyone who causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him that a millstone of a donkey be hung on his neck and he be sunk in the depths of the sea.
Woe to the world from the stumbling blocks! For it is necessary that stumbling blocks come. But woe to the man by whose hand the stumbling blocks come.

But if your hand or your foot makes you stumble, cut it off and throw it from you. It is better for you to enter into life while you are lame or while maimed, and not, while you have two hands or two feet, fall into the fire of forever.
And if it is that your eye makes you stumble, dig it out and throw it from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, and not, while you have two eyes, fall into the gehenna of fire.
See that you do not despise one of these little ones. For I say to you that their messengers in heaven at all times see the face of my Father who is in heaven.
For the Son of man has come to give life to that which was lost.
How does it appear to you? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, does he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountain and go seek the one that went astray?
And if he finds it, I tell you truly that he rejoices in it more than in the ninety-nine that did not stray.
So it is not the will before your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
But if your brother sins against you, go reprove him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother.
And if he does not hear you, take with you one or two, so that on the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may stand.
And if he will not hear them either, tell ‹it› to the church. And if he will not hear the church either, let him be to you as a tax collector and as a pagan.
I tell you truly that whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
Again I say to you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning every matter that they will ask, it will be theirs from my Father who is in heaven.
For where two or three ‹are› assembled in my name, there ‹am› I in the midst of them.
Then Keefa came near to him and said, my Master, how many times if my brother sins against me shall I forgive him? up to seven times?
Y'shua said to him, I do not say to you up to seven, but up to seventy times seven.
Because of this the kingdom of heaven has been likened to a man, a king, who wanted to take account from his servants.
And when he began to take, they brought to him one who owed ten thousand talents.
And when he had nothing with which to pay, his master ordered that he be sold, him and his wife and his children and everything he had, and payment be made.
And that servant fell down and bowed to him and said, My master, give me time, and I will pay you everything.
And the master of that servant had compassion and released him and forgave him his debt.
Then that servant went out and found one of his fellow-servants who owed him a hundred denarii. And he seized him and was choking him and said to him, Give me what you owe me.
And that fellow-servant fell at his feet and begged him and said to him, Give me time, and I will pay you.
But he was not willing, but went and threw him into prison until he would give him what he owed him.
And when their fellow-servants saw what had happened, it grieved them greatly; and they came and made known to their master all that had happened.
Then his master called him and said to him: Evil servant! I forgave you that whole debt because you begged me.
Was it not right for you also to have compassion on your fellow-servant, as I had compassion on you?
And his master was angry and delivered him to the torturers until he should pay all he owed him.
So will my Father who is in heaven do to you, unless you forgive each his brother his offence from your heart.
And when Y'shua finished these words, he left Galila and came to the borders of Yehuda beyond the Yordanan.
And great crowds followed after him, and he healed them there.
And Pharisees came near to him and were testing him and saying, Is it allowed for a man to put away his wife for every cause?
But he answered and said to them, Have you not read that he who made ‹them› from the beginning made them male and female?
And he said, For this reason a man will leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife, and the two of them will be one flesh.
So they are not two, but one body. What Elohim has joined, then, let not a son of man separate.
They say to him, Why then did Moshe command to give a writing of divorce and dismiss her?
He said to them, Moshe, because of the hardness of your heart, permitted you to dismiss your wives; but from the beginning it was not so.
But I say to you that whoever leaves his wife, not for adultery, and takes another commits adultery, and whoever takes a dismissed woman commits adultery.
His disciples say to him, If the case between a man and a woman is like this, it is not profitable to take a wife.
But he said to them, Not everyone is able for this word, but only the one to whom it is given.

For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs because of the kingdom of heaven. Whoever is able to be content, let him be content.
Then they brought children to him, that he might lay his hand on them and pray. And his disciples rebuked them.
But Y'shua said to them: Let the children come to me, and do not forbid them; for of those who are like these is the kingdom of heaven.
And he laid his hand on them, and went from there.
And one came, drew near, and said to him: Good Teacher, what good thing must I do, that I may have life that is forever?
But he said to him: Why do you call me good? There is none good except one, ‹namely,› Elohim. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.
He said to him, Which ones? And Y'shua said to him: You shall not kill; and you shall not commit adultery; and you shall not steal; and you shall not bear false testimony;
and honor your father and your mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.
The young man says to him, All these I have kept from my childhood. What do I lack?
Y'shua says to him, If you desire to be perfect, go, sell your property and give to the poor, and there will be for you a treasure in heaven, and come after me.
But that young man heard this word and went away grieving, for he had much property.
But Y'shua said to his disciples, Amen I say to you, that it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.
And again I say to you, that it is easier for a camel to enter the aperture of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of Elohim.
But when the disciples heard ‹it›, they were greatly astonished, and said: Who then can live!
Y'shua looked at them and said to them: With the sons of men this is not possible, but with Elohim everything is possible.
Then Keefa answered and said to him: We have left everything and come after you. What then will there be for us?

Y'shua said to them: Amen I say to you, that you who have come after me, in the new world when the Son of man sits on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones and will judge the twelve tribes of Yisrael.
And everyone who leaves houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for my name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.
But many first will be last, and last ‹who shall be› first.
For the kingdom of heaven is like a man, a master of a house, who went out in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.
And he agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, and sent them into his vineyard.
And he went out at the third hour and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.
And he said to them, Go also you into the vineyard, and what is right I will give you.
And they went. And he went out again at the sixth and at the ninth hours and did the same.
And about the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing and idle, and he said to them, Why are you standing all the day idle?
They say to him, No one has hired us. He says to them, Go you also into the vineyard, and you will receive what is right.
And when evening came, the master of the vineyard said to his steward, Call the laborers and give them their wages, and begin from the last and go on to the first.
And those of the eleventh hour came and received a denarius each.
And when the first came, they supposed they would receive more, and they also received a denarius each.
And when they received ‹it›, they murmured against the master of the house,
and say, These last have worked one hour, and you have made them equal with us who have borne the burden of the day and its heat.
But he answered and said to one of them: My friend, I am not wronging you. Did you not contract with me for a denarius?
Take what is yours and go. But I want to give to this last one as to you.
Or is it not lawful for me to do what I want with what is mine? Or is your eye evil because I am good?
So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, and few are chosen.
Now Y'shua was about to go up to Urishlim, and he took his twelve disciples aside on the way and said to them:
Look, we are going up to Urishlim, and the Son of man will be delivered to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death.
And they will hand him over to the peoples, and they will mock him, and they will scourge him, and they will crucify him, and on the third day he will rise.
Then the mother of the sons of Zabdi came near to him, she and her sons, and she bowed to him and was asking something of him.
And he said to her, What do you want? She said to him, Say that these two my sons will sit, one on your right and one on your left, in your kingdom.

Y'shua answered and said, You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, or be immersed with the immersion that I am immersed with? They say to him, We are able.

He said to them, My cup you will drink, and the immersion that I am immersed with you will be immersed: but to sit on my right and on my left is not mine to give, except to those for whom it is prepared by my Father.
And when the ten heard ‹it›, they were angry at those two brothers.
And Y'shua called them and said to them, You know that the heads of the nations are their masters, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
It will not be so among you. But whoever among you wants to be great will be a minister to you.
And whoever among you wants to be first will be a servant to you.
Just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
And as Y'shua went out from Yericho, a great crowd was following him.
And two blind men were sitting by the side of the road, and when they heard that Y'shua was passing they raised their voice and said, Have mercy on us, my Master, son of Dawid!
But the crowd was rebuking them to be silent, and they raised their voice even more and said, Our Master, have compassion on us, son of Dawid.
And Y'shua stood still and called them and said, What do you want me to do for you?
They said to him, Our Master, that our eyes may be opened.
And Y'shua had compassion on them and touched their eyes, and at once their eyes were opened, and they went after him.
And when he drew near to Urishlim and came to Beth-Paga beside the mount of Olives, Y'shua sent two of his disciples,
and said to them, Go to this village that is opposite you, and at once you will find a donkey tied and a colt with her. Untie and bring ‹them› to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, say to him that they are needed by our Master, and at once he will send them here.
Now this took place so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled, who said,
