Say to the daughter of Tsehyon, Look, your king comes to you, meek and riding on a donkey, and on a colt the foal of a donkey.
And the disciples went and did as Y'shua commanded them.
And they brought the donkey and the colt, and they put their garments on the colt, and Y'shua rode on it.
And a great throng were spreading their garments in the road; and others were cutting branches from the trees and throwing them in the road.
And the crowds that were going before him and coming after him were shouting and saying, Hosanna to the son of Dawid. Blessed is he who comes in the name of Master YHWH. Hosanna in the highest.
And when he entered Urishlim, the whole city was stirred, and they were saying, Who is this?
And the crowds were saying, This is Y'shua the prophet, who is from Natsrath of Galila.
And Y'shua entered the temple of Elohim and drove out all who were buying and selling in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those who were selling doves.
And he said to them, It is written, My house will be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of robbers.
And the blind and the lame came near to him in the temple, and he healed them.
But when the chief priests and the Pharisees saw the wonders that he did, and the children crying out in the temple and saying, Hoshana to the son of Dawid, it displeased them.
And they said to him, Do you hear what these are saying? Y'shua said to them, Yes. Have you never read, From the mouth of children and infants
you have prepared praise? And he left them and went out of the city to Beth-Anya, and lodged there.
But in the morning, when he returned to the city, he was hungry.
And he saw one fig tree by the road, and he came to it and found nothing on it except leaves only. And he said to it: Fruit will not be on you again forever. And at once that fig tree withered.
And the disciples saw ‹it› and were amazed, and said: How did the fig tree wither in a moment?

Y'shua answered and said to them: Amen I say to you, that if faith is in you and you do not doubt, you will not only do this of the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, Be lifted up and fall into the sea, it will be.
And everything that you ask in prayer and believe, you will receive.

And when Y'shua came to the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came near to him as he was teaching, and said to him: By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority?
Y'shua answered and said to them: I also will ask you one word, and if you tell me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.
The immersion of Yochanan, from where is it? From heaven, or from men? And they were reasoning among themselves and saying: If we say, From heaven, he will say to us, Why did you not believe him?
And if we say, From men, we are afraid of the crowd, for all of them hold Yochanan as a prophet.
They answered and said to him: We do not know. Y'shua said to them: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
But what do you think? A certain man had two sons, and he came to the first and said to him, My son, go today, work in the vineyard.
But he answered and said, I am not willing. But afterward he regretted and went.
And he came to the other and said the same to him. And he answered and said, I ‹go›, my master, and did not go.
Which of these two did the will of his father? They say to him, The first. Y'shua says to them, Amen, I say to you that tax collectors and prostitutes go before you into the kingdom of Elohim.

For Yochanan came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. And you, even when you saw ‹it›, did not afterward repent so that you would believe in him.

Hear another parable. There was a certain man, a master of a house, and he planted a vineyard and put a hedge around it and dug a winepress in it and built a tower in it and leased it to cultivators and went away.
And when the time of the fruits arrived, he sent his servants to the cultivators so that they would send him some of the fruits of his vineyard.
And the cultivators seized his servants, and some they beat, and some they stoned, and some they killed.
And again he sent other servants, more numerous than the first, and they did the same to them.
And at last he sent his son to them, saying, Perhaps they will respect my son.
But the laborers, when they saw the son, said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.
And they seized him, cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
When the master of the vineyard comes, then, what will he do to those laborers?
They say to him, He will destroy them badly, and will lease the vineyard to other laborers who will give him the fruits in their seasons.
Y'shua said to them, Have you never read in the scripture, The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; this was from Master YHWH, and it is marvelous in our eyes?
Because of this I say to you that the kingdom of Elohim will be taken from you and will be given to a people that does fruit.
And whoever falls on this stone will be shattered, and everyone on whom it falls, it will crush him.
And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they knew that he spoke about them.
And they sought to seize him, and they feared the crowd because they held him as a prophet.
And Y'shua answered again in parables and said:
The kingdom of heaven is likened to a man, a king, who made a wedding feast for his son.
And he sent his servants to call those who were invited to the feast, and they did not want to come.
Again he sent other servants and said, Say to those invited, My banquet is prepared, and my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and everything is prepared; come to the feast.
But they despised it and went away, one to his field and one to his merchandise.
And the rest seized his servants and abused them and killed them.
When the king heard ‹of it›, he was angry, and he sent his armies and destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
Then he said to his servants, The feast is prepared, and those who were invited were not worthy.
Go therefore to the outlets of the roads, and everyone you find, call to the feast.
And those servants went out into the roads and gathered all they found, bad and good, and the house of the feast was filled with guests.
And the king went in to see the guests, and he saw there a man who was not clothed in the garment of the feast.
And he said to him, My friend, how did you come in here when you do not have the garment of the feast? But he was silent.
Then the king said to the servants, Bind his hands and his feet, and cast him into the outer darkness: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
For the called are many, and the chosen are few.
Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might ensnare him in a word.

And they sent to him their disciples with those of the house of Herodes, and they say to him, Teacher, we know that you are true, and you teach the way of Elohim in truth, and you do not take care for any man, for you do not regard the face of men.
Tell us, therefore, how it appears to you: is it lawful to give the head-tax to Caesar, or not?
But Y'shua knew their wickedness, and said, Why are you testing me, you face-takers?
Show me a denarius of the head-tax silver. And they brought him a denarius.
And Y'shua said to them: Whose is this image and inscription?
They say, Caesar's. He says to them: Give then what is Caesar's to Caesar, and what is Elohim's to Elohim.
And when they heard ‹it› they were amazed, and they left him and went away.
On that day the Sadducees came near and say to him: There is no life of the dead. And they asked him,
and say to him: Teacher, Moshe said to us that if a man dies while he has no sons, his brother shall take his wife and raise up seed to his brother.
Now there were with us seven brothers. The first took a wife and died, and as he had no sons, he left his wife to his brother.
Likewise also the second, and also the third, and on to the seven of them.
And after all of them, the woman also died.
In the resurrection, then, to which of these seven will she be the wife? For all of them took her.
Y'shua answered and said to them: You err, because you do not know the writings, nor the power of Elohim.
For in the resurrection of the dead they do not take women, nor do women become to husbands, but they are like the messengers of Elohim in heaven.
But about the rising of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by Elohim, who said:
I am the Elohim of Avraham, the Elohim of Yitz'chak, the Elohim of Ya'akov? And Elohim is not of the dead, but of the living.
And when the crowds heard ‹it› they were astonished at his teaching.
But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, assembled together.
And one of them who knew the law asked him, testing him:
Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?
Y'shua said to him: You will love Master YHWH your Elohim with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might and with all your mind.
This is the great and first commandment.
And the second, which is like it, is: You will love your neighbor as yourself.
On these two commandments hang the Torah and the prophets.
And while the Pharisees were assembled, Y'shua questioned them,
and said: What do you say about the Mashiyach? Whose son is he? They say to him: The son of Dawid.
He says to them: And how does Dawid by the Ruach call him Master YHWH? For he said:
Master YHWH said to my Master, Sit at my right hand, until I place your enemies under your feet.
If Dawid then calls him Master YHWH, how is he his son?
And no one was able to give him an answer. And no one dared again from that day to question him.
Then Y'shua spoke with the crowd and with his disciples,
and said to them: The scribes and Pharisees sit on the seat of Moshe.
Everything therefore that they tell you to keep, keep and do. But according to their deeds do not do: for they say, and do not do.
They bind heavy burdens and lay ‹them› on the shoulders of the sons of men; but they themselves do not want to touch them with their finger.
And all their works they do to be seen by the sons of men: for they make their phylacteries broad, and lengthen the fringes of their garments.
And they love the highest places at banquets and the highest seats in the synagogues,
and the greeting in the marketplaces, and to be called by people Rabbi.
But you are not to be called Rabbi, for one is your Rabbi, and you are all brothers.
And do not call anyone among you Father on earth, for one is your Father who is in heaven.
And do not be called guides, because one is your Guide, the Mashiyach.
But the one who is great among you will be your servant.
For whoever raises himself up will be brought low, and whoever lowers himself will be raised up.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you devour the houses of widows under the pretext of lengthening your prayers. Because of this you will receive greater judgment.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you shut the kingdom of heaven before the sons of men; for you yourselves do not enter, and those who are entering you do not allow to enter.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you go around sea and dry land to make one convert, and when he becomes one you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves.
Woe to you, blind guides, who say that whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing, but whoever swears by the gold that is in the temple is bound.
Fools and blind ones, for which is greater, the gold or the temple that makes the gold holy?
And whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing, but whoever swears by the offering upon it is bound.
Fools and blind ones: which is greater, the offering or the altar that sanctifies the offering?
So whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything that is on it.
And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by him who dwells in it.
And whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of Elohim and by him who sits above it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: for you tithe mint and anise and cummin, and you have left the weightier ‹matters› of the law, judgment and mercy and faithfulness. These you ought to do, and those not to leave.
Blind guides, who strain out gnats and swallow camels.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: for you cleanse the outside of the cup and of the dish, but inside they are full of rapine and iniquity.
Blind Pharisee, cleanse first the inside of the cup and of the dish, so that their outside may also be clean.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: for you are like whitewashed tombs, which from the outside appear beautiful, but inside are full of the bones of the dead and all uncleanness.
So you also from the outside appear to the children of men as righteous, but inside you are full of iniquity and hypocrisy.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: for you build the tombs of the prophets and you adorn the burial places of the righteous;
and you say: If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in the blood of the prophets.
Therefore you are witnesses against yourselves that you are the children of those who killed the prophets.
And you also, fill up the measure of your fathers.
Serpents, offspring of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment of Gehenna?

Because of this, I am sending to you prophets and wise men and scribes; some of them you kill and crucify, and some of them you scourge in your synagogues, and you will persecute them from city to city,

so that all the blood of the righteous that has been shed on the earth may come upon you, from the blood of righteous Habeel to the blood of Zakharya son of Barakhya, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.
Amen, I say to you that all these things will come upon this generation.
Urishlim, Urishlim, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her: how often I wanted to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not.
Look, your house is left to you desolate.
For I say to you that you will not see me from now until you say, Blessed is he who comes in the name of Master YHWH.
And Y'shua went out from the temple to go away, and his disciples came near, showing him the buildings of the temple.
But he said to them: Do you not see all these? I say to you truly, that there will not be left here a stone upon a stone that will not be torn down.

And as Y'shua sat on the mount of Olives, his disciples came near and said between themselves and to him: Tell us when these things will be, and what is the sign of your coming and of the completion of the world.
Y'shua answered and said to them: Take care that no one deceives you.
For many will come in my name and will say, I am the Mashiyach, and they will deceive many.
But you are going to hear of conflicts and the report of wars. See that you are not disturbed, for all these things must happen, but the end is not yet.
For a people will rise against a people, and a kingdom against a kingdom, and there will be famines and plagues and earthquakes in place after place.
But all these are the beginning of birth-pains.
Then they will hand you over to distress and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the peoples because of my name.
Then many will stumble, and they will hate one another and will hand one another over.
And many false prophets will rise, and they will lead many astray.
And because of the abundance of lawlessness, the love of many will grow cold.
But he who perseveres to the end, he will have life.
And this announcement of the kingdom will be proclaimed in all the world for a testimony to all the peoples, and then the end will come.
But when you see the unclean sign of desolation that was spoken by Daniyel the prophet standing in the holy place, let the one who reads understand.
Then those who are in Yehuda, let them flee to the mountain.
And he who is on the roof, let him not come down to take what is in his house.
And he who is in the field, let him not turn back to take his garment.
But woe to the pregnant and to those who nurse in those days.
But pray that your flight will not be in winter, and not on the Sabbath.
For there will then be great distress, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, and will not be.
And if those days were not cut short, no flesh would live. But for the sake of the chosen, those days will be cut short.
Then if anyone says to you, Look, here is the Mashiyach, or here, do not believe.
For false Mashiyachs will arise, and prophets of falsehood, and they will give great signs, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
Look, I have told you beforehand.
If therefore they say to you, Look, he is in the wilderness, do not go out; or, Look, he is in a secret chamber, do not believe.
For as the lightning comes out from the east and is seen as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of man.
Wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will be gathered.
But immediately after the distress of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not show its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken.

And then the sign of the Son of man will be seen in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
And he will send his messengers with a great trumpet, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from the ends of the heavens to their ends.
Now learn the parable from the fig tree. As soon as its branches become tender and its leaves shoot forth, you know that summer has come.
So also you, when you see all these things, know that it has come ‹even› to the door.
Truly I say to you, that this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But of that day and of that hour no one knows, not even the messengers of heaven, but the Father only.
But as the days of Noach, so will the coming of the Son of man be.
For as they were before the flood, eating and drinking, and taking women and giving to men, until the day that Noach entered the ark,
and they did not know until the flood came and took them all away; so will the coming of the Son of man be.
Then two ‹men› will be in the field; one will be taken, and one will be left.
And two ‹women› will be grinding at the mill; one is taken, and one is left.
Stay awake, therefore, for you do not know at what hour your Master is coming.
But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
Because of this, you also be ready, for in the hour that you do not expect, the Son of man will come.
Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his master has set over the members of his household, to give them their food in its time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.
Truly I say to you, he will set him over all that he has.
But if that evil servant says in his heart, My master delays to come;
and he will begin to beat his fellow-servants, and will eat and drink with drunkards;
the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect, and in an hour he does not know,
and will cut him in two, and will put his portion with the hypocrites; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
And five of them were wise, and five were foolish.
And the foolish ones took their lamps, but did not take oil with them.
But the wise ones took oil in vessels with their lamps.
And while the bridegroom delayed, they all grew sleepy and fell asleep.
And in the middle of the night there was a cry: The bridegroom is coming; go out to meet him.
Then all those virgins rose and trimmed their lamps.
And the foolish ones said to the wise ones, Give us some of your oil, for our lamps have gone out.
The wise ones answered and said, ‹We must refuse,› or else there will not be enough for us and for you. But go to those who sell and buy for yourselves.
And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding house, and the door was shut.
And afterward the other virgins also came and said, Our Master, our Master, open for us.
But he answered and said to them, Truly I say to you, I do not know you.
Stay awake, therefore, for you do not know that day or the hour.
For it is like a man who journeyed, called his servants and handed over to them his property;
to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, each according to his ability, and he journeyed at once.
Then he who took the five talents went and traded with them and gained five others.
And likewise also he of the two traded and gained two others.
But he who took the one went, dug in the earth, and hid his master's silver.
But after a long time, the master of those servants came and took account from them.
And he who had received five talents came near and brought five others, and said, My master, you gave me five talents; look, I have gained by trading five others on them.
His master said to him, Well done, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a little, I will set you over much; enter into the joy of your master.
And he who had two talents came near and said, My master, you gave me two talents; look, I have gained by trading two others on them.
His master said to him, Well done, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a little, I will set you over much; enter into the joy of your master.
Then he also who had received one talent came near and said, My master, I knew you, that you are a hard man, and you reap where you did not sow, and gather from where you did not scatter.
And I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the earth. Here, you have what is yours.
His master answered and said to him, Wicked and lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I have not sown, and gather from where I have not scattered.
And was it not for you to cast my money on the table, and I would have come and demanded what is mine with its interest.
Take therefore the talent from him, and give it to him who has ten talents.
For to him who has, it will be given, and it will be added to him; but from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
And cast the idle servant into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
And when the Son of man comes in his glory, and all his holy messengers with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
And all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd who separates the sheep from the goats.
And he will set the sheep on his right, and the goats on his left.
Then the king will say to those on his right: Come, you blessed of my Father; inherit the kingdom that was prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry, and you gave me food; and I was thirsty, and you gave me drink; I was a stranger, and you took me in;
I was naked, and you clothed me; I was sick, and you visited me; and I was in prison, and you came to me.
Then those righteous will say to him: Our Master, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink?
And when did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?
And when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?
And the king will answer and say to them: Amen I say to you, that as much as you did to one of these my little brothers, you did to me.
Then he will say also to those on his left: Go from me, you cursed, into the everlasting fire that is prepared for the Accuser and his messengers.
For I was hungry and you gave me nothing to eat, and I was thirsty and you gave me nothing to drink.
and I was a stranger, and you did not gather me in, and I was naked, and you did not cover me, and I was sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.
Then they also will answer and say, Our Master, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not serve you?
Then he will answer and say to them, Truly I say to you, that as much as you did not do to one of these little ones, you did not do to me.
And these will go into everlasting torment, and the righteous into everlasting life.
And it was that when Y'shua finished all these words, he said to his disciples:
You know that after two days the Passover happens, and the Son of man is handed over to be crucified.
Then the chief priests and the scribes and the elders of the people gathered to the courtyard of the high priest who is called Qayapa.
And they took counsel against Y'shua that they might seize him by deceit and kill him.
And they were saying, Not at the feast, so that there will not be an uproar among the people.
And when Y'shua was in Beth-Anya, in the house of Shimon the leper,
A woman came to him who had on her a flask of aromatic ointment of great price, and she poured it on the head of Y'shua as he was reclining.
But his disciples saw ‹it› and were displeased, and said: Why this waste?
For this might have been sold for much and given to the poor.
But Y'shua knew and said to them: Why are you troubling the woman? She has done a good deed toward me.
For you have the poor with you at all times; but you do not have me at all times.
But this ‹act of› pouring this ointment on my body she has done as for my burial.
Amen, I say to you that wherever this good news of mine is proclaimed in all the world, what she has done will also be told for a memorial of her.
Then one of the twelve, who is called Yehuda Skaryota, went to the chief priests,
and said to them, What do you want to give me, and I will deliver him to you? And they set for him thirty pieces of silver.
And from then on he was seeking an opportunity to deliver him.
Now on the first day of unleavened bread the disciples came to Y'shua and said to him, Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?
And he said to them, Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, Our Master says, My time has come; I will keep the Passover with you with my disciples.
And his disciples did as Y'shua directed them, and made ready the Passover.
And when it was evening, he reclined with his twelve disciples.
And while they were eating, he said, Amen I say to you, that one of you will betray me.
And it troubled them greatly, and they began to say to him, each one of them, Is it I, my Master?
And he answered and said, The one who dips his hand with me in the dish, he will betray me.
And the Son of man goes as it is written of him. But woe to that man by whose hand the Son of man is betrayed. It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.
Yehuda the betrayer answered and said, Rabbi, is it I? Y'shua said to him, You have said.
And as they were eating, Y'shua took bread and blessed and broke it and gave to his disciples and said, Take, eat; this is my body.
And he took the cup and gave thanks and gave ‹it› to them and said, Take, drink from it, all of you.
This is my blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many for the forgiveness of sins.
But I say to you that from now on I will not drink from this fruit of the vine until the day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.
Then Y'shua said to them, You will all stumble because of me this night; for it is written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of his flock will be scattered.
But after I rise, I go before you to Galila.
Keefa answered and said to him: Even if everyone stumbles in you, I will never stumble in you.
Y'shua said to him: Amen I say to you, that in this night before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.
Keefa said to him: If it is for me to die with you, I will not deny you. And so also all the disciples said.
Then Y'shua came with them to a place called Gadsman, and he said to his disciples: Sit here while I go pray.
And he took Keefa and the two sons of Zawdi, and began to be grieved and distressed.
And he said to them, My soul is in anguish, even to death. Stay here for me, and keep watch with me.
And he went a little farther and fell on his face and was praying and said, My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you.
And he came to his disciples and found them sleeping, and he said to Keefa, So, could you not keep watch with me one hour?
Wake up and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is ready, but the body is weak.
Again he went a second time and prayed and said, My Father, if this cup cannot pass except I drink it, your will be done.
And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
And he left them and went again and prayed a third time, and said the same word.
Then he came to his disciples and said to them, Sleep on now, and rest. Look, the hour has come, and the Son of man is handed over into the hands of sinners.
Rise, let us go. Look, he who hands me over has come.
And while he was still speaking, look, Yehuda the betrayer, one of the twelve, came, and a great crowd with him with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
And Yehuda the betrayer had given them a sign, and said to them: The one I kiss is he; seize him.
And at once he came near to Y'shua and said, Peace, Rabbi, and kissed him.
But Y'shua said to him: My friend, is it for this you have come? Then they came near and laid their hands on Y'shua and seized him.
And one of those with Y'shua stretched out his hand and drew a sword and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
Then Y'shua said to him: Put the sword back in its place, for all who take up a sword will die by a sword.
Or do you think that I cannot ask my Father, and he would raise up for me now more than twelve legions of messengers?
How then would the writings be fulfilled, that it must be this way?
At that hour Y'shua said to the crowd: Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me? Every day I sat with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me.
But this happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled. Then all the disciples left him and fled.
And those who had seized Y'shua led him to Qayapa the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled.
But Shimon Keefa was going after him from a distance as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and he went in and sat inside with the guards to see the end.
Now the chief priests and the elders and the whole assembly were seeking witnesses against Y'shua so that they might put him to death,
and they did not find any. And many false witnesses came, but afterward two came forward
and said, This one said, I am able to tear down the temple of Elohim and in three days build it.
And the high priest rose and said to him, Do you answer nothing? What are these testifying against you?
But Y'shua was silent. And the high priest answered and said to him: I adjure you by the living Elohim, that you tell us if you are the Mashiyach, the Son of Elohim.
Y'shua said to him: You have said. But I say to you that from now you will see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming on the clouds of heaven.
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said: See, he has blasphemed! Why then do we still need witnesses? See, now you have heard his blasphemy.
What do you want? They answered and said: He is liable to death.
Then they spit in his face and were buffeting him, and others were striking him,
and saying: Prophesy to us, Mashiyach, who is it that struck you?
But Keefa was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a certain maid approached him and said to him: You also were with Y'shua the Natsraya.
But he denied ‹it› before them all, and said: I do not know what you are saying.
And when he went out to the porch, another ‹maid› saw him and said to them: This one also was there with Y'shua the Natsraya.
And again he denied with an oath: I do not know the man.
But a little after, those standing ‹there› came up and said to Keefa: Truly you also are one of them, for your speech also makes you known.
Then he began to curse and to swear: I do not know the man. And in that hour the rooster crowed.
And Keefa remembered the word of Y'shua that he said to him: Before the rooster crows, three times you will deny me. And he went outside and wept bitterly.
And when it was morning, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Y'shua, so that they might put him to death.
And they bound him and led him and delivered him to Pilatos the governor.
Then Yehuda the betrayer, when he saw that Y'shua was condemned, repented, and he went and returned these thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and the elders,
and said, I have sinned, for I have betrayed innocent blood. But they said to him, What is that to us? You know.
And he threw down the silver in the temple, and withdrew and went and hanged himself.
But the chief priests took the silver and said, It is not lawful to put it into the house of the offering, because it is the price of blood.
And they took counsel and bought with it the potter's field for a burial place for strangers.
Because of this that field is called the field of blood to this day.
Then was fulfilled what was spoken by the prophet who said: I took the thirty ‹shekels› of silver, the price of the precious one, which they of the children of Yisrael had stipulated;
and I gave them for the potter's field, as Master YHWH directed me.
And Y'shua stood before the governor. And the governor asked him and said to him: Are you the king of the Yehudaye? Y'shua said to him: You have said.
And when the chief priests and elders were accusing him, he answered nothing.
Then Pilatos said to him, Do you not hear how much they testify against you?
And he gave him no answer, not even one word, and at this he wondered greatly.
Now at every feast the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner to the people, whichever they wanted.
And they had a notable prisoner who was called Bar Abba.
And when they were assembled, Pilatos said to them, Whom do you want me to release to you, Bar Abba or Y'shua who is called the Mashiyach?
For Pilatos knew that it was from envy they had delivered him up.
Now while the governor was sitting on his judgment seat, his wife sent to him and said to him, Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered much today in a dream because of him.
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowd that they should ask for Bar-Abba, and destroy Y'shua.
And the governor answered and said to them, Which of the two do you want me to release to you? And they said, Bar-Abba.
Pilatos said to them, And what shall I do with Y'shua who is called the Mashiyach? They all say, Let him be crucified.
The governor said to them, But what evil has he done? And they cried out all the more and said, Let him be crucified.

Now Pilatos, when he saw that nothing was gained but rather a greater uproar was arising, took water and washed his hands before the eyes of the crowd and said, I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man; you see to it.
And all the people answered and said, His blood on us and on our children.
Then he released to them Bar Abba, and scourged Y'shua with whips and delivered him to be crucified.
Then the soldiers of the governor took Y'shua into the Praetorium, and assembled the whole regiment against him.
And they stripped him and put on him a scarlet military cloak.
And they wove a crown of thorns and set it on his head, and ‹put› a reed in his right hand, and they bowed their knees before him and were mocking him and saying, Hail, king of the Yehudaye.
And they spit in his face, and took the reed and were striking him on his head.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped him of the cloak, and clothed him in his garments, and led him away to be crucified.
And as they went out, they found a man of Qurinya whose name was Shimon; this one they compelled to carry his cross.
And they came to a place that is called Gagulta, which is interpreted a skull.
And they gave him vinegar mixed with gall to drink. And he tasted ‹it›, and would not drink.
And when they had crucified him, they divided his garments by lot.
And they sat and kept watch over him there.
And they placed over his head the cause of his death in writing: This is Y'shua, the king of the Yehudaye.
And two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.
And those who were passing by were reviling him and shaking their heads
and saying, Destroyer of the temple and builder of it in three days, deliver yourself; if you are the Son of Elohim, come down from the cross.
In the same way the chief priests also were mocking, with the scribes and elders and Pharisees,
and saying, He gave life to others; he is not able to give life to his own soul. If he is the king of Yisrael, let him come down now from the cross and we will believe in him.
He trusted on Elohim; let him rescue him now if he delights in him, for he said, I am the Son of Elohim.
Likewise also those robbers who were crucified with him were reproaching him.
Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
And about the ninth hour Y'shua cried out with a loud voice and said, Eli, Eli, why have you left me?
But some of those who were standing there, when they heard ‹it›, were saying, This one is calling for Eliyahu.
And at once one of them ran and took a sponge and filled it with vinegar and put it on a reed and was giving him to drink.
But the rest were saying, Leave ‹him›; we will see if Eliyahu comes to deliver him.
Then Y'shua cried out again with a loud voice and gave up his spirit.
And at once the face of the door of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth was shaken, and the rocks were split.
And the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy ones who were sleeping arose,
and came out; and after his rising they entered the holy city and appeared to many.
And the centurion and those with him who were guarding Y'shua, when they saw the quake and the things that happened, feared greatly and said, Truly this was the Son of Elohim.
And there were also many women there who were looking on from a distance, those who had followed Y'shua from Galila and were ministering to him.
One of them was Maryam Magdalitha, and Maryam the mother of Ya'akov and of Yosa, and the mother of the sons of Zabdai.
And when it was evening, a rich man came from Ramtha whose name was Yosip, who also had been discipled to Y'shua.
This one approached Pilatos and asked for the body of Y'shua, and Pilatos commanded that the body be given to him.
And Yosip took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
and laid it in his new tomb that was hewn in the rock. And they rolled a great stone and set it against the door of the tomb and went away.
And Maryam Magdalitha and the other Maryam were there, who were sitting opposite the grave.
And on the next day, which is after the preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees assembled to Pilatos,
and say to him: Our Master, we remember that that deceiver said while he was alive, After three days I rise.

Command therefore that they guard the grave until three days, lest his disciples come and steal him away in the night and say to the people that he has risen from the house of the dead, and the last error be worse than the first.
Pilatos said to them: You have a guard; go guard ‹it› as you know how.
And they went and guarded the grave, and sealed that stone with the guard.
Now in the evening of the sabbath, as the first ‹day› of the week was dawning, Maryam Magdalitha and the other Maryam came to see the tomb.
And there was a great earthquake, for a messenger of Master YHWH came down from heaven and drew near, rolled the stone from the entrance, and was sitting on it.
And his appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white like snow.
And from fear of him those who were keeping watch were shaken, and they became like the dead.
And the messenger answered and said to the women: Do not be afraid, for I know that you are seeking Y'shua who was crucified.
He is not here, for he has risen, just as he said. Come, see the place where our Master was laid.
And ‹then› go quickly, tell his disciples that he has risen from the house of the dead; and look, he goes before you to Galila; there you will see him. Look, I have said to you.
And they went quickly from the tomb with fear and with great joy, and ran to tell his disciples.
And look, Y'shua met them and said to them, Peace to you. And they came near, took hold of his feet, and worshipped him.
Then Y'shua said to them, Do not fear, but go, tell my brothers that they should go to Galila, and there they will see me.
And while they were going, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests everything that had happened.
And they assembled with the elders and took counsel, and gave no little silver to the guards,
and they say to them, Say that his disciples came and stole him away by night while we were asleep.
And if this is heard before the governor, we will persuade him, and you will have no concern.
But they, when they took the silver, did as they were taught. And this word has gone out among the Yehudaye to this day.
But the eleven disciples went to Galila, to the mountain where Y'shua had appointed them.
And when they saw him, they bowed down to him, but some of them doubted.
And Y'shua drew near, spoke with them, and said to them, All authority is given to me in heaven and on earth. And as my Father sent me, I send you.
Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, and immerse them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Ruach haKodesh.
And teach them to keep all that I have commanded you. And I am with you all the days until the completion of the world. Amen.
The beginning of the gospel of Y'shua the Mashiyach, the Son of Elohim.
As it is written in Ashaya the prophet: I am sending my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way.
The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of Master YHWH, and make his paths smooth.
Yochanan was in the wilderness immersing and proclaiming an immersion of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
And all the region of Yehuda was going out to him, and all the sons of Urishlim, and he was immersing them in the Yordanan while they confessed their sins.
Now Yochanan was clothed in a garment of camel's hair and was bound with a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
And he was proclaiming and saying, After me comes one more powerful than I, of whom I am not worthy to stoop and untie the straps of his sandals.
I have immersed you with water, but he will immerse you with the Ruach haKodesh.
And it was in those days that Y'shua came from Natsrath of Galila and was immersed in the Yordanan by Yochanan.
And at once as he came up from the water he saw the heavens split open and the Ruach like a dove descending upon him.
And a voice came from heaven: You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased.
And at once the Ruach drove him out into the wilderness.
And he was there in the wilderness forty days, while being tempted by Satana. And he was with the wild beasts, and messengers were ministering to him.
After Yochanan was delivered up, Y'shua came to Galila and was proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of Elohim,
and said: The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of Elohim has come near. Turn back, and believe in the good news.
And as he was walking around the sea of Galila, he saw Shimon and Andraos his brother casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
And Y'shua said to them: Come after me, and I will make you fishers of the sons of men.
And at once they left their nets and went after him.
And as he passed on a little, he saw Ya'akov the son of Zabday, and Yochanan his brother, who also were in the boat mending their nets.
And he called them; and at once they left Zabday their father in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.
And when they entered Kfar-Nachum, at once he was teaching on the sabbath in their synagogue.
And they were astonished at his teaching; for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.
And there was in their synagogue a man in whom was an unclean spirit; and he cried out,
and said, What have we to do with you, Y'shua the Natsraya? Have you come to destroy us? I know you, who you are, the Holy One of Elohim.
And Y'shua rebuked him and said, Shut your mouth and come out of him.
And the unclean spirit threw him down and cried out with a loud voice and came out of him.
And they were all amazed and were inquiring one with another and saying, What is this? And what is this new teaching, that with authority he even commands the unclean spirits and they obey him.
And at once his fame went out into all the region of Galila.
And they went out from the synagogue and came to the house of Shimon and of Andrawos, with Ya'akov and Yochanan.
And Shimon's mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever, and they told him about her.
And he came near, took her by the hand, and raised her up; and at once the fever left her, and she was serving them.
And in the evening, at the setting of the sun, they brought to him all who were badly afflicted, and the demoniacs.
And the whole city was gathered at the door.
And he healed many who were badly afflicted with various diseases, and cast out many demons; and he did not allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
And in the morning, very early, he rose and went to a deserted place, and there he was praying.
And Shimon and those with him were seeking him.
And when they found him, they say to him, All the people are seeking you.
He said to them, Go to the villages and to the cities that are near, that I may preach there also, for this is why I have come.
And he was preaching in all their assemblies in all Galila, and casting out demons.
And a leper came to him and fell at his feet and was seeking from him and said to him, If you will, you can cleanse me.
And Y'shua had compassion on him and stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, I will; be clean.
And in that hour his leprosy went from him, and he was cleansed.
And he charged him and sent him away,
and he said to him, See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the offering for your cleansing, as Moshe commanded, for a testimony to them.

But he, as he went out, began to proclaim ‹it› much and to spread the word, so that Y'shua could not openly enter the city, but was outside in desert places; and they were coming to him from every place.
And Y'shua entered again into Kfar-Nachum after some days. And when they heard that he was in the house,
many gathered, so that ‹the house› could not hold them, not even before the door. And he was speaking the word with them.
And they came to him and brought to him a paralytic, as they were carrying him between four.
And when they could not come near him because of the crowd, they went up to the roof and lifted the covering of the place where Y'shua was, and lowered the bed on which the paralytic was lying.
And when Y'shua saw their faith, he said to the paralytic: My son, your sins are forgiven you.
And there were some scribes and Pharisees there, who were sitting and reasoning in their hearts:
Why is this one speaking blasphemy? Who is able to forgive sins except one Elohim?
But Y'shua knew in his spirit that they were reasoning these things in themselves, and he said to them, Why are you reasoning these things in your heart?
Which is easier, to say to the paralytic, Your sins are forgiven you, or to say, Get up, take up your bed, and walk?
But that you may know that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins, he said to the paralytic,
I say to you, Get up, take up your bed, and go to your house.
And he got up at once, took up his bed, and went out before them all, so that they were all amazed and gave praise to Elohim, saying, We have never seen anything like this.
And he went out again to the sea, and all the crowd were coming to him, and he was teaching them.
And as he passed by he saw Levi the son of Chalpai sitting at the toll house, and he said to him, Come after me. And he rose and went after him.
And it was that as he reclined in his ‹Levi's› house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Y'shua and with his disciples, for they were many, and they came after him.
And the scribes and Pharisees, when they saw him eating with tax collectors and with sinners, said to his disciples, Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?
When Y'shua heard, he said to them, The healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are badly diseased. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.
Now the disciples of Yochanan and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and say to him, Why do the disciples of Yochanan and of the Pharisees fast, and your own disciples do not fast?
Y'shua said to them: Can the sons of the bridal chamber fast as long as the bridegroom is with them? No.
But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken from them, and then they will fast in that day.
No one puts a new patch and sews it on an old garment, lest the new fullness take from the old, and the tear become greater.
And no one puts new wine into old skins, lest the wine burst the skins, and the skins be ruined and the wine spilled; but they put new wine into new skins.
And it was that as Y'shua went on the sabbath through the grain fields, his disciples were walking and plucking the ears.
And the Pharisees said to him: Look, why are they doing on the sabbath what is not lawful?
Y'shua said to them, Have you never read what Dawid did when he had need and was hungry, he and those with him?

How he entered the house of Elohim when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the bread of the table of Master YHWH, which it was not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave ‹it› also to those who were with him?
And he said to them, The sabbath was created for the son of man, and not the son of man for the sabbath.
Therefore the Son of man is Master also of the sabbath.
And Y'shua entered again into the synagogue. And there was a man there whose hand was withered.
And they were watching him, that if he would heal him on the sabbath, they might accuse him.
And he said to that man whose hand was withered: Stand in the middle.
And he said also to them: Is it lawful on the sabbath to do good or to do evil, to give life to a soul or to destroy? But they were silent.
And he looked at them with anger, being grieved over the hardness of their heart. And he said to that man: Stretch out your hand. And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
And the Pharisees went out that very hour with the house of Herodes, and took counsel against him how they might destroy him.
And Y'shua went away with his disciples to the sea. And a great people from Galila was following him, and from Yehuda,
and from Urishlim, and from Adom, and from beyond the Yordanan, and from Tsur, and from Tsidon: a great assembly who had heard all that he did came to him.
And he said to his disciples that they should bring a boat near for him because of the crowd, so they would not throng him.
For he was healing many, so that they were falling on him in order to come near to him.
And those who had plagues of unclean spirits, when they saw him, were falling down and crying out and saying, You are the Son of Elohim.
And he was charging them much not to make him known.
And he went up the mountain and called those he wanted, and they came to him.
And he chose twelve to be with him, and that he might send them out to proclaim,
and that they might have authority to heal the sick and cast out demons.
And to Shimon he gave the name Keefa.
And to Ya'akov son of Zabdai and to Yochanan the brother of Ya'akov he gave them the name Bnai Regshi, that is, Sons of Thunder.
And ‹he chose also› Andrawos and Philipos and Bar-Tulmai and Matai and Toma and Ya'akov son of Chalpai and Tadai and Shimon the Qananya,
and Yehuda Skaryota, he who handed him over. And they came to the house.
And a crowd gathered again, so that they were not able to eat bread.
And his kinsmen heard and went out to seize him, for they were saying, He has gone out of his mind.
And the scribes who had come down from Urishlim were saying, Baalzebub is in him, and by the head of the demons he casts out demons.
And Y'shua called them and said to them in parables, How can Satana cast out Satana?
For if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom is not able to stand.
And if a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
And if Satana rises against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but his end is.
No one can enter the house of a strong man and snatch his goods, unless he first binds the strong man, and then he will plunder his house.
Amen I say to you that all the sins and the blasphemies that the sons of men will blaspheme will be forgiven them.
But whoever blasphemes against the Ruach haKodesh, there is no forgiveness for him forever, but he is liable to the judgment of forever.
Because they were saying that an unclean spirit is in him.
And his mother and his brothers came, standing outside, and sent to call him to them.
Now a crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him: Your mother and your brothers are outside seeking you.
And he answered and said to them: Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?
And he looked at those who were sitting with him, and said: Here is my mother, and here are my brothers!
For whoever does the will of Elohim, he is my brother and my sister and my mother.

And again he began to teach by the side of the sea. And great multitudes were assembled about him; so that he embarked and sat in a ship on the sea, and all the multitude stood on the land by the side of the sea.
And he taught them much by parables. And in his teaching he said:
Listen: a sower went out to sow.
And as he sowed, some ‹seed› fell on the side of the path; and a bird came and ate it.
And other ‹seed› fell on rock where there was not much earth; and at once it sprang up because it had no depth of earth.
But when the sun rose it was scorched; and because it had no root it dried up.
And other ‹seed› fell among thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it gave no fruit.
And other ‹seed› fell on good earth, and came up and grew and gave fruit, some thirty and some sixty and some a hundred.
And he said, Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
And when they were alone, those with him, together with the twelve, asked him about that parable.
And Y'shua said to them, To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of Elohim, but to those outside everything is in similitudes:
that when they see they will see and not see, and when they hear they will hear and not understand, lest they turn and their sins be forgiven them.
And he said to them, Do you not know this similitude? And how will you know all the similitudes?
The sower who sows sows the word.
Now these by the side of the path are those in whom the word is sown; and when they have heard ‹it›, at once Satana comes and takes away the word that was sown in their hearts.
And those sown on the rock are those who, when they hear the word, at once receive it with joy.
And they have no root in themselves, but are temporary; and when affliction or persecution happens because of the word, they quickly stumble.
And those sown among the thorns are those who have heard the word,
and the cares of this world and the deceit of riches and the rest of other desires enter in and choke the word, and it becomes without fruit.
And those sown on the good ground are these who hear the word and receive it and give fruit by thirty and by sixty and by a hundred.
And he said to them: Is a lamp brought to be put under a basket or under a bed? Is it not to be put on a lampstand?
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, and nothing in secret that will not be made known.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.
And he said to them: See what you hear. With the measure you measure, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you who hear.
For to him who has, it will be given; and from him who has not, even what he has will be taken from him.
And he was saying: So is the kingdom of Elohim, like a man who throws seed on the ground,
and sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed grows and lengthens while he does not know.
For the earth brings forth the fruit for him; first the grass, and after it the ear, and then the full wheat in the ear.
But when the fruit is ripe, at once he brings the sickle, because the harvest has come.
And he said: To what shall we liken the kingdom of Elohim, and with what parable shall we compare it?
It is like a grain of mustard which, when it is sown in the earth, is smaller than all the seeds that are on the earth;
And when it is sown, it springs up and becomes greater than all the herbs, and makes great branches, so that the birds can nest under its shade.
With parables like these Y'shua was speaking with them, parables as they were able to hear.
And without a parable he was not speaking with them; but to his disciples, between himself and them, he was explaining everything.
And he said to them on that day in the evening, Let us cross over to the other side.
And they left the crowd and took him as he was in the boat, and other boats were with them.
And there was a great storm and wind, and the waves were falling into the boat, and it was near to being filled.
But Y'shua was asleep on a pillow in the hinder part of the boat. And they came and woke him, and said to him: Our Rabbi, do you not care that we are perishing?
And he rose and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea: Be still; be muzzled. And the wind was still, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them: Why are you so fearful? and why is there no faith in you?
And they feared with a great fear, and were saying one to another: Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
And he came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gadarenes.
And when he went out from the boat, a man from the house of tombs met him, in whom was an unclean spirit.
And he was living in the house of tombs, and no one was able to bind him with chains.
because every time he was bound with fetters and with chains, he would break the chains and cut the fetters, and no one was able to subdue him.
And at all times, by night and by day, he was in the house of tombs and in the mountains, and he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.
And when he saw Y'shua from a distance, he ran and bowed down to him.
And he cried out with a loud voice and said, What do I have to do with you, Y'shua, Son of Elohim the Most High? I adjure you by Elohim that you not torment me.
For he had been saying to him, Come out of the man, unclean spirit.
And he asked him, What is your name? He said to him, Legion is our name, because we are many.
And he was begging him much that he not send him out of the region.
And there was there by the mountain a great herd of pigs feeding.
And those demons were begging him and saying, Send us upon those pigs, that we may enter them.
And he permitted them. And these unclean spirits went out and entered the swine, and that herd ran to the precipice and fell into the sea, about two thousand, and they were choked in the waters.
And those who were tending them fled and told ‹it› in the city and also in the villages, and they went out to see what had happened.
And they came to Y'shua and saw him who had the demons, clothed and sober and sitting, him in whom the legion had been, and they were afraid.
And those who had seen told them how it was for him who had the demons, and also about those swine.
And they began to beg him that he would go from their borders.
And when he went up into the boat, he who had the demons was begging him that he might be with him.
And he did not allow him, but said to him: Go to your house to your people, and tell them what Master YHWH has done for you and has had compassion on you.
And he went and began to proclaim in the ten cities what Y'shua had done for him, and all of them were amazed.
And when Y'shua crossed over in the boat to that other side, again a great crowd gathered to him while he was by the sea.
And one came whose name was Yawarash, from the rulers of the synagogue, and when he saw him he fell at his feet,
and he was begging him much and said to him: My daughter is badly afflicted; come, lay your hand on her, and she will be healed and live.
And Y'shua went with him, and a great crowd was following him and pressing upon him.
Now a certain woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years,
who had suffered much from many physicians and spent everything she had, and was not helped at all, but rather grew worse;
when she heard about Y'shua, came in the press of the crowd from behind him and touched his garment,
for she was saying, If I only touch his garment, I will live.
And at once the spring of her blood dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
And Y'shua at once knew in himself that power had gone out from him, and he turned to the crowd and said, Who touched my clothes?
And his disciples say to him, You see the throng that presses upon you, and you say, Who touched me?
And he looked around to see who had done this.
But the woman, fearing and trembling, for she knew what had happened to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
And he said to her, My daughter, your faith has given you life; go in peace, and be healed of your plague.
And while he was speaking, some from the house of the ruler of the synagogue came and say, Your daughter has died; why then do you still trouble the teacher?
But Y'shua heard the word they spoke, and said to the ruler of the synagogue, Do not fear; only believe.
And he did not allow anyone to go with him, except Shimon Keefa, and Ya'akov, and Yochanan the brother of Ya'akov.
And they came to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and he saw that they were in a tumult and weeping and wailing.
And he went in and said to them: Why are you in a tumult and weeping? The girl is not dead, but is asleep.
And they were laughing at him. But he put them all out, and took the father of the girl and her mother and those who were with him, and went in where the girl was lying.
And he took the girl by the hand and said to her: Girl, arise.
And at once the girl rose and was walking, for she was twelve years old. And they were amazed with a great amazement.
And he commanded them much that no one should know this. And he said that they should give her to eat.
And Y'shua went out from there and came to his city, and his disciples were clinging to him.

And when the sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue. And many who heard ‹him› were astonished, and were saying: Where did this man get these things? And what is this wisdom that is given to him, that mighty works like these are done by his hands!
Is this not the carpenter, the son of Maryam, and the brother of Ya'akov and of Yosa and of Yehuda and of Shimon? And are not his sisters here with us? And they were stumbling over him.
And Y'shua said to them: There is no prophet who is despised except in his city and among his kinsmen and in his house.
And he was not able to do even one mighty work there, except that he laid his hand on a few sick people and healed them.
And he was amazed at the lack of their faith. And he was going around the villages while teaching.
And he called his twelve and began to send them two by two, and he gave them authority over unclean spirits to cast them out.
And he commanded them not to take anything for the road except a staff only, no wallet and no bread and no copper in their purses;
but to wear sandals, and not put on two coats.
And he said to them: Into whichever house you enter, stay there until you go out from there.

And whoever will not receive you and will not hear you, when you go out from there shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony to them. Amen I say to you that it will be more comfortable for Sedom and for Amora in the day of judgment than for that city.
And they went out and proclaimed that ‹men› should repent.
And they were casting out many demons, and they were anointing many sick with oil, and they were healing ‹them›.

And Herodes the king heard about Y'shua, for his name had become known to him, and he was saying: Yochanan the Immerser has risen from the house of the dead; because of this, mighty works are done by him.
Others were saying: He is Eliyahu; and others: He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.
But when Herodes heard ‹of him›, he said: He is that Yochanan whose head I cut off; he has risen from the house of the dead.
For Herodes had sent and seized Yochanan and bound him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of Philipos his brother, whom he had taken.
For Yochanan had said to Herodes: It is not lawful for you to take your brother's wife.
But Herodias herself was hostile to him and wanted to kill him, and she was not able.
For Herodes was afraid of Yochanan, because he knew that he was a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe, and he heard him in many things and did ‹the things›, and he heard him with pleasure.
And there was a known day when Herodes made a supper in the house of his birth for his nobles and the chiliarchs and the chiefs of Galila.
And the daughter of Herodias came in, danced, and pleased Herodes and those reclining with him. And the king said to the girl: Ask of me whatever you want, and I will give it to you.
And he swore to her: Whatever you ask, I will give you, even to half of my kingdom.
But she went out and said to her mother: What shall I ask him? She said to her: The head of Yochanan the Immerser.
And at once she went in with eagerness to the king and said to him, I want you this hour to give me on a dish the head of Yochanan the Immerser.
And it grieved the king greatly; yet because of the oath and because of the guests he would not refuse her.
But at once the king sent an executioner and commanded ‹him› to bring the head of Yochanan. And he went and cut off the head of Yochanan in the prison.
And he brought it on a dish and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
And his disciples heard ‹of it›; and they came and took up his corpse and laid it in a tomb.
And the apostles gathered to Y'shua and told him all they had done and all they had taught.
And he said to them, Come, let us go into the wilderness by ourselves and rest a little. For there were many going and coming, and they had no place even to eat.
And they went by boat to a wilderness place by themselves.
And many saw them as they were going, and recognized them, and they ran on foot from all the cities and arrived there before him.
And Y'shua went out and saw a great crowd, and he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep that have no shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.
And when much time had passed, his disciples came near to him and said to him, This place is a wilderness, and the time is advanced.
Send them away, that they may go into the farms around and into the villages and buy bread for themselves, for they have nothing to eat.
But he said to them, You give them to eat. They say to him, Shall we go buy two hundred denarii of bread and give them to eat?
But he said to them, Go, see how many loaves you have here. And when they saw, they say to him, Five loaves and two fishes.
And he commanded them to make everyone recline by companies on the grass.
And they reclined by companies of a hundred and of fifty.

And he took those five loaves and the two fishes, and looked toward heaven, and blessed and broke the bread and gave to his disciples to set before them, and they divided ‹also› the two fishes among them all.
And they all ate and were satisfied.
And they took up the fragments, twelve baskets full, and of the fish.
And those who ate the bread were five thousand men.
And at once he compelled his disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, to Beth-Tsayda, while he dismissed the crowd.
And when he had dismissed them, he went to the mountain to pray.
And when evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he alone on the land.
And he saw them straining as they rowed, for the wind was against them. And in the fourth watch of the night Y'shua came to them, walking on the water, and he wanted to pass by them.
But they saw him walking on the waters, and they supposed it was a false appearance, and they cried out.
For they all saw him and were afraid. And at once he spoke with them and said to them, Take heart; it is I; do not be afraid.
And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased. And they were greatly amazed and astonished in themselves.
For they had not understood about the bread, because their heart was dull.
And when they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesar.
And when they went out of the boat, at once the men of the place recognized him.
And they ran through all that land, and began to bring those who were badly afflicted, carrying them on beds to where they were hearing that he was.

And wherever he entered into villages and into cities, in the streets they were laying the sick, and they were seeking from him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment; and all those who were touching him were being healed.
And Pharisees and scribes who had come from Urishlim gathered to him.
And they saw some of his disciples eating bread with their hands unwashed, and they found fault.
For all the Yehudaye and the Pharisees, unless they carefully wash their hands, do not eat, because they hold fast the tradition of the elders.

And ‹coming› from the marketplace, unless they immerse, they do not eat. And there are many other things which they have received to keep, ‹such as› the immersions of cups and of pots and of bronze vessels and of couches.
And the scribes and Pharisees asked him: Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with their hands unwashed?
But he said to them: Well did Eshaya the prophet prophesy about you, pretenders, as it is written: This people honors me with its lips, but their heart is very far from me.
And in vain they revere me, while they teach as doctrines the commandments of the sons of men.
For you have forsaken the commandment of Elohim, and you hold fast the tradition of the sons of men, immersions of cups and of pots and many things like these.
He said ‹also› to them: You do well to reject the commandment of Elohim, that you may establish your tradition.
For Moshe said: Honor your father and your mother; and whoever reviles father or mother will surely die.
But you say: If a man says to his father or to his mother, It is my offering, whatever you might gain from me,
and you do not allow him to do anything for his father or his mother.
And you reject the word of Elohim because of the tradition that you hand down. And many things like these you do.
And Y'shua called the whole crowd and said to them: Hear me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that enters him that can defile him. But what comes out of him, that is what defiles a person.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
And when Y'shua entered the house away from the crowd, his disciples asked him about this parable.
He said to them: Are you also so dull? Do you not know that everything that enters a person from outside cannot defile him?
because it does not enter into his heart, but into his belly, and is thrown out in the purge that cleanses all the food.
But that which goes out from a man, that defiles the man.
For from within, from the heart of the sons of men, go out evil thoughts, adultery, fornication,
theft, murder, greed, wickedness, deceit, shamelessness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, folly.
All these evil things go out from within and defile the man.
From there Y'shua rose and came to the border of Tsur and of Tsidon. And he entered a house and did not want anyone to know of him, and he could not be hidden.
For immediately a certain woman heard of him, who had an unclean spirit for her daughter, and she came and fell before his feet.
Now that woman was a pagan from Punyqa of Surya, and she was begging him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
Y'shua said to her: Let the children first be satisfied, for it is not good to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs.
But she answered and said to him: Yes, my Master; even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs.
Y'shua said to her: Go; because of this word, the demon has gone out from your daughter.
And she went to her house and found her daughter lying on the bed, and the demon gone out from her.
Again Y'shua went out from the border of Tsur and of Tsidon and came to the sea of Galila, in the border of the Ten Cities.
And they brought to him one who was deaf and stammering, and they were asking him to lay a hand on him.
And he led him aside from the crowd by himself, and put his fingers into his ears, and spit and touched his tongue,
and looked toward heaven and sighed and said to him: Be opened.
And in that hour his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke plainly.
And he warned them that they should tell no one; and the more he was warning them, the more they were proclaiming it.
And they were marveling exceedingly and saying, He does everything well: he makes the deaf hear, and those who do not speak speak.
And in those days, when there was a great crowd and they had nothing to eat, he called his disciples and said to them:
I have compassion on this crowd, for look, they have stayed with me three days and they have nothing to eat.
And if I send them away fasting to their homes, they will faint on the way; for some of them have come from far away.
His disciples say to him: From where can anyone here in the wilderness satisfy all these with bread?
And he asked them: How many loaves do you have? They say to him, Seven.
And he directed the crowd to recline on the ground; and he took those seven loaves and blessed and broke and gave to his disciples to set out, and they set them before the crowd.
And there were a few fish; and he also blessed them and said that they should set them forth.
And they ate and were satisfied, and they took up the leftover fragments, seven baskets.
Now the people who ate were about four thousand.
And he dismissed them and at once went up into the boat with his disciples and came to the place Dalmanutha.
And the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with him, and they were asking him for a sign from heaven while testing him.
And he sighed in his spirit and said, Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I say to you, no sign will be given to this generation.
And he left them and got into the boat, and they went over to the other side.
And they had forgotten to take bread, and there was only one loaf with them in the boat.
And he charged them and said to them: Look, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the leaven of Herodes.
And they were reasoning with one another and saying: It is because we have no bread.
But Y'shua knew ‹it› and said to them: Why are you reasoning that you have no bread? Do you still not know and not understand? Do you still have a hard heart?
You have eyes and do not see, and you have ears and do not hear, and you do not remember?
He says to them, And when the seven to four thousand, how many baskets full of the fragments did you take up? They say, Seven.
He says to them, How is it that until now you do not understand?
And he came to Beth-Tsayda, and they brought a blind man to him, and they were seeking from him that he would touch him.
And he took the blind man by his hand and led him outside the village, and spit on his eyes and put his hand on him and asked him what he saw.
He looked and said, I see men like trees that are walking.
Again he put his hand on his eyes, and he was restored, and he saw everything clearly.
And he sent him to his house, and said: Do not even enter the village, and do not tell anyone in the village.
And Y'shua and his disciples went out to the villages of Qasarya of Philippos. And as they were on the way he asked his disciples, and said to them: Who do men say about me that I am?
And they said: ‹You are› Yochanan the Immerser; and others: ‹You are› Eliyahu; and others: ‹You are› one of the prophets.
Y'shua said to them: But who do you say about me that I am? Shimon answered and said to him: You are the Mashiyach, the Son of the living Elohim.
And he charged them that they should tell no one about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of man is about to suffer much, and be rejected by the elders and by the chief priests and by the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise.
And he was speaking the word openly. And Keefa took him and began to rebuke him.
But he turned and looked at his disciples and rebuked Shimon and said, Go behind me, Satana, for you are not thinking of what is of Elohim, but of what is of the sons of men.
And Y'shua called the crowd together with his disciples and said to them, Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and come after me.
For whoever wants to keep his life will lose it, and whoever will lose his life because of me and because of my good news will keep it.
For what will a man be profited if he gains the whole world and loses his life?
Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?
For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this sinful and adulterous generation, the Son of man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with his holy messengers.
And he was saying to them, Amen I say to you, that there are people standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of Elohim that has come with power.
And after six days Y'shua took Keefa and Ya'akov and Yochanan and led them up a high mountain by themselves, and he was transformed before their eyes.
And his clothing was shining and very white like snow, such that the sons of men on earth are not able to whiten.
And Eliyahu and Moshe appeared to them while speaking with Y'shua.
And Keefa said to him, Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. And let us make three shelters, one for you and one for Moshe and one for Eliyahu.
But he did not know what he was saying, for they were in fear.
And there was a cloud, and it was overshadowing them, and a voice from the cloud that said: This is my beloved Son. Hear him.
And suddenly when the disciples looked, they saw no one except Y'shua alone with them.
And as they were going down from the mountain, he was commanding them that they should tell no one anything they had seen, except when the Son of man has risen from the dead.
And they held that word in their soul, and were inquiring what this word is: when he has risen from the house of the dead.
And they were asking him and saying: Why then do the scribes say that Eliyahu must come first?
