He said to them: Eliyahu comes first, that he may restore everything; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he will suffer much and be rejected.
But I say to you that Eliyahu has also come, and they have done to him all that they wanted, just as it is written of him.
And when he came to the disciples, he saw a great crowd with them, and the scribes disputing with them.
And at once the whole crowd saw him and were amazed, and they ran and greeted him.
And he asked the scribes, What are you disputing with them?
And one from the crowd answered and said, Teacher, I have brought my son to you, who has a spirit that does not speak.
And wherever it seizes him, it dashes him and he foams and gnashes his teeth and withers. And I told your disciples to cast it out, and they could not.
Y'shua answered and said to him: O unbelieving generation! Until when will I be with you, and until when will I bear with you? Bring him to me.
And they brought him to him. And when the spirit saw him, at once it threw him down, and he fell on the ground and was wallowing and foaming.
And Y'shua asked his father how long a time it had been for him like this. He said to him: From his childhood.
And many times it has thrown him into the fire and into the water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help me and have compassion on me.
Y'shua said to him: If you can believe, everything can be for the one who believes.
And at once the father of the boy cried out while weeping and said: I believe, my Master; help the lack of my faith.
And when Y'shua saw that the people were running and gathering to him, he rebuked that unclean spirit and said to it: Deaf and mute spirit, I command you, come out of him, and do not enter him again.
And that demon cried out greatly and convulsed him and came out. And he was like a dead person, so that many said he had died.
But Y'shua took him by his hand and raised him up.
And when Y'shua entered the house, his disciples asked him privately: Why could we not cast it out?
He said to them: This kind cannot come out by anything except by fasting and by prayer.
And when he went out from there, they were passing through Galila, and he did not want anyone to know him.
But they did not understand the word, and they were afraid to ask him.
And they came to Kfar-Nachum. And when they entered the house, he was asking them, What were you reasoning among yourselves on the way?
But they were silent, for on the way they had argued with one another who was the greatest among them.
And Y'shua sat down and called the twelve and said to them, Whoever wants to be first will be last of all and servant of all.
And he took a child and set him in the middle and took him on his arms and said to them,
Everyone who receives one like this child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me does not receive me ‹only›, but him who sent me.
Yochanan said to him, Rabbi, we saw a man casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him because he does not follow us.
Y'shua said to them, Do not forbid him, for there is no one who does a mighty work in my name and can readily speak evil of me.
Whoever therefore is not against you is for you.
But whoever will give you a cup of water only in the name that you are of the Mashiyach, amen I say to you, he will not lose his reward.
And whoever will cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a millstone of a donkey were hung on his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is better for you to enter into life maimed than, having two hands, to go into Gehenna;
where their worm does not die, and their fire is not extinguished.
And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is better for you to enter into life lame, than when you have two feet to fall into Gehenna;
where their worm does not die, and their fire is not extinguished.
And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out: it is better for you to enter with one eye into the kingdom of Elohim, than when you have two eyes to fall into the Gehenna of fire;
where their worm does not die, and their fire is not extinguished.
For everything will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
Salt is a good thing: but if the salt becomes insipid, with what will it be salted? Let there be salt in you, and be in peace one with another.
And he rose from there and came to the border of Yehuda, to the crossing of the Yordanan. And great crowds went there to him, and he was teaching them again as he was accustomed.
And the Pharisees came near, testing him, and asking if it is lawful for a man to leave his wife.
He said to them: What did Moshe command you?
But they say: Moshe allowed us to write a bill of divorce and send ‹her› away.
Y'shua answered and said to them: Because of the hardness of your heart he wrote you this commandment.
But from the beginning Elohim made them male and female.
Because of this a man will leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife:
and the two of them will be one flesh. From then on they are not two, but one flesh.
What Elohim has therefore joined, a human must not separate.
And his disciples asked him again in the house about this.
And he said to them, Everyone who divorces his wife and takes another commits adultery.
And if a woman divorces her husband and becomes another's, she commits adultery.
And they were bringing children to him, that he might touch them. But his disciples were rebuking those who were bringing them.
But Y'shua saw it and was displeased, and he said to them, Let the children come to me, and do not forbid them, for of those who are like these is the kingdom of Elohim.
Truly I say to you, that everyone who does not receive the kingdom of Elohim like a child will not enter it.
And he took them up in his arms, and laid his hand on them, and blessed them.
And as he was going on the road, one ran and fell on his knees and was asking him, and said, Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit life forever?
Y'shua said to him, Why do you call me good? There is none good but one, Elohim.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not kill, and do not give false testimony, do not defraud; honor your father and your mother.
But he answered and said to him: Teacher, all these I have kept from my childhood.

But Y'shua looked at him and loved him and said to him: One thing is lacking to you. Go, sell everything that you have and give to the poor, and you will have a treasure in heaven; and take up the cross and come after me.
But he was saddened by this word and went away grieving, for he had many possessions.
But Y'shua looked at his disciples and said to them: How hard it is for those who have possessions to enter the kingdom of Elohim!
But the disciples were wondering at his words. And Y'shua answered again and said to them: My children, how hard it is for those who trust in their possessions to enter the kingdom of Elohim!
It is easier for a camel to enter the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of Elohim.
But they were wondering still more and saying among themselves, Who is able to live?
Y'shua looked at them and said to them, With the sons of men this is not possible, but with Elohim ‹it is›; for with Elohim everything is possible.
And Keefa began to say, Look, we have left everything and have followed you.
Y'shua answered and said, Amen I say to you, There is no one who leaves house or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields because of me and because of my good news,
who will not receive a hundredfold now in this time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields with persecutions, and in the world that is coming life forever.
But many who are first will be last, and the last ‹who will be› first.

And as they were going up on the road to Urishlim, Y'shua was going ahead of them, and they were amazed and were walking after him while afraid. And he took his twelve and began to tell them what was going to happen to him.
We are going up to Urishlim, and the Son of man is delivered to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and will deliver him to the nations.
And they will mock him and scourge him and spit in his face and kill him, and on the third day he will rise.
And Ya'akov and Yochanan, the sons of Zabdi, came near to him and said to him: Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask.
He said to them: What do you want me to do for you?
They say to him, Give us that one may sit at your right and one at your left in your glory.
But he said to them, You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be immersed with the immersion that I am immersed with?
They say to him, We are able. Y'shua says to them, The cup that I drink you will drink, and the immersion that I am immersed with you will be immersed with.
But that you should sit at my right and at my left is not mine to give, except to those for whom it is prepared.
And when the ten heard ‹it›, they began to murmur against Ya'akov and Yochanan.
And Y'shua called them and said to them, You know that those who are accounted chiefs of the nations are their masters, and their great ones have authority over them.
But it will not be so among you. But whoever among you wants to be great will be a servant to you.
And whoever among you wants to be first will be a servant of everyone.
For even the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
And they came to Iriycho. And as Y'shua went out from Iriycho, he and his disciples and a great crowd, Timai son of Timai, a blind man, was sitting by the side of the road and begging.
And he heard that it was Y'shua the Natsraya, and he began to cry out and to say, Son of Dawid, have mercy on me.
And many were rebuking him that he should be silent. But he cried out all the more and said, Son of Dawid, have mercy on me.
And Y'shua stood and directed that they call him. And they called the blind man and said to him, Take courage, get up, he is calling you.
And the blind man threw off his garment and rose and came to Y'shua.
Y'shua said to him, What do you want me to do for you? And the blind man said to him, Rabbi, that I may see.
And Y'shua said to him, See; your faith has given you life. And at once he received sight, and he went on the way.
And when he drew near to Urishlim, beside Beth-Paga and Beth-Anya, toward the mountain of olives, he sent two of his disciples,
and said to them: Go to the village that is opposite us, and as soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied, on which no one of the sons of men has ridden: loose ‹him›, and bring him.
And if anyone says to you, Why are you doing this? Say to him: Because our Master has need of him. And at once he will send him here.
And they went, and found the colt tied by the door outside in the street. And as they were loosing ‹him›,
some of those standing there said to them: What are you doing, loosing the colt?
But they said to them as Y'shua had commanded them; and they let them go.
And they brought the colt to Y'shua, and threw their garments on him, and Y'shua rode on him.
And many were spreading their garments on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
And those before him and those after him were shouting and saying, Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of Master YHWH.
And blessed is the coming kingdom of our father Dawid. Hosanna in the highest ‹heavens›.
And Y'shua entered Urishlim to the temple and saw everything. And when the time of evening came, he went out to Beth-Anya with the twelve.
And on another day, when he went out from Beth-Anya, he was hungry.

And he saw one fig tree from a distance that had leaves on it, and he came to it, if he might find something on it. And when he came, he found nothing on it except leaves, for the time of figs had not come.
And he said to it: From now on and forever, no one will eat fruit from you. And his disciples heard it. And they came to Urishlim.

And Y'shua entered the temple of Elohim and began to drive out those who were buying and selling in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those who were selling doves.
And he would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
And he was teaching and saying to them: Is it not written that my house will be called a house of prayer for all the peoples? But you have made it a den of robbers.
And the chief priests and the scribes heard, and they were seeking how they might destroy him, for they were afraid of him, because all the people were amazed at his teaching.
And in the morning, as they were passing by, they saw that fig tree dried up from its root.
And Shimon remembered and said to him, Rabbi, look, that fig tree that you cursed has dried up.
And Y'shua answered and said to them, Let the faith of Elohim be in you.

Amen, I say to you that whoever says to this mountain, Be taken up and fall into the sea, and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he said will be, it will be for him, the thing he said.
Because of this I say to you that everything you pray and ask, believe that you receive, and it will be yours.
And when you stand to pray, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your offenses.
But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive you your offences.
And they came again to Urishlim. And as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders came to him,
and said to him: By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority to do these things?
But Y'shua said to them: I also will ask you one word, that you may tell me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
The immersion of Yochanan, from where is it? from heaven, or from the sons of men? Tell me.
And they reasoned in themselves and said: If we say to him, From heaven, he will say to us, And why did you not believe him?
But if we say, From the sons of men, there is fear from the people; for all of them were holding Yochanan that he is truly a prophet.
And they answered and say to Y'shua: We do not know. He says to them: Neither do I say to you by what authority I do these things.

And he began to speak with them in similitudes. A certain man planted a vineyard and enclosed it with a hedge, and dug in it a winepress, and built a tower in it, and handed it over to laborers, and went far away.
And he sent his servant to the laborers at the season, that he might take from the fruits of the vineyard.
But they beat him and sent him away empty.
And he sent again to them another servant; and him also they stoned and wounded and sent him away in shame.
And he sent again another, and him they killed. And he sent many other servants, and of them they beat, and of them they killed.
But at the last he had one beloved son, and he sent him to them afterward; for he said, Perhaps they will be ashamed before my son.
But those laborers said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.
And they took him and killed ‹him› and cast ‹him› out of the vineyard.
What then will the master of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy those laborers, and give the vineyard to others.
And have you not even read this writing: The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.
From Master YHWH was this, and it is wonderful in our eyes.
And they were seeking to seize him, and they feared the people, for they knew that he spoke this parable against them. And they left him and went away.
And they sent to him some from the scribes and from the house of Herodes, to trap him in a word.

And they came and asked him: Teacher, we know that you are true, and you do not take concern for anyone, for you do not look on the face of the sons of men, but in truth you teach the way of Elohim. Is it lawful to give the head-tax to Caesar, or not? Shall we give, or shall we not give?
But he knew their craftiness and said to them: Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see.
And they brought ‹one› to him. He said to them: Whose is this image and this inscription? And they said: Caesar's.
Y'shua said to them: What is Caesar's, give to Caesar, and what is Elohim's, ‹give› to Elohim. And they wondered at him.
And Sadducees came to him, those who say there is no resurrection, and they were asking him and saying:
Teacher, Moshe wrote to us that if a man's brother dies and leaves a wife and leaves no children, his brother is to take his wife and raise up seed for his brother.
There were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died and left no seed.
And the second took her and died, and he also left no seed, and the third likewise.
And the seven of them took her and left no seed. Last of all of them the woman also died.
In the resurrection, then, of which of them will she be the wife? For the seven of them took her.
Y'shua said to them, Is it not because of this that you err, that you do not know the writings, nor the power of Elohim?
For when they rise from the dead, they do not take wives, nor do wives become ‹joined› to husbands; but they are like the messengers who are in heaven.

But concerning the dead, that they rise, have you not read in the book of Moshe, how from the bush Elohim said to him: I am the Elohim of Avraham, and the Elohim of Yitz'chak, and the Elohim of Ya'akov?
And he is not Elohim of the dead, but of the living. You therefore err greatly.
And one of the scribes came near and heard them disputing, and saw that he answered them well, and asked him, Which is the first commandment of all?
Y'shua said to him: The first of all the commandments ‹is›: Hear, Yisrael; Master YHWH our Elohim, Master YHWH is one.
And you shall love Master YHWH your Elohim with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength. This is the first commandment.
And the second, which is like it, ‹is›: You will love your neighbor as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these.
The scribe said to him, Well said, Rabbi. You have spoken the truth, that he is one, and there is no other besides him.
And that a person love him with all the heart and with all the mind and with all the soul and with all the strength, and love his neighbor as himself, is more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.
But Y'shua saw that he answered the word wisely; he answered and said to him: You are not far from the kingdom of Elohim. And no one dared again to question him.
And Y'shua answered and said while teaching in the temple: How do the scribes say that the Mashiyach is the son of Dawid?
For Dawid himself said by the Ruach haKodesh: Master YHWH said to my Master, Sit at my right hand until I place your enemies as a footstool under your feet.
Dawid therefore calls him my Master; and how is he his son? And all the crowd was hearing him gladly.
And in his teaching he was saying to them, Watch out for the scribes who want to walk in robes and love greetings in the marketplace,
and the chief seats in the synagogues and the chief couches at feasts.
They devour the houses of widows under the pretext that they lengthen their prayers. These will receive a greater judgment.
And as Y'shua sat opposite the treasury, he was watching how the crowd cast money into the treasury. And many rich ones were casting in much.
And one poor widow came and cast in two mites, which are a shamuna.
And Y'shua called his disciples and said to them, Amen I say to you that this poor widow has cast into the treasury more than all the people who are casting.
For they all cast in from what abounded to them, but she from her poverty has cast in all that she had, her whole property.
And when Y'shua went out from the temple, one of his disciples said to him: Teacher, look, see what stones and what buildings!
But Y'shua said to him: Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here a stone upon a stone that will not be torn down.
And when Y'shua sat on the mount of Olives opposite the temple, Keefa and Ya'akov and Yochanan and Andraos asked him privately:
Tell us, when will these things be? and what ‹will be› the sign when all these things are near to being fulfilled?
But he, Y'shua, began to say to them: Watch, lest someone mislead you.
For many will come in my name and will say, I am, and they will mislead many.
But when you hear of battles and the rumor of battles, do not be afraid; it is going to be, but the end is not yet.

For people will rise against people, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in place after place, and there will be famines and tumults. These are the beginning of the birth-pains.
But look to yourselves; for they will deliver you up to judges, and in their assemblies you will be beaten, and before kings and governors you will stand because of me, for a testimony to them.
But first my good news is to be proclaimed among all the peoples.

And when they bring you near to deliver you up, do not be anxious beforehand what you will speak, and do not meditate; but whatever is given to you in that hour, speak that; for it is not you who speak, but the Ruach haKodesh.
And brother will deliver up his brother to death, and father his son; and children will rise against their parents and put them to death.
And you will be hated by everyone on account of my name. But whoever perseveres to the end, he will live.

But when you see the profane sign of desolation that was spoken by Daniyel the prophet standing where it ought not (let him who reads understand), then those who are in Yehuda are to flee to the mountain:
and let him who is on the roof not come down and not enter ‹it› to take anything from his house:
and let him who is in the field not turn back to take his clothing.
But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse in those days!
But pray that your flight will not be in winter.
For in those days there will be affliction such as has not been from the beginning of the creation that Elohim created until now, and will not be.
And if Master YHWH had not shortened those days, no flesh would live. But because of the chosen ones whom he chose, he has shortened those days.
Then if anyone says to you, Look, here is the Mashiyach, or look, there, do not believe.
For false Mashiyachs will arise, and prophets of falsehood, and they will give signs and wonders, and will lead astray if possible even the chosen ones.
But you take heed. I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days after that affliction, the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light.
And the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of man when he comes in the clouds with great power and with glory.
Then he will send his messengers and gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from the end of the earth as far as the end of heaven.
Now learn a parable from the fig tree. When its branch has become tender and put forth its leaves, you know that summer has arrived.
So also you, when you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the door.
Amen, I say to you that this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But of that day and of that hour no one knows, not even the messengers of heaven, and not the Son, but only the Father.
Look, stay awake and pray, for you do not know when the time is.
For it is like a man who went on a journey and left his house and gave authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.
Stay awake therefore, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming, in the evening or at midnight or at the rooster’s crowing or in the morning,
lest he come suddenly and find you sleeping.
And what I say to you, I say to all of you: Be watchful.
And after two days was the Passover of unleavened bread. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize him by deceit and kill him.
And they were saying, Not at the feast, lest there be a disturbance among the people.

And when he was in Beth-Anya in the house of Shimon the leper, as he reclined, a woman came who had on her an alabaster flask of nard perfume, pure, of great price; and she opened it and poured it on the head of Y'shua.
But there were some of the disciples who were displeased in themselves and said, Why was this waste of the perfume?
For it could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor. And they were angry with her.
But Y'shua said, Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has done a beautiful deed for me.
For the poor are always with you, and whenever you want you can do what is good for them. But I am not always with you.
What she had she has done, and she has gone ahead and anointed my body as for burial.
Truly I say to you that wherever this good news of mine is proclaimed in all the world, what this woman has done will also be told in memory of her.
But Yehuda Sakaryota, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests in order to hand Y'shua over to them.
And when they heard, they rejoiced and promised to give him money. And he was seeking an opportunity to hand him over.
And on the first day of unleavened bread, on which the Yehudaye sacrifice the passover, his disciples said to him: Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the passover?
And he sent two of his disciples and said to them: Go to the city, and look, a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Go after him.
And wherever he enters, say to the master of the house: Our Rabbi says, Where is the lodging place where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?
And look, he will show you a large upper room that is furnished and prepared. There make ready for us.
And his disciples went out and came into the city and found it as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when it was evening, he came with his twelve.
And as they were reclining and eating, Y'shua said: Amen, I say to you that one of you who eats with me will betray me.
And they began to be distressed, and they said to him one by one, Is it I?
And he said to them, It is one of the twelve who dips with me in the dish.
And the Son of man goes as it is written of him. But woe to that man by whose hand the Son of man is delivered up. It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.
And as they were eating, Y'shua took bread and blessed and broke and gave to them, and said to them, Take; this is my body.
And he took the cup and gave thanks and blessed and gave to them, and they all drank from it.
And he said to them, This is my blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many.
Truly I say to you, that I will not drink again of the produce of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of Elohim.
And they sang praise and went out to the mount of Olives.
And Y'shua said to them: All of you will be stumbled in me this night, for it is written, I will strike the shepherd, and his sheep will be scattered.
But when I have risen, I will go before you to Galila.
Keefa said to him: Even if all of them are stumbled, yet I will not.
Y'shua said to him: Truly I say to you, that today, in this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.
But he was saying all the more: If it should be for me to die with you, I will not deny you, my Master. And like him, they also all said.
And they came to the place which is called Gadsaman, and he said to his disciples, Sit here while I pray.
And he took with him Keefa and Ya'akov and Yochanan, and began to be gloomy and distressed.
And he said to them: My soul is in anguish even to death. Stay here and be watchful.
And he drew near a little and fell on the ground, and was praying that if it is possible the hour might pass from him.
And he said: Abba, my Father, you can do all things. Let this cup pass from me. Yet not my will, but yours.
And he came and found them sleeping. And he said to Keefa, Shimon, are you sleeping? Could you not watch one hour?
Watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is willing and ready, but the body is weak.
And he went again and prayed, and said the same word.
And he returned and came again and found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy. And they did not know what to say to him.
And he came the third time and said to them, Sleep on now and take your rest. The end has come, and the hour has come, and look, the Son of man is delivered into the hands of sinners.
Get up, let us go. Look, the one who hands me over is near.
And while he was still speaking, Yehuda Skaryota, one of the twelve, came, and a large crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
And the betrayer who was handing ‹him› over had given them a sign and said, The one I kiss is he. Seize him carefully and lead him away.
And at once he came near and said to him, Rabbi, Rabbi, and kissed him.
But they laid hands on him and seized him.
But one of those standing by drew a sword and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
But Y'shua answered and said to them, Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me?
Every day I was with you while I taught in the temple, and you did not seize me. But this has happened so that the writings may be fulfilled.
Then his disciples left him and fled.
And a certain young man followed after him, wrapped in a linen cloth on ‹his› naked ‹body›, and they seized him.
But he left the linen cloth and fled naked.
And they led Y'shua away to Qayapa the high priest, and all the chief priests and the scribes and the elders assembled to him.
But Shimon followed after him from a distance as far as inside the courtyard of the high priest, and he sat with the servants and warmed himself opposite the fire.
But the chief priests and all their assembly were seeking testimony against Y'shua to put him to death, and they did not find ‹it›.
For many were testifying against him, ‹but› their testimonies were not equal.
But some false witnesses stood up against him and said:
We heard him say, I will tear down this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I will build another that is not made with hands.
And not even so was their testimony equal.
And the chief priest stood up in the middle and asked Y'shua and said, Do you not return an answer? What are these testifying against you?
But he was silent and answered him nothing. And again the high priest asked him and said, Are you the Mashiyach, the Son of the Blessed?
But Y'shua said to him, I am. And you will see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of power and coming on the clouds of heaven.
Then the high priest tore his tunic and said, What further need do we have of witnesses?
Look, from his mouth you have heard the blasphemy. How does it seem to you? And they all judged that he is guilty of death.
And some began to spit in his face and to cover his face and strike him and say, Prophesy! And the servants were hitting him on his cheeks.
And while Shimon was below in the courtyard, one maid of the high priest came,
and saw him warming himself; and she looked at him and said to him: And you also were with Y'shua the Natsraya.
But he denied and said: I do not know what you are saying. And he went out outside to the porch; and the rooster crowed.
And the maid saw him again, and she began to say to those standing by: This one also is one of them.
But he again denied ‹it›. And a little after, those standing there said again to Keefa: Truly you are one of them; for you are also a Galilaya, and your speech is like ‹it›.
And he began to curse and swear: I do not know this man of whom you speak.
And at that hour the rooster crowed a second time. And Shimon remembered the word of Y'shua, who had said to him: Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times. And he began to weep.
And right away in the morning the chief priests made a counsel with the elders and with the scribes and with the whole assembly, and they bound Y'shua and led him away and handed him over to Pilatos.
And Pilatos asked him, Are you the king of the Yehudaye? But he answered and said to him, You have said.
And the chief priests were accusing him of many things.
But Pilatos again asked him and said to him, Do you not give an answer? See how many things they testify against you!
But Y'shua gave no answer at all, so that Pilatos wondered.
Now it was his custom at every feast to release to them one prisoner, whoever they asked.
And there was one who was called Bar Abba, who was bound with the doers of sedition, those who had done murder in the sedition.
And the people cried out and began to ask that he do for them as he was accustomed.
But Pilatos answered and said, Do you want me to release to you the king of the Yehudaye?
For Pilatos knew that from envy the chief priests had delivered him up.
But the chief priests all the more urged the crowd that he release Bar Abba to them.
But Pilatos said to them, What then do you want me to do to this one whom you call the king of the Yehudaye?
But they again cried out, Crucify him.
But Pilatos said to them, What evil has he done? And they were crying out all the more, Crucify him.
But Pilatos wanted to do the will of the crowd, and he released Bar-Abba to them, and after scourging Y'shua he delivered him to them to be crucified.
But the soldiers led him inside the courtyard, which is the Praetorium, and they called together the whole cohort.
And they clothed him in purple, and braided a crown of thorns and put it on him.
And they began to salute him, Peace, king of the Yehudaye!
And they were striking him on his head with a reed and spitting in his face, and bowing on their knees and worshipping him.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped him of the purple and clothed him in his own garments, and led him out to crucify him.
And they pressed one who was passing by, Shimon a Qurinyan, who was coming from the village, the father of Alexandros and of Rufus, to take up his cross.
And they brought him to Gagulta, a place that is interpreted The Skull.
And they gave him wine mixed with myrrh to drink; but he did not take it.
And when they had crucified him, they divided his garments and cast lots on them, who should take what.
It was the third hour when they crucified him.
And the cause of his death was written in this inscription: This is the king of the Yehudaye.
And they crucified with him two robbers, one on his right and one on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled that says: He was reckoned with the wicked.
And those who were passing by were also reviling him, shaking their heads and saying: Ah, you who destroy the temple and build it in three days,
save yourself and come down from the cross.
And so also the chief priests were mocking one with another, and the scribes, and saying: He gave life to others; he cannot give life to his own life.
The Mashiyach, the king of Yisrael, let him come down now from the cross, that we may see ‹it› and believe in him. And those also who were crucified with him were reviling him.
And when the sixth hour came, there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Y'shua cried out with a loud voice and said: Eil, Eil, lemana shabaqthani; that is: My Elohim, my Elohim, why have you left me?
And some of those who stood by, when they heard it, were saying: He is calling Eliyahu.
But one ran and filled a sponge with vinegar and tied it on a reed to give him drink. And they said: Leave him; let us see if Eliyahu will come to take him down.
But Y'shua cried out with a loud voice and finished.
And the curtain of the temple door was torn in two from top to bottom.
And when the centurion who was standing near him saw that he cried out like this and finished, he said, Truly this man was the Son of Elohim.
And there were also women looking on from a distance: Maryam Magdalitha, and Maryam the mother of Ya'akov the little and of Yosa, and Shalom;
who, when he was in Galila, were following him and serving him; and many other women who had gone up with him to Urishlim.
And when it was evening of the preparation, which is before the sabbath,
Yosip of Ramtha, an honorable counselor, who also himself was waiting for the kingdom of Elohim, came and took courage and went in to Pilatos and asked for the body of Y'shua.
But Pilatos wondered if he was already dead, and he called the centurion and asked him if he had died before the time.
And when he learned it, he gave his body to Yosip.
And Yosip bought linen and took him down and wrapped him in it and placed him in a tomb that was hewn in the rock, and rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
But Maryam Magdalitha and Maryam ‹the mother› of Yosa saw where he was laid.
And when the Sabbath had passed, Maryam Magdalitha and Maryam ‹the mother› of Ya'akov and Shalom bought aromatics, that they might come and anoint him.
And in the morning of the first of the week they came to the house of the tomb as the sun rose.
And they were saying in their souls: Who then will roll the stone away for us from the door of the house of the tomb?
And they looked and saw that the stone was rolled away, for it was very great.
And they entered the house of the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right, wrapped in a white robe, and they were amazed.
But he said to them: Do not be afraid. You are seeking Y'shua the Natsraya who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look, the place where he was laid.
But go, tell his disciples and Keefa: He goes before you to Galila; there you will see him, as he said to you.
And when they heard, they fled and went out from the tomb, for astonishment and trembling had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
But in the morning of the first day of the week he rose, and he appeared first to Maryam Magdalitha, she from whom he had cast out seven demons.
And she went and told those who had been with him, while they were mourning and weeping.
And they, when they heard ‹the women› say that he is alive and has appeared to them, did not believe them.
After these things he appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking and going to a village.
And they went and told the rest; they did not believe them either.
And afterward he appeared to the eleven as they reclined, and he reproved the deficiency of their faith and the hardness of their heart, because they did not believe those who had seen him risen.
And he said to them, Go into all the world and proclaim my good news in all creation.
Whoever believes and is immersed lives, and whoever does not believe is condemned.
And these signs will follow those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons, and they will speak in new tongues.
And they will take up snakes, and if they drink a deadly poison it will not harm them, and they will lay their hands on the sick and they will be healed.
And Y'shua our Master, after he spoke with them, ascended to heaven and sat at the right hand of Elohim.
And they went out and proclaimed in every place, and our Master was helping them and confirming their words by the signs they were doing.
Because many have wanted to write the account of the events of which we are fully assured,
as those who from the first were eyewitnesses and ministers of his word delivered them to us;
it seemed right to me also, because I had carefully followed all of them, to write everything to you in order, excellent Theophilus,
so that you may know the truth of the words in which you were instructed.

In the days of Herodes the king of Yehuda there was a certain priest whose name was Zakharya, of the service of the house of Abiya, and his wife was of the daughters of Aharon, and her name was Elishaba.
And both of them were upright before Elohim, and they walked in all his commandments and in the righteousness of Master YHWH without blame.
But they had no child, because Elishaba was barren, and both of them were advanced in their days.
Now it happened that while he was serving as priest in the order of his service before Elohim,
according to the custom of the priesthood it fell to him to place the incense, and he went into the temple of Master YHWH,
and the whole assembly of the people was praying outside at the time of the incense.
And a messenger of Master YHWH appeared to Zakharya, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
And Zakharya was agitated when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
And the messenger said to him, Do not fear, Zakharya, because your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elishaba will bear you a son, and you will call his name Yochanan.
And you will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great before Master YHWH, and wine and strong drink he will not drink, and he will be filled with the Ruach haKodesh while he is still in his mother's womb.
And many of the sons of Yisrael he will turn to Master YHWH their Elohim.

And he will go before him in the spirit and power of Eliyahu the prophet, to turn the heart of the fathers upon the children, and those who are not persuaded to the knowledge of the righteous, and he will prepare for Master YHWH a perfect people.
And Zakharya said to the messenger, How will I know this? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in her days.
And the messenger answered and said to him, I am Gabriel, who stand before Elohim, and I was sent to speak with you and to announce these things to you.
From now on you will be silent and unable to speak until the day when these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which are fulfilled in their time.
And the people were standing and waiting for Zakharya, and they wondered at his delay in the temple.
And when Zakharya came out, he was not able to speak with them, and they understood that he had seen a vision in the temple. And he was making signs to them, and remained mute.
And when the days of his service were fulfilled, he went to his house.
And it was after those days that Elishaba his wife conceived, and she hid herself five months, and she was saying:
These things Master YHWH has done for me, in the days when he looked on me to take away my reproach among the sons of men.
And in the sixth month the messenger Gabriyel was sent from Elohim to Galila, to a city whose name is Natsrath,
to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name is Yosip, of the house of Dawid; and the virgin's name was Maryam.
And the messenger went in to her and said to her: Peace to you, full of favor; our Master is with you, blessed among women.
But when she saw ‹him›, she was troubled at his word, and was pondering what this greeting might be.
And the messenger said to her: Do not fear, Maryam, for you have found favor with Elohim.
For you will conceive in the womb and will bear a son, and you will call his name Y'shua.
He will be great, and will be called the Son of the Most High, and Master YHWH Elohim will give him the throne of Dawid his father.
And he will reign over the house of Ya'akov forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end.
Maryam said to the messenger: How will this be, since a man is not known to me?

The messenger answered and said to her: Ruach haKodesh will come, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; because of this, he who is born of you is holy, and will be called the Son of Elohim.
And Elishaba your kinswoman, even she has conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who is called barren.
Because nothing is difficult for Elohim.
Maryam said: I am the handmaid of Master YHWH; let it be to me according to your word. And the messenger went from her.
And Maryam rose in those days and went hurriedly to the mountain ‹district›, to a city of Yehuda;
and entered the house of Zakharya and greeted Elishaba.
And it happened that when Elishaba heard the greeting of Maryam, the child leaped in her womb, and Elishaba was filled with Ruach haKodesh.
And she cried out with a loud voice and said to Maryam: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
And from where is this to me, that the mother of my Master should come to me?
For when the voice of your greeting fell on my ears, the child leaped with great joy in my womb.
And blessed is she who believed that there will be a fulfillment of those things that were spoken with her from Master YHWH.
And Maryam said: My soul magnifies Master YHWH
and my spirit has rejoiced in Elohim my Life-Giver.
For he has looked on the lowliness of his maidservant; for from now on all generations will ascribe blessedness to me.
for he who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
And his mercy is on those who fear him, to generations and families.
He has wrought victory with his arm, and has scattered the proud in the imagination of their heart.
He has cast down the mighty from thrones, and has raised up the lowly.
He has filled the hungry with good things, and has sent the rich away empty.
He has helped Yisrael his servant, and has remembered his mercy,
as he spoke with our fathers, with Avraham and with his seed forever.
And Maryam remained with Elishaba about three months, and she returned to her house.
And for Elishaba the time came that she should give birth, and she bore a son.
And her neighbors and the sons of her kin heard that Elohim had multiplied his mercy toward her, and they were rejoicing with her.
And it was on the eighth day, and they came to circumcise the boy, and they were calling him by the name of his father Zakarya.
And his mother answered and said to them, Not so, but he will be called Yochanan.
And they said to her, There is no one among your kindred who is called by this name.
And they made signs to his father, how he wanted him to be named.
And he asked for a tablet and wrote and said, Yochanan is his name. And everyone was amazed.
And at once his mouth was opened and his tongue, and he spoke and blessed Elohim.
And fear came on all their neighbors, and these things were being spoken of in all the mountain ‹district› of Yehuda.
And all who heard were pondering in their heart and saying, What then will this child be? And the hand of Master YHWH was with him.
And Zakarya his father was filled with Ruach haKodesh and prophesied and said:
Blessed is Master YHWH the Elohim of Yisrael, who has visited his people and made redemption for him:
And he has raised up a horn of redemption for us in the house of Dawid his servant:
as he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets who ‹were› from of old,
that he would redeem us from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us.
And he has done his mercy with our fathers and has remembered his holy covenants,
and the oath that he swore to Avraham our father, that he would give to us,
that we would be delivered from the hand of our enemies, and that without fear we would serve before him,
all our days, in uprightness and righteousness.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of Master YHWH to prepare his way,
to give knowledge of life to his people by the forgiveness of their sins,
through the compassion of the mercy of our Elohim, whereby the day-spring from on high will visit us,
to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to straighten our feet in the way of peace.
But the child grew and was strengthened in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the day of his appearing to Yisrael.
And it was in those days that a decree went out from Augustus Caesar that all the people of his dominion should be enrolled.
This enrollment was the first one, under the governorship of Quirinius in Syria.
And everyone went to be enrolled in his own city.
And Yosip also went up from Natsrath, a city of Galila, to Yehuda, to the city of Dawid that is called Beth-Lekhem, because he was from the house and from the lineage of Dawid,
with Maryam his betrothed, while she was pregnant, to be enrolled there.
And it was that while they were there, the days were completed for her to give birth.
And she gave birth to her firstborn son, and wrapped him in bandages, and laid him in the stall, because there was no place for them where they were lodging.
Now there were shepherds in that region who were staying there and keeping the night watch over their flock.
And a messenger of Elohim came to them, and the glory of Master YHWH shone upon them, and they feared with a great fear.
And the messenger said to them, Do not fear, for I announce to you great joy that will be for all the world.
For there is born to you today a deliverer who is Master YHWH the Mashiyach, in the city of Dawid.
And this is the sign for you: you will find the infant wrapped in bandages and laid in the stall.
And suddenly there were seen with the messenger many hosts of heaven, praising Elohim and saying:
Glory to Elohim in the highest ‹heavens›, and on earth peace and good hope to the sons of men.

And it was that when the messengers went from them to heaven, the shepherds spoke one with another and said: Let us go as far as Beth-Lekhem and see this word that has happened, as Master YHWH has made known to us.
And they came in haste and found Maryam and Yosip and the infant laid in the manger.
And when they saw, they made known the word that was spoken with them concerning the boy.
And all who heard wondered at the things that were spoken to them by the shepherds.
But Maryam was keeping all these words, and pondering ‹them› in her heart.
And those shepherds returned, glorifying and praising Elohim for all they had seen and heard, just as it was spoken with them.
And when eight days were completed for the boy to be circumcised, his name was called Y'shua, which was called by the messenger before he was conceived in the womb.
And when the days of their purification were completed, according to the law of Moshe, they brought him up to Urishlim to present him before Master YHWH,
as it is written in the law of Master YHWH, that every male that opens the womb will be called holy to Master YHWH,
and to give a sacrifice, as it is said in the law of Master YHWH, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
And there was a certain man in Urishlim whose name was Shimon. This man was upright and just, and was waiting for the consolation of Yisrael, and Ruach haKodesh was upon him.
And it had been told him by Ruach haKodesh that he would not see death until he should see the Mashiyach of Master YHWH.
This man came by the Ruach into the temple; and when his parents brought in the child Y'shua to do for him as is commanded in the law,
he took him on his arms and blessed Elohim and said:
My Master, now you release your servant in peace, as you have said:
for look, my eyes have seen your mercy,
which you have prepared in the presence of all the nations,
a light for revelation to the peoples, and a glory for your people Yisrael.
And Yosip and his mother were astonished at those things that were being spoken about him.
And Shimon blessed them and said to Maryam his mother, Look, this ‹child› is set for the fall and for the rising of many in Yisrael, and for a sign of contention;
and a spear will pass through your own soul, so that the thoughts of the hearts of many may be revealed.
And Hanna a prophetess, the daughter of Fanu'el, from the tribe of Ashir, she also was advanced in her days, and had lived seven years with her husband from her virginity,
And she was a widow of about eighty-four years, and she did not leave the temple, and with fasting and with prayer she was serving by day and by night.
And she too stood up in that hour and gave thanks to Master YHWH, and she was speaking about him with everyone who was waiting for the redemption of Urishlim.
And when they had completed everything according to the law of Master YHWH, they returned to Galila, to Natsrath their city.
But the child was growing and being strengthened in spirit, and being filled with wisdom, and the grace of Elohim was upon him.
And his people were going every year to Urishlim at the feast of the Passover.
And when he was twelve years old, they went up as they were accustomed to the feast.
And when they completed the days, they returned. But the boy Y'shua remained in Urishlim, and Yosip and his mother did not know ‹of it›.
for they were thinking that he was with the sons of their company. And when they had gone a journey of one day, they sought him among their people and among those who knew them.
And they did not find him. And they returned again to Urishlim, and they were seeking him.
And after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, and listening to them and asking them.
And all who were hearing him were amazed at his wisdom and at his answers.
And when they saw him they were amazed. And his mother said to him, My son, why have you done this to us? For your father and I have been seeking you with much distress.
He said to them, Why were you seeking me? Do you not know that it is necessary for me to be in my Father's house?
But they did not understand the word that he spoke to them.
And he went down with them and came to Natsrath, and was obedient to them. And his mother was keeping all these words in her heart.
And Y'shua was growing in stature and in wisdom and in favor with Elohim and with the children of men.

In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, in the governorship of Pontius Pilatos in Yehuda, when Herodes was tetrarch in Galila, and Philipos his brother tetrarch in Ituraea and in the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
in the high priesthood of Chanan and of Qayapha, the word of Elohim came upon Yochanan son of Zakharya in the wilderness.
And he came into all the region around the Yordanan, proclaiming the immersion of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

As it is written in the book of the words of Eshaya the prophet, who said, A voice of one calling in the wilderness, Prepare the way of Master YHWH, and make straight in the plain a path for our Elohim.
All valleys will be filled, and all mountains and hills will be brought low, and the crooked will become level, and the rough place a plain.
And all flesh will see the life of Elohim.
And he was saying to the crowds who were coming to him to be immersed: Offspring of vipers, who showed you to flee from the coming wrath?

Produce therefore fruits worthy of repentance. And do not begin to say in yourselves: We have Avraham as father; for I say to you that from these stones Elohim is able to raise up children for Avraham.
And look, the axe is laid at the root of the trees. Every tree therefore that does not produce good fruit is cut down and falls into the fire.
And the crowds were asking him and saying: What then shall we do?
He answered and said to them: Whoever has two tunics, let him give ‹one› to him who has none; and whoever has food, let him do the same.
And tax collectors also came to be immersed, and they said to him: Teacher, what shall we do?
But he said to them, Do not exact anything more than what is commanded for you to exact.
And those serving in war were asking him and saying, What shall we also do? He said to them, Do not be insolent to anyone, and do not oppress anyone, and let your pay be enough for you.
Now while the people were hoping about Yochanan, and all were pondering in their hearts whether he was the Mashiyach,

Yochanan answered and said to them, I immerse you with water, but one is coming who is mightier than I, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to loosen; he will immerse you with the Ruach haKodesh and with fire.
He holds his winnowing shovel in his hand and will clean his threshing floor, and will gather the wheat into his storehouses, and the chaff he will burn with fire that is not quenched.
And many other things also he was teaching and proclaiming to the people.
But Herodes the tetrarch, because he was reproved by Yochanan on account of Herodia the wife of Philipos his brother, and on account of all the evil things he had done,
added this also upon all of them, and shut up Yochanan in the house of prisoners.
And it was when all the people were immersed, and Y'shua also was immersed, and while he was praying, the heavens were opened,
and the Ruach haKodesh descended upon him in the likeness of the body of a dove, and a voice was from heaven that said: You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
Now Y'shua was about thirty years old, and he was considered the son of Yosip, the son of Heli,
the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melki, the son of Yani, the son of Yosip,
the son of Mattatha, the son of Amots, the son of Nachum, the son of Chasli, the son of Nagi,
the son of Maath, the son of Mattath, the son of Sh'mai, the son of Yosip, the son of Yehuda,
the son of Yochanan, the son of Rasa, the son of Zurubbabel, the son of Shaltiel, the son of Neri,
the son of Malki, the son of Addi, the son of Qusam, the son of Elmodad, the son of Ir,
the son of Yosa, the son of Eliezer, the son of Yoram, the son of Matitha, the son of Levi,
the son of Shimon, the son of Yehuda, the son of Yosip, the son of Yonam, the son of Eliqim,
the son of Melya, the son of Ma'ni, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of Dawid,
the son of Ishai, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nachshon,
the son of Aminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Chetsron, the son of Pharets, the son of Yehuda,
the son of Ya'akov, the son of Yitz'chak, the son of Avraham, the son of Terach, the son of Nachor,
the son of Serug, the son of Ar'u, the son of Palag, the son of Eber, the son of Shalach,
the son of Qainan, the son of Arpakhshar, the son of Shim, the son of Nuch, the son of Lamek,
the son of Matoshlech, the son of Chanok, the son of Yared, the son of Mahalalayel, the son of Qaynan,
the son of Anosh, the son of Shith, the son of Adam, who is from Elohim.
Y'shua then, when full of the Ruach haKodesh, returned from the Yordanan. And the Ruach led him into the wilderness,
forty days, to be tempted by the Calumniator. And he ate nothing in those days; and when he completed them, at the end he was hungry.
And the Calumniator said to him: If you are the Son of Elohim, say to this stone that it become bread.
Y'shua answered and said to him: It is written that a human does not live by bread alone, but by every word of Elohim.
And Satana took him up to a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the earth in a short time.
And the Calumniator said to him: To you I will give all this authority and its glory, which is delivered to me, and to whomever I will I give it.
If therefore you will worship before me, all of it will be yours.
Y'shua answered and said to him: It is written, You will worship Master YHWH your Elohim, and him only you will serve.
And he brought him to Urishlim and set him on the wing of the temple and said to him: If you are the Son of Elohim, throw yourself down from here.
for it is written that he will command his messengers concerning you, to keep you,
and on their arms they will lift you up, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.
But Y'shua answered and said to him: It is said, You will not test Master YHWH your Elohim.
And when the Calumniator finished all his temptations, he departed from him for a time.
And Y'shua returned in the power of the Ruach to Galila, and a good report about him went out in all the region around them.
And he was teaching in their synagogues, and was praised by every person.
And he came to Natsrath, where he had been brought up, and he entered as he was accustomed into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
And the book of Eshaya the prophet was given to him. And Y'shua opened the book and found the place where it is written:

The Ruach of Master YHWH is upon me, and because of this he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor, and has sent me to heal the broken of heart, and to proclaim release to the captives and sight to the blind, and to set free the oppressed with forgiveness ‹of their sins›;
and to proclaim the acceptable year of Master YHWH.
And he rolled up the book and gave it to the servitor, and went and sat down. And the eyes of all who were in the synagogue were gazing on him.
And he began to say to them: Today this writing is fulfilled in your ears.
And all were witnessing to him and were marveling at the words of grace that were going out from his mouth, and they were saying: Is this not the son of Yosip?
Y'shua said to them: Perhaps you will say to me this proverb, Physician, heal yourself; and all that we have heard you did in Kfar-Nachum, do also here in your city.
But he said: Amen I say to you, that there is no prophet who is accepted in his city.

For I tell you the truth, that there were many widows in Yisrael in the days of Eliyahu the prophet, when the heavens were closed three years and six months, and there was a great famine in all the land.
Yet to none of them was Eliyahu sent, except to Tsarfat of Tsidon, to a widow woman.
And there were many lepers in the house of Yisrael in the days of Elisha the prophet, and not one of them was cleansed, except Naaman the Aramean.
And when they heard these things, those in the synagogue were all filled with wrath.
And they rose up and thrust him outside the city and brought him to the brow of the mountain on which their city was built, so they might throw him down from the cliff.
But he passed through their midst and went away.
And he went down to Kfar-Nachum, a city of Galila, and was teaching them on the sabbath.
And they were astonished at his teaching, for his word was authoritative.
And there was in the synagogue a man in whom was a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a loud voice,
and said: Leave me alone! What is there between us and you, Y'shua the Natsraya? Have you come to destroy us? I know you, who you are, the Holy One of Elohim.
And Y'shua rebuked him and said: Shut your mouth, and come out of him. And the demon threw him down in the midst and came out of him, without harming him at all.
And great wonder seized everyone, and they were talking with one another and saying: What is this word? For with authority and with power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out.
And a report about him went out into all the region around them.
And when Y'shua went out from the synagogue, he entered the house of Shimon. And Shimon's mother-in-law was afflicted with a great fever, and they sought from him on her behalf.
And he stood over her and rebuked her fever, and it left her. And at once she rose and was serving them.
And when the sun was setting, all those who had sick ones afflicted with various diseases brought them to him. And he was laying his hand on each one of them and healing them.
And demons were also going out from many, crying out and saying, You are the Mashiyach, the Son of Elohim. And he was rebuking them and not allowing them to say that they knew he was the Mashiyach.
And at the dawn of the day he went out and went to a deserted place. And the crowds were seeking him and came as far as him and held him so that he would not go away from them.
But Y'shua said to them, I must also announce the kingdom of Elohim to other cities, for on this I was sent.
And he was preaching in the synagogues of Galila.
And it happened that a crowd gathered about him to hear the word of Elohim. And he was standing by the side of the sea of Gennesaret,
and he saw two ships standing by the side of the sea, and the fishermen had gone up from them and were washing their nets.
And one of them was Shimon Keefa’s. And Y'shua went up and sat in it. And he said to draw it a little from the dry land into the water. And he was sitting and teaching the crowd from the ship.
And when he ceased from speaking, he said to Shimon: Launch out into the deep, and cast your nets for a catch.
Shimon answered and said to him: Rabbi, all night we have toiled and caught nothing. But at your word I will cast the net.
And when they did this, they enclosed a great many fish, and their net was breaking.
And they signaled to their companions in the other boat to come and help them. And when they came, they filled both the boats so that they were near to sinking.
And when Shimon Keefa saw ‹it›, he fell before the feet of Y'shua and said to him: I beg you, my Master, leave me, for I am a sinful man.
For astonishment had seized him and all who were with him at the catch of fish that they had caught.
And likewise also Ya'akov and Yochanan, the sons of Zabdi, who were partners of Shimon. But Y'shua said to Shimon: Do not fear; from now on you will catch men for life.
And they brought the boats to the land and left everything and came after him.
And when Y'shua was in one of the cities, a man came who was full of all leprosy. He saw Y'shua and fell on his face and was begging him and said to him: My Master, if you will, you can cleanse me.
And Y'shua stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him: I will ‹it›; be clean. And immediately his leprosy went from him and he was cleansed.
And he charged him: Speak to no one; but go show yourself to the priest, and offer the offering for your purification, as Moshe commanded, for a testimony to them.
And his fame went out about him still more, and many people were gathering to hear from him and to be healed of their diseases.
But he was withdrawing to the wilderness and praying.

And it happened on one of the days while Y'shua was teaching, that Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting by, who had come from all the villages of Galila and of Yehuda and of Urishlim; and the power of Master YHWH was present to heal them.
And some men brought a paralyzed man on a bed, and they were seeking to bring him in and place him before him.
And when they could not find how to bring him in because of the multitude of the people, they went up to the roof and let him down with his couch from the covering into the middle before Y'shua.
And when Y'shua saw their faith, he said to the paralytic: Man, your sins are forgiven you.
And the scribes and Pharisees began reasoning and saying: Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but Elohim alone?
But Y'shua knew their thoughts, and answered and said to them: What are you thinking in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say, Your sins are forgiven you, or to say, Get up and walk?
But that you may know that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins, he said to the paralytic: I say to you, Get up, take up your couch, and go to your house.
And at once he rose up before their eyes, and took up his couch, and went to his house while glorifying Elohim.
And amazement seized everyone, and they were glorifying Elohim, and they were filled with fear, and said, We have seen wonders today.
After these things Y'shua went out and saw a tax collector whose name was Levi sitting at the tax office, and he said to him, Come after me.
And he left everything, and rose, and went after him.
And Levi made a great feast for him in his house, and there was a large crowd of tax collectors and of others who were reclining with them.
And the scribes and Pharisees were murmuring and saying to his disciples, Why are you eating and drinking with tax collectors and sinners?
And Y'shua answered and said to them: A physician is not sought after for the well, but for those who are very sick.
I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
And they said to him: Why do the disciples of Yochanan fast often, and pray, and also ‹those› of the Pharisees; but yours eat and drink?
But he said to them: You cannot make the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them.
But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken up from them, and then they will fast in those days.
And he spoke a parable to them: No one tears a patch from a new garment and puts it on an old garment, lest he tear the new, and the patch from the new not make the old ‹garment› whole.
And no one puts new wine into old sacks; otherwise the new wine bursts the sacks, and the wine is spilled, and the sacks are ruined.
But they put new wine into new sacks, and both are preserved.
And no one drinks old wine and at once wants new; for he says, The old is pleasant.
And it happened on a sabbath, as Y'shua was walking through the grain fields, that his disciples were plucking the ears and rubbing them in their hands and eating.
And some of the Pharisees said to them: Why are you doing something that is not lawful to do on the sabbath?
Y'shua answered and said to them: Have you not read what Dawid did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him?
How he entered the house of Elohim and took the bread of the table of Master YHWH, ate, and gave ‹it› to those who were with him; which it was not lawful to eat except for the priests only?
And he said to them: The Son of man is master of the sabbath.
And it happened on another sabbath that he entered the synagogue and was teaching. And there was a man there whose right hand was withered.
And the scribes and Pharisees were watching him, whether he would heal on the sabbath, that they might be able to accuse him.
But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man whose hand was withered: Rise, come into the middle of the congregation. And when he came and stood ‹there›,
Y'shua said to them: I ask you, What is allowed on the sabbath, to do good or to do evil, to give life to a person or to destroy ‹it›?
And he looked at them all, and said to him: Stretch out your hand. And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored like its fellow.
But they were filled with envy, and were talking with one another what they should do to Y'shua.
And in those days Y'shua went out to the mountain to pray, and there he spent the night in prayer to Elohim.
And when day dawned, he called his disciples and chose from them twelve, those whom he named apostles:
Shimon whom he named Keefa, and Andrawos his brother, and Ya'akov, and Yochanan, and Philipos, and Bar-Tulmay,
and Matai, and Toma, and Ya'akov son of Chalpai, and Shimon who is called the Zealot,
and Yehuda son of Ya'akov, and Yehuda Skaryota who became the betrayer.

And Y'shua went down with them and stood in the plain; and a great company of his disciples, and a multitude of the people from all Yehuda and from Urishlim and from the seacoast of Tsur and of Tsidon,
who came to hear his word and to be healed of their diseases; and those who were tormented by unclean spirits, and they were healed.
And the whole crowd was seeking to come near to him, for power was going out from him and he was healing them all.
And he lifted his eyes on his disciples and said: Blessed are you poor, for yours is the kingdom of Elohim.
Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be satisfied. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you and separate you and revile you and cast out your name as evil for the sake of the Son of man.
Rejoice in that day and leap, for your reward is great in heaven; for so their fathers were doing to the prophets.
But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation.
Woe to you who are full, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will weep and mourn.
Woe to you when the sons of men speak well of you, for so their fathers used to do to the false prophets.
But to you who hear, I say: Love your enemies, and do what is good to those who hate you;
and bless those who curse you, and pray for those who drag you with violence.
To the one who strikes you on your cheek, offer him the other; and from the one who takes your cloak, do not withhold even your tunic.
To everyone who asks of you, give to him; and from the one who takes what is yours, do not demand it back.
And as you want the sons of men to do to you, so do also you to them.
For if you love those who love you, what is your goodness? For even sinners love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what is your goodness? For even sinners do the same.
And if you lend to one from whom you expect to be repaid, what is your goodness? For even sinners lend to sinners, that they may be repaid the same way.

But love your enemies, and do good to them, and lend, and do not cut off anyone’s hope; and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Highest, for he is kind to the evil and to the unthankful.
Be therefore merciful, as also your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Release, and you will be released.
Give, and it will be given to you; in good measure, pressed down and shaken together and running over, they will pour into your lap. For with the measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
And he was saying a parable to them: Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will not both of them fall into a pit?
There is no disciple who is greater than his master; for everyone who is perfected will be like his master.
Why then do you see the straw that is in your brother's eye, but the beam that is in your own eye is not seen by you?

Or how can you say to your brother, My brother, let me take out the straw from your eye, when look, the beam that is in your own eye is not seen by you? Hypocrite! First take the beam out of your eye, and then it will be clear for you to take out the straw from your brother's eye.
There is no good tree that makes bad fruit, nor a bad tree that makes good fruit.
For every tree is known from its fruits. Figs are not gathered from thorns, nor do they pick grapes from a bramble.

A good man from the good treasure that is in his heart brings out good things, and a bad man from the bad treasure that is in his heart brings out bad things. For from the abundance of the heart the lips speak.
Why do you call me, my Master, my Master, and you do not do what I say?
Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you what he is like:

He is like a man who built a house and dug and went deep and laid the foundation on rock. And when a flood came, the flood beat against that house and could not shake it, for its foundation was laid on the rock.
And he who hears and does not do is like a man who built his house on the earth without a foundation; and when the river rushed against it, it fell at once, and the fall of that house was great.
And when he finished all these words in the hearing of the people, Y'shua entered Kfar-Nachum.
And the servant of a certain centurion was badly afflicted, one who was precious to him, and he was near to dying.
And he heard about Y'shua and sent the elders of the Yehudaye to him, and was requesting from him that he would come and give life to his servant.
And when they came to Y'shua, they were requesting from him earnestly, and saying: He is worthy that you should do this for him;
for he loves our people, and he also built a house of assembly for us.

And Y'shua was going with them. And when he was not far from the house, the centurion sent his friends to him, and said to him: my Master, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof.
Therefore I myself am not worthy to come to you, but say the word and my young man will be healed.
For I also am a man under authority, and I have soldiers under my hand, and I say to this one, Go, and he goes, and to another, Come, and he comes, and to my servant, Do this, and he does ‹it.›
And when Y'shua heard these things, he marveled at him, and he turned and said to the crowd that came after him, I say to you that not even in the house of Yisrael have I found faith like this.
And those who were sent returned to the house and found that servant who had been sick now well.
And it was on the day after that he was going to a city whose name is Nain, and his disciples ‹were› with him, and a great crowd.
And when he drew near to the gate of the city, he saw a dead man being carried out who was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow, and a great crowd of the sons of the city was with her.
And Y'shua saw her and had compassion on her, and said to her, Do not weep.
And he went and touched the bier, and those who were carrying him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say to you, Arise.
And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and he gave him to his mother.
And fear seized all the people, and they were glorifying Elohim and saying, A great prophet has arisen among us, and Elohim has visited his people.
And this word about him went out through all Yehuda and through all the region around them.
And the disciples of Yochanan told him all these things.
And Yochanan called two of his disciples and sent them to Y'shua and said: Are you he who is coming, or are we to look for another?
And they came to Y'shua and say to him: Yochanan the Immerser has sent us to you and says: Are you he who is coming, or are we to look for another?
And in that same hour he healed many from diseases and from plagues and from evil spirits, and to many blind he was giving sight.

And Y'shua answered and said to them: Go, say to Yochanan everything you have seen and heard: that the blind see, and the lame walk, and the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, and the dead rise, and the poor are given good news.
And blessed is the one who is not stumbled in me.
And when the disciples of Yochanan had gone, he began to say to the crowds about Yochanan: What did you go out to the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
Or if not, what did you go out to see? a man wearing soft clothes? Look, those who are in splendid clothing and in luxury are in kings' houses.
Or if not, what did you go out to see? a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
‹For› this is he of whom it is written: Look, I send my messenger before your face, to prepare the way before you.
I say to you that there is no prophet among those born of women greater than Yochanan the Immerser; but the little one in the kingdom of Elohim is greater than he.
And all the people who heard, even the tax collectors, justified Elohim, for they were immersed with the immersion of Yochanan.
But the Pharisees and scribes rejected the will of Elohim against themselves, for they were not immersed by him.
To what then will I compare the people of this generation, and to what are they like?
They are like children who sit in the marketplace and call out to their companions and say: We played music for you and you did not dance; we wailed for you and you did not weep.
For Yochanan the Immerser came, not eating bread and not drinking wine, and you say: There is a demon in him.
The Son of man came eating and drinking, and you say: Look, a gluttonous man and a wine drinker, and a friend of tax collectors and of sinners.
And wisdom is justified by all her children.
Then one of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him. And he went into the house of that Pharisee and reclined.
And a sinful woman was in that city, and when she knew that he was reclining in the house of the Pharisee, she took an alabaster flask of perfume,

and stood behind him at his feet and was weeping, and she began to wet his feet with her tears and wipe them with the hair of her head, and she was kissing his feet and anointing ‹them› with the perfume.

And when the Pharisee who had invited him saw ‹it›, he thought in himself and said, This ‹man›, if he were a prophet, would know who she is and what her reputation is, for the woman who has approached him is a sinner.
