And Y'shua answered and said to him, Shimon, I have something to say to you. And he said to him, Say ‹it›, Rabbi. Y'shua said to him,
There were two debtors to one creditor; one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty denarii.
And when they had nothing with which to repay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him more?
Shimon answered and said: I suppose he to whom much was forgiven. Y'shua said to him: You have judged correctly.

And he turned to the woman and said to Shimon: Do you see this woman? I entered your house, and you gave ‹me› no water for my feet; but she has washed my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You did not kiss me; but this woman, look, from the time she entered has not ceased to kiss my feet.
You did not anoint my head with oil; but she has anointed my feet with perfumed oil.
For this reason I say to you that her many sins are forgiven her, because she loved much. But he to whom little is forgiven loves little.
And he said to the woman: Your sins are forgiven you.
Then those who were reclining began to say in themselves, Who is this who even forgives sins?
But Y'shua said to her, Woman, your faith has given you life. Go in peace.
And after these things Y'shua was going about the cities and the villages, and was proclaiming and announcing the kingdom of Elohim. And his twelve ‹disciples› were with him,
and these women who were healed of sicknesses and of evil spirits: Maryam who is called Magdalitha, she from whom seven demons went out,
and Yochanan the wife of Kuza, steward of Herodes, and Shushan, and many other women who were ministering to them from their possessions.
And when a great crowd was gathering, and they were coming to him from all the cities, he said in a parable:
A sower went out to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell beside the road and was trampled, and the birds ate it.
And other fell on the rock, and at once it sprang up, and because it had no moisture it dried up.
And another fell among thorns, and the thorns sprang up with it and choked it.
And another fell on good and fair ground, and sprang up and bore fruit, a hundred for one. As he said these things, he cried out, Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
And his disciples asked him, What is this parable?
And he said to them, To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of Elohim, but to the rest it is spoken in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
Now this is the parable: The seed is the word of Elohim.
And those by the side of the path are the ones who hear the word, and the enemy comes and takes the word from their heart, so that they may not believe and live.
And those on the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy, but they have no root in them, but their faith is for a time, and in the time of testing they stumble.
And that which fell among thorns, these are those who hear the word, and by cares and by riches and by the desires of the world they are choked, and they give no fruit.
And that on the good ground, these are those who with a pure and good heart hear the word and hold it, and give fruit with patience.
No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed, but puts it on a lampstand so that everyone who comes in may see its light.
For there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not be known and come into the open.
See how you hear: for to the one who has, it will be given, and from the one who has not, even what he thinks he has will be taken from him.
Then his mother and his brothers came to him, and they were not able to speak with him because of the crowd.
And they said to him, Your mother and your brothers are standing outside and want to see you.
But he answered and said to them, These are my mother and my brothers, those who hear the word of Elohim and do it.
And it happened on one of the days that Y'shua went up and sat in the boat, he and his disciples, and he said to them, Let us cross over to the other side of the lake.
And while they were sailing, Y'shua fell asleep. And a storm of wind came on the lake, and the boat was near to sinking.
And they came near and woke him and said to him, Our Master, our Master, we are perishing! But he got up and rebuked the wind and the raging of the sea, and they ceased, and there was a calm.
And he said to them, Where is your faith? But they, being afraid, were amazed and said one to another, Who then is this, that he even commands the wind and the waves and the sea, and they obey him?
And they rowed on and came to the region of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galila.
And when he went out onto the land, a certain man from the city met him, in whom demons had been for a long time; and he wore no clothes, and did not live in a house but among the tombs.
And when he saw Y'shua, he cried out and fell before him, and said with a loud voice, What have we to do with you, Y'shua, son of Elohim the Most High? I beg you, do not torment me.

For Y'shua had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For a long time he had been held by it, and he was bound with chains and kept in fetters, yet he would break his bonds and be driven by the demon into the wilderness.
And Y'shua asked him, What is your name? He said to him, Legion, because many demons had entered into him.
And they were begging him not to command them to go away into the abyss.
And there was there a herd of many swine feeding on the mountain. And they were begging him that he would allow them to enter the swine. And he allowed them.
And the demons went out from the man and entered the swine, and the whole herd rushed down the cliff and fell into the sea and were choked.
And when the herdsmen saw what had happened, they fled and told ‹it› in the city and in the villages.
And people went out to see what had happened. And they came to Y'shua and found that man from whom the demons had gone out, clothed and modest and sitting at the feet of Y'shua. And they were afraid.
And those who saw ‹it› told them how that man who had the demons was healed.
And the whole crowd of the Gadarenes were asking him to go away from them, because a great fear had seized them. But Y'shua went up into the boat and returned from them.
But the man from whom the demons had gone out was asking him that he might be with him. And Y'shua released him and said to him:
Go back to your house and tell what Elohim has done for you. And he went and was proclaiming in all the city what Y'shua had done for him.
And when Y'shua returned, a great crowd received him, for they were all looking for him.
And a certain man whose name was Yoarash, a head of the synagogue, fell before the feet of Y'shua and was asking him to enter his house,
for he had an only daughter about twelve years old, and she was near dying. And as Y'shua went with him, a great crowd was pressing him.
And a certain woman whose blood had been flowing twelve years, who had spent all her property among physicians and could not be healed by anyone,
came up from behind him and touched the fringe of his garment, and at once the flow of her blood stopped.
And Y'shua said, Who touched me? And when all denied it, Shimon Keefa and those with him said to him, Our Master, the crowds are pressing and thronging you, and you say, Who touched me?
But he said, Someone touched me, for I know that power has gone out from me.

And the woman, when she saw that she had not escaped his notice, came trembling and fell down and worshipped him, and declared before all the people for what cause she had touched him and how she was immediately healed.
And Y'shua said to her, Take courage, my daughter; your faith has given you life. Go in peace.
And while he was speaking, someone came from the house of the chief of the synagogue and said to him: Your daughter has died; do not trouble the teacher.
But Y'shua heard ‹it› and said to the father of the girl: Do not fear; only believe, and she will live.
And Y'shua came to the house, and he did not allow anyone to enter with him except Shimon and Ya'akov and Yochanan and the father of the girl and her mother.
And all of them were weeping and wailing over her. But Y'shua said: Do not weep, for she has not died, but is sleeping.
And they were laughing at him, knowing that she had died.
But he put everyone outside, and took her by the hand, and called and said: Girl, arise.
And her spirit returned, and at once she rose up. And he ordered that they give her to eat.
And her parents were astonished. But he warned them that they should tell no one what had happened.
And Y'shua called his twelve and gave them power and authority over all demons and diseases, to heal ‹them›.
And he sent them to proclaim the kingdom of Elohim and to heal the sick.
And he said to them, Take nothing for the road, no staff and no wallet and no bread and no silver, and do not have two tunics for yourselves.
And into whatever house you enter, stay there, and from there go out.
And against those who do not receive you, when you go out from that city, shake off even the dust from your feet against them for a testimony.
And the sent ones went out and were going around in the villages and the cities, and were proclaiming and healing in every place.
Now Herodes the tetrarch heard all that was happening by his hand, and he was amazed, because some were saying that Yochanan had risen from the house of the dead.
But others were saying that Eliyahu had appeared, and others that a prophet from among the ancient prophets had risen.
And Herodes said, The head of Yochanan I cut off; but who is this of whom I hear these things? And he wanted to see him.
And when the apostles returned, they related to Y'shua everything they had done. And he took them aside alone to a deserted place of Beth-Tsayda.
But the crowds, when they knew ‹it›, went after him; and he received them, and was speaking with them about the kingdom of Elohim, and those who were in need of healing he was healing.

And when the day began to decline, his disciples drew near and said to him, Dismiss the crowd, that they may go to the villages around us and to the hamlets to lodge in them and find food for themselves, for we are in a deserted place.
Y'shua said to them: You give them to eat. But they say: We have no more than five loaves and two fishes, unless we go and buy food for all this people.
For there were about five thousand men. Y'shua said to them: Make them recline in companies, fifty persons in a company.
And the disciples did so, and made them all recline.
And Y'shua took those five loaves and two fishes, and looked toward heaven, and blessed, and broke, and gave to his disciples to set before the crowd.
And they all ate and were satisfied, and they took up the fragments that remained, twelve baskets.
And while he was praying alone, and his disciples with him, he asked them and said: Who do the crowds say that I am?
They answer and say to him, Yochanan the Immerser; and others, Eliyahu; and others, that a prophet, one of the first prophets, has risen.
He says to them, But who do you say that I am? Shimon answered and said, The Mashiyach of Elohim.
But he rebuked them and warned them that they should not say this to anyone.

And he said to them that the Son of man is about to suffer many things, and to be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.
And he was saying before everyone, Whoever wants to come after me must deny himself and take up his cross every day and ‹so› come after me.
For whoever wants his life to live loses it; but whoever will lose his life for my sake, this one gives it life.
For what will a son of man be helped if he gains the whole world, but loses his life or is deprived ‹of it›?
Whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of man will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with his holy messengers.
I tell you truly that there are people standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of Elohim.
And it was about eight days after these words that Y'shua took Shimon and Ya'akov and Yochanan and went up a mountain to pray.
And while he was praying, the appearance of his face was changed, and his garments became white and brilliant.
And two men were talking with him, who were Moshe and Eliyahu.
who appeared in glory. And they were speaking about his departure, which was about to be fulfilled in Urishlim.
And Shimon and those with him were heavy with sleep; and when they barely awoke, they saw his glory, and those two men who were standing with him.

And when they began to separate from him, Shimon said to Y'shua, Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. And let us make three shelters, one for you, and one for Moshe, and one for Eliyahu. But he did not know what he was saying.
And while he was saying these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them; and they were afraid when they saw Moshe and Eliyahu enter the cloud.
And a voice came from the cloud that said, This is my beloved Son; listen to him.
And when the voice had been, Y'shua was found alone. And they kept silent, and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen.
And it was on the day after, when they were coming down from the mountain, a great crowd met them.
And a certain man from that crowd cried out and said, Teacher, I beg you, turn to me. My only son is mine:
and a spirit comes upon him, and suddenly he cries out and gnashes his teeth and foams, and it hardly departs from him when it has crushed him.
And I asked your disciples to cast him out, and they could not.
But Y'shua answered and said, O faithless and twisted generation, until when will I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.
And while he was bringing him near, that demon threw him down and convulsed him. And Y'shua rebuked that unclean spirit and healed the boy and gave him to his father.
And they were all amazed at the majesty of Elohim. And while everyone was amazed at all that Y'shua did, he said to his disciples:
Set these words in your ears, for the Son of man is about to be delivered into the hands of the sons of men.
But they did not understand this word, because it was hidden from them so that they would not know it, and they were afraid to ask him about this word.
And a thought arose among them, which of them ‹was to be› the greatest.
But Y'shua knew the thought of their heart, and he took a child and set him beside him,
and said to them: Whoever receives a child like this in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me. For the one who is least among all of you, this one will be great.
And Yochanan answered and said, Our Rabbi, we saw a man casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him because he does not come with us after you.
Y'shua said to them, Do not forbid, for whoever is not against you is for you.
And it was that when the days of his ascent were fulfilled, he set his face to go to Urishlim.
And he sent messengers before his face, and they went and entered a village of the Samaritans to prepare ‹lodgings› for him.
And they did not receive him, because his face was set to go to Urishlim.
And when Ya'akov and Yochanan his disciples saw ‹it›, they said to him, Our Master, do you want that we speak and fire come down from heaven and consume them, as also Eliyahu did?
And he turned and rebuked them, and said: You do not know of what spirit you are.
For the Son of man has not come to destroy souls, but to give life ‹them›. And they went to another village.
And as they went on the way, a man said to him: I will come after you to the place where you go, my Master.
Y'shua said to him: The foxes have holes, and the birds of heaven have shelters; but the Son of man has nowhere he may lay his head.
And he said to another: Come after me. But he said to him: My Master, allow me first to go bury my father.
Y'shua said to him: Leave the dead to bury their dead, and you go proclaim the kingdom of Elohim.
Another said to him, I will come after you, my Master; but first allow me to go bid farewell to those of my house, and I will come.
Y'shua said to him, No one who puts his hand to the plow of the oxen and looks behind him is fit for the kingdom of Elohim.
After these things Y'shua separated from his disciples seventy others, and sent them two by two before his face to every place and city where he was about to go.
And he said to them, The harvest is great and the laborers are few; pray therefore of the master of the harvest that he send out laborers into his harvest.
Go; I am sending you as lambs among wolves.
Do not take for yourselves a purse, nor a bag, nor sandals, and greet no one on the road.
And into whichever house you enter, first say, Peace to this house.
And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; but if not, it will return upon you.
And remain in that house, eating and drinking from what is theirs, for the laborer is worthy of his wage. And do not move from house to house.
And into whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat whatever is set before you.
And heal those who are sick in it, and say to them: The kingdom of Elohim has come near to you.
And into whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, go out into the street and say:
Even the dust that sticks to us on our feet from your city we shake off against you. But know this, that the kingdom of Elohim has come near to you.
I say to you that for Sodom it will be more comfortable in that day than for that city.
Woe to you, Kurazin; woe to you, Beth-Tsaida; for if in Tsur and in Tsidon had been the mighty works that were in you, long ago then in sackcloth and in ashes they would have repented.
But for Tsur and for Tsidon it will be more comfortable in the judgment than for you.
And you, Kfar-Nachum, that were lifted up as far as heaven, will be brought down as far as Sheol.
Whoever hears you hears me, and whoever rejects you rejects me, and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.
And those seventy whom he sent returned with great joy and say to him, Our Master, even the demons are subject to us in your name.
But he said to them, I was seeing Satana that he fell like lightning from heaven.
Look, I give you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions and on all the power of the adversary, and nothing will harm you.
Yet do not rejoice in this, that the demons are subject to you; but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.

In that hour Y'shua rejoiced in the Ruach haKodesh and said: I thank you, my Father, Master of heaven and of earth, that you hid these things from the wise and the intelligent and revealed them to little children. Yes, my Father, for so was the will before you.

And he turned to his disciples and said to them: Everything is committed to me by my Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son, and to whomever the Son wishes to reveal ‹him›.
And he turned to his disciples privately and said: Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
For I say to you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, and did not see ‹it›, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear ‹it›.
And a scribe stood up to try him and said, Teacher, what must I do to inherit life everlasting?
But Y'shua said to him, How is it written in the law? How do you read?
He answered and said to him, You shall love Master YHWH your Elohim with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself.
Y'shua said to him, You have said correctly; do this, and you will live.
But he, wanting to justify himself, said to him, And who is my neighbor?
Y'shua said to him, A certain man was going down from Urishlim to Yericho, and robbers fell on him and stripped him and beat him and left him with little life in him, and went away.
And it happened a certain priest was going down on that road, and he saw him and passed by.
And likewise also a Levite came, reached that place, and saw him and passed by.
But a Samaritan man, while he was journeying, came where he was, and saw him, and had compassion on him,
and he drew near and bound up his wounds, and poured wine and oil on them, and put him on his donkey, and brought him to the inn, and took care of him.
And on the morning of the ‹next› day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper and said to him, Take care of him; and if you spend anything more, when I return I will repay you.
Who therefore of these three seems to you to have been neighbor to him who fell into the hands of robbers?
And he said, He who had pity on him. Y'shua said to him, Go, you also do likewise.
And it happened that as they were traveling on the road, he entered a certain village, and a woman whose name was Martha received him into her house.
And she had a sister whose name was Maryam, and she came and sat at the feet of our Master and was listening to his words.
But Martha was occupied with much serving, and she came and said to him, My Master, are you not concerned that my sister has left me alone to serve? Tell her to help me.
Y'shua answered and said to her, Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things.
But one thing is needed, and Maryam has chosen for herself the good portion, which will not be taken from her.
And it happened that while he was praying in a certain place, when he finished, one of his disciples said to him: our Master, teach us to pray just as Yochanan also taught his disciples.
Y'shua said to them: When you pray, say this: Our Father who is in heaven, may your name be hallowed; may your kingdom come; may your will be done, as in heaven, also on earth;
give us the bread of our need every day;
and forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who is indebted to us; and do not bring us into trial, but deliver us from the evil one.
And he said to them: Who among you has a friend, and goes to him at midnight and says to him: my friend, lend me three loaves;
because a friend has come to me from the road, and I have nothing to set before him?
And his friend from inside will answer and say to him, Do not disturb me, for the door is shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give to you.
I say to you: If he will not give to him on account of friendship, yet on account of ‹his› importunity he will rise and give ‹him› as much as is asked for him.
I also say to you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and who seeks finds, and to him who knocks it is opened.
For which of you who is a father, if his son asks him for bread, will he hand him a stone? Or if he asks him for a fish, will he instead of a fish hand him a serpent?
And if he asks him for an egg, will he hand him a scorpion?
And if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father from heaven give the Ruach haKodesh to those who ask him?
And when he was casting out a demon that was mute, it happened that when that demon had gone out, the mute ‹man› spoke, and the crowds were amazed.
But some of them said, By Baalzebub the head of the demons this one casts out demons.
And others, while testing him, were asking him for a sign from heaven.
But Y'shua, who knew their thoughts, said to them, Every kingdom that is divided against itself will be ruined, and a house that is divided against itself will fall.
And if Satana is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? Since you say that I cast out demons by Baalzebub.
And if I by Beelzebub cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast ‹them› out? Therefore they will be judges for you.
But if I by the finger of Elohim cast out demons, the kingdom of Elohim has come near to you.
When a strong man armed keeps his doorway, his property rests in peace.
But if one stronger than he comes and overpowers him, he takes away all his armor on which he relied, and divides his spoil.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.

An unclean spirit, when it goes out from a son of man, goes wandering in places where there is no water, to seek rest for itself; and when it does not find ‹it›, it says: I will return to my house from which I went out.
And when he comes, he finds it swept and set in order.
Then he goes and takes seven other spirits worse than himself, and they enter and dwell there; and the last state of that man is worse than the first.
And while he was saying these things, a certain woman from the crowd lifted up her voice and said to him: Blessed is the womb that carried you, and the breasts that nursed you.
He said to her: Blessed are they who hear the word of Elohim and keep it.
And when the crowds were assembling, he began to say: This evil generation seeks a sign; and no sign will be given to it, except the sign of Yonah the prophet.
For as Yonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so also will the Son of man be to this generation.

The queen of the south will stand up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the other sides of the earth to hear the wisdom of Shlemun, and one greater than Shlemun is here.
The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Yonan, and one greater than Yonan is here.
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a secret place or under a basket, but above on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see its light.
The lamp of your body is your eye. When your eye is simple, your whole body also will be light; but if it is bad, your body also will be dark.
Take care, then, that the light in you is not darkness.
But if your whole body is light and no part in it is dark, the whole will be light, as when a lamp by its flame gives light to you.
And while he was speaking, one Pharisee asked him to dine with him; and he went in and reclined.
But the Pharisee, when he saw him, wondered that he did not first immerse before his dinner.
But Y'shua said to him: Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and of the dish, but your inside is full of extortion and evil.
You who lack understanding! Did not he who made the outside also make the inside?
But give as alms what is there, and look, everything is clean to you.
But woe to you Pharisees, for you tithe mint and rue and every herb, yet you pass over justice and the love of Elohim. These you ought to do, and not leave those undone.
Woe to you, Pharisees, who love the chief seats in the synagogues and a greeting in the streets.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you are like graves that are not known, and the sons of men walk over them and do not know ‹it›.
And one of the scribes answered and said to him, Teacher, when you say these things you also insult us.
But he said, Woe also to you, scribes, who load the sons of men with heavy burdens, and you yourselves do not touch those burdens with one of your fingers.
Woe to you who build the graves of the prophets that your fathers killed.
You therefore testify and consent to the deeds of your fathers, for they killed them and you build their graves.
Because of this the wisdom of Elohim also said: I will send to them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will persecute and kill,
so that the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the world was created may be required from this generation,
from the blood of Habel to the blood of Zakharya who was killed between the temple and the altar. Yes, I say to you, it will be required from this generation.
Woe to you, scribes, for you have taken away the key of knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and those who are entering you have hindered.
And while he was saying these things to them, the scribes and Pharisees began to be offended and grew angry and carped at his words,
and they laid many snares for him, seeking to catch something from his mouth so they might accuse him.

And when great crowds of people had gathered by the thousands, so that they were trampling one another, Y'shua began to say to his disciples: First of all, beware in yourselves of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, and nothing concealed that will not be known.
For everything you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered in the ear in inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
But I say to you, my friends: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have nothing more they can do.
But I will show you whom you should fear: fear the one who, after he kills, has authority to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I say to you, fear this one.
Are not five sparrows sold for two assarii? And not one of them is forgotten before Elohim.
But as for you, even the hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not fear, for you are better than many sparrows.
But I say to you that everyone who confesses me before the children of men, the Son of man will also confess him before the messengers of Elohim.
But whoever denies me before the children of men will be denied before the messengers of Elohim.
And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever blasphemes against the Ruach haKodesh, it will not be forgiven him.
But when they bring you to the assemblies before heads and authorities, do not be anxious how you will make defense or what you will say;
for the Ruach haKodesh will teach you in that hour what you ought to say.
And someone from the crowd said to him: Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.
But Y'shua said to him: Man, who set me as a judge and divider over you?
And he said to his disciples: Guard yourselves from all greed, because life is not in the abundance of possessions.
And he spoke a parable to them: The land of a certain rich man brought him a large crop.
And he was thinking in himself and said: What will I do, for I have no place where I can gather my crops?
And he said: This I will do: I will tear down my storehouses and build and enlarge them, and there I will gather all my grain and my goods.
And I will say to my soul, My soul, you have many good things laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, and be merry.
But Elohim said to him, You lacking in mind! This night they will require your soul from you; and these things you have prepared, whose will they be?
Such is the one who lays up treasure for himself and is not rich in Elohim.
And he said to his disciples, Because of this I say to you, Do not be anxious for your soul, what you will eat, nor for your body, what you will wear.
For the soul is more than food, and the body than clothing.
Consider the ravens, that do not sow and do not reap, and have no storehouse or barn, and Elohim feeds them. How much more are you than the birds!
And which of you, by being anxious, can add one cubit to his stature?
And if you cannot do even the least, why are you anxious about the rest?
Look at the lilies, how they grow: they do not toil, and they do not spin. But I say to you that not even Shlemun in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
And if Elohim so clothes the grass that today is in the field and tomorrow falls into the oven, how much more you, little of faith?
And you, do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not let your mind wander on these things.
For all these things the peoples of the world seek; and your Father knows that these things are needed for you also.
But seek the kingdom of Elohim, and all these things will be added to you.
Do not fear, little flock, for your Father desires to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give alms. Make for yourselves purses that do not wear out, and a treasure that does not fail in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning.
And be like people who are waiting for their master when he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.
Blessed are those servants, those whom their master will come and find awake. Amen, I say to you, that he will gird his loins and make them recline, and will pass and serve them.
And if in the second watch or in the third he comes and finds ‹them› so, blessed are those servants.
But know this, that if the master of the house had known in which watch the thief was coming, he would have been awake and would not have let his house be broken into.
You also therefore be ready, for in that hour that you do not expect, the Son of man comes.
Shimon Keefa said to him, Our Master, are you saying this parable to us, or also to everyone?
Y'shua said to him, Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his master will set over his service, to give the portion in its time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.
Truly I say to you that he will set him over all his possessions.
But if that servant says in his heart, My master delays his coming, and begins to beat the servants and the maidservants of his master, and begins to eat and to drink and to get drunk,
the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign him his portion with those who are unfaithful.
But the servant who knows his master's will and does not prepare for him according to his will will be beaten with many ‹stripes›.

But he who does not know and does what deserves stripes will be beaten with few stripes. For to everyone who is given much, much will be required from him, and to the one to whom they have entrusted much, more will be required at his hand.
I have come to cast fire on the earth, and I desire that it already burned.
And I have an immersion to be immersed with, and I am much pressed until it is accomplished.
Do you suppose that I have come to cast peace on the earth? I say to you, No, but division.
For from now on there will be five ‹persons› in one house who will be divided, three against two and two against three.

For a father will be divided against his son, and a son against his father, a mother against her daughter, and a daughter against her mother, a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
And he said to the crowds: When you see a cloud rising from the west, at once you say, Rain is coming, and it is so.
And when a south wind blows, you say, It is hot, and it is so.
Hypocrites, you know how to distinguish the face of the earth and of the heavens; but this time, how do you not distinguish it?
And why do you not judge what is right from yourselves?

For when you go with your adversary to the ruler, while you are on the way, make a settlement and be released from him, lest he bring you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the collector, and the collector throw you into prison.
And I say to you, you will not come out from there until you pay the last mite.
At that time some came and told him about those Galileans whose blood Pilatos had mixed with their sacrifices.
And Y'shua answered and said to them: Do you suppose that these Galileans were sinners more than all the Galileans, because this happened to them?
No, I say to you, that unless you all repent, you will likewise perish.
Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Shiloach fell and killed them: do you suppose that they were sinners more than all the people who live in Urishlim?
No, I say to you, that unless you all repent, you will perish like them.
And he told this parable: A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.
And he said to the cultivator: Look, three years I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and I find none. Cut it down. Why does it make the ground useless?
The cultivator said to him: My master, leave it also this year, until I work it and manure it.
And if it makes fruit, ‹well;› and if not, afterward you will cut it down.
And when Y'shua was teaching on the sabbath in one of the synagogues,
there was a woman there who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and she was bent over and could not straighten herself at all.
And Y'shua saw her and called her and said to her: Woman, you are released from your infirmity.
And he put his hand on her, and at once she straightened up and glorified Elohim.

But the chief of the synagogue answered, being angry that Y'shua had healed on the sabbath, and said to the crowd: There are six days on which it is lawful to work; on them come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.
But Y'shua answered and said to him: Hypocrite! Does not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his donkey from the stall and go water it?
And this woman, who is a daughter of Avraham, and the Accuser bound her, look, eighteen years—ought she not to be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?
And when he said these things, all who stood against him were ashamed, and all the people rejoiced in all the wonders that were done by his hand.
And Y'shua said: To what is the kingdom of Elohim like, and to what shall I compare it?
It is like a grain of mustard that a man took and cast into his garden, and it grew and became a great tree, and the bird of heaven nested in its branches.
Y'shua said again: To what shall I liken the kingdom of Elohim?
It is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three seahs of meal until all of it was leavened.
And he was traveling through the villages and cities, teaching and going to Urishlim.
And a person asked him whether those who live are few.
And Y'shua said to them: Strive to enter by the narrow gate, for I say to you that many will seek to enter and will not be able.

From the hour that the master of the house will rise and shut the door, and you will be standing outside and knocking at the door, and you will begin to say, Our Master, our Master, open for us, and he will answer and say, I say to you that I do not know you, where you are from.
And you will begin to say, Before you we ate and drank, and in our streets you taught.
And he will say to you, I do not know you, where you are from. Depart from me, workers of falsehood.
There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Avraham and Yitz'chak and Ya'akov and all the prophets in the kingdom of Elohim, but you will be cast outside.
And they will come from the east and from the west and from the south and from the north and will recline in the kingdom of Elohim.
And there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.
On that same day some of the Pharisees came near and said to him, Go out, go away from here, because Herodes wants to kill you.
Y'shua said to them, Go say to this fox, Look, I cast out demons and do healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am completed.
But I must labor today and tomorrow, and on the following day I go, because it is not possible that a prophet perish outside Urishlim.

Urishlim, Urishlim, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How many times I wanted to gather your children like a hen that gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing.
Look, your house is left to you desolate. For I say to you that you will not see me until you say, Blessed is he who comes in the name of Master YHWH.
And it happened that when he entered the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees to eat bread on the day of the Sabbath, they were watching him.
And look, a certain man who was swollen with water was before him.
And Y'shua answered and said to the scribes and to the Pharisees: Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?
But they kept silent. And he took hold of him and healed him and let him go.
And he said to them: Which of you, if his son or his ox falls into a pit on the day of the Sabbath, will not at once pull him up?
And they could not give him an answer about this.
And he was speaking a parable to those who were invited there, because he saw them choosing the places of the head of the couch.
When you are invited by someone to a house of feasting, do not go recline for yourself at the head of the couch, lest someone more honored than you be invited there,
and the one who invited you and him come and say to you, Give place to this one, and you be ashamed as you stand and take the last place.

But when you are invited, go recline for yourself in the last ‹couch›, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, My friend, come up higher and recline. And you will have glory before all who recline with you.
Because everyone who lifts up his soul will be brought low, and everyone who brings his soul low will be lifted up.

And he said also to the one who had invited him, When you make a meal or a supper, do not be inviting your friends, nor your brothers or your relatives, and not your rich neighbors, lest they also invite you and this repayment be yours.
But when you make a feast, invite the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind.
And you will be blessed, for they have nothing with which to repay you; for your repayment will be in the resurrection of the righteous.
And when one of those reclining heard these things, he said to him: Blessed is he who will eat bread in the kingdom of Elohim.
Y'shua said to him: A certain man made a great supper and invited many.
And he sent his servant at the time of the supper to say to those who were invited: Everything is ready for you; come.
And they all began, as one, to excuse themselves. The first said to him: I have bought a field, and I am constrained to go out and see it. I ask of you, allow me to be excused.
Another said, I bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to examine them. I ask of you, excuse me, for I am excused.
And another said, I took a wife, and because of this I cannot come.

And that servant came and said to his master these things. Then the master of the house was angry and said to his servant, Go out quickly to the streets and to the lanes of the city and bring in here the poor and the afflicted and the lame and the blind.
And the servant said, My master, it is as you commanded, and still there is room.
And the master said to his servant, Go out to the roads and to the hedges and compel them to enter, so that my house may be filled.
For I say to you that not one of those men who were invited will taste of my supper.
And when great crowds were going with him, he turned and said to them:
Whoever comes to me and does not hate his father and his mother and his brothers and his sisters and his wife and his children and even his own life cannot be a disciple to me.
And whoever does not take up his cross and come after me cannot be a disciple to me.
For which of you who wants to build a tower does not first sit down and count its cost, whether he has ‹enough› to finish it?
so that when he has laid the foundation and is not able to finish, all who see it will mock him,
and say, This man began to build and was not able to finish.
Or what king goes to battle to fight with another king and does not first consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one who comes against him with twenty thousand?
And if not, while he is still far from him, he sends an envoy and seeks peace.
So everyone of you who does not leave all his possessions cannot be a disciple to me.
Salt is good; but if the salt itself becomes bland, with what will it be salted?
It is fit neither for the earth nor for the dunghill. They throw it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
Now tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.
And the scribes and Pharisees were murmuring and saying, This one receives sinners and eats with them.
And Y'shua said to them this parable:
Who among you is a man who has a hundred sheep, and if he loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go seek the one that is lost until he finds it?
And when he has found it, he rejoices and takes it on his shoulders,
and comes to his house and calls his friends and his neighbors and says to them, Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.
I say to you that there will thus be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine just ones to whom repentance is not necessary.
Or what woman is there who has ten drachmas and loses one of them, and does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search for it carefully until she finds it?
And when she has found it, she calls her friends and her neighbors and says to them, Rejoice with me, for I have found my drachma that was lost.
I say to you that there will thus be joy before the messengers of Elohim over one sinner who repents.
And Y'shua said to them again: A certain man had two sons.
And his younger son said to him: My father, give me the portion that falls to me from your house. And he divided to them his property.
And after a few days, that younger son gathered everything that came to him and went to a distant place and there scattered his property while living wastefully.
And when he finished everything that he had, there was a great famine in that place and he began to be in want.
And he went and joined himself to one of the sons of the city of that place and he sent him into the field to tend swine.
And he was longing to fill his belly with those pods that the swine were eating and no one was giving to him.
And when he came to himself he said, How many hired servants are there now in my father's house who have more than enough bread and I here am perishing with hunger.
I will arise and go to my father and say to him, My father, I have sinned in heaven and before you;
and I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.
And he rose and came to his father. And while he was still far off, his father saw him and had pity on him, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
And his son said to him: My father, I have sinned in heaven and before you, and I am not worthy to be called your son.
But his father said to his servants: Bring out the best robe and clothe him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes on him.
And bring and kill the fattened bull, and let us eat and be merry.
For this my son was dead and is alive, and was lost and is found. And they began to be merry.
Now his older son was in the field, and when he came and drew near to the house, he heard the sound of the singing of many.
And he called one of the boys and asked him what this was.
He said to him, Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened bull because he has received him healthy.
And he was angry and would not go in, and his father went out and begged him.
But he said to his father, Look, how many years I have served you, and I have never transgressed your command, and you never gave me a kid that I might make merry with my friends.
But for this your son, when he had wasted your property with harlots and came ‹home›, you have killed the fattened bull for him.
His father said to him, My son, you are always with me, and everything that is mine is yours.
But it was right for us to make merry and rejoice, because this your brother was dead and is alive, and was lost and is found.
And he spoke a parable to his disciples. There was a certain rich man, and he had a steward; and accusations were brought against him that he was squandering his possessions.
And his master called him and said to him: What is this that I hear about you? Give me an account of your stewardship; for you can no longer be a steward for me.
The steward said in himself: What will I do, since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not able to dig, and I am ashamed to beg.
I know what I will do, so that when I have gone out from the stewardship, they will receive me into their houses.
And he called each one of his master's debtors, and said to the first: How much do you owe my master?
He said to him: A hundred measures of oil. He said to him: Take your bill, and sit down quickly, write fifty measures.
And he said to another, And you, how much do you owe my master? He said to him, A hundred kors of wheat. He said to him, Take your writing and sit down, write eighty kors.
And our Master praised the steward of unrighteousness, because he acted wisely: for the sons of this world are wiser than the sons of light in this their generation.
And I also say to you, Make for yourselves friends from this mammon of unrighteousness, so that when it is finished, they may receive you into their everlasting shelters.
Whoever is faithful in little is also faithful in much, and whoever is unjust in little is also unjust in much.
If therefore you have not been faithful in the mammon of unrighteousness, who will entrust the truth to you?
And if you have not been found faithful in what is not yours, who will give you what is yours?
There is no servant who can serve two masters. For either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will honor the one and despise the other. You cannot serve Elohim and mammon.
And the Pharisees, when they heard all these things, because they loved money, were mocking him.
But Y'shua said to them: You are those who justify themselves before the sons of men; but Elohim knows your hearts. For what is exalted among the sons of men is abominable before Elohim.
The law and the prophets were until Yochanan. From then the kingdom of Elohim is proclaimed, and everyone presses to enter it.
And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one letter from the law to pass.
Everyone who puts away his wife and takes another commits adultery, and everyone who takes her who is put away commits adultery.
Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in fine linen and purple, and every day he was feasting splendidly.
And there was a certain poor man whose name was Lazar, and he was laid at the gate of that rich man, struck with sores.
And he was longing to fill his belly from the crumbs that fell from the table of that rich man; but even the dogs were coming and licking his sores.
And it happened that the poor man died, and the messengers carried him to the bosom of Avraham. The rich man also died and was buried.
And while he was tormented in Sheol, he raised his eyes from far off and saw Avraham, and Lazar in his bosom.
And he called with a loud voice and said, Father Avraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazar to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for look, I am tormented in this flame.
Avraham said to him, My son, remember that you received your good things in your life, and La'zar his bad things; and now look, he is refreshed here, and you are tormented.
And with all these things, a great barrier is set between us and you, so that those who want to pass from here to you cannot, and neither ‹can they› pass from there to us.
He said to him, Then I ask of you, my father, that you send him to my father's house,
for I have five brothers; let him go and testify to them, so that they also will not come to this place of torment.
Avraham said to him, They have Moshe and the prophets; let them hear them.
But he said to him, No, my father Avraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent.
Avraham said to him, If they do not hear Moshe and the prophets, they will not believe even if a man should rise from the dead.
And Y'shua was saying to his disciples: It is not possible that stumbling-blocks will not come, but woe to him by whose hand they come.
It would be better for him if a donkey's millstone were hung on his neck and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
Take heed to yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turns back to you and says, I repent, forgive him.
And the emissaries said to our Master: Increase our faith.
He said to them: If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, Be uprooted and be planted in the sea, and it would obey you.
Who among you has a servant who drives a plow or tends sheep, and when he comes in from the field will say to him at once, Come over and recline?
But he will say to him, Prepare something for me to eat, and gird your loins and serve me until I have eaten and drunk; and afterward you also will eat and drink.
Does he thank that servant because he did what was commanded him? I think not.
So also you, when you have done all the things commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants, for we have done what we were obligated to do.
And it happened that as Y'shua was going to Urishlim, he was passing between the Samaritans to Galila.
And when he drew near to enter a certain village, ten leprous men met him, and they stood at a distance.
And they raised their voice and said, Our Master Y'shua, have compassion on us.
And when he saw them, he said to them, Go, show yourselves to the priests. And as they were going, they were cleansed.
But one of them, when he saw that he was cleansed, turned back, and with a loud voice was glorifying Elohim.
And he fell on his face before the feet of Y'shua while thanking him. And he was a Samaritan.
But Y'shua answered and said, Were not these ten cleansed? Where are the nine?
Have they so separated that they do not come to give glory to Elohim, except this one who is of a foreign people?
And he said to him, Get up, go; your faith has given you life.
And when the Pharisees asked Y'shua when the kingdom of Elohim would come, he answered and said to them, The kingdom of Elohim does not come with observables.
And they will not say, Here it is! or, There it is! For the kingdom of Elohim is within you.
And he said to his disciples, Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of man, and you will not see ‹them›.
And if they say to you, Here he is! or, There he is! do not go.
For as the lightning flashes from heaven and lights all under heaven, so will the Son of man be in his day.
But first he is destined to suffer many things and to be rejected by this generation.
And as it was in the days of Noach, so will it be in the days of the Son of man.
They were eating and drinking and taking wives and giving to husbands until the day that Noach entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed every person.
And again, as it was in the days of Lut: they were eating and drinking and buying and selling and planting and building.
But on the day that Lut went out from Sdom, Master YHWH rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all.
So it will be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.
In that day, whoever is on the housetop and his goods are in the house must not come down to take them, and whoever is in the field must not turn back ‹after what is› behind him.
Whoever desires to keep his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life will give it life.
I say to you that in that night two will be in one bed; one will be taken and the other left.
Two women will be grinding together; one will be taken and the other left.
Two will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left.
They answered and said to him, Where, our Master? He said to them, Where the body is, there the eagles will assemble.
And he said to them also a parable, that they should pray at all times and not grow weary.
There was a certain judge in a certain city who did not fear Elohim and did not regard people.
And there was a certain widow in that city, and she kept coming to him and saying, Vindicate me against my adversary.
And he was unwilling for a long time. But afterwards he said to himself, Even if I do not fear Elohim and do not regard people,
yet because this widow wearies me, I will vindicate her, so that she will not keep coming and wearying me.
And our Master said, Hear what the unjust judge says.
But will not Elohim much more do the vindication of his chosen ones who call to him by day and by night, and he lengthens his spirit over them?
I tell you that he will do their vindication quickly. Yet the Son of man will come, and will he find faith on the earth?
And he was saying this parable against people who trust in themselves that they are righteous and despise everyone.
Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

And that Pharisee was standing by himself and was praying these things: Elohim, I thank you that I have not been like the rest of men, rapacious and oppressive and adulterous, and not like this tax collector.
But I fast twice in a week, and I tithe everything that I acquire.
But that tax collector was standing at a distance, and he was not willing even to lift his eyes toward heaven, but was beating on his breast and saying, Elohim, have mercy on me, a sinner.
I say to you that this ‹man› went down to his house justified more than that Pharisee. For everyone who raises himself up will be humbled, and everyone who humbles himself will be raised up.
Now they were also bringing infants to him so that he might touch them, and his disciples saw them and rebuked them.
But Y'shua called them and said to them, Let the children come to me, and do not hinder them, for of those who are like these is the kingdom of heaven.
Truly I say to you that whoever does not receive the kingdom of Elohim like a child will not enter it.
And one of the rulers asked him and said to him, Good Teacher, what shall I do so that I may inherit life forever?
Y'shua said to him: Why do you call me good? There is none good except one, Elohim.
You know the commandments: Do not kill; and do not commit adultery; and do not steal; and do not testify a false testimony; honor your father and your mother.
He said to him: All these I have kept from my childhood.
And when Y'shua heard these ‹words›, he said to him: One thing is lacking to you: go, sell all that you have, and give to the poor; and you will have a treasure in heaven; and come after me.
And he, when he heard these ‹words›, was dejected; for he was very rich.
And when Y'shua saw that he was dejected, he said: How difficult ‹it is› for those who have wealth to enter into the kingdom of Elohim!
It is easier for a camel to enter the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of Elohim.
Those who heard ‹it› said to him: And who is able to have life?
But Y'shua said: Those things that are not possible with the sons of men are possible with Elohim.
Shimon Keefa said to him: Look, we have left everything and come after you.
Y'shua said to him: Amen I say to you, there is no one who has left house or parents or brothers or wife or children for the sake of the kingdom of Elohim,
who will not receive many times more in this time, and in the world that is coming life forever.
And Y'shua took his twelve and said to them: Look, we are going up to Urishlim, and all the things written in the prophets concerning the Son of man will be fulfilled.
For he will be delivered over to the Gentiles, and they will mock him and spit in his face,
and they will scourge him and treat him with ignominy and kill him, and on the third day he will rise.
But they did not understand one of these things; rather, this word was hidden from them, and they did not know the things that were spoken with them.
And he heard the sound of the crowd that was passing, and he was asking who this was.
They say to him: Y'shua the Natsraya is passing.
And he cried out and said, Y'shua, son of Dawid, have mercy on me.
And those who were going before Y'shua were rebuking him that he should be silent. But he was crying out all the more, Son of Dawid, have mercy on me.
And Y'shua stood and commanded that they bring him to him. And when he came near to him, he asked him
and said to him, What do you want me to do for you? And he said, my Master, that I may see.
And Y'shua said to him, See; your faith has given you life.
And at once he saw, and he was coming after him and glorifying Elohim. And all the people who saw were giving glory to Elohim.
And as Y'shua entered and passed through Irikho,
‹there was› a certain man whose name was Zakki; he was rich, and chief of the publicans;
and he wanted to see Y'shua, who he was; and he could not because of the crowd, because Zakki was small in stature.
And he ran ahead of Y'shua and climbed a wild fig-tree to see him, because he was going to pass that way.
And when Y'shua came to that place, he saw him and said to him: Hurry, come down, Zakki, for today I must be at your house.
And he hurried and came down and received him with joy.
When they all saw ‹it›, they were murmuring and saying, He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.
Then Zakay stood and said to Y'shua, Look, my Master, half of my goods I give to the poor, and to every person anything I have defrauded I repay fourfold.
Y'shua said to him, Today life has come to this house, because he also is a son of Avraham.
For the Son of man came to seek and to give life to that which was lost.
And while they were hearing these things, he went on to speak a parable, because he was near to Urishlim, and they supposed that at that hour the kingdom of Elohim was about to be revealed.
And he said, A certain man of high birth went to a distant place to receive a kingdom for himself and return.
And he called his ten servants and gave them ten minas, and said to them, Trade until I come.
But the sons of his city hated him, and they sent envoys after him, saying, We do not want this one to reign over us.
And when he had received the kingdom and returned, he said that those servants should be called to him to whom he had given the money, that he might know what each one of them had gained by trading.
And the first came and said, My master, your mina has gained ten minas.
He said to him, Well done, good servant! Because you have been found faithful in a little, you will have authority over ten cities.
And the second came and said, My master, your mina has made five minas.
He said also to this one: You also will be ruler over five towns.
And another came and said: My Master, look, your mina that was with me, laid up in a cloth.
For I was afraid of you, because you are a hard man, and you take up what you did not lay down, and reap what you did not sow.
He said to him: From your mouth I will judge you, evil servant. You knew that I am a hard man, and I take up what I did not lay down, and reap what I did not sow.
Why did you not put my money on the table, and I would have come and claimed it with its interest?
And to those standing before him he said: Take the mina from him and give it to him who has ten minas with him.
They say to him, Our Master, he has ten minas with him.
He says to them, I say to you that to everyone who has, it will be given; and from him who does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.
But those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them, bring them and kill them before me.
And when Y'shua said these things, he went on ahead to go to Urishlim.
And when he reached Beth-Paga and Beth-Anya, beside the mountain that is called of Beth-Zayta, he sent two of his disciples,
and said to them, Go to the village that is opposite us, and as you enter ‹it›, look, you find a colt tied that no one has ever ridden on; untie it and bring it.
And if anyone asks you, Why are you loosing him? say to him this way: Our Master needs him.
And those who were sent went and found just as he said to them.
And as they were loosing the colt, its masters said to them, Why are you loosing that colt?
And they said to them, Because our Master needs him.
And they brought him to Y'shua, and they threw their garments on the colt, and they set Y'shua on it.
And as he went, they were spreading their garments on the road.
And when he came near to the descent of the mountain of Olives, the whole crowd of the disciples began rejoicing and praising Elohim with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen.
And they were saying: Blessed is the king who comes in the name of Master YHWH; peace in heaven and glory in the highest.
But some of the Pharisees from among the crowd said to him: Rabbi, rebuke your disciples.
He said to them: I say to you that if these should be silent, the stones would cry out.
And when he came near and saw the city, he wept over it.
And he said: If only you had known the things that are for your peace, even in this your day! But now they are hidden from your eyes.
But the days will come upon you when your enemies will surround you and press you in from every side.
And they will tear you down, and your children inside you, and will not leave in you a stone upon a stone, because you did not know the time of your visitation.
And when he entered the temple, he began to drive out those who were buying and selling in it.
And he said to them, It is written that my house is a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of robbers.
And he was teaching every day in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the elders of the people were seeking to destroy him.
And they could not find what they might do to him, for all the people were hanging on him to hear him.
And it was on one of the days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming, the chief priests and the scribes with the elders rose up against him,
and they say to him, Tell us, by what authority you do these things? And who is he that gave you this authority?
Y'shua answered and said to them, I also will ask you a word, and tell me.
The immersion of Yochanan, was it from heaven, or from the sons of men?
But they were reasoning in themselves and saying, If we say, From heaven, he will say to us, And why did you not believe him?
But if we say, From the sons of men, all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded that Yochanan is a prophet.
And they said to him, We do not know from where it is.
Y'shua said to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
And he began to say this parable to the people: A certain man planted a vineyard and leased it to laborers and went abroad for a long time.
And in time he sent his servant to the laborers, that they might give him of the fruit of the vineyard. But the laborers beat him and sent him away empty.
And again he sent another servant; but they also beat him and treated him with shame and sent him away empty.
And again he sent a third; but they also wounded him and cast him out.
The master of the vineyard said, What will I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will see him and be ashamed.
But when the cultivators saw him, they were reasoning in themselves and saying, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.
And they cast him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the master of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy those cultivators, and will give the vineyard to others. And when they heard ‹it›, they said, This will not be.
But he looked at them and said, And what is this that is written: The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner?
And everyone who falls on that stone will be broken, and everyone on whom it falls, it will crush him.
But the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to lay hands on him at that hour, and they feared the people, for they knew that against them he spoke this parable.
And they sent spies to him who pretended to be righteous, that they might catch him in a word and deliver him to the judgment and to the authority of the governor.
And they asked him and said to him, Teacher, we know that you speak and teach correctly, and you do not take faces, but in truth you teach the way of Elohim.
Is it lawful for us to give head-money to Caesar, or not?
But he perceived their craftiness and said, Why are you testing me?
Show me a denarius. Whose image and writing is on it? And they said, Caesar's.
Y'shua said to them, Give therefore what is Caesar's to Caesar, and what is Elohim's to Elohim.
And they could not catch a word from him ‹of accusation› before the people, and they marveled at his answer, and were silent.
Then some of the Zaduqaye came near, those who say there is no rising, and they asked him,
and said to him, Teacher, Moshe wrote for us that if a man's brother dies who has a wife and he has no children, his brother should take his wife and raise up seed for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died without children.
And the second took her as wife, and this one died without children.
And the third again took her, and likewise also all seven of them, and they died and left no children.
And at the last the woman also died.
In the resurrection, then, of which of them will she be the wife? For the seven took her.
Y'shua said to them, The children of this world take wives, and wives become to husbands.
But those who are worthy of that world and of the resurrection from among the dead do not take wives, and wives do not become to husbands.
For they cannot die any more; for they are like the messengers, and they are children of Elohim, because they are children of the resurrection.
But that the dead rise, even Moshe showed; for at the bush he made mention when he said: Master YHWH, the Elohim of Avraham and the Elohim of Yitz'chak and the Elohim of Ya'akov.
Now Elohim is not ‹the Elohim› of the dead, but of the living; for they all live to him.
And some of the scribes answered and said to him: Teacher, you have spoken well.
And they did not again dare to question him about anything.
And he was saying to them: How do the scribes say of the Mashiyach that he is the son of Dawid?
And Dawid himself said in the book of Psalms: Master YHWH said to my Master, Sit at my right hand,
until I place your enemies under your feet.
If therefore Dawid called him my Master, how is he his son?
And while all the people were hearing, he said to his disciples:
Beware of the scribes who choose to walk in robes and love greetings in the marketplace and the chief seats in the synagogues and the chief couches at banquets,
who eat up the houses of widows under the pretext that they lengthen their prayers. These will receive a greater judgment.
And Y'shua looked at the rich who were casting their offerings into the treasury.
And he saw also one poor widow who cast in two mites.
And he said, Truly I say to you that this poor widow has cast in more than anyone.
For all these from what was more than enough for them have cast into the house of the offering of Elohim, but she from her lack has cast in all that she possessed.
And when some were speaking about the temple, that with beautiful stones and with offerings it was adorned, Y'shua said to them,
‹As for› these things that you see, days will come in which a stone will not be left upon a stone that will not be thrown down.
And they were asking him and saying, Teacher, when will these things be, and what is the sign when these things are near to take place?
But he said to them, Look, do not be led astray. For many will come in my name and will say, I am the Mashiyach, and the time is near. But do not go after them.
And when you hear of wars and upheavals, do not be afraid, for these things are first to take place, but the end has not yet come.
For people will rise against people, and kingdom against kingdom.
And great earthquakes will be in place after place, and famines and plagues, and there will be terrors and alarms, and great signs from heaven will be seen, and there will be great storms.
But before all these things they will lay hands on you and persecute you and hand you over to the assemblies and to prison, and bring you before kings and governors because of my name.
But it will be to you for a testimony.
But settle it in your hearts that you will not be preparing beforehand to make a defense.
For I will give you a mouth and wisdom that all your enemies will not be able to stand against.
And your fathers and your brothers and your relatives and your friends will hand you over, and they will put some of you to death.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name.
And a hair from your head will not perish.
But by your patience you will establish your souls.
But when you see Urishlim that armies are surrounding it, then know that its destruction has drawn near.
Then those who are in Yehuda, let them flee to the mountain ‹district›; and those who are in the midst of it, let them flee; and those in the villages, let them not enter it.
For these are days of vengeance, that all that is written may be fulfilled.
But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse in those days; for there will be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.
And they will fall by the mouth of the sword and be led captive to every place. And Urishlim will be trampled by the peoples until the times of the peoples are completed.
And there will be signs in the sun and in the moon and in the stars, and on the earth distress of the peoples, and clasping of hands from the astonishment at the sound of the sea.
and a shaking that drives out the souls of the sons of men from fear of what is about to come on the earth, and the powers of heaven will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with much power and with great glory.
But when these things begin to be, take courage and lift up your heads, because your deliverance has drawn near.
And he was saying a parable to them: Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
When they bud forth, you at once understand from them that summer has drawn near.
So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of Elohim is near.
Amen I say to you, that this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, and my words will not pass away.
But take heed to yourselves, that your hearts never be weighed down with gluttony and drunkenness and the cares of the world, and that day come upon you suddenly.
For like a snare it will spring upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth.
Be therefore watchful at all times and praying, that you may be worthy to escape from these things that are about to happen, and to stand before the Son of man.
And in the daytime he was teaching in the temple, and at night he went out and lodged on the mountain that is called the House of Olives.
And all the people were coming early to him in the temple to hear his word.
Now the feast of unleavened cakes, which is called the Passover, was near.
And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might kill him, for they were afraid of the people.
And Satana entered into Yehuda who is called Skaryota, who was of the number of the twelve.
And he went ‹and› spoke with the chief priests and the scribes and the chiefs of the force of the temple, so as to hand him over to them.
And they rejoiced and agreed to give him silver.
And he promised them, and was seeking an opportunity to hand him over to them apart from the crowd.
And the day of unleavened bread arrived, on which it was the custom for the passover to be slain.
And Y'shua sent Keefa and Yochanan, and said to them, Go, prepare the passover for us, that we may eat.
And they said to him, Where do you want us to prepare?
He said to them, When you enter the city, a man will meet you carrying a vessel of water. Go after him,
and where he enters, say to the master of the house, Our Master says, Where is the guest room where I may eat the passover with my disciples?
And he will show you a large upper room that is furnished; prepare there.
And they went and found as he had said to them, and they prepared the passover.
And when the time came, Y'shua came and reclined, and the twelve apostles with him.
And he said to them, I have greatly desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer.
For I say to you that from now on I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of Elohim.
And he took the cup and gave thanks and said, Take this and divide it among you.
For I say to you that I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of Elohim comes.
And he took bread and gave thanks and broke it and gave to them and said, This is my body which is given for your sakes. This you are doing for my remembrance.
And likewise also over the cup after they had supped, he said, This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which for your sakes is poured out.
But the hand of him who betrays me is on the table.
And the Son of man goes as it was determined. But woe to that man by whose hand he is betrayed.
And they began to inquire among themselves which of them it was that was about to do this.
And there was also a contention among them, who among them is the greatest.
But Y'shua said to them: The kings of the nations are their masters, and those who hold authority over them are called doers of good.
But you are not so; rather, whoever is great among you must be as the least, and whoever is chief as the one who serves.
For who is greater, the one who reclines or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as the one who serves.
You are the ones who have stayed with me in my trials.
And I promise you, as my Father has promised me, a kingdom,
that you may eat and drink at the table of my kingdom, and sit on thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Yisrael.
And Y'shua said to Shimon: Shimon, look, Satana has asked to sift you like wheat:
but I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail. And you also, in time, turn back and strengthen your brothers.
But Shimon said to him: my Master, with you I am ready, both for prison and for death.
Y'shua said to him: I say to you, Shimon, that the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know me.
And he said to them: When I sent you without purse and without wallet and shoes, did you lack anything? They say to him: Nothing.
He said to them: From now on, whoever has a purse, take it, and likewise also a wallet. And whoever does not have a sword, sell his garment and buy himself a sword.
For I say to you that this also which is written must be fulfilled in me: I will be numbered with the unjust. For all that is upon me will be completed.
And they say to him, Our Master, look, here are two swords. He says to them, They are enough.
And he went out and went, as he was accustomed, to the mountain of the house of olives, and his disciples also went after him.
And when he reached the place, he said to them, Pray that you will not enter into temptation.
And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw, and set his knees, and was praying,
and said, Father, if you will, let this cup pass from me. Yet not my will, but yours be done.
And a messenger from heaven appeared to him, who strengthened him.
And when he was in fear, he prayed earnestly; and his sweat was like drops of blood, and it fell on the ground.
And he rose from his prayer and came to his disciples, and he found them sleeping from sorrow.
And he said to them: Why are you sleeping? Rise, pray, so that you will not enter into temptation.

And while he was speaking, a crowd, and he who was called Yehuda, one of the twelve, came at their head. And he came up to Y'shua and kissed him. For he had given them this sign: The one I kiss, he is the one.
Y'shua said to him: Yehuda, with a kiss are you handing over the Son of man?
And when those who were with him saw what happened, they say to him, Our Master, shall we strike them with the sword?
And one of them struck a servant of the high priest and took off his right ear.
But Y'shua answered and said, Enough, thus far. And he drew near to the ear of the one who was struck and healed him.
