And Y'shua said to those who had come upon him, the chief priests and elders and captains of the temple force, Have you come out against me as against a robber, with sword and with club, to seize me?
Every day I was with you in the temple, and you did not stretch out hands against me. But this is your hour and the authority of darkness.
And they seized him and brought him to the house of the high priest. And Shimon was coming after him from a distance.
But they kindled a fire in the middle of the court and were sitting around it, and Shimon also was sitting among them.
And a certain young woman saw him sitting by the fire, and she looked at him and said, This one also was with him.
But he denied and said, Woman, I do not know him.
And a little after, another ‹person› saw him and said to him, You also are one of them. But Keefa said, I am not.
And after one hour another was contending and said, Truly this one also was with him, for he is also a Galilayan.
Keefa said, Man, I do not know what you are saying. And at once, while he was speaking, the rooster crowed.
And Y'shua turned and looked at Keefa. And Shimon remembered the word of our Master, which he had said to him: Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.
And Shimon went out and wept bitterly.
And the men who were holding Y'shua were mocking him and covering him,
and striking him on his face and saying: Prophesy, who struck you?
And many other things they were blaspheming and saying against him.
And when day dawned, the elders and the chief priests and the scribes assembled, and they led him up to the house of their assembly.
And they say to him: If you are the Mashiyach, tell us. He said to them: If I tell you, you will not believe me.
And if I ask you, you will not give me an answer, or release me.
From now the Son of man will sit at the right hand of the power of Elohim.
And they all say: Are you then the Son of Elohim? Y'shua said to them: You say that I am.
They say: What more need have we of witnesses? For we have heard from his mouth.
And their whole assembly rose up and brought him to Pilatos.
And they began accusing him and saying: We have found this one leading our people astray, and forbidding that the head-tax be given to Caesar, and saying of himself that he is king Mashiyach.
But Pilatos asked him and said to him: Are you the king of the Yehudaye? He said to him: You have said.
And Pilatos said to the chief priests and to the assembly: I find no cause at all against this man.
But they were crying out and saying: He stirs up our people, teaching throughout all Judea, and he began from Galila even to this place.
But Pilatos, when he heard the name of Galila, asked if the man was a Galilean.
And when he learned that he was under the authority of Herodes, he sent him to Herodes, because he was in Urishlim in those days.
But Herodes, when he saw Y'shua, rejoiced greatly, for he had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had heard many things about him, and he was hoping to see some sign from him.
And he asked him many things, but Y'shua gave him no answer.
And the chief priests and the scribes were standing and accusing him vehemently.
But Herodes despised him, he and his soldiers, and when he had mocked him he clothed him in a scarlet robe and sent him to Pilatos.
And on that day Pilatos and Herodes became friends with each other, for enmity had been between them from before.
Then Pilatos called the chief priests and the rulers and the people,

and said to them: You have brought this man to me as one who overturns your people; and look, I have examined him before you, and I have found nothing in this man from all that you charge against him.
But neither Herodes; for I sent him to him, and look, nothing deserving death has been done by him.
I will therefore chastise him and release him.
For it was a custom that he should release one to them at the festival.
But the whole crowd cried out and said: Take this one away, and release Bar-Abba to us.
He was the one who, on account of a sedition that happened in the city and a murder, had been thrown into prison.
But Pilatos spoke with them again, wanting to release Y'shua.
But they were crying out and saying, Crucify him, crucify him.
But he said to them the third time, What evil has this one done? I have found in him no cause worthy of death. I will therefore chastise him and release him.
But they were insisting with a loud voice and asking him that they might crucify him. And their voice was strong, and that of the chief priests.
And Pilatos commanded that their request should be.
And he released to them the one who for sedition and murder had been cast into prison, the one they asked for; but Y'shua he delivered up to their will.
And as they led him away, they seized Shimon the Qurinya, who came from the village, and laid the cross on him to carry ‹it› after Y'shua.
And a great crowd of the people came after him, and women who were wailing and lamenting over him.
And Y'shua turned to them and said, Daughters of Urishlim, do not weep over me, but weep over yourselves and over your children.
For days are coming in which they will say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.
Then they will begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us! and to the hills, Cover us!
For if they do these things in a green tree, what will be in the dry?
And two other doers of evil were coming with him to be killed.
And when they came to a place called a Skull, they crucified him there, and those doers of evil, one on his right and one on his left.
But Y'shua was saying, Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing. And they divided his garments and cast lots on them.
And the people were standing and looking on, and the rulers also were mocking him and saying, He gave life to others; let him give life to himself, if he is the Mashiyach, the chosen of Elohim.
And the soldiers also were mocking him, coming near to him and offering him vinegar,
and they were saying to him: If you are the king of the Yehudaye, give life to yourself.
And there was also a writing written above him in Greek and Roman and Hebrew: This is the king of the Yehudaye.
And one of those doers of evil who were crucified with him was blaspheming against him and saying: If you are the Mashiyach, rescue yourself, and rescue us also.
And his companion rebuked him and said to him: Do you not even fear Elohim, since you also are in the same judgment?
And we justly, for we are worthy, for we are repaid as we have done; but this one has done nothing hateful.
And he said to Y'shua: My Master, remember me when you come in your kingdom.
Y'shua said to him: Amen I say to you, that today you will be with me in paradise.
And it was about the sixth hour, and darkness was over all the earth until the ninth hour.
And the sun was darkened, and the face of the door of the temple was torn from its middle.
And Y'shua cried out with a loud voice and said: My Father, into your hands I place my spirit. This he said, and finished.
And when the centurion saw what happened, he glorified Elohim and said: Truly this man was righteous.
And all the crowds who were gathered for this sight, when they saw what happened, turned back while beating on their breasts.
And all who knew Y'shua were standing at a distance, and the women who came with him from Galila, and they were seeing these things.
Now a certain man whose name was Yosip, a counsellor from Ramtha a city of Yehuda; he was a good and righteous man.
This man had not consented to their will and their deed; and he was waiting for the kingdom of Elohim.
This man came to Pilatos and asked for the body of Y'shua.
And he took it down and wrapped it in a linen cloth and laid it in a hewn tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
And it was the day of preparation, and the sabbath was dawning.
Now those women who came with him from Galila approached and saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
And they returned and prepared spices and ointments, and on the Sabbath they rested as it is commanded.
On the first day of the week, in the morning while it was still dark, they came to the tomb and brought these aromatics they had prepared. And there were other women with them.
And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
And they went in and did not find the body of Y'shua.
And while they were wondering at this, two men stood over them, and their clothing was shining.
And they were in fear and bowed their faces to the ground. And they said to them, Why are you seeking the living among the dead?
He is not here; he has risen. Remember what he spoke with you when he was in Galila,
and he was saying that the Son of man is about to be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and to be crucified, and on the third day to rise.
And they returned from the tomb and told all these things to the eleven and to the rest.
Now they were Maryam Magdalytha and Yochan and Maryam the mother of Ya'akov and the rest who were with them; these were saying these things to the apostles.
And these words appeared in their eyes like nonsense, and they did not believe them.
But Shimon rose and ran to the tomb and looked in and saw the linen cloths lying alone, and he went away wondering in himself at what had happened.
And two of them on that same day were going to a village whose name is Emmaus, sixty stadia distant from Urishlim.
And they were speaking with one another about all these things that had happened.
And while they were speaking and inquiring with one another, Y'shua came and reached them and was walking with them.
And their eyes were held, so that they would not recognize him.
And he said to them: What are these words that you are speaking with one another as you walk, and you are sad?
One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered and said to him: Are you only a stranger from Urishlim, that you do not know the thing that happened in it in these days?
He said to them, What? They say to him, About Y'shua who is from Natsrath, a man who was a prophet and was mighty in word and in deed before Elohim and before all the people.
And the chief priests and the elders delivered him up to the judgment of death, and they crucified him.
But we were hoping that he was the one who was going to deliver Yisrael. And three days ‹have passed› since all these things happened.
But also some women from among us astonished us, for they went early to the tomb.
And when they did not find his body, they came and said to us that they had seen messengers there, and they said about him that he is alive.
And also some men from among us went to the tomb, and they found it just as the women had said, but him they did not see.
Then Y'shua said to them, O you short of understanding and heavy of heart to believe all those things that the prophets spoke.
Were not these things to be, that the Mashiyach should suffer and that he should enter into his glory?
And he began from Moshe and from all the prophets, and he was expounding to them concerning himself from all the writings.
And they drew near to the village to which they were going, and he was making them think as if he were going to a more distant place.
And they urged him and said to him, Stay with us, for the day has now declined toward dark. And he went in to stay with them.
And it was that while he reclined with them, he took bread and blessed and broke and gave to them.
And at once their eyes were opened, and they recognized him. And he was taken from them.
And they were saying one to another: Was not our heart heavy within us while he spoke with us on the road and explained the writings to us?
And they rose up in that hour and returned to Urishlim, and found the eleven gathered, and those with them,
who were saying: Truly our Master has risen, and has appeared to Shimon.
And they also related what happened on the road, and how he was made known to them when he broke the bread.
And while they were speaking these things, Y'shua stood among them and said to them: Peace be with you. It is I; do not be afraid.
And they were alarmed and were in fear, for they supposed they were seeing a spirit.
And Y'shua said to them: Why are you agitated? And why do thoughts rise up in your hearts?
Look at my hands and my feet, that it is I myself. Touch me and know, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.
And as he said these things, he showed them his hands and his feet.
And while they still did not believe from their joy and were astonished, he said to them: Do you have anything here to eat?
And they gave him a piece of broiled fish and of a honeycomb.
And he took ‹and› ate before them.

And he said to them, These are the words that I spoke with you while I was with you, that it is necessary that everything written in the law of Moshe and in the prophets and in the psalms about me be fulfilled.
Then he opened their mind to understand the writings.
And he said to them, Thus it is written, and thus it was right for the Mashiyach to suffer, and to rise from among the dead on the third day;
and that repentance for forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in his name among all the peoples, and the beginning will be from Urishlim.
And you are the witnesses of these things.
And I will send upon you the promise of my Father. But you remain in Urishlim the city until you are clothed with power from on high.
And he led them out as far as Beth-Anya, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.
And it was that while he was blessing them, he was separated from them and went up to heaven.
And they bowed down to him and returned to Urishlim with great joy.
And they were at all times in the temple, praising and blessing Elohim. Amen.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim, and Elohim was the Word.
He was in the beginning with Elohim.
Everything was by his hand, and without him not even one thing was that came to be.
In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
And that light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not take hold of it.
There was a man sent from Elohim; his name was Yochanan.
This one came for testimony, to testify about the light, that every person might believe by his hand.
He was not the light, but ‹came› to testify about the light.
For the light of truth was that which gives light to every person who comes into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was by his hand, and the world did not know him.
He came to his own, and his own did not receive him.
But those who received him, he gave them authority to be children of Elohim, to those who believe in his name.
who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of Elohim.
And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory, a glory as of the Only Begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.
Yochanan testified concerning him and cried out and said: This is he of whom I said, He who comes after me was before me, because he was prior to me.
And from his fullness we all have received, and grace upon grace.
For the law was given by the hand of Moshe; but truth and grace came by the hand of Y'shua the Mashiyach.
No one has ever seen Elohim; the only begotten Elohim, he who is in the bosom of his Father, he has declared ‹him›.
And this is the testimony of Yochanan, when the Yehudaye from Urishlim sent priests and Levites to him to ask him, Who are you?
And he confessed, and did not deny, and confessed, I am not the Mashiyach.
And they asked him again, Who then? Are you Eliyahu? And he said, I am not. Are you a prophet? And he said, No.
And they said to him, Who are you? that we may give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?
He said, I am a voice calling in the wilderness, Make smooth the way of Master YHWH, as Eshaya the prophet said.
Now those who were sent were from the Prishe.
And they asked him and said to him, Why then do you immerse, if you are not the Mashiyach, nor Eliyahu, nor a prophet?
Yochanan answered and said to them, I immerse with water; but among you stands one whom you do not know.
This is the one who comes after me, and was before me, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to untie.
These things took place in Beth-Anya, across the Yordanan, where Yochanan was immersing.
And the day after, Yochanan saw Y'shua coming toward him, and said, Look, the Lamb of Elohim who takes away the sin of the world.
This is he of whom I said, After me comes a man who was before me, because he was prior to me.
And I did not know him, but that he might be known to Yisrael, for this I came immersing with water.
And Yochanan testified and said: I saw the Ruach descending from heaven like a dove, and it remained on him.
And I did not know him, but he who sent me to immerse with water, he said to me: The one on whom you see the Ruach descending and remaining on him, this is he who immerses with the Ruach haKodesh.
And I saw, and I testify that this is the Son of Elohim.
And the next day Yochanan was standing, and two of his disciples.
And he looked at Y'shua as he walked, and said: Look, the Lamb of Elohim!
And his two disciples heard him when he said ‹it›, and they went after Y'shua.
And Y'shua turned and saw them coming after him, and he said to them: What are you seeking? They said to him: Our Rabbi, where are you staying?
He said to them: Come, and you will see. And they came and saw where he was staying, and they were with him that day. And it was about the tenth hour.
And one of those who heard from Yochanan and went after Y'shua was Andrawos, the brother of Shimon.
This one first saw Shimon his brother, and said to him: We have found the Mashiyach.
And he brought him to Y'shua. And Y'shua looked at him and said: You are Shimon the son of Yona; you will be called Keefa.
And on the next day Y'shua wanted to go out to Galila, and he found Philipos and said to him, Come after me.
Now Philipos was from Beth-Tsayda, from the city of Andrawos and of Shimon.
And Philipos found Nataniel and said to him, The one Moshe wrote about in the law and in the prophets, we have found him: Y'shua the son of Yosip, from Natsrath.
Nataniel said to him, Can anything good come from Natsrath? Philipos said to him, Come and see.
And Y'shua saw Nataniel coming toward him, and said of him, Look, truly a son of Yisrael in whom there is no deceit.
Nataniel said to him, From where do you know me? Y'shua said to him, Before Philipos called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.
Nataniel answered and said to him, Rabbi, you are the Son of Elohim; you are the King of Yisrael.
Y'shua said to him, Because I said to you that I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than these.
He said to him, Amen, amen, I say to you, that from now you will see heaven opened, and the messengers of Elohim ascending and descending to the Son of man.
And on the third day there was a feast in Qatna, a city of Galila, and the mother of Y'shua was there.
And Y'shua also and his disciples were invited to the feast.
And the wine ran short, and his mother said to Y'shua, They have no wine.
Y'shua said to her, What is ‹in common› to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.
His mother said to the servants, Whatever he says to you, do ‹it›.
Now there were six stone water-jars there, set for the purification of the Yehudaye, each holding two or three measures.
Y'shua said to them, Fill the water-pots with water. And they filled them up to the top.
He said to them, Draw now, and bring to the chief of the feast. And they brought.

And when the chief of the feast tasted those waters that had become wine, and did not know from where it was—but the servants knew, for they had filled them with the water—the chief of the feast called the bridegroom,
and said to him, Every man first brings the good wine, and when they have drunk, then that which is inferior; but you have kept the good wine until now.
This is the first sign that Y'shua did in Qatna of Galila, and he made known his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this he went down to Kfar-Nachum, he and his mother and his brothers and his disciples, and they were there a few days.
And the Passover of the Yehudaye was near, and Y'shua went up to Urishlim.
And he found in the temple those who sell oxen and sheep and doves, and the money-changers sitting ‹there›.
And he made himself a whip from cord, and drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep and the oxen and the money-changers; and he poured out their money, and overturned their tables.
And to those who sell doves he said, Take these things from here, and do not make my Father's house a house of trade.
And his disciples remembered that it is written: The zeal of your house has eaten me.
But the Yehudaye answered and said to him: What sign do you show us, since you do these things?
Y'shua answered and said to them, Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
The Yehudaye said to him, Forty-six years this temple was being built, and will you raise it in three days?
But he was speaking of the temple of his body.
And when he rose from the house of the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the writings and the word that Y'shua spoke.
And while Y'shua was in Urishlim at the Passover feast, many believed in him because they saw the signs he did.
But Y'shua did not entrust himself to them, because he knew every person.
And he did not need that anyone should testify to him about any man, for he himself knew what is in man.
Now there was a man of the Pharisees there, his name was Niqodemus, a ruler of the Yehudaye.
This one came to Y'shua by night and said to him, Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher sent from Elohim, for no one can do these signs that you do unless Elohim is with him.
Y'shua answered and said to him, Amen, amen, I say to you, that if a person is not born from the beginning, he cannot see the kingdom of Elohim.
Niqodemus said to him, How can an old man be born? Can he enter a second time into his mother's womb and be born?
Y'shua answered and said to him, Amen, amen, I say to you, that if a person is not born from water and spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of Elohim.
That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the spirit is spirit.
Do not be surprised that I said to you, You must be born from the beginning.
The ruach blows where it chooses, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from and where it goes; so is everyone who is born of the ruach.
Nikodemos answered and said to him, How can these things be?
Y'shua answered and said to him, You are the teacher of Yisrael, and you do not know these things?
Truly, truly I say to you, We speak what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and you do not receive our testimony.
If I have spoken to you of things on earth and you do not believe, how will you believe me if I speak to you of things in heaven?
And no one has gone up to heaven except he who came down from heaven, the Son of man who is in heaven.
And as Moshe lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of man is about to be lifted up:
that everyone who believes in him will not perish, but will have life forever.
For Elohim so loved the world that he gave his only Son, that everyone who believes in him will not perish, but will have life forever.
For Elohim did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world might live by his hand.
Whoever believes in him is not judged; and whoever does not believe is already judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only Son of Elohim.
And this is the ‹ground of› judgment, that the light has come into the world, and the sons of men have loved the darkness more than the light, for their deeds were evil.
For everyone who does hateful things hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his deeds will not be reproved.
But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his deeds may be known as done in Elohim.
After these things Y'shua and his disciples came to the land of Yehuda, and there he was staying with them and immersing.
And Yochanan also was immersing at Ein-Yon, which is near Shalim, because there were many waters there, and they were coming and being immersed.
For Yochanan had not yet fallen into prison.
Now there was a dispute of one of the disciples of Yochanan with a certain Yehudi about purification.
And they came to Yochanan and said to him, Our Rabbi, he who was with you beyond the Yordanan, of whom you gave testimony, he also immerses, and many are coming to him.
Yochanan answered and said to them, A son of man is not able to take anything from his own will, unless it is given to him from heaven.
You yourselves are witnesses for me that I said, I am not the Mashiyach, but I am sent before him.
He who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and listens to him, rejoices with great joy because of the bridegroom’s voice. This my joy, then, is made full.
He must increase, and I must decrease.
For he who comes from above is above all; and he who is from the earth is from the earth, and speaks from the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all.
And what he has seen and heard he testifies, and no one receives his testimony.
But he who receives his testimony has sealed that Elohim is true.
For he whom Elohim has sent speaks the words of Elohim; for Elohim has not given the Ruach by measure ‹to him›.
The Father loves the Son and has given everything into his hands.
He who believes in the Son has eternal life; and he who does not obey the Son will not see life, but the wrath of Elohim will remain on him.
Now Y'shua knew that the Pharisees had heard that he made many disciples and immersed more than Yochanan.
Though it was not Y'shua himself who was immersing, but his disciples.
And he left Yehuda and went again to Galila.
And it was necessary for him to come and pass through the land of the Samaritans.
And he came to a city of the Samaritans called Shkar, beside the field that Ya'akov had given to Yosip his son.
And Ya'akov's spring of water was there. And Y'shua was weary from the toil of the road and sat down by the spring; and it was the sixth hour.
And a woman from Shamrin came to draw water. And Y'shua said to her, Give me water to drink.
For his disciples had gone into the city to buy themselves food.
That Samaritan woman said to him, How is it that you, a Yehudi, ask a drink from me, when I am a Samaritan woman? For Yehudeans have no dealings with Shamraye.
Y'shua answered and said to her, If you had known the gift of Elohim, and who this is who says to you, Give me to drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.
The woman said to him, My Master, you have no bucket, and the well is deep. From where do you get living water?
Are you greater than our father Ya'akov, who gave us this well, and drank from it himself, and his sons, and his flock?
Y'shua answered and said to her: Everyone who drinks from these waters will thirst again;
but everyone who drinks from the waters that I give him will not thirst forever; but the waters that I give him will be in him a spring of waters that gush up to life forever.
The woman said to him: My Master, give me from these waters, so that I will not thirst again and will not keep coming to draw from here.
Y'shua said to her: Go, call your husband, and come here.
She said to him: I have no husband. Y'shua said to her: You have said well, I have no husband;
for you have had five husbands, and this one you have now is not your husband. In this you have spoken truly.
The woman says to him, My Master, I see that you are a prophet.
Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you say that in Urishlim is the place where it is right to worship.
Y'shua says to her, Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Urishlim.
You worship what you do not know; but we worship what we know, for life is from the Yehudaye.
But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth; for the Father also seeks worshipers such as these.
For Elohim is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth.
The woman says to him, I know that the Mashiyach is coming, and when he comes, he will teach us everything.
Y'shua says to her, I who am speaking with you am he.
And while he was speaking, his disciples came, and they were amazed that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said, What do you want? or, Why are you speaking with her?
And the woman left her water-pot and went to the city and said ‹to the people›:
Come, see a man who told me everything I did. Is this not the Mashiyach?
And the people went out from the city and were coming to him.
Meanwhile his disciples were asking him and saying to him, Our Rabbi, eat.
But he said to them, I have food to eat that you do not know.
The disciples said among themselves, Has anyone brought him something to eat?
Y'shua said to them, My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to finish his work.
Do you not say that after four months the harvest comes? I say to you, lift up your eyes and see the fields that are white and have already reached the harvest.
And he who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit for life that is forever, and the sower and the reaper rejoice together.
For in this is the true word, that one sows and another reaps.
I sent you to reap what you have not labored in; for others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.
And many Samaritans from that city believed in him because of the word of the woman who was testifying, He told me everything I did.
And when those Samaritans came to him, they asked him to stay with them; and he stayed with them two days.
And many believed in him because of his word.
And they were saying to the woman, From now on we do not believe in him because of your word; for we ourselves have heard and know that this is truly the Mashiyach, the Life-Giver of the world.
And after two days Y'shua went out from there and went to Galila.
For Y'shua himself testified that a prophet is not honored in his city.
But when he came to Galila, the Galilayans received him, who had seen all the signs he did in Urishlim at the feast, for they too had gone to the feast.
Then Y'shua came again to Qatna of Galila, where he made the water wine. And there was in Kfar-Nachum a servant of a king whose son was sick.
This one heard that Y'shua had come from Yehud to Galila, and he went to him and was asking of him that he would come down and heal his son, for he was near to dying.
Y'shua said to him: If you do not see signs and wonders, you will not believe.
That king's servant said to him: My Master, come down before the boy dies.
Y'shua said to him: Go, your son is alive. And the man believed the word that Y'shua said to him, and he went.
And as he was going down, his servants met him and informed him and said to him: Your son is alive.
And he asked them at what hour he recovered. They said to him: Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
And his father knew that it was at that hour in which Y'shua said to him, Your son is alive. And he believed, and all his house.
This again is the second sign that Y'shua did when he came from Yehuda to Galila.
After these things there was a feast of the Yehudaye, and Y'shua went up to Urishlim.
And there was there in Urishlim a certain place of immersion, which is called in Hebrew Beth-Chesda; and there were in it five porches.
And in these were lying a great many of the sick, and the blind, and the lame, and the withered, and they were waiting for the moving of the waters.
For a messenger from time to time went down into the immersion place and stirred the waters; and whoever first went down after the stirring of the waters was healed of whatever disease he had.
And a certain man was there who had been in his disease thirty-eight years.
Y'shua saw him lying, and knew that ‹his disease› had been a long time upon him, and said to him: Do you want to be healed?
The sick man answered and said, Yes, my Master; but I have no one who, when the water is stirred, will put me into the immersion; but while I am coming, another goes down before me.
Y'shua said to him, Get up, take up your bed, and walk.
And at once that man was healed, and he got up, took up his bed, and walked. And that day was the Sabbath.
And the Yehudaye said to him who was healed, It is the Sabbath; it is not lawful for you to take up your bed.
But he answered and said to them, He who made me whole, he said to me, Take up your bed and walk.
And they asked him, Who is this man who said to you, Take up your bed and walk?
But the one who was healed did not know who it was; for Y'shua had withdrawn himself in the great crowd that was in that place.
After a time Y'shua found him in the temple and said to him: See, you are healed; do not sin again, so that nothing worse than before comes upon you.
And the man went and told the Yehudaye that it was Y'shua who had healed him.
And because of this the Yehudaye were persecuting Y'shua and seeking to kill him, because he was doing these things on the Sabbath.
But Y'shua said to them: My Father works until now, and I also work.

And because of this the Yehudaye were seeking all the more to kill him, not only because he was loosening the Sabbath, but also because he was saying of Elohim that he is his Father, and was making himself equal with Elohim.

Y'shua answered and said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you, the Son can do nothing from the will of his own soul, but what he sees the Father do; for whatever the Father does, these the Son also does like him.
For the Father loves his Son, and shows him everything he does; and greater works than these he will show him, that you may wonder.
For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to those he wills.
For the Father does not judge anyone, but has given all judgment to the Son,
that everyone may honor the Son as he honors the Father. He who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
Amen, amen, I say to you, that whoever hears my word and believes the one who sent me has life that is forever, and does not come to judgment, but has passed from death to life.
Amen, amen, I say to you that the hour is coming, and even now it is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of Elohim, and those who hear will live.
For as the Father has life in himself, so he has given also to the Son to have life in himself.
And he has authorized him to be the doer of judgment also.
That he is the Son of man. Do not wonder at this, that the hour is coming when all who are in the grave will hear his voice,
and will come forth; those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
I can do nothing from the will of my own soul, but as I hear, I judge; and my judgment is just, for I do not seek my will, but the will of him who sent me.
If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true.
There is another who testifies about me, and I know that the testimony he testifies about me is true.
You sent to Yochanan, and he testified to the truth.
But I do not receive testimony from a son of man; yet I say these things so that you may live.
He was a lamp that burns and shines, and you were willing for a time to glory in his light.
But I have a testimony greater than that of Yochanan; for the works my Father gave me to finish, those works that I do, testify about me that the Father sent me.
And the Father who sent me, he testifies of me. You have never at any time heard his voice, and you have not seen his visage.
And his word does not abide in you, because you do not believe in him whom he has sent.
Search the scriptures; for in them you think there is life eternal for you; and they testify of me.
And you are not willing to come to me, that life eternal may be yours.
I do not receive glory from the sons of men.
But I know you, that the love of Elohim is not in you.
I came in the name of my Father, and you do not receive me; and if another comes in the name of his own self, him you will receive.
How can you believe, you who receive glory from one another, and do not seek the glory that is from the one Elohim?
Do you suppose that I accuse you before the Father? There is one who accuses you, Moshe, in whom you have hoped.
For if you had believed Moshe, you would also be believing me; for Moshe wrote about me.
And if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?
After these things Y'shua went to the other side of the sea of Galila ‹or› of Tiberias.
And great crowds went after him, because they were seeing the signs he did on the sick.
And Y'shua went up the mountain, and there he was sitting with his disciples.
And the feast of the Passover of the Yehudaye was near.
And Y'shua lifted up his eyes and saw a great crowd coming toward him, and he said to Philipos, From where will we buy bread so that these may eat?
But this he said while testing him, for he knew what he was about to do.
Philipos said to him: Two hundred denarii of bread is not enough for them, when each one of them takes a little.
One of his disciples, Andrawos the brother of Shimon Keefa, said to him:
There is a lad here who has on him five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these for all those ‹people›?
Y'shua said to them: Make all the people recline. Now there was much grass in that place, and the men reclined, in number five thousand.
And Y'shua took the bread and blessed and distributed to those who were reclining, and likewise also from the fish, as much as they wanted.
And when they were satisfied, he said to his disciples: Gather the fragments that remain, so that nothing is lost.
And they gathered and filled twelve baskets with the fragments that were left over for those who had eaten from the five barley loaves.
But those people who saw the sign that Y'shua did were saying, Truly this is the prophet who is coming into the world.
But Y'shua knew that they were about to come and seize him and make him king, and he withdrew to the mountain by himself alone.
And when it was evening, his disciples went down to the sea,
and sat in the boat and were going across to Kfar-Nachum. And it had grown dark, and Y'shua had not come to them.
And the sea was rising against them, because a great wind was blowing.
And they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, and they saw Y'shua walking on the sea, and when he drew near to their ship, they were afraid.
But Y'shua said to them, I am; do not be afraid.
And they wanted to receive him into the ship, and at that hour the ship was at the land to which they were going.

And the next day, that crowd that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other ship there except the one the disciples had gone up in, and that Y'shua had not gone up with his disciples into the ship.
But other boats had come from Tiberias near the place where they ate the bread when Y'shua blessed ‹it›.
And when that crowd saw that Y'shua was not there, nor his disciples, they went up into those boats and came to Kfar-Nachum and were seeking Y'shua.
And when they found him on the other side of the sea, they say to him: Our Rabbi, when did you come here?
Y'shua answered and said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you, you seek me not because you saw the signs, but because you ate the bread and were satisfied.
Do not labor for the food that perishes, but for the food that abides to life forever, which the Son of man will give to you; for this one the Father, Elohim, has sealed.
They say to him: What shall we do, that we may work the works of Elohim?
Y'shua answered and said to them: This is the work of Elohim, that you believe in him whom he has sent.
They say to him: What sign do you do, that we may see and believe in you? What do you work?
Our fathers ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
Y'shua said to them, Amen, amen, I say to you, Moshe did not give you the bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of Elohim is he who came down from heaven and gives life to the world.
They say to him, Our Master, give us this bread at all times.
Y'shua said to them, I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will not thirst forever.
But I said to you that you have seen me, and you do not believe.
All that my Father gives me will come to me, and the one who comes to me I will not cast outside.
For I came down from heaven, not to do my will, but the will of him who sent me.
And this is the will of him who sent me, that of all he has given me I will lose nothing from it, but will raise it up on the last day.
For this is the will of my Father, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him will have life forever, and I will raise him up on the last day.
But the Yehudaye were murmuring at him because he said, I am the bread that came down from heaven.
And they were saying, Is this not Y'shua the son of Yosip, whose father and mother we know? And how does this one say, I came down from heaven?
Y'shua answered and said to them, Do not murmur one with another.
No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For it is written in the prophet: They will all be taught of Elohim. Everyone therefore who hears from the Father and learns from him comes to me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from Elohim; he has seen the Father.
Amen, amen, I say to you: Whoever believes in me has life that is forever.
I am the bread of life.
Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness, and they died.
But this is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that a person may eat of it and not die.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven, and if a person eats of this bread, he will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my body, which I give for the life of the world.
Then the Yehudaye were contending one with another and saying, How can this one give us his body to eat?
And Y'shua said to them, Amen, amen, I say to you, that unless you eat the body of the Son of man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves.
But whoever eats of my body and drinks of my blood has life forever, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For my body truly is food, and my blood truly is drink.
Whoever eats my body and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him.
As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so whoever eats me will also live because of me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven. Not as your fathers ate the manna and died; whoever eats this bread will live forever.
These things he said in the synagogue while teaching in Kfar-Nachum.
And many of his disciples who heard ‹him› said, This word is hard. Who can hear it?
But Y'shua knew in himself that his disciples were murmuring about this, and he said to them, Does this stumble you?
If then you see the Son of man ascending to the place where he was from the beginning!
It is the spirit that gives life; the body profits nothing. The words that I have spoken with you are spirit, and they are life.
But there are some of you who do not believe. For Y'shua knew from the beginning who they were that do not believe, and who it is that betrays him.
And he said to them, For this reason I said to you that no one can come to me unless it is given to him from my Father.
Because of this word many of his disciples went back and were not walking with him.
And Y'shua said to his twelve, Do you also want to go away?
Shimon Keefa answered and said, My Master, to whom will we go? You have the words of life forever.
And we have believed and know that you are the Mashiyach, the Son of the living Elohim.
Y'shua said to them, Have I not chosen you twelve? And one of you is Satana.
Now he was speaking of Yehuda bar Shimon Skaryota, for he was about to hand him over, one of the twelve.
After these things Y'shua was walking in Galila, for he was not willing to walk in Yehuda, because the Yehudaye were seeking to kill him.
And the feast of booths of the Yehudaye was near.
And his brothers said to Y'shua: Leave here and go to Yehuda, that your disciples may see the works you do.
For there is no one who does anything in secret and wishes to be public. If you do these things, show yourself to the world.
For even his brothers did not believe in him, in Y'shua.
Y'shua said to them: My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
The world cannot hate you, but me it hates, because I testify about it that its works are evil.
You go up to this feast; I am not going up to this feast now, because my time is not yet complete.
These things he said, and he stayed in Galila.
But when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then he also went up, not openly, but as in secret.
And the Yehudeans were seeking him at the feast, and they were saying, Where is he?
And there was much murmuring about him in the crowd, for there were some who were saying, He is good, and others were saying, No, but he deceives the people.
Yet no one was speaking openly about him, because of fear of the Yehudaye.
But when the days of the feast were half over, Y'shua went up to the temple and was teaching.
And the Yehudaye were amazed and said: How does this one know the writings, when he has not learned?
Y'shua answered and said: My teaching is not mine, but of him who sent me.
Whoever wants to do his will understands my teaching, whether it is from Elohim, or whether I speak from the desire of my own soul.
Whoever speaks from the desire of his own mind seeks glory for himself; but he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and there is no injustice in his heart.
Did not Moshe give you the law? And no one of you keeps the law.
Why are you seeking to kill me? The crowd answered and said, You have a demon. Who is seeking to kill you?
Y'shua answered and said to them, I did one work, and all of you are amazed.
Because of this Moshe gave you circumcision—‹not that it is from Moshe, but it is from the fathers›—and on the Sabbath you circumcise a man.
If a man is circumcised on the Sabbath day so that the law of Moshe may not be broken, are you murmuring at me because I made a whole man well on the Sabbath day?
Do not judge by taking faces, but judge a just judgment.
And some people from Urishlim were saying, Is not this the one they seek to kill?
And look, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Do the elders know that this is truly the Mashiyach?
But we know this one, from where he is; yet the Mashiyach, when he comes, no one knows from where he is.

And Y'shua raised his voice while teaching in the temple and said, You both know me, and you know from where I am. And I have not come from my own will, but he who sent me is true. Him you do not know;
but I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.
And they sought to seize him; but no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come.
And many from the crowd believed in him, and they say: When the Mashiyach comes, will he do greater signs than these that this man does?
And the Pharisees heard the crowd saying these things about him, and they and the chief priests sent officers to seize him.
And Y'shua said: A little while longer I am with you, and I go to him who sent me.
And you will seek me and will not find me, and where I am you cannot come.
The Yehudaye said among themselves: Where is this one about to go, that we cannot find him? Will he go to the regions of the nations and teach the pagans?
What is this word that he said: You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am you cannot come?
On the great day, which is the last of the feast, Y'shua stood and cried out and said, If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink.
Everyone who believes in me, as the writings have said, rivers of living water will flow from his belly.
This he said about the Ruach which those who believe in him were about to receive, for the Ruach had not yet been given, because Y'shua was not yet glorified.
Many from the crowd who heard his words were saying, Truly this is the prophet.
Others were saying, This is the Mashiyach. Others were saying, Does the Mashiyach come from Galila?
Does not the writing say that the Mashiyach comes from the seed of Dawid, and from Beth-Lekhem the town of Dawid?
And there was a division in the crowd because of him.
And there were some of them who wanted to seize him. But no one laid hands on him.
And those guards came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and the priests said to them: Why have you not brought him?
The guards say to them: Never has a man spoken as this man speaks.
The Pharisees say to them: Have you also been led astray?
Has anyone from the leaders or from the Pharisees believed in him?
But this people who do not know the law are cursed.
Niqdemus, one of them, he who had come to Y'shua by night, said to them:
Does our law condemn a man unless it first hears from him and knows what he has done?
They answered and said to him: Are you also from Galila? Search and see that a prophet does not arise from Galila.
So each one went to his house.
But Y'shua went to the mount of Olives.
But in the morning he came again to the temple, and all the people came to him, and when he sat he was teaching them.
But the scribes and Pharisees brought a woman who was caught in adultery, and when they stood her in the middle,
they say to him, Teacher, this woman was caught openly in the act of adultery.
And in the law of Moshe, ‹Elohim› has commanded that we stone such as these. What therefore do you say?
This they said while testing him, so that they might have ‹ground› to accuse him. But Y'shua, when he stooped down, was writing on the earth.
But when they kept asking him, he straightened up and said to them, Whoever among you is without sin, let him first throw a stone at her.
And again when he stooped down, he was writing on the ground.
But they, when they heard ‹it›, were going out one by one, beginning from the elders, and the woman was left alone, while she was in the middle.
But when Y'shua straightened up, he said to the woman, Where are they? Has no one condemned you?
But she said, No one, Master YHWH. But Y'shua said, Neither do I condemn you. Go, and from now on sin no more.
But again Y'shua spoke with them and said, I am the light of the world. Whoever comes after me will not walk in darkness, but will find for himself the light of life.
The Pharisees say to him, You bear witness about yourself; your testimony is not true.

Y'shua answered and said to them, Even if I bear witness about myself, my testimony is true, because I know from where I came and where I am going. But you do not know from where I came and where I am going.
You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
Yet if I judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and my Father who sent me.
And in your law it is written that the testimony of two men is true.
I am one who bears witness about myself, and my Father who sent me bears witness about me.
They say to him, Where is your Father? Y'shua answered and said to them, You know neither me nor my Father. If you had known me, you would also have known my Father.
These words he spoke in the treasury as he taught in the temple, and no one took hold of him, for his hour had not yet come.
Y'shua said again to them, I go away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sins, and where I go you are not able to come.
The Yehudaye say, Is he about to kill himself, that he says, Where I go you are not able to come?
And he said to them, You are from below, and I am from above. You are from this world; I am not from this world.
I said to you that you will die in your sins. For if you do not believe that I am, you will die in your sins.
The Yehudaye say: Who are you? Y'shua says to them: Even if I have begun to speak with you,
I have much to say concerning you and to judge. But he who sent me is true, and those things that I have heard from him, these I speak in the world.
And they did not know that he spoke to them of the Father.
Y'shua said to them again: When you lift up the Son of man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing from my own pleasure, but as my Father taught me, so I speak.
And he who sent me is with me, and my Father has not left me alone, because I do at all times what is pleasing to him.
When he was speaking these things, many believed in him.
And Y'shua said to those Yehudaye who believed in him: If you continue in my word, you are truly my disciples.
And you will know the truth, and that truth will free you.
They say to him: We are the seed of Avraham, and never has servitude to any man been done to us. How do you say that you will become free men?
Y'shua said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you, that everyone who does sin is the servant of sin.
And a servant does not remain forever in the house, but the Son remains forever.
If therefore the Son frees you, you will truly be free men.
I know that you are the seed of Avraham, but you seek to kill me because you are not able ‹to hold› my word.
I speak what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have seen with your father.
They answered and said to him: Our father is Avraham. Y'shua said to them: If you were children of Avraham, you would be doing the works of Avraham.
But now you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth with you, which I heard from Elohim. This Avraham did not do.
But you do the works of your father. They say to him: We are not ‹the offspring› of whoredom; we have one Father, Elohim.
Y'shua said to them: If Elohim were your Father, you would love me; for I came forth from Elohim and came, and I did not come of my own will, but he sent me.
Why do you not understand my word? It is because you cannot hear my word.

You are of your father the calumniator, and the lust of your father you want to do. He was a manslayer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own, because he is a liar and also its father.
But I, because I speak the truth, you do not believe me.
Who of you convicts me of sin? And if I speak the truth, why do you not believe me?
Whoever is of Elohim hears the words of Elohim. For this reason you do not hear, because you are not of Elohim.
The Yehudaye answered and said to him: Do we not say well that you are a Shomraya, and that a demon is in you?
Y'shua said to them: I have no demon, but I honor my Father, and you are despising me.
But I do not seek my glory. There is one who seeks ‹it› and judges.
Amen, amen, I say to you: Whoever keeps my word will not see death forever.
The Yehudaye say to him: Now we know that you have a demon. Avraham died, and the prophets; and you say: Whoever keeps my word will not taste death forever.
Are you greater than our father Avraham who died, and than the prophets who died? Who do you make yourself?
Y'shua said to them: If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say that he is our Elohim.
And you have not known him. But I know him; and if I say that I do not know him, I would be a liar like you. But I know him, and I keep his word.
Avraham your father longed to see my day, and he saw and rejoiced.
The Yehudaye say to him: You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Avraham?
Y'shua said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you, that before Avraham was, I am.
And they took up stones to stone him. But Y'shua hid himself and went out from the temple and passed among them and went.
And as he passed by, he saw a man blind from his mother's womb.
And his disciples asked him and said, Our Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?
Y'shua said to them, Neither did he sin, nor his parents, but that the works of Elohim might be seen in him.
I must do the works of him who sent me while it is day; the night is coming, when no one can work.
As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
And when he had said these things, he spat on the ground and made clay from his spittle and spread it on the eyes of that blind man.
And he said to him, Go wash in the immersion-pool of Shiloach. And he went, washed, and came seeing.
But his neighbors and those who had seen him before when he was begging were saying, Is this not he who sat and begged?
Some were saying, It is he. And some were saying, No, but he is like him. But he was saying, I am.
They say to him, How were your eyes opened?
He answered and said to them, A man whose name is Y'shua made mud and spread it on my eyes and said to me, Go wash in the waters of Shiloach. And I went, washed, and I saw.
They say to him, Where is he? He said to them, I do not know.
And they brought him who had previously been blind to the Pharisees.
Now it was the Sabbath when Y'shua made mud and opened his eyes.
And again the Pharisees asked him, How was it seen by you? And he said to them, He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and I saw.
And some of the Pharisees were saying, This man is not from Elohim, for he does not keep the Sabbath. But others were saying, How can a sinful man do these signs? And there was a division among them.
They say again to the blind man, What do you say about him who opened your eyes? He said to them, I say that he is a prophet.
But the Yehudeans did not believe concerning him that he had been blind and saw, until they called the parents of him who saw.
And they asked them: Is this your son, of whom you say that he was born blind? How does he see now?
But his parents answered and said: We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind.
But how he sees now, or who opened his eyes for him, we do not know. He has come of age; ask him. He will speak for himself.

His parents said these things because they were afraid of the Yehudaye. For the Yehudaye had decided that if anyone should confess him, that he is the Mashiyach, they would expel him from the synagogue.
Because of this his parents said: He has come of age; ask him.
And they called a second time the man who had been blind, and said to him: Give glory to Elohim, for we know that this man is a sinner.
He answered and said to them: If he is a sinner, I do not know. One thing I know, that I was blind, and now I see.
They said to him again: What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?
He said to them: I told you, and you did not hear. Why do you want to hear again? Do you also want to become his disciples?
But they reproached him and said to him: You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moshe.
And we know that Elohim spoke with Moshe; but this one, we do not know where he is from.
The man answered and said to them: In this then is ‹something› to be wondered at, that you do not know where he is from, and he opened my eyes.
Now we know that Elohim does not hear the voice of sinners; but whoever fears him and does his will, him he hears.
From the ages it has never been heard that anyone opened the eyes of one born blind.
If this man were not from Elohim, he could not do this thing.
They answered and said to him, You were wholly born in sins, and do you teach us? And they threw him out.
And Y'shua heard that they had thrown him out, and he found him and said to him, Do you believe in the Son of Elohim?
He who was healed answered and said, My Master, who is he, that I may believe in him?
Y'shua said to him, You have seen him, and he who speaks with you is he.
And he said, I believe, my Master; and he fell down and worshipped him.
And Y'shua said, For the judgment of this world I have come, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.
And ‹some› of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and they said to him, Are we also blind?
Y'shua said to them, If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now you say, We see; therefore your sin remains.
Amen, amen, I say to you, that whoever does not enter by the door into the fold of the flock, but climbs up from some other place, he is a thief and a robber.
But he who enters by the door is the shepherd of the flock.
And to this one the door-keeper opens the door, and the flock hears his voice, and he calls his sheep by their names and leads them out.
And when he has led out his flock, he goes before it, and his own sheep go after him, because they know his voice.
But after a stranger the flock does not go, but flees from him, because it does not know the voice of a stranger.
This allegory Y'shua spoke to them; but they did not know what he said to them.
Y'shua said to them again, Amen, amen, I say to you, that I am the door of the flock.
And all who came are thieves and robbers, but the flock did not hear them.
I am the door, and if anyone enters by me, he will live, and will enter and go out, and will find pasture.
The thief does not come except to steal and to kill and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and may have what is more.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his flock.
But a hireling, who is not the shepherd, and whose own the sheep are not, when he sees the wolf coming, leaves the flock and flees; and the wolf comes and snatches and scatters the flock.
But the hireling flees because he is a hireling, and he has no concern for the flock.
I am the good shepherd, and I know my own, and I am known by my own.
As my Father knows me, I also know my Father, and I lay down my life for the flock.
But I also have other sheep that are not from this fold, and them also I must bring, and they will hear my voice, and the whole flock will be one, and one shepherd.
For this reason my Father loves me, that I lay down my life so that I may take it again.
No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own will. For I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it again. This command I have received from my Father.
And again there was a division among the Yehudaye because of these words.
And many of them were saying, He has a demon and is completely out of his mind; why do you listen to him?
But others were saying, These words are not those of one who has a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?
And the feast of the dedication was ‹held› in Urishlim, and it was winter.
And Y'shua was walking in the temple, in the porch of Shlemun.
And the Yehudaye surrounded him and said to him, How long will you take our soul? If you are the Mashiyach, tell us plainly.
Y'shua answered and said to them: I have told you, and you do not believe. And the works that I do in the name of my Father, those testify about me.
But you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep, as I have said to you.
My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they come after me.
And I give them life forever, and they will not be lost forever, and no one will snatch them from my hand.
For my Father who gave ‹them› to me is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch from my Father's hand.
I and my Father, we are one.
And the Yehudaye again took up stones to stone him.
Y'shua said to them: Many good works I have shown you from my Father; for which work from them are you stoning me?
The Yehudaye say to him: It is not because of good works that we are stoning you, but because you blaspheme; and while you are a son of man, you make yourself Elohim.
Y'shua said to them: Is it not written thus in your law, that I said, You are Elohim?
If he called them Elohim, because the word of Elohim was with them, and the writing cannot be nullified;
do you say of him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, You blaspheme, because I said to you, I am the Son of Elohim?
But if I do not the works of my Father, do not believe me.
But if I do ‹them›, even if you do not believe me, believe the works, that you may know and believe that my Father is in me and I in my Father.
And they were seeking again to seize him, and he went out from their hands.
And he went to the other side of the Yordanan, to the place where Yochanan was at first when he was immersing, and he was there.
And many people came to him, and they were saying that Yochanan did not even one sign, but everything that Yochanan said about this man is true.
Now there was a certain man who was sick, Lazar of Beth-Anya the village, the brother of Maryam and of Martha.
Now this Maryam is the one who anointed the feet of Y'shua with perfume and wiped ‹them› with her hair; her brother Lazar was the one who was sick.
And his two sisters sent to Y'shua and said, Our Master, look, he whom you love is sick.
But Y'shua said, This sickness is not of death, but for the glory of Elohim, that the Son of Elohim may be glorified by it.
Now Y'shua loved Martha and Maryam and Lazar.
And when he heard that he was sick, he stayed in the place where he was two days.
And afterwards he said to his disciples: Come, let us go again to Yehuda.
His disciples say to him: Our Rabbi, the Yehudaye were just seeking to stone you; and are you going again there?
Y'shua said to them: Are there not twelve hours in the day? And if a man walks in the daytime, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
But if a man walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.
These things Y'shua said, and afterwards he said to them: Lazar our friend is lying down. But I am going to awaken him.
His disciples say to him: Our Master, if he is sleeping, he is recovering.
But Y'shua spoke of his death; and they thought he spoke of the sleep of slumber.
Then Y'shua said to them plainly, Lazar is dead.
And I rejoice that I was not there, for your sakes, that you may believe. But let us go there.
Toma, who is called Tama, said to the disciples his companions, Let us also go die with him.
And Y'shua came to Beth-Anya and found that he had been four days in the tomb.
Now Beth-Anya was near Urishlim, about fifteen stadia distant from it.
And many of the Yehudaye were coming to Martha and Maryam to speak to their hearts concerning their brother.
But Martha, when she heard that Y'shua was coming, went out to meet him; but Maryam was sitting in the house.
And Martha said to Y'shua, My Master, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
But even now I know that whatever you ask of Elohim, he gives you.
Y'shua said to her, Your brother will rise.
Martha said to him, I know that he will rise in the consolation at the last day.
Y'shua said to her: I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live.
And everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?
She said to him: Yes, my Master; I believe that you are the Mashiyach, the Son of Elohim, who comes into the world.
And when she said these things, she went and called Maryam her sister secretly, and said to her: Our Rabbi has come, and calls for you.
And Maryam, when she heard ‹it›, rose up quickly and was coming to him.
But Y'shua had not yet come into the village, but was in that place where Martha met him.
Those Yehudaye also who were with her in the house consoling her, when they saw that Maryam rose quickly and went out, went after her; for they supposed she was going to the grave to weep.
But Maryam, when she came where Y'shua was and saw him, fell at his feet and said to him: If you had been here, my Master, my brother would not have died.
But Y'shua, when he saw her weeping, and those Yehudaye who came with her weeping, was stirred in his spirit and agitated himself.
And he said: Where have you laid him? And they say to him: Our Master, come, see.
And the tears of Y'shua came.
And the Yehudaye were saying: See how much he loved him.
And some of them said, Could not this one who opened the eyes of that blind man have caused that this one also should not die?
And Y'shua, still agitated within himself, came to the tomb. Now the tomb was a cave, and a stone was laid upon its entrance.
And Y'shua said, Take away this stone. Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him, my Master, by now he stinks, for four days have passed for him.
Y'shua said to her, Did I not say to you that if you believe, you will see the glory of Elohim?
And they took away the stone. And Y'shua raised his eyes upward and said, Father, I thank you that you have heard me.
And I know that you always hear me; but because of this crowd that stands here, I say these things, that they may believe that you sent me.
And when he said these things, he cried out with a loud voice: Lazar, come outside!
And the dead man came outside, his hands and his feet bound with bandages, and his face bound with a cloth. Y'shua said to them: Untie him, and let him go.
And many of the Yehudaye who had come to Maryam, when they saw what Y'shua did, believed in him.
And some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Y'shua did.
And the chief priests and the Pharisees assembled and were saying: What will we do? For this man does many signs.
And if we leave him alone like this, all the people will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away our place and our nation.
But one of them, whose name was Qayapa, was the high priest of that year, and he said to them: You do not know anything.
And you are not considering that it is expedient for us that one man die for the people, and not that the whole people perish.
But this he did not say from his own mind; rather, because he was the high priest of that year, he prophesied that Y'shua was about to die for the people,
and not only for the people, but also that he might gather into one the children of Elohim who are scattered.
And from that day they plotted to kill him.
But Y'shua was not walking openly among the Yehudaye; instead he went from there to a place near the wilderness, to a town called Ephrayim, and there he was staying with his disciples.
Now the passover of the Yehudaye was near, and many went up from the villages to Urishlim before the feast, that they might purify themselves.
And they were seeking for Y'shua, and saying one to another in the temple: What do you think? That he will not come to the feast?
Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had commanded that if anyone knew where he was, he should make it known to them, that they might seize him.
But Y'shua, six days before the Passover, came to Beth-Anya, where Lazar was, whom Y'shua had raised from the house of the dead.
And they made a supper for him there, and Martha was serving, and Lazar was one of those reclining with him.
But Maryam took a flask of perfume of pure nard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Y'shua, and wiped his feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the scent of the perfume.
And Yehuda Scriota, one of his disciples, he who was about to hand him over, said:
Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?
But this he said, not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief, and the money-box was with him, and he carried whatever was put into it.
But Y'shua said, Leave her alone; she has kept it for the day of my burial.
For the poor are always with you, but I am not always with you.
And a great crowd of the Yehudaye heard that he was there, and they came, not only because of Y'shua, but also that they might see Lazar, whom he raised from the house of the dead.
And the chief priests were deliberating that they might kill Lazar also,
because many of the Yehudaye, on his account, were going and believing in Y'shua.
And the next day a great crowd that had come to the feast, when they heard that Y'shua was coming to Urishlim,
They took palm branches and went out to meet him, and they were crying out and saying, Oshana! Blessed is he who comes in the name of Master YHWH, the king of Yisrael!
And Y'shua found a donkey and sat on it, as it is written,
Do not fear, daughter of Tsiyon. Look, your king comes to you, riding on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

But his disciples did not understand these things at that time; yet when Y'shua was glorified, his disciples remembered that these things were written about him, and that they had done these things to him.
And the crowd that was with him was testifying that he had called Lazar from the grave and raised him from the house of the dead.
And because of this a great crowd went out to meet him, for they had heard that he had done this sign.
But the Pharisees were saying to one another: You see that you are gaining nothing? For the whole world is going after him.
And there were also some from the peoples among them who had gone up to worship at the feast.
These came and approached Philipos, who was from Beth-Tsayda of Galila, and asked him and said to him: My master, we want to see Y'shua.
And Philipos came and told Andrawos, and Andrawos and Philipos told Y'shua.
But Y'shua answered and said to them: The hour has come that the Son of man should be glorified.
Amen, amen, I say to you, that a grain of wheat, unless it falls and dies in the ground, remains alone; but if it dies, it brings many fruits.
Whoever loves his life will lose it, and whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for life everlasting.
If anyone serves me, he will come after me; and where I am, there my servant will also be. Whoever serves me, the Father will honor him.
Now my soul is troubled, and what will I say? My Father, deliver me from this hour? But for this I came to this hour.
Father, glorify your name. And a voice was heard from heaven: I have glorified ‹it›, and again I will glorify ‹it›.
And the crowd that was standing heard ‹it›, and they say, It was thunder. But others say, A messenger spoke with him.
Y'shua answered and said to them: This voice was not for my sake, but for yours.
Now is the judgment of this world. Now the ruler of this world is cast outside.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw every person to me.
But this he said to show by what death he would die.
The crowd says to him, We have heard from the law that the Mashiyach remains forever. ‹And› how do you say that the Son of man is about to be lifted up? Who is this Son of man?

Y'shua said to them, A little while longer the light is with you. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness does not overtake you. And whoever walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may be sons of the light. These things Y'shua spoke, and he went and hid himself from them.
And though he did all these signs before them, they did not believe in him.
that the word of Ashaya the prophet might be fulfilled, who said: My Master, who has believed our report? And the arm of Master YHWH, to whom has it been revealed?
For this reason they were not able to believe, because Ashaya said again:
He has blinded their eyes and darkened their hearts, so that they will not see with their eyes and understand with their heart and turn, and I heal them.
These things Ashaya said when he saw his glory and spoke of him.
Also of the chiefs many believed in him, but because of the Prishe they were not confessing ‹him›, lest they should be outside the assembly.
For they loved the glory of the sons of men more than the glory of Elohim.
But Y'shua cried out and said, Whoever believes in me is not believing in me, but in him who sent me.
And whoever sees me sees him who sent me.
I have come into the world as light, so that everyone who believes in me will not remain in darkness.
And whoever hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world, but to give life to the world.
Whoever rejects me and does not receive my words, there is one who judges him; the word that I have spoken, it will judge him on the last day.
For I have not spoken from myself, but the Father who sent me, he gave me commandment what I say and what I speak.
And I know that his commandment is life eternal. Therefore those things that I speak, as my Father has said to me, so I speak.

And before the feast of the passover, Y'shua knew that the hour had come when he would depart from this world to his Father. And he loved his own ‹people› who were in this world; and he loved them to the end.
And when supper had come, Satana had cast into the heart of Yehuda son of Shimon Skaryota to deliver him up.
But Y'shua, because he knew that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come out from Elohim and was going to Elohim,
rose from the supper and laid aside his garments and took a linen cloth and wrapped it about his loins;
and poured water into the wash-basin and began to wash the feet of his disciples and was wiping them with the linen cloth with which he had girded his loins.
And when he came to Shimon Keefa, Shimon said to him: My Master, are you washing my feet for me?
Y'shua answered and said to him, What I am doing you do not know now, but afterward you will know.
Shimon Keefa said to him, Never will you wash my feet. Y'shua said to him, If I do not wash you, you have no part with me.
Shimon Keefa said to him, Then, my Master, not only my feet will you wash for me, but also my hands and my head.
Y'shua said to him, He who has bathed needs only to wash his feet, for he is all clean. And you also are clean, but not all of you.
For Y'shua knew who would betray him; because of this he said, Not all of you are clean.
And when he had washed their feet, he took his garments and reclined, and said to them, Do you know what I have done to you?
You call me our Rabbi and our Master, and you speak well, for I am.
If then I, your Master and your Rabbi, have washed your feet, how much more are you bound to wash one another's feet?
For I have given you this example, that as I have done to you, you also should do.
Amen, amen, I say to you, that no servant is greater than his master, and no apostle is greater than the one who sent him.
If you know these things, you are blessed if you do them.
I am not speaking about all of you. For I know those I have chosen. But that the writing may be fulfilled: He who eats bread with me has lifted his heel against me.
From now I tell you, before it happens, so that when it happens you will believe that I am.
Amen, amen, I say to you: Whoever receives the one I send receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.
These things Y'shua said, and he was agitated in his spirit, and he testified and said: Amen, amen, I say to you that one of you will hand me over.
Then the disciples looked at one another, because they did not know of whom he spoke.
Now there was one of his disciples who was reclining on his bosom, the one whom Y'shua loved.
Shimon Keefa signaled to this one that he should ask him who it was of whom he spoke.
And that disciple fell on the breast of Y'shua and said to him, my Master, who is this?
Y'shua answered and said, It is he to whom I dip the bread and give it. And Y'shua dipped the bread and gave it to Yehuda son of Shimon Skaryota.
And after the bread, then Satana entered into him. And Y'shua said to him, What you are doing, do quickly.
But no one of those reclining knew why he said this to him.
For some supposed, because the purse was with Yehuda, that he was commanding him to buy something needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor.
But Yehuda took the bread at once and went out. And it was night when he went out.
And Y'shua said, Now the Son of man is glorified, and Elohim is glorified in him.
And if Elohim is glorified in him, Elohim also glorifies him in himself, and at once glorifies him.
