My children, a little longer I am with you, and you will seek me; and as I said to the Yehudaye, Where I go you are not able to come, I also say to you now.
A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. As I have loved you, you also love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if love is among you one toward another.
Shimon Keefa said to him, Our Master, where are you going? Y'shua answered and said to him, Where I go, you are not able now to come after me; but at the last you will come.
Shimon Keefa said to him, My Master, why can I not come after you now? I lay down my life for you.
Y'shua said to him, You lay down your life for me? Amen, amen, I say to you, the rooster will not crow until you deny me three times.
Do not let your heart be troubled. Believe in Elohim, and believe in me.
There are many dwellings in my Father's house. And if not, I would have told you that I go to prepare a place for you.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself, so that where I am, you also may be.
And where I go, you know, and the way you know.
Toma said to him, Our Master, we do not know where you are going, and how can we know the way?
Y'shua said to him, I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to my Father except by me.
If you had known me, you would also have known my Father; and from now on you know him and have seen him.
Philipos said to him, Our Master, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.
Y'shua said to him, All this time I have been with you, and you have not known me, Philipos? Whoever sees me sees the Father; and how do you say, Show us the Father?
Do you not believe that I am in my Father and my Father in me? The words that I speak, I do not speak from myself; but my Father who dwells in me, he does these works.
Believe that I am in my Father and my Father in me; and if not, believe at least because of the works.
Amen, amen, I say to you, whoever believes in me, the works that I do he will also do, and greater than these he will do, because I go to my Father.
And whatever you ask in my name, I will do for you, that the Father may be glorified in his Son.
And if you ask me in my name, I will do ‹it›.
If you love me, keep my commands.
And I will ask of my Father, and he will give you another Comforter, that he may be with you forever,
the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see him and does not know him; but you know him, because he dwells with you and is in you.
I will not leave you orphans, for I am coming to you a little later.
And the world will not see me, but you will see me. Because I live, you also will live.
In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you are in me, and I am in you.
He who has my commandments with him and keeps them, he is the one who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and will show myself to him.
Yehuda, not Sakaryuta, said to him: My Master, how is it that you are about to show yourself to us and not to the world?
Y'shua answered and said to him: He who loves me keeps my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our abode with him.
But he who does not love me does not keep my word. And this word that you hear is not mine, but of the Father who sent me.
These things I have spoken with you while I am with you.
But the Comforter, the Ruach haKodesh, whom my Father sends in my name, he will teach you everything, and he will remind you of all that I say to you.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Do not let your heart be troubled, and do not be afraid.
You have heard that I said to you that I go away, and I come ‹again› to you. If you had loved me, you would have rejoiced that I go to my Father, for my Father is greater than I.
And now I have said to you before it happens, so that when it has happened, you may believe.
From now on I will not speak many things with you, for the ruler of the world is coming, and he has nothing in me.
But that the world may know that I love my Father, and as my Father commanded me, so I do. Get up, let us go from here.
I am the true vine, and my Father is the cultivator.
Every branch in me that does not give fruit, he takes away; and the one that gives fruit, he cleanses it so that it may give much fruit.
You are already clean because of the word I have spoken with you.
Remain in me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot give fruit from itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you unless you remain in me.
I am the vine, and you are the branches. The one who remains in me and I in him, this one gives much fruit, because without me you can do nothing.
But if a man does not remain in me, he is cast outside like a branch that dries up, and they gather them and throw them into the fire to burn.
But if you abide in me, and my words abide in you, whatever you wish to ask will be yours.
In this the Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit and be my disciples.
Just as my Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Abide in my love.
If you keep my commands, you will abide in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commands and abide in his love.
These things I have spoken with you, that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be made complete.
This is my command, that you love one another as I have loved you.
There is no love greater than this, that a person lay down his life for his friends.
You are my friends if you do everything that I command you.
I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know what his master does; but I have called you my friends, because everything that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you.

It is not you who chose me, but I who have chosen you, and I have set you so that you also will go and bring forth fruit, and your fruit will remain, so that whatever you ask my Father in my name he will give you.
These things I command you, that you love one another.
And if the world hates you, know that it hated me before you.
And if you were of the world, the world would love its own. But you are not of the world, for I have chosen you out of the world; for this reason the world hates you.

Remember the word that I spoke to you, that there is no servant who is greater than his master. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; and if they have kept my word, they will also keep yours.
But all these things they will do to you on account of my name, because they do not know him who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken with them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
Whoever hates me hates my Father also.
And if I had not done among them the works that no other person did, they would not have sin; but now they have seen and have hated both me and my Father.
so that the word that is written in their law may be fulfilled: They hated me without a cause.
But when the Comforter comes, whom I send to you from my Father, the Spirit of truth who goes out from my Father, he will testify about me.
And you also testify, for you have been with me from the beginning.
These things I have spoken with you so that you will not be stumbled.
For they will put you out from their synagogues; and the hour will come that everyone who kills you will suppose that he offers an offering to Elohim.
And these things they will do because they have not known either my Father or me.
These things I have spoken with you so that when their time comes you will remember them, that I said them to you. But these things from the beginning I did not say to you, because I was with you.
But now I am going to him who sent me, and no one of you asks me, Where are you going?
For I have said these things to you, and sorrow has come and filled your hearts.
But I speak the truth to you, that it is profitable for you that I go; for if I do not go, the Paraclete will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment.
Concerning sin, because they do not believe in me.
And concerning righteousness, because I go to my Father, and you see me no more.
And concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world is judged.
I still have much to say to you, but you are not able to grasp ‹it› now.

But when the Spirit of truth comes, he will lead you into all the truth. For he will not speak from his own mind, but whatever he hears, that he will speak, and he will make known to you the things to come.
He will glorify me, because he will receive of what is mine and will show ‹it› to you.
All that my Father has is mine. Because of this I said to you that he will receive of what is mine and will show ‹it› to you.
A little while and you will not see me, and again a little while and you will see me, because I go to the Father.
And his disciples were saying one to another: What is this that he says to us, A little while and you will not see me, and again a little while and you will see me, and that I go to my Father?
And they were saying: What is this little while that he says? We do not know what he is speaking.

But Y'shua knew that they were wanting to ask him, and he said to them: About this you are seeking with one another, that I said to you, A little while and you will not see me, and again a little while and you will see me.
Amen, amen, I say to you, that you will weep and lament, and the world will rejoice, and to you will be sorrow. But your sorrow will become joy.

A woman, when she is giving birth, has sorrow, because her day of birth-giving has come. But when she has given birth to a son, she does not remember her distress because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
Also you now have sorrow. But again I will see you, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
And in that day you will not ask me anything. Amen, amen, I say to you, that whatever you ask my Father in my name, he will give to you.
Until now you have not asked anything in my name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be complete.
These things I have spoken with you in allegories, but the hour is coming when I will not speak with you in allegories, but openly I will declare to you about the Father.
In that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask of the Father for you;
for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came forth from Elohim.
I came forth from with the Father and came into the world, and again I leave the world and go to the Father.
His disciples say to him, Now you are speaking openly, and you are not saying one allegory.
Now we know that you know everything, and you have no need that anyone should ask you; by this we believe that you came forth from Elohim.
Y'shua said to them, Do you believe?
Look, the hour is coming, and now has come, when you will be scattered, each to his place, and you will leave me alone. And I am not alone, for the Father is with me.
These things I have said to you, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble, but take courage; I have conquered the world.
These things Y'shua spoke, and he lifted up his eyes to heaven and said: My Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may glorify you.
As you have given him authority over all flesh, that he may give life forever to all that you have given him.
Now this is life forever, that they may know you, that you are the only true Elohim, and the one you have sent, Y'shua the Mashiyach.
I have glorified you on the earth; the work that you gave me to do, I have finished.
And now, my Father, glorify me with you, with the glory that I had with you before the world was.
I have made known your name to the men whom you gave me from the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
Now I know that everything you have given me is from you.
For the words you gave me I have given to them, and they received them and knew truly that I came out from you, and they believed that you sent me.
And I ask for them; I am not asking for the world, but for those you have given me, for they are yours.
And all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I am glorified in them.
From now on I am not in the world, and these are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name that you have given me, that they may be one as we are.
While I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. Those you gave me I have kept, and none of them is lost except the son of destruction, that the writing might be fulfilled.
But now I come to you; and these things I speak in the world, that my joy may be complete in them.
I have given them your word; and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from the evil.
for they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
Father, set them apart in your truth; your word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, I also have sent them into the world.
And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified in the truth.
And it is not for these only that I ask, but also for those who believe in me through their word;
that they all may be one, as you, my Father, ‹are› in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us, that the world may believe that you sent me.
And the glory that you gave me I have given them, that they may be one as we are one.
I in them, and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, and that the world may know that you sent me, and that you loved them as you also loved me.
Father, those whom you gave me, I desire that where I am they also may be with me, that they may see my glory that you gave me, for you loved me before the foundation of the world.
My righteous Father, the world has not known you; but I have known you, and these have known that you sent me.
And I have made known to them your name, and I am making it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.
These things Y'shua said, and he went out with his disciples across the brook Qedron, a place where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered.
Now Yehuda the betrayer also knew that place, because Y'shua often gathered there with his disciples.
So Yehuda took a cohort and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, and he came there with lanterns and lamps and weapons.
But Y'shua, who knew everything that was coming upon him, went out and said to them, Whom do you seek?
They say to him, Y'shua the Natsraya. Y'shua said to them, I am. And Yehuda the betrayer was also standing with them.
And when Y'shua said to them, I am, they went back and fell on the ground.
Again Y'shua asked them, Whom do you seek? And they said, Y'shua the Natsraya.
Y'shua said to them, I have told you that I am ‹he›; and if you seek me, let these go away:
that the word might be fulfilled which he said, Of those whom you have given me, I have not lost even one from them.
Now Shimon Keefa had a sword on him, and he drew it and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear. And the servant's name was Malek.
And Y'shua said to Keefa, Put the sword into its sheath. The cup that my Father has given me, shall I not drink it?
Then the cohort and the chiliarch and the officers of the Yehudaye seized Y'shua and bound him;
And they brought him first to Chanan, because he was father-in-law of Qayapa, who was high priest of that year.
Now it was Qayapa who had advised the Yehudaye that it was profitable for one man to die for the people.
But Shimon Keefa and one other of the disciples were coming after Y'shua. And that other disciple knew the high priest, and he went in with Y'shua into the courtyard.
But Shimon was standing outside at the door. And that other disciple who knew the high priest went out and spoke to the doorkeeper and brought Shimon in.
Then the young woman who kept the door said to Shimon, Are you also one of the disciples of this man? He said to her, No.
And the servants and the officers were standing and had set a fire to warm themselves, because it was cold. And Shimon also was standing with them and warming himself.
Then the high priest asked Y'shua about his disciples and about his teaching.
And Y'shua said to him, I spoke openly with the people, and at all times I taught in the synagogue and in the temple, where all the Yehudaye assemble, and I spoke nothing in secret.
Why do you ask me? Ask those who heard what I spoke with them. Look, they know everything I said.
And as he said these things, one of the officers standing by struck Y'shua on the cheek and said to him, Do you give such an answer to the high priest?
Y'shua answered and said to him, If I spoke evil, bear witness of the evil; but if well, why did you strike me?
Now Hanan sent Y'shua bound to Qayapa the high priest.
And Shimon Keefa was standing and warming himself, and they said to him, Are you not also one of his disciples? And he denied and said, I am not.
One of the servants of the high priest, a kinsman of him whose ear Shimon cut off, said to him, Did I not see you with him in the garden?
And again Shimon denied, and at that moment the rooster crowed.
And they led Y'shua from the presence of Qayapa to the praetorium, and it was morning. And they did not enter the praetorium, so that they would not be defiled before they ate the passover.
And Pilatos went out to them outside and said to them, What accusation do you have against this man?
They answered and said to him, If he were not an evildoer, we would not even have delivered him over to you.
Pilatos said to them, Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law. The Yehudaye said to him, It is not lawful for us to put a person to death.
so that the word of Y'shua would be fulfilled, when he made known by what death he was about to die.
Then Pilatos went into the praetorium and called Y'shua and said to him, Are you the king of the Yehudaye?
Y'shua said to him, Do you say this from yourself, or have others said ‹it› to you about me?
Pilatos said to him, Am I a Yehudi? Your own people and the chief priests have delivered you to me. What have you done?

Y'shua said to him, My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would have fought so that I would not be delivered up to the Yehudaye. But now my kingdom is not from here.

Pilatos said to him: Then you are a king? Y'shua said to him: You have said that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world, that I might testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice.
Pilatos said to him: What is the truth? And when he said this, he went out again to the Yehudaye and said to them: I find not even one cause in him.
Now you have a custom that I release one to you at the Pesach. Do you want, therefore, that I release to you this king of the Yehudaye?
And they all cried out and said: Not this one, but Bar Abba. Now this Bar Abba was a robber.
And the soldiers braided a crown from thorns and put it on his head, and they clothed him with purple garments.
And they were saying, Peace to you, king of the Yehudaye! And they were striking him on his cheeks.
And Pilatos went out again outside and said to them, Look, I am bringing him out to you outside, so that you may know that I find against him not even one cause.
And Y'shua went out outside, having on him the crown of thorns and the purple garments. And Pilatos said to them, Look, the man!
But when the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out and said, Crucify him, crucify him! Pilatos said to them, You take him and crucify him, for I find no cause in him.
The Yehudaye say to him, We have a law, and according to our law he is guilty of death, because he made himself the Son of Elohim.
And when Pilatos heard this word, he feared all the more.
And he went again into the praetorium, and said to Y'shua, Where are you from? But Y'shua gave him no answer.
Pilatos said to him, Will you not speak with me? Do you not know that I have authority to release you, and I have authority to crucify you?
Y'shua said to him, You would have no authority at all over me if it were not given to you from above. Because of this, the one who delivered me up to you, his sin is greater than yours.

And because of this Pilatos wanted to release him. But the Yehudaye were crying out, If you release this man, you are not Caesar's friend, for everyone who makes himself a king is an adversary of Caesar.
Now when Pilatos heard this word, he brought Y'shua out and sat on the judgment seat in the place that is called the Stone Pavement, but in Hebrew it is called Gabbatha.
And it was the preparation of the Passover, and it was about the sixth hour. And he said to the Yehudaye, Here is your king.
But they were crying out, Take him away, take him away, crucify him, crucify him. Pilatos said to them, Shall I crucify your king? The chief priests said, We have no king except Caesar.
Then he delivered him to them to crucify him. And they took Y'shua and led him out,
carrying his cross, to the place that is called a Skull, but in Hebrew it is called Golgotha,
where they crucified him, and with him two others, one on this side and one on that, and Y'shua in the middle.
And Pilatos also wrote a tablet and put it on his cross. And it was written thus: This is Y'shua the Natsraya, king of the Yehudaye.
And many of the Yehudaye read this tablet, because the place where Y'shua was crucified was near to the city; and it was written in Hebrew and Greek and Latin.
And the chief priests said to Pilatos: Do not write that he is king of the Yehudaye, but that he said, I am king of the Yehudaye.
Pilatos said: What I have written, I have written.
Now the soldiers, when they had crucified Y'shua, took his garments and made four parts of them, a part for each of the soldiers. But his tunic was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

And they said one to another: We will not tear it, but will cast lots for it, whose it will be. And the scripture was fulfilled which said: They divided my garments among them, and upon my clothing they cast the lot. These things the soldiers did.
Now standing near the cross of Y'shua were his mother and his mother's sister and Maryam ‹the wife› of Qliyopa and Maryam Magdalitha.
Y'shua saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing there, and he said to his mother, Woman, look, your son.
And he said to that disciple, Look, your mother. And from that hour the disciple took her to himself.
After these things Y'shua knew that everything was finished, and that the writing might be fulfilled, he said, I thirst.
And a vessel was standing there full of vinegar. They filled a sponge with the vinegar and put it on a hyssop ‹stalk› and brought it to his mouth.
When Y'shua had taken the vinegar he said, Look, it is finished. And he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

The Yehudaye then, because it was the preparation, were saying, These bodies must not remain on their crosses, because the Shabbat was dawning; for that day of the Shabbat was a great day. And they asked from Pilatos that they should break the legs of those crucified and take them down.
And the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first and of the other who was crucified with him.
And when they came to Y'shua, they saw that he was already dead, and they did not break his legs.
But one of the soldiers struck him in his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
And he who saw ‹it› has testified, and his testimony is true; and he knows that he speaks the truth, that you also may believe.
For these things happened that the writing might be fulfilled that said, A bone will not be broken in him.
And again another writing that says, They will look on him whom they pierced.

After these things Yosip, the one from Ramtha, asked Pilatos—because he was a disciple of Y'shua and was hiding from fear of the Yehudaye—that he might take the body of Y'shua. And Pilatos permitted it. And he came and took the body of Y'shua.
And Niqodemos also came, the one who had come before to Y'shua by night, and he brought with him a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred litras.
And they took the body of Y'shua and wrapped it in linen and in spices, as is the custom of the Yehudaye to bury.
Now there was in that place where Y'shua was crucified a garden, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
And there they laid Y'shua, because the Sabbath was coming in, and because the tomb was near.
On the first ‹day› of the week Maryam of Magdala came in the morning while it was still dark to the tomb, and she saw that the stone was taken away from the grave.
And she ran and came to Shimon Keefa and to that other disciple whom Y'shua loved, and said to them, They have taken our Master from the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him.
And Shimon went out, and that other disciple, and they were going to the tomb.
And the two were running together, but that disciple ran ahead of Shimon and came first to the tomb.
And he looked in and saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.
Then Shimon came after him and entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there;
and the face-cloth that had been wrapped on his head was not with the linen cloths, but was folded and laid aside in one place.
Then that disciple who came first to the tomb also went in, and he saw and believed.
For they did not yet know from the writings that he was going to rise from the dead.
And those disciples went again to their place.
But Maryam was standing at the tomb and weeping, and as she wept she looked into the tomb
and she saw two messengers in white sitting, one at his head and one at his feet, where the body of Y'shua had been laid.
And they say to her, Woman, why are you weeping? She says to them, Because they have taken away my Master, and I do not know where they have laid him.
She said this and turned behind her and saw Y'shua standing, and she did not know that it was Y'shua.

Y'shua says to her, Woman, why are you weeping, and whom are you seeking? But she supposed that he was the gardener, and she says to him, My master, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have laid him, ‹and› I will go take him away.
Y'shua says to her, Maryam! And she turned and says to him in Hebrew, Rabbuli, which is said Teacher.
Y'shua says to her, Do not come near me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and say to them, I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my Elohim and your Elohim.
Then Maryam Magdalitha came and told the disciples that she had seen our Master, and that he had said these things to her.

And when it was evening on that first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples were, because of fear of the Yehudaye, Y'shua came, stood among them, and said to them, Peace be with you.
He said this and showed them his hands and his side. And the disciples rejoiced when they saw our Master.
Y'shua said to them again, Peace be with you. As my Father has sent me, I also send you.
And when he said these things, he breathed on them and said to them, Receive the Ruach haKodesh.
If you forgive sins for anyone, they are forgiven him; and if you hold ‹those› of anyone, they are held.
But T'oma, one of the twelve, who is called the Twin, was not there with them when Y'shua came.

And the disciples say to him, We have seen our Master. But he says to them, Unless I see in his hands the places of the nails, and put my fingers into them, and stretch out my hand into his side, I will not believe.
And after eight days the disciples were again inside, and Toma with them. And Y'shua came, while the doors were shut, stood in the midst, and said to them, Peace be with you.
And he said to Toma, Reach your finger here and see my hands, and reach your hand and stretch it into my side, and do not be unbelieving, but believing.
And Toma answered and said to him, My Master and my Elohim!
Y'shua said to him, Now that you have seen me, you believe. Blessed are those who have not seen me and have believed.
But many other signs Y'shua did before his disciples, which are not written in this book.
But these are written, that you may believe that Y'shua is the Mashiyach, the Son of Elohim; and that when you believe, you may have life eternal by his name.
After these things Y'shua showed himself again to his disciples at the sea of Tiberias. And he showed ‹himself› thus:
There were together Shimon Keefa, and Toma who is called the Twin, and Nataniel who was from Qatna of Galila, and the sons of Zabdai, and two others of the disciples.
Shimon Keefa said to them: I am going to catch fish. They say to him: We also are coming with you. And they went out and went up into the boat, and that night they caught nothing.
But when it was morning, Y'shua stood on the shore of the sea, and the disciples did not know that it was Y'shua.
And Y'shua said to them: Lads, do you have anything to eat? They say to him: No.
He said to them: Cast your net on the right side of the boat, and you will find. And they cast, and they could not draw the net because of the multitude of fish it had caught.

And that disciple whom Y'shua loved said to Keefa, This is our Master. But Shimon, when he heard that it is our Master, took his tunic and girded it on his loins, because he was naked, and threw himself into the sea to come to Y'shua.
But the other disciples came in the boat, for they were not very far from the land, only about two hundred cubits, and they were dragging the net of fishes.
And when they went up onto the land, they saw coals of fire placed, and fish laid on them, and bread.
And Y'shua said to them, Bring ‹some› of those fishes that you have just caught.
And Shimon Keefa went up and dragged the net to the land, full of large fishes, a hundred and fifty-three. And with all this weight the net was not torn.
And Y'shua said to them, Come, dine. But none of the disciples dared to ask him who he is, for they knew that it is our Master.
Then Y'shua came near and took the bread and the fish and gave them to them.
This was the third time Y'shua appeared to his disciples after he rose from the house of the dead.

And when they had breakfasted, Y'shua said to Shimon Keefa, Shimon son of Yonah, do you love me more than these? He said to him, Yes, my Master, you know that I love you. He said to him, Tend my lambs for me.
He said to him again a second time, Shimon son of Yonah, do you love me? He said to him, Yes, my Master, you know that I love you. Y'shua said to him, Tend my sheep for me.

He said to him the third time, Shimon son of Yonah, do you love me? And it grieved Keefa that he said to him the third time, Do you love me? And he said to him, My Master, you know everything; you know that I love you. Y'shua said to him, Tend my ewes for me.

Amen, amen, I say to you, when you were young, you used to gird your own waist and walk where you wanted; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird your waist for you and lead you where you do not want.
And this he said to show by what death he was going to glorify Elohim. And when he said these things, he said to him, Come after me.
And Shimon Keefa turned and saw the disciple whom Y'shua loved coming after him, the one who fell on Y'shua's breast at the supper and said, My Master, who is it that betrays you?
When Keefa saw this one, he said to Y'shua, My Master, and this one, what?
Y'shua said to him, If I will that this one remain until I come, what ‹is that› to you? You come after me.
And this word went out among the brothers that that disciple would not die. Yet Y'shua did not say that he would not die, but, If I will that this one remain until I come, what ‹is that› to you.
This is the disciple who testified about all these things, and also wrote them, and we know that his testimony is true.
And there are also many other things that Y'shua did, which if they were written one by one, even the world itself, as I suppose, would not suffice for the books that would be written.
The former book I wrote, O Theophilus, about all those things which our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach began to do and to teach,
until the day when he was taken up, after he had commanded the apostles whom he had chosen by the Ruach haKodesh.
To them he also showed himself alive after he had suffered, by many proofs, during forty days, while he was seen by them, and spoke about the kingdom of Elohim.
And when he ate bread with them, he commanded them not to depart from Urishlim, but to wait for the promise of the Father, which you have heard from me.
For Yochanan immersed with water, but you will be immersed with the Ruach haKodesh after not many days.
But they, when assembled, asked him and said to him: Our Master, are you at this time restoring the kingdom to Yisrael?
He said to them, It is not yours to know the time or the times which the Father has set in his own authority.
But when the Ruach haKodesh comes upon you, you will receive power, and you will be witnesses for me in Urishlim and in all Yehuda and also among the Samaritans, and to the end of the earth.
And when he had said these things, while they were looking at him, he was taken up, and a cloud received him, and he was hidden from their eyes.
And while they were gazing into heaven as he was going, two men were found standing by them in white garments,
and saying to them, Men of Galila, why are you standing and gazing into heaven? This Y'shua, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you have seen him go up into heaven.
And afterward they returned to Urishlim from the mountain that is called of Olives, which is beside Urishlim and about seven stadia distant from it.

And after they went in, they went up to the upper room where they were staying: Petros and Yochanan and Ya'akov and Andrawos and Philipos and Toma and Matai and Bar-Tulmay and Ya'akov son of Chalpai and Shimon the Zealot and Yehuda son of Ya'akov.
These all were continuing together as one in prayer, with one soul, with the women and with Maryam the mother of Y'shua and with his brothers.
And in those days Shimon Keefa stood up in the middle of the disciples—there was a gathering of people there of about a hundred and twenty—and said:
Men, brothers, it was right that the writing should be fulfilled which the Ruach haKodesh spoke beforehand by the mouth of Dawid concerning Yehuda, who was guide to those who seized Y'shua.
Because he was numbered with us, and he had a portion in this ministry.
This is the one who acquired a field for himself from the wage of sin, and he fell on his face on the ground, and burst open from his middle, and all his insides were poured out.
And this became known to all who dwell in Urishlim, and so that field was called in the language of the country Chaqal Dema, which is its translation Field of Blood.
For it is written in the book of Psalms: Let his dwelling be desolate, and let no dweller be in it; and let another take his service.
It is right therefore that one of these men who were with us all this time in which our Master Y'shua went in and went out among us,
beginning from the immersion of Yochanan until the day he was taken up from us, should be with us a witness of his resurrection.
And they set forward two, Yosip who is called Barshaba, who was named Yustus, and Mathiya.
And when they had prayed, they said: You, Master YHWH, knower of what is in the hearts of all, show which one you have chosen of these two,
that he should receive the lot of the ministry and apostleship from which Yehuda broke away, that he might go to his place.
And they cast lots, and it came up for Mathiya; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.
And when the days of Pentecost were fulfilled, while they were all gathered as one,
there came suddenly from heaven a sound like a strong wind, and the whole house where they were sitting was filled with it.
And tongues appeared to them that were divided like fire, and they sat on each one of them.
And they were all filled with the Ruach haKodesh, and they began to speak in tongue after tongue as the Ruach was giving them to speak.
Now there were men dwelling in Urishlim who feared Elohim, Yehudaye from every people under heaven.
And when that sound came, all the people gathered, and they were stirred because each one of them was hearing them speaking in their own tongues.
They were all astonished and wondering as they said one to another, Are not all these who are speaking Galileans?
How do we hear, each one, his own language in which we were born?
Parthians and Medes and Elamites and those who dwell in Beth-Nahrin, Yehudaye and Cappadocians and those from the land of Pontus and of Asia,
and those from the land of Phrygia and of Pamphylia and of Mitsrayin and of the regions of Libya that are near Cyrene, and those who came from Rome, Yehudaye and proselytes,
and those from Crete and Arabians. We hear them speaking in our own languages the wonders of Elohim.
They were all wondering and astonished as they said one to another, What is this thing?
But others were mocking them, saying, These have drunk new wine and are drunk.
Afterwards Shimon Keefa stood up with the eleven apostles, raised his voice, and said to them, Men, Yehudaye, and all who live in Urishlim, let this be known to you, and listen to my words.
For these are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is only the third hour until now.
But this is what was spoken by Yoel the prophet:

It will be in the last days, says Elohim, I will pour out my Ruach on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
And on my servants and on my handmaids I will pour out my Ruach in those days, and they will prophesy.
And I will give signs in the heavens and mighty works on the earth, blood and fire and vapor of smoke.
The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and fearful day of Master YHWH comes.
And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of Master YHWH will live.

Men, sons of Yisrael, hear these words: Y'shua the Natsraya, a man who was shown among you from Elohim by power and by signs and by mighty works, which Elohim did among you by his hand, as you yourselves know;
this one, who was set apart for this by the foreknowledge and will of Elohim, you delivered into the hands of the wicked, and you crucified and killed.
But Elohim raised him up and loosed the cords of Sheol, because it was not possible that he should be held in Sheol.
For Dawid said concerning him: I was seeing my Master at all times, for he is at my right hand, that I will not be moved.
Because of this my heart is glad and my glory rejoices, and also my body will dwell on hope.
Because you will not leave my soul in Sheol, and you will not give your devout one to see corruption.
You have revealed to me the path of life; you will fill me with gladness with your face.
Men, brothers, it is allowed to speak openly to you about the head of the fathers Dawid, that he died and also was buried, and his tomb is with us until this day.
For he was a prophet, and he knew that Elohim had sworn to him with an oath: From the fruit of your belly I will seat ‹one› on your throne.
And he foresaw and spoke of the rising of the Mashiyach, that he was not left in Sheol, nor did his body see corruption.
This Y'shua Elohim has given life to, and we all are his witnesses.
And he is the one who was exalted at the right hand of Elohim, and received from the Father the promise of the Ruach haKodesh, and has poured out this gift which you see and hear.
For Dawid did not go up to heaven, because he himself said: Master YHWH said to my Master, Sit at my right hand,
until I place your enemies as a footstool for your feet.
So let all the house of Yisrael know for certain that Elohim has made this Y'shua whom you crucified both Master YHWH and Mashiyach.
And when they heard these things, they were cut in their heart, and they said to Shimon and to the rest of the apostles: Our brothers, what shall we do?
Shimon said to them: Turn, and be immersed each one of you in the name of Master YHWH Y'shua for the forgiveness of sins, so that you may receive the gift of the Ruach haKodesh.
For the promise is to you and to your children and to all those who are far off, those whom Elohim will call.
And with many other words he was testifying to them and was entreating them, saying: Live from this crooked generation.
And some of them readily received his word and believed and were immersed, and there were added on that day about three thousand souls.
And they were continuing in the teaching of the apostles, and were sharing in prayer and in the breaking of the eucharist.
And fear was on every soul, and many signs and mighty works were ‹wrought› by the hand of the apostles in Urishlim.
And all those who believed were together, and everything that belonged to them was held in common.
And those who had possessions were selling them and dividing to each one as he had need.
And every day they continued in the temple with one soul, and at home they broke bread and took food rejoicing and in the simplicity of their heart.
They were praising Elohim, having favor before all the people. And our Master was adding every day to the assembly those who were living.
And it was, as Shimon Keefa and Yochanan went up together to the temple at the time of prayer, the ninth hour,

and a certain man lame from his mother's womb—those who were accustomed were carrying him and setting him at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, so that he might ask alms from those entering the temple.
This man, when he saw Shimon and Yochanan entering the temple, asked them to give him alms.
And Shimon and Yochanan looked at him and said to him, Look at us.
And he looked at them, expecting to receive something from them.
Shimon said to him, Gold and silver I do not have, but what I have I give to you: in the name of Y'shua the Mashiyach the Natsraya, rise up, walk.
And he took him by his right hand and raised him up, and in that hour his feet and his heels were strengthened.
And he leaped, stood up, and walked, and he entered with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising Elohim.
And all the people saw him as he walked and praised Elohim.
And they recognized that it was he, the beggar who sat every day and asked alms at the gate that is called Beautiful, and they were filled with amazement and wonder at what had happened.
And as he held fast to Shimon and Yochanan, all the people ran amazed to them at the porch that is called of Shlemun.

And when Shimon saw ‹it›, he answered and said to them: Men, sons of Yisrael, why are you wondering at this? or why are you gazing at us, as if by our own power or authority we had made this man walk?

The Elohim of Avraham and of Yitz'chak and of Ya'akov, the Elohim of our fathers, has glorified his Son Y'shua, whom you delivered up and denied before the face of Pilatos, when he was judging it right to release him.
But you denied the holy and just one, and asked for yourselves that a murderer be given to you.
And the Head of life you killed, whom Elohim raised from the house of the dead, and we all are his witnesses.
And by faith in his name, this one whom you see and know, he has made firm and healed; and the faith that is in him has given him this soundness before you all.
But now, my brothers, I know that in error you did this, as also your chiefs did.
And Elohim, as he had previously proclaimed by the mouth of all the prophets that his Mashiyach would suffer, has in this way fulfilled ‹it›.
Repent therefore and turn, so that your sins may be blotted out, and times of rest may come to you from before the face of Master YHWH.
And he may send to you the one who was prepared for you, Y'shua the Mashiyach:
whom the heavens must receive until the fulfillment of the times of all those things that Elohim spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets from of old.
For Moshe said: A prophet will Master YHWH raise up for you from your brothers, like me; listen to him in all that he will speak with you.
And it will be that every soul that will not listen to that prophet, that soul will perish from his people.
And all the prophets from Shmuel and those who were after him have spoken and proclaimed about these days.
You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant which Elohim set for our fathers, when he said to Avraham that in your seed all the families of the earth will be blessed.
To you first he has established, and Elohim has sent his Son blessing you if you turn and repent from your evils.
And while they were speaking these words to the people, the priests and the Sadducees and the rulers of the temple rose up against them;
being angry with them, that they taught the people and proclaimed in the Mashiyach about the resurrection from the dead.
And they laid hands on them and kept them until the next day, because evening was drawing near.
And many who had heard the word believed, and they were in number about five thousand men.
And the next day the rulers and the elders and the scribes assembled,
and also Chanan the high priest, and Qayafa, and Yochanan, and Aleksandros, and those who were of the kindred of the high priests.
And when they had set them in the midst, they were asking them: By what power or by what name have you done this?
Then Shimon Keefa was filled with Ruach haKodesh and said to them: Rulers of the people and elders of the house of Yisrael, hear.
If we this day are being judged by you concerning the good deed that was done to the infirm man, by what means this one was healed;

let this be known to you and to all the people of Yisrael, that by the name of Y'shua the Mashiyach the Natsraya, whom you crucified, whom Elohim raised from the house of the dead, by him this ‹man› stands before you whole.
This is the stone that you builders rejected, and it has become the head of the corner.
And there is no deliverance in any other person; for there is no other name under heaven that has been given to the sons of men by which it is necessary to live.

And when they heard the word of Shimon and of Yochanan, which they spoke openly, they understood that they were unlearned and ordinary men, and they were amazed at them, and recognized them that they had been going about with Y'shua.
And they saw that the lame man who had been healed was standing with them, and they could not say anything against them.
Then they commanded that they should go out from their assembly, and they were saying one to another:
What shall we do to these men? For look, a clear sign that has been done by their hands is known to all the inhabitants of Urishlim, and we cannot deny ‹it›.
But so that this good ‹thing› may not go out further among the people, let us threaten them that they should not speak again in this name to any of the sons of men.
And they called them and commanded them that they should not speak at all nor teach in the name of Y'shua.
Shimon Keefa and Yochanan answered and said to them: If it is right before Elohim that we listen to you more than to Elohim, you judge.
For we are not able not to speak what we have seen and heard.
And they threatened them and released them. For they found no cause to lay on their heads because of the people, for everyone was glorifying Elohim over what had happened.
For the man on whom this sign of healing had been done was more than forty years old.
And when they were released, they came to their brothers and related to them all that the priests and the elders had said.
And they, when they heard ‹it›, together lifted up their voice to Elohim and said: Master YHWH, you are Elohim who made heaven and earth and the seas and all that is in them.
And you are the one who spoke by the Ruach haKodesh through the mouth of Dawid your servant: Why have the nations raged, and the peoples plotted emptiness?
The kings of the earth have stood up, and the rulers have taken counsel together against Master YHWH and against his Mashiyach.
For in truth they have gathered in this city against your holy Son Y'shua, whom you anointed, Herodes and Pilatos with the peoples and the assembly of Yisrael,
to do all that your hand and your will beforehand marked out to take place.
And now also, Master YHWH, look and see their threats, and give to your servants that with openness they may proclaim your word,
while you stretch out your hand for healings and mighty works and signs to be done in the name of your holy Son Y'shua.
And when they prayed and made supplication, the place in which they were assembled was shaken, and they were all filled with the Ruach haKodesh, and they were speaking the word of Elohim openly.

And there was to the assembly of the people who had believed one soul and one mind, and no one of them was saying of the property he possessed that it was his own, but everything that was theirs was held in common.
And with great power those apostles were testifying to the resurrection of Y'shua the Mashiyach, and great grace was with them all.
And there was no one among them who was in need, for those who possessed fields and houses were selling them and bringing the prices of what was sold,
and placing ‹it› at the feet of the apostles, and it was given to each person as he had need.
But Yosip, who by the apostles was surnamed Bar-Naba (which is interpreted Son of Consolation), a Levite from the country of Cyprus,
He had a field, and he sold it, and brought its price, and laid ‹it› before the feet of the apostles.
And a certain man whose name was Chananya, with his wife whose name was Shapira, sold his field,
and took from its price and concealed ‹it›, his wife being aware of it, and brought from it of the money and laid ‹it› before the feet of the apostles.
And Shimon said to him: Chananya, why has Satana so filled your heart that you should lie against the Ruach haKodesh and conceal from the money of the price of the field?

Was it not your own before it was sold? And after it was sold, again you had authority over its price. Why have you set in your heart to do this thing? You have not lied against men, but against Elohim.
And when Chananya heard these words, he fell and died. And great fear came upon all those who heard ‹of it›.
And the young men among them rose and gathered him up and carried ‹him› out and buried him.
And after three hours had passed, his wife also came in, not knowing what had happened.
Shimon said to her, Tell me if you sold the field for this price. And she said, Yes, for this price.
Shimon said to her, Because you agreed together to test the Ruach of Master YHWH, look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.
And at that moment she fell before their feet and died. And those young men came in and found her dead, and they wrapped her, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
And great fear came on all the assembly and on all who heard ‹it›.
And many signs and mighty works were done by the hands of the apostles among the people. And they were all gathered together in the porch of Shlemun.
And of other people, no one dared to come near them, but the people magnified them.
And more and more were being added those who believed in Master YHWH, multitudes of men and of women.
so that they were bringing the sick out into the streets, laid on beds, so that when Shimon came, even his shadow might fall on them.
And many were coming to them from the other cities around Urishlim, bringing the sick and those who had unclean spirits, and they were all healed.
And the high priest was filled with great envy, and all those with him who were of the teaching of the Sadducees.
And they laid hands on the apostles, and seized and bound them in prison.
Then in the night a messenger of Master YHWH opened the door of the prison house and brought them out and said to them:
Go, stand in the temple and speak to the people all these words of life.

And they went out at dawn and entered the temple and were teaching. But the high priest and those with him called their associates and the elders of Yisrael and sent to the prison house to bring the apostles.
And when those who were sent by them went, they did not find them in the prison house, and they returned and came
saying: We found the prison house shut carefully, and also the keepers standing at the door; and we opened and found no one there.
And when the chief priests and the rulers of the temple heard these words, they were astonished at them and were thinking what this could be.
And a man came and informed them: Those men whom you shut up in the prison, look, they are standing in the temple and teaching the people.
Then the rulers went with the attendants to bring them, not by force, for they were afraid the people might stone them.
And when they brought them, they stood them before the whole council, and the high priest began to say to them:
Did we not strictly charge you not to teach anyone in this name? But look, you have filled Urishlim with your teaching, and you want to bring the blood of this man upon us.
Shimon answered with the apostles and said to them: We must obey Elohim rather than men.
The Elohim of our fathers raised up Y'shua, whom you killed when you hung him on a tree.
This one Elohim has established as head and Life-Giver, and has raised him up at his right hand so that he might give repentance and forgiveness of sins to Yisrael.
And we are witnesses of these words, and the Ruach haKodesh whom Elohim gives to those who believe in him.
And when they heard these words, they were cut with rage and were thinking of killing them.
And one of the Pharisees stood up, whose name was Gamaliel, a teacher of the law and honored by all the people, and he ordered that they put the emissaries outside for a little while.
And he said to them: Men, sons of Yisrael, take care for yourselves and see what is right for you to do about these men.

For before this time Theudas rose up and said of himself that he was something great, and about four hundred men went after him. And he was killed, and those who went after him were scattered and became as nothing.

And after him rose up Yehuda the Galilayan, in the days when people were being enrolled for the head-tax, and he led astray many people after him. And he died, and all those who were going after him were scattered.
And now I say to you: Keep yourselves away from these men and leave them alone. For if this counsel and this work is from the sons of men, they dissolve and pass away.
But if it is from Elohim, it does not reach into your hands to nullify it, lest you be found standing against Elohim.
And they were persuaded by him, and they called the shlicha and scourged them and commanded them not to be speaking in the name of Y'shua, and they released them.
And they went out from before them rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for the name.
And they did not cease every day to teach in the temple and in the house, and to proclaim about our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
And in those days, when the disciples had multiplied, the Greek disciples were murmuring against the Hebrews, because their widows were being neglected in the daily service ‹to the needy›.
And the twelve apostles called the whole assembly of the disciples and said to them: It is not right that we should leave the word of Elohim and serve tables.
So then, my brothers, search out and choose from among you seven men of whom there is testimony, full of the Ruach of Master YHWH and of wisdom, and we will appoint them over this matter.
And we will continue constantly in prayer and in the service of the word.

And this word was pleasing before all the people. And they chose Estephanos, a man who was full of faith and of the Ruach haKodesh, and Philipos, and Prokoros, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmena, and Nikolaos, a proselyte of Antiokia.
These stood before the apostles, and when they had prayed, they laid a hand on them.
And the word of Elohim was growing, and the number of the disciples was increasing greatly in Urishlim, and a great people from among the Yehudaye were obedient to the faith.
And Estepanos was full of grace and power, and he was doing signs and wonders among the people.
And men rose up from the synagogue that is called of the Freedmen, and of the Quriniye and the Aleksandraye, and of those from Qiliqiya and from Asiya, and they were disputing with Estepanos.
And they were not able to stand against the wisdom and the Ruach that was speaking in him.
Then they sent men and instructed them to say, We have heard him speaking words of blasphemy against Moshe and against Elohim.
And they stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and they came and rose against him and seized him and brought him into the midst of the council.
And they set up false witnesses who said: This man does not cease to speak words against the law and against this holy place.
For we have heard him say that this Y'shua the Natsraya will destroy this place and will change the customs that Moshe delivered to you.
And all those who were sitting in the council looked at him, and they saw his face like the face of a messenger.
And the high priest asked him, Are these things so?
And he said, Men, brothers and our fathers, hear. Elohim of glory appeared to our father Avraham when he was in Beth-Nahrin, before he came to dwell in Charan,
and he said to him, Go out from your land and from among the sons of your family, and come to the land that I will show you.
And then Avraham went out from the land of the Chaldeans and came and dwelt in Charan. And from there, when his father died, Elohim moved him to this land in which you dwell today.
And he did not give him an inheritance in it, not even a footstep, and he had promised to give it to him as an inheritance to him and to his seed, when he had no son.
And Elohim spoke with him, saying to him that your seed will be a sojourner in a foreign land, and they will enslave it and treat it badly four hundred years.
And the nation to whom they will serve bondage, I will judge, says Elohim. And after these things they will go out and will serve me in this place.
And he gave him the covenant of circumcision. And then he begot Yitz'chak and circumcised him on the eighth day. And Yitz'chak begot Ya'akov, and Ya'akov begot our twelve fathers.
And those our fathers envied Yosip and sold him into Mitsrayin, and Elohim was with him,
and he delivered him from all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Mitsrayin, and he set him as head over Mitsrayin and over all his house.
And there was a famine and great distress in all Mitsrayin and in the land of Kenaan, and our fathers had nothing to be satisfied.
And when Ya'akov heard that there was grain in Mitsrayin, he sent our fathers first.
And when they went the second time, Yosip made himself known to his brothers, and the kindred of Yosip was made known to Pharaoh.
And Yosip sent and brought his father Ya'akov and all his kindred, and they were in number seventy and five souls.
And Ya'akov went down to Mitsrayin, and he died there, he and our fathers.
And he was transferred to Shekim and was laid in the tomb that Avraham bought with silver from the sons of Hamor.
And when the time arrived for that which Elohim had promised with an oath to Avraham, the people multiplied and grew strong in Mitsrayin,
until another king arose over Mitsrayin, who did not know Yosip.
And he dealt craftily with our kindred and treated our fathers badly, and ordered that their infants be cast away so they would not live.
At that time Moshe was born, and he was lovely to Elohim, and he was nursed three months in his father's house.
And when he was cast out from his mother, the daughter of Pharaoh found him and raised him for herself as a son.
And Moshe was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was ready in his words and also in his deeds.
And when he was a son of forty years, it came up on his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Yisrael.
And he saw one of the sons of his race who was being treated with violence, and he avenged him and did him justice, and killed the Egyptian who was wronging him.
And he supposed that his brothers the sons of Yisrael would understand that Elohim by his hand was giving them deliverance; and they did not understand.
And on another day he appeared to them as they were quarreling one with another, and he was urging them to be reconciled, saying, Men, you are brothers; why are you wronging one another?
But the one who was wronging his companion pushed him away from him and said to him, Who appointed you a ruler and a judge over us?
Do you seek to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?
And Moshe fled at this word and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, and two sons were born to him.
And when forty years were completed for him there, the messenger of Master YHWH appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sinai in a fire that burned in a bush.
And when Moshe saw ‹it›, he marveled at the sight; and when he drew near to see, Master YHWH said to him in a voice:
I am I am Elohim of your fathers, Elohim of Avraham and of Yitz'chak and of Ya'akov. And Moshe was trembling and did not dare to look at the sight.
And Master YHWH said to him: Loose your sandals from your feet, for the earth on which you stand is holy.
Seeing I have seen the oppression of my people who are in Mitsrayin, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to give them life. And now come, I will send you to Mitsrayin.
This Moshe whom they rejected, saying, Who set you over us as head and judge? this one Elohim sent to them as head and Life-Giver by the hand of the messenger who appeared to him in the bush.
This is he who brought them out, doing signs and wonders and mighty works in the land of Mitsrayin and in the Sea of Suf and in the wilderness forty years.
This is Moshe who said to the children of Yisrael: A prophet will Master YHWH Elohim raise up for you from your brothers, like me; to him you will listen.

This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the messenger who spoke with him and with our fathers on the mountain of Sinai, and he is the one who received living words to give ‹them› to us.
And our fathers were not willing to obey him, but forsook him, and in their hearts turned back to Mitsrayin,
when they said to Aharon: Make us gods that will go before us; because this Moshe who brought us out from the land of Mitsrayin, we do not know what has become of him.
And they made a calf for themselves in those days, and offered sacrifices to the idol, and were delighting in the work of their hands.

And Elohim turned and gave them over to serve the hosts of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: Did you for forty years in the wilderness bring me slain offerings or sacrifices, children of Yisrael?
But you carried the tabernacle of Malkum and the star of the Elohim of Rephan, the images that you made so that you would bow down to them. I will remove you far beyond Bavel.
The tabernacle of the testimony of our fathers was in the wilderness, as he who spoke with Moshe commanded to make it in the likeness that he showed him.

And this same tabernacle our fathers also brought in with Y'shua into the land that Elohim gave them as an inheritance from those peoples that he drove out from before them, and it was carried until the days of Dawid.
He found favor before Elohim and asked that he might find a tabernacle for the Elohim of Ya'akov.
But Shlemun built a house for him.
Yet the Most High does not dwell in works of ‹human› hands, as the prophet says:
Heaven is my throne, and earth the footstool under my feet. What is the house that you will build for me? says Master YHWH. Or what is the place of my rest?
Has not my hand made all these things?
O stiff of neck, and uncircumcised in their heart and in their hearing, you always stand against the Ruach haKodesh; as your fathers, so also you.
For which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute and kill, ‹even› those who foretold the coming of the Just One, whom you delivered up and killed?
And you received the law by the commandment of messengers, and you have not kept it.
And when they heard these things, they were filled with rage in their souls, and they were gnashing their teeth against him.
And he, when he was full of faith and of the Ruach haKodesh, looked into heaven and saw the glory of Elohim, and Y'shua standing at the right hand of Elohim.
And he said, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing at the right hand of Elohim.
And they cried out with a loud voice and stopped their ears, and they all rushed upon him.
And they seized him and took him outside the city and were stoning him. And those who testified against him laid their clothes at the feet of a certain young man who was called Shaul.
And they were stoning Estepanos as he prayed and said, Our Master Y'shua, receive my spirit.
And when he had knelt down he cried out with a loud voice and said, Our Master, do not establish this sin against them. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

And Shaul was consenting and taking part in his killing. And there was in that day a great persecution against the assembly that was in Urishlim, and they were all scattered through the villages of Yehuda and also in the house of the Shomraye, except the apostles alone.
And believing men gathered up and buried Estephanos, and they mourned over him greatly.
And Shaul was persecuting the assembly of Elohim, entering houses and dragging out men and women and handing them over to prison.
And those who were scattered were going about and proclaiming the word of Elohim.
And Philipos went down to a city of the Shomraye and was proclaiming to them about the Mashiyach.
And when the people who were there were hearing his word, they were listening to him and being persuaded by everything he was saying, because they were seeing the signs he was doing.
For many who were held by unclean spirits were crying out with a loud voice and coming out of them, and others who were paralyzed and lame were healed.
And there was great joy in that city.

Now there was a certain man there whose name was Shimon, who had lived in that city a long time and was deceiving the people of the Samaritans by his sorceries, while magnifying himself and saying, I am someone great.
And all of them, great and small, were turning to him and saying, This is the great power of Elohim.
And they were all persuaded by him, because for a long time he had astonished them with his sorceries.
But when they believed Philipos as he was proclaiming the kingdom of Elohim in the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, men and women were being immersed.
And Shimon himself also believed, and was immersed, and was adhering to Philipos. And when he saw the signs and the great powers that were happening by his hand, he was amazed and astonished.
And when the apostles in Urishlim heard that the people of the Samaritans had received the word of Elohim, they sent to them Shimon Keefa and Yochanan.
And they went down and prayed over them, that they might receive the Ruach haKodesh.
For it was not yet on any one of them; but they had only been immersed in the name of our Master Y'shua.
Then they were laying the hand on them, and they were receiving the Ruach haKodesh.
And when Shimon saw that by the laying on of the hand of the apostles the Ruach haKodesh was given, he offered them money,
saying, Give me also this authority, that on whomever I lay a hand, he will receive the Ruach haKodesh.
Shimon Keefa said to him, Your silver go with you to destruction, because you supposed that the gift of Elohim is acquired by worldly possession.
You have no part nor lot in this faith, because your heart is not right before Elohim.
But turn again from this your wickedness, and request of Elohim that perhaps the deceit of your heart may be forgiven you.
For I see that you are in bitter gall and in the bond of iniquity.
Shimon answered and said, Request you for me from Elohim, that nothing of these things you have said may come upon me.
And Shimon and Yochanan, when they had testified and taught them the word of Elohim, returned to Urishlim. And they preached in many villages of the Samaritans.
And a messenger of Master YHWH spoke with Philipos and said to him: Get up, go south on the desert road that goes down from Urishlim to Gaza.
And he got up and went. And a eunuch met him who had come from Kush, an officer of Kandak queen of the Kushites, and he was in charge of all her treasure; and he had come to worship in Urishlim.
And as he turned to go, he was sitting on his chariot and was reading in Eshaya the prophet.
And the Ruach said to Philipos: Come near and join yourself to the chariot.
And when he came near, he heard him reading in Eshaya the prophet; and he said to him: Do you understand what you are reading?
And he said, How can I understand unless someone instructs me? And he asked of Philipos that he would come up and sit with him.
Now the section of the writing that he was reading was this: Like a lamb to the slaughter he was led, and like a sheep before its shearer he was silent, and so he did not open his mouth.
In his humility he was led from imprisonment and from judgment, and who will declare his generation? For his life is taken away from the earth.
And that believer said to Philipos, I ask you about whom the prophet said this—about himself, or about some other man?
Then Philipos opened his mouth and began from this writing to proclaim to him about our Master Y'shua.
And as they were going on the way, they came to a certain place that had water in it. And the believer said, ‹Here is› water; what is the hindrance that I should be immersed?
‹And Philipos said: If you believe with all your heart, it is allowable. And he answered and said: I believe that Y'shua the Mashiyach is the Son of Elohim.›
And he commanded the chariot to stand, and they both went down to the water, and Philipos immersed that believer.
And when they came up from the water, the Ruach of Master YHWH snatched Philipos, and that believer saw him no more, but he went on his way rejoicing.
But Philipos was found at Azotus; and from there he went about and proclaimed in all the cities until he came to Qesarya.
But Shaul was still full of threat and murderous rage against the disciples of our Master.

And he asked for letters from the high priest to be given him to Darmasuq, to the assemblies, so that if he found any who were following this way, men or women, he might bind them and bring them to Urishlim.
And as he was going and began to draw near to Darmasuq, suddenly a light from heaven flashed upon him.
And he fell on the ground, and he heard a voice that said to him, Shaul, Shaul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.
He answered and said, Who are you, my Master? And our Master said, I am Y'shua the Natsraya, whom you are persecuting.
But get up, go into the city, and there it will be told you what you ought to do.
And the men who were going with him on the road were standing amazed, because they were hearing only the voice, but no one was visible to them.
And Sha'ul rose from the ground, and nothing was visible to him though his eyes were open. And taking hold of his hands, they led him into Darmasuq.
And he had no sight for three days, and he neither ate nor drank.
Now there was in Darmasuq a certain disciple whose name was Chananya. And Master YHWH said to him in a vision, Chananya. And he said, Look, I ‹am here›, my Master.
And our Master said to him, Rise, go to the street that is called Straight, and seek in the house of Yehuda for Sha'ul who is from the city of Tarsus, for look, he is praying,
he saw in a vision a man whose name is Chananya, who came in and laid a hand on him so that his eyes might be opened.
And Chananya said, my Master, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has inflicted on your holy ones in Urishlim.
And here also he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on your name.
And Master YHWH said to him, Get up, go, for he is a chosen vessel for me to carry my name among the peoples and among kings and among the house of the sons of Yisrael.
For I will show him how much he is going to suffer because of my name.

Then Chananya went to the house to him and laid a hand on him and said to him, Shaul my brother, our Master Y'shua who appeared to you on the road as you were coming has sent me so that your eyes may be opened and you may be filled with the Ruach haKodesh.
And at once something like scales fell from his eyes and his eyes were opened, and he got up and was immersed.
And he took food and was strengthened. And he was ‹some› days with those disciples who were in Darmasuq.
And at once he was proclaiming in the synagogues of the Yehudaye about Y'shua, that he is the Son of Elohim.

And all who were hearing him were amazed, and they were saying, Is this not he who was persecuting all who call on this name in Urishlim? And even here for this he was sent, that he might bind and bring them to the chief priests.
But Shaul was strengthened all the more, and he was confounding those Yehudaye who were dwelling in Darmasuq, while he was showing that this is the Mashiyach.
And when many days had passed for him there, the Yehudaye made a plot against him to kill him.
But the plot they were seeking to carry out against him was made known to Shaul, and they were watching the gates of the city day and night to kill him.
Then the disciples put him in a basket and let him down from the wall by night.
And he went to Urishlim and wanted to join himself to the disciples, but they were all afraid of him and did not believe that he was a disciple.

But Bar-Naba took him and brought him to the shlicha and related to them how Master YHWH appeared to him on the road and how he spoke with him, and how in Darmasuq he spoke openly in the name of Y'shua.
And he went in and out with them in Urishlim.
And he spoke openly in the name of Y'shua and disputed with the Yehudaye who knew Greek. But they wanted to kill him.
And when the brothers knew ‹it›, they brought him by night to Qesarya, and from there they sent him to Tarsos.

But the assembly in all Yehuda and in Galila and in Shamrin had peace in it while it was being built up, and it was walking in the fear of Elohim, and by the comfort of the Ruach haKodesh it was greatly increasing.
And it was that while Shimon was going around the cities, he came down also to the holy ones who were dwelling in Lud the city.
And he found a certain man whose name was Anis, who was lying on a bed and had been paralyzed eight years.
And Shimon said to him, Anis, Y'shua the Mashiyach heals you; rise and make your bed. And at once he rose.
And all who were dwelling in Lud and in Saron saw him, and they turned to Elohim.
And there was a certain female disciple in Yopa the city whose name was Tavitha; ‹and› she was rich in good works and in the alms that she was doing.
And she fell sick in those days and died, and they washed her and laid her in an upper room.
And the disciples had heard that Shimon was in the city of Lud, that city which is beside Yopa, and they sent two men to him to request of him that he not delay to come to them.

And Shimon rose and went with them, and when he came they brought him up to the upper room, and all the widows stood around him weeping and showing him the tunics and cloaks that Tabitha had given them while she was alive.
But Shimon put all the people outside and knelt on his knees and prayed, and he turned toward the body and said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes, and when she saw Shimon she sat up.
And he stretched out his hand to her and raised her up, and he called the holy ones and the widows and presented her to them alive.
And this became known throughout all the city, and many believed in our Master.
Now he was in Yoppa not a few days, while he stayed in the house of Shimon the tanner.
Now in Qesarya there was a certain man, a centurion whose name was Qorneliyos, from the cohort that is called Italiqa.
And he was righteous and feared Elohim, he and all his house, ‹and› he did many alms among the people, and at all times he was seeking from Elohim.
This man saw a messenger of Elohim in a vision openly about the ninth hour of the day, who came in to him and said to him, Qorneliya!
And he looked at him and was afraid, and said, What, my master? And the messenger said to him, Your prayer and your alms have gone up for a memorial before Elohim.
And now send men to the city of Yopa and bring Shimon who is called Keefa.
He is lodging in the house of Shimon the tanner, who is by the side of the sea.
And when the messenger who spoke with him went away, he called two from the sons of his house and one soldier who feared Elohim, the one who was obedient to him.
And he related to them everything he had seen, and sent them to Yopa.
And the next day, while they were traveling on the road and drawing near the city, Shimon went up to the roof to pray at the sixth hour.
And he grew hungry and wanted to eat. And while they were preparing for him, a trance fell on him.
And he saw heaven opened and a certain vessel bound at the four corners, and it was like a great sheet, and it was let down from heaven onto the earth.
And in it were all the four-footed animals and creeping things of the earth and birds of heaven.
And a voice came to him that said, Shimon, get up, kill and eat.
And Shimon said, Far be it, my Master, for I have never eaten anything unclean and defiled.
And again a second time a voice came to him: What Elohim has cleansed, do not make unclean.
And this happened three times, and the vessel was taken up to heaven.

And while Shimon was wondering in himself what the vision he had seen was, those men who had been sent from Qorneliyos arrived, and they asked about the house where Shimon was lodging, and they came and stood at the gate of the courtyard.
And they were calling out there and asking if Shimon who is called Keefa is lodging here.
And while Shimon was reflecting on the vision, the Ruach said to him: Three men are seeking you.
Get up, go down, and go with them, and do not let your mind be divided, because I am the one who sent them.
Then Shimon went down to those men and said to them: I am the one you are seeking. What is the cause for which you have come?

They say to him: A certain man whose name is Qorneliyos, a centurion, righteous, who fears Elohim, and of whom all the people of the Yehudaye bear witness, was told in a vision by a holy messenger to send and bring you into his house and hear the word from you.
And Shimon brought them in and received them where he was lodging. And he rose the next day and went out and went with them, and some men from the brothers of Yopa went with him.
And on another day he entered Qesariya. Now Qorneliyos was waiting for them, while all the sons of his family and also the dear friends he had were gathered to him.
And when Shimon entered, Qorneliyos met him and fell down and worshipped at his feet.
And Shimon raised him up and said to him, Get up; I also am a man.
And as he talked with him, he went in and found many who had come there.
