And he said to them, You know that it is not allowed for a Yehudi man to associate with a foreign person who is not of his race; but Elohim has shown me that I should not say of any person that he is unclean or defiled.
Because of this I came readily when you sent for me. But I ask you, for what reason did you send for me?
Qorneliyos said to him, It is four days until now that I was fasting, and at the ninth hour while I was praying in my house a certain man stood before me clothed in white.
and said to me: Qorneliyos, your prayer is heard, and your alms have become a remembrance before Elohim.
But send to the city of Yopa and bring Shimon who is called Keefa. He is lodging in the house of Shimon the tanner, which is by the side of the sea. And he will come and speak with you.
And at once I sent to you, and you have done well that you came. And we are all here before you, and we desire to hear all that is commanded to you from Elohim.
Then Shimon opened his mouth and said: In truth I grasp that Elohim is not a taker of faces.
but in all the nations, whoever fears him and works righteousness is accepted with him.
For ‹this is› the word which he sent to the sons of Yisrael, announcing to them peace and rest by Y'shua the Mashiyach. He is Master YHWH of all.
And you also know the word that was in all Yehuda, that began from Galila after the immersion that Yochanan preached,

concerning Y'shua who was from Natsrath, whom Elohim anointed with the Ruach haKodesh and with power. And he is the one who went about and healed those who were oppressed by the evil one, because Elohim was with him.
And we ‹are› his witnesses of all that he did in all the land of Yehuda and of Urishlim. Him the Yehudaye hanged on a tree and killed him.
And him Elohim raised up on the third day, and gave him to be seen openly with the eye;
not to all the people, but to us who were chosen from Elohim to be witnesses for him, ‹and› who ate and drank with him after his rising from among the dead.
And he commanded us to preach and testify to the people that this is he who was appointed by Elohim as judge of the living and of the dead.
And of him all the prophets testify, that everyone who believes in his name will receive forgiveness of sins.
And while Shimon was speaking these words, the Ruach haKodesh fell upon all who were hearing the word.
And the circumcised brothers who came with him were amazed and astonished that the gift of the Ruach haKodesh was poured out even on the peoples.
For they were hearing them speaking in tongues, tongue by tongue, and magnifying Elohim. And Shimon said,
Can anyone withhold water, that these should not be immersed who have received the Ruach haKodesh just as we have?
Then he commanded them to be immersed in the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach. And they asked him to stay with them ‹some› days.
And it was reported to the apostles and the brothers in Yehuda that the peoples also had received the word of Elohim.
And when Shimon went up to Urishlim, those who were of the circumcision were contending with him,
saying that he had gone in to uncircumcised men and had eaten with them.
And Shimon began to speak to them step by step:

While I was praying in Yopa, I saw in a vision that a certain vessel came down, one that was like a linen cloth, and it was tied at its four corners, and it was let down from heaven and came as far as me.
And I looked into it and saw that there were in it four-footed animals and creeping things of the earth and also birds of heaven.
And I heard a voice that was saying to me, Shimon, get up, kill and eat.
And I said, Far be it, my Master, for never has anything polluted or unclean entered my mouth.
And again a voice said to me from heaven, What Elohim has cleansed, you do not make unclean.
This happened three times, and everything was taken up to heaven.
And at that very hour three men who were sent to me from Qorneliyos from Qesariya came and stood at the gate of the courtyard where I was lodging.
And the Ruach said to me, Go with them without hesitation. And these six brothers also came with me, and we entered the man's house.
And he related to us how he saw a messenger in his house, who stood and said to him, Send to the city of Yopa and bring Shimon who is called Keefa.
And he will speak with you words by which you will live, you and all your house.
And when I had begun there to speak, the Ruach haKodesh overshadowed them, as it did us from the beginning.
And I remembered the word of our Master, who said, Yochanan immersed with water, but you will be immersed with the Ruach haKodesh.
If then Elohim equally gave the gift to the peoples who believed in our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, as also to us, who was I that I could forbid Elohim?
And when they heard these words, they were silent, and they glorified Elohim and were saying, Now Elohim has also given to the peoples repentance to life.

Now those who were scattered by the oppression that happened over Stephen reached as far as Phoenicia and also to the land of Cyprus and to Antiokia, speaking the word with no one except only with Yehudaye.
But there were some of them from Cyprus and from Cyrene who went up to Antiokia and were speaking with the Greeks and proclaiming about our Master Y'shua.
And the hand of Master YHWH was with them, and many believed and turned to Master YHWH.
And this was heard in the ears of the sons of the assembly that is in Urishlim, and they sent Bar-Naba to Antiokia.
And when he came there and saw the grace of Elohim, he rejoiced and was seeking from them that with all their heart they would cling to our Master.
For he was a good man and was full of the Ruach haKodesh and of faith. And a great people was added to our Master.
And he went out to Tarsos to seek for Shaul.

And when he found him, he brought him with him to Antiyokya. And a whole year they were assembling together in the assembly, and they taught a great many people. From then the disciples were first called Christians in Antiyokya.
And in those days prophets came there from Urishlim.
And one of them whose name was Agabus stood up and made known to them by the Ruach that a great famine was going to be in all the land. And this famine happened in the days of Claudius Caesar.
But the disciples, each one of them according to what he had, set aside to send for the service of the brothers who dwell in Yehuda.
And they sent by the hand of Bar-Naba and Shaul to the elders there.
And in that time Herodes the king, who was surnamed Agrippa, laid hands on some who were in the church, to harm them.
And he killed Ya'akov the brother of Yochanan with the sword.
And when he saw that this pleased the Yehudaye, he went on also to seize Shimon Keefa. And the days of unleavened bread were.
And he seized him and cast him into prison, and delivered him to sixteen soldiers to guard him, so that after the Passover he might deliver him up to the people of the Yehudaye.
And while Shimon was being kept in the prison, continual prayer was offered by the church for him to Elohim.

And on that night before the morning when he was ready to be delivered up, while Shimon was sleeping between two soldiers and was bound with two chains, and others were guarding the doors of the prison,
A messenger of Master YHWH stood over him, and a light shone in all the house; and he struck him on his side and raised him up, and said to him: Get up quickly. And the chains fell from his hands.
And the messenger said to him: Bind your loins and put on your sandals. And he did so. And again he said to him: Wrap yourself in your cloak and come after me.
And he went out and was going after him, not knowing that what was happening by the messenger was real; for he supposed that he was seeing a vision.

And when they passed the first guard and the second, they came as far as the iron gate, and it opened for them of its own accord. And when they went out and passed one street, the messenger departed from him.

Then Shimon recognized ‹where he was›; and he said: Now I know in truth that Master YHWH has sent his messenger and delivered me from the hand of Herodes the king, and from what the Yehudaye were devising against me.
And when he had considered, he came to the house of Maryam the mother of Yochanan who was surnamed Marqos, because many brothers were gathered there and praying.
And he knocked at the gate of the court, and a maid whose name was Rhoda went out to answer him.
And she recognized the voice of Shimon, and in her joy she did not open the gate for him, but ran back and said to them, Shimon is standing at the gate of the court.
They said to her, You are out of your mind. But she kept insisting that it was so. They said to her, Perhaps it is his messenger.
And Shimon kept knocking at the gate, and they went out, saw him, and were astonished.

And he motioned to them with his hand to be quiet, and he went in and related to them how Master YHWH had brought him out from the prison house. And he said to them, Tell these things to Ya'akov and to the brothers. And he went out and departed to another place.
And when it was morning, there was a great disturbance among the soldiers about Shimon, what had become of him.
Now Herodes, when he sought him and did not find him, examined the guards and ordered that they should die. And he went out from Yehuda and was in Qesarya.

And because he was angry with the Tsuraya and with the Tsidonaya, they gathered and came to him together, and they persuaded Blastus the chamberlain of the king, and asked from him that there would be peace for them, because the provision of their country was from the kingdom of Herodes.
Now on a set day Herodes put on the clothing of the kingdom and sat on the bema and was speaking with the crowd.
But all the people were crying out and saying, These are the voice of Elohim, and not of the sons of men.
And because he did not give glory to Elohim, in that hour the messenger of Master YHWH struck him, and he was eaten by worms and died.
And the good news of Elohim was being proclaimed and was growing.
But Bar-Naba and Sha'ul returned from Urishlim to Antioki after they completed their service, and they took with them Yochanan who was surnamed Marqos.

Now there were in the church at Antiokia prophets and teachers: Bar-Naba, and Shimon who is called Niger, and Luqius who was from the city Qurina, and Manael, a son of the foster-brothers of Herodes the tetrarch, and Shaul.
And while they were fasting and making supplication to Elohim, Ruach haKodesh said to them: Separate to me Shaul and Bar-Naba for the work to which I have called them.
And after they had fasted and prayed, they laid the hand on them and sent them away.
And they, being sent forth by Ruach haKodesh, went down to Seluqia, and from there they went by sea as far as Qupros.
And when they entered the city of Salmina, they were announcing the word of our Master in the synagogues of the Yehudaye. And Yochanan was ministering to them.
And when they had gone around the whole island as far as the city Paphos, they found a certain man, a sorcerer, a Yehudi who was a false prophet, and whose name was Bar-Shuma.
This one was attached to a wise man who was the proconsul and was called Sergius Paulos. And the proconsul called for Shaul and Bar-Naba and sought to hear from them the word of Elohim.
But this sorcerer Bar-Shuma, whose name is translated Elymas, stood against them, because he wanted to turn the proconsul aside from the faith.
But Shaul, he who was called Paulos, was filled with the Ruach haKodesh and looked at him
and said, O full of all deceit and all evil, son of the slanderer and enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease to pervert the straight ways of Master YHWH?

And now the hand of Master YHWH is upon you, and you will be blind and will not see the sun for a time. And at that moment a mist and darkness fell on him, and he went about seeking who would take him by the hand.
And when the proconsul saw what had happened, he was amazed and believed in the teaching of Master YHWH.
But Paulos and Bar-Naba went by sea from the city of Paphos and came to Perga, a city of Pamphylia. And Yochanan separated from them and went away to Urishlim.
But they went out from Perga and came to Antiokia, a city of Pisidia, and entered the synagogue and sat down on the day of the Sabbath.
And after the law and the prophets were read, the elders of the synagogue sent to them and said, Men, brothers, if you have a word of encouragement, speak with the people.
And Paulos stood up and waved his hand and said, Men, sons of Yisrael, and those who fear Elohim, hear.
The Elohim of this people chose our fathers and raised them up and made them great when they were sojourners in the land of Mitsrayin, and with a high arm he brought them out of it.
And he fed them in the wilderness forty years.
And he destroyed seven nations in the land of Kenaan, and gave them their land for an inheritance.
And four hundred and fifty years he gave them judges, until Shmuel the prophet.
And then they asked for themselves a king, and Elohim gave them Shaul son of Qish, a man from the tribe of Benyamin, for forty years.
And he took him away and raised up for them Dawid as king, and he testified about him and said, I have found Dawid son of Aishi, a man like my heart; he will do all my will.
From the seed of this one Elohim raised up for Yisrael, as he promised, Y'shua the Life-Giver.
And he sent Yochanan to proclaim before his coming the immersion of repentance to all the people of Yisrael.
And while Yochanan was completing his ministry, he said: Who do you suppose that I am? I am not he. But he comes after me, the one whose sandal straps I am not worthy to loosen.
Men, brothers, sons of the family of Avraham, and those who fear Elohim with you, to you the word of life has been sent.

For these inhabitants of Urishlim and their leaders did not understand him, nor the writings of the prophets that are read every sabbath; but they condemned him and fulfilled these things that are written.
And when they found no cause of death, they asked of Pilatos that they might kill him.
And when they had completed everything that was written concerning him, they took him down from the cross and laid him in a tomb.
But Elohim raised him from the house of the dead.
And he was seen many days by those who came up with him from Galila to Urishlim, and they are now his witnesses to the people.
And we also announce to you that the promise which was made to our fathers,
Elohim has fulfilled it to us their children, in that he raised up Y'shua; as it is written in the second psalm: You are my Son; this day I have begotten you.
And thus Elohim raised him from the house of the dead, that he will not return again and see corruption; as he said: I will give to you the sure grace of Dawid.
And again he said in another place: You have not given your devout one to see corruption.
For Dawid, in his generation, served the will of Elohim, and went to rest, and was added to his fathers, and saw corruption.
But this one, whom Elohim raised up, did not see corruption.
Know therefore, my brothers, that through this one forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you.
And from all that you were not able to be justified by the law of Moshe, in this one everyone who believes is justified.
Take heed therefore, lest there come upon you something that is written in the prophets:
See, you despisers, and wonder, and perish; for I do a work in your days, which you will not believe even if a man tells it to you.
And when they were going out from their presence, they begged them that on the next shabbat they would speak these words with them.
And when the synagogue was dismissed, many Yehudaye went after them, and also converts who feared Elohim. And they were speaking and persuading them to remain attached to the grace of Elohim.
And on the next Sabbath the whole city assembled to hear the word of Elohim.
And when the Yehudaye saw the great assembly, they were filled with envy, and were standing against the words that Paulos was saying, and were blaspheming.

But Paulos and Bar-Naba said openly: To you first it was that the word of Elohim should be spoken; but because you reject it from yourselves, and have decided against yourselves that you are not worthy of life forever, look, we turn to the peoples.
For so our Master commanded us, as it is written: I have set you a light to the peoples, that you should be for life to the ends of the earth.
And when the peoples heard ‹this›, they rejoiced and glorified Elohim. And those believed who were appointed to life forever.
And the word of Master YHWH was spoken in all that region.
But the Yehudaye stirred up the chiefs of the city and the rich women who feared Elohim with them, and raised a persecution against Paulos and against Bar-Naba, and expelled them from their borders.
And when they went out, they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came to the city of Iconium.
And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Ruach haKodesh.
And they came and entered the synagogue of the Yehudaye, and so spoke with them that many of the Yehudaye and of the Greeks believed.
But the Yehudaye who were not persuaded stirred up the peoples to treat the brothers badly.
And they stayed there a long time and spoke openly about Master YHWH, and he was testifying to the word of his grace by the signs and wonders that he was doing by their hands.
And the whole assembly of the city was divided; some of them were with the Yehudaye, and some of them were adhering to the apostles.
And an assault came against them from the peoples and from the Yehudaye and their chiefs, to insult them and to stone them with stones.
And when they knew ‹it›, they withdrew and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, to Lystra and Derbe, and the villages around them.
And a certain man was sitting in the city Lystra, who was crippled in his feet, lame from his mother's womb, who had never walked.
This one heard Paulos speaking. And when Paulos saw him and recognized that there was in him faith to live,
he said to him with a loud voice: I say to you, in the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, stand on your feet. And he leaped up, stood, and walked.

And the crowd of the people, when they saw what Paulos had done, raised their voice in the language of the place and said: The gods have taken on the likeness of the sons of men and have come down to us.
And they were naming Bar-Naba the lord of the gods, and Paulos Hermes, because he was the one who began in the word.
And the priest of the master Elohim, who was outside the city, brought oxen and garlands to the gate of the courtyard where they were lodging, and he wanted to offer sacrifice to them.
But Bar-Naba and Paulos, when they heard ‹it›, tore their clothes and sprang up and went out to the crowd, and were crying out

and saying, Men, what are you doing? We also are men, suffering like you, who preach to you that you should turn from these useless things to the living Elohim, who made the heavens and the earth and the seas and all that is in them.
He who in former generations left all the nations to go in the ways of their own soul.

though he did not leave himself without witness, while he did them good from heaven and sent down rain to them and made the fruits grow in their seasons and filled their hearts with food and gladness.
And while they were saying these things, they barely restrained the people from offering sacrifice to them.
But Yehudaye came there from Iqnon and from Antiokiya and stirred up the people against them. And they stoned Paulos and dragged him outside the city, because they supposed that he was dead.
And the disciples gathered around him, and he rose up and entered the city. And the next day he went out from there with Bar-Naba, and they came to the city of Darba.
And while they were proclaiming to the people of that city, they made many disciples. And they turned back and came to the city of Lustra and to Iqnon and to Antiokiya,

while they were strengthening the souls of the disciples and asking them to continue in the faith, and they were saying to them that through many afflictions it is necessary to enter the kingdom of Elohim.
And they appointed for them elders in every assembly, while they were fasting with them and praying, and they committed them to our Master in whom they had believed.
And when they had gone around in the region of Pisidiya, they came to Pampuliya.
And when they spoke the word of Master YHWH in the city of Perga, they went down to Attalia.
And from there they went by sea and came to Antiokia, because from there they had been commended to the grace of Master YHWH for that work which they had completed.
And when they gathered the whole church, they were narrating everything that Elohim had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.
And they remained there a long time with the disciples.
And some men came down from Yehuda and were teaching the brothers that if you are not circumcised in the custom of the law, you cannot have life.

And there was much agitation and dispute for Paulos and Bar-Naba with them. And it came about that Paulos and Bar-Naba and others with them should go up to the apostles and elders who were in Urishlim because of this dispute.

And the church escorted them and sent them off, and they were traveling through all Phoenicia and also among the Samaritans, narrating the conversion of the peoples and causing great joy to all the brothers.
And when they came to Urishlim, they were received by the church and by the apostles and by the elders, and they related to them all that Elohim had done with them.
But some men rose up who had believed from the teaching of the Pharisees and said, It is necessary for you to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moshe.
And the apostles and the elders assembled to look into this matter.

And when there was much discussion, Shimon stood and said to them: Men, brothers, you know that from the earlier days Elohim chose that from my mouth the peoples should hear the word of the good news and believe.
And Elohim, who knows what is in the hearts, testified about them and gave them the Ruach haKodesh just as to us.
And he made no distinction between us and them, because he purified their hearts by faith.
And now, why are you testing Elohim by putting a yoke on the necks of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
But by the grace of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach we believe that we will have life just as they.
And the whole assembly was silent and listened to Paulos and to Bar-Naba, who were relating all that Elohim had done by their hands, signs and mighty works among the peoples.
And after they were silent, Ya'akov stood up and said: Men, brothers, listen to me.
Shimon has related to you how Elohim began to choose from the nations a people for his name.
And with this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written:
After these things I will return and set up the tabernacle of Dawid that has fallen, and I will build what has fallen from it, and I will raise it up,
so that the rest of the sons of men may seek Master YHWH, and all the nations on whom my name is called, says Master YHWH who does all these things.
Known from of old are the works of Elohim.
Because of this I say that they should not be troubling those who from the peoples turn to Elohim.
But let word be sent to them that they keep themselves free from the defilement of sacrifice ‹to idols›, and from sexual immorality, and from what is strangled, and from blood.
For Moshe from the first generations has had heralds in every city in the synagogue, who read him every sabbath.

Then the apostles and elders, with all the assembly, chose men from among them and sent them to Antiokia with Paulos and Bar-Naba: Yehuda who is called Bar-Shaba, and Shila, men who were leaders among the brothers.
And they wrote a letter by their hands thus: The apostles and elders and brothers to those who are in Antiokia and in Syria and in Cilicia, brothers who are from the peoples, peace.
It has been heard by us that some from us went out and troubled you with words and overturned your souls, saying that you must be circumcised and keep the law—things which we did not command them.
Because of this we all thought fit, when we were assembled, and chose men and sent them to you with Paulos and Bar-Naba our beloved ones,
men who have handed over their lives for the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
And we have sent with them Yehuda and Shila, that they by the word may tell you these same things.
For it was the will of the Ruach haKodesh, and also of us, that no greater burden should be laid on you besides these necessary things:

that you keep away from what is sacrificed ‹to idols›, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from fornication. When you keep your souls from these, you will do well. Be steadfast in our Master.
Then those who were sent came to Antiokia and gathered all the people and delivered the letter.
And when they read ‹it›, they rejoiced and were comforted.
And with abundant word they strengthened the brothers, and Yehuda and Shila established them, because they also were prophets.
And when they had been there a time, the brothers dismissed them in peace to the apostles.
‹But it was the pleasure of Shila to remain there.›
Paulos and Bar-Naba remained in Antiokia, and they were teaching and proclaiming, with many others, the word of Elohim.
And after days, Paulos said to Bar-Naba: Let us return and visit the brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of Elohim, and see what they are doing.
But Bar-Naba wanted to take Yochanan, the one who was surnamed Marqos.
But Paulos was not willing to take him with them, because he had left them when they were in Pamphylia and did not go with them.
Because of this contention they separated one from the other, and Bar-Naba took Marqos and they sailed by sea and went to Qupros.
But Paulos chose Shila for himself and went out, being commended by the brothers to the grace of Elohim.
And he was traveling through Syria and through Qiliqiya and strengthening the assemblies.
And he arrived at the city Derbe and at Lustra. And there was there a certain disciple whose name was Timotheos, the son of a believing Yehudita, and his father was an Aramean.
And all the disciples from Lustra and from Iqnon were testifying about him.
This one Paulos wanted to take with him, and he took and circumcised him because of the Yehudaye who were in the region, for they all knew that his father was an Aramean.
And as they were going through the cities, they were proclaiming and teaching them that they should be keeping the commandments which the emissaries and elders who were in Urishlim wrote.
But the assemblies were being established in the faith and were increasing in number every day.
Now they walked through the regions of Phrygia and of Galatia, and the Ruach haKodesh forbade them to speak the word of Elohim in Asia.
And when they came to the region of Mysia, they wanted to go from there to Bithynia, and the Ruach of Y'shua did not permit them.
And when they went out from Mysia, they went down to the region of Troas.
And in a vision of the night there appeared to Paulos a certain Macedonian man who stood and begged from him, saying: Come to Macedonia and help me.
But when Paulos saw this vision, at once we wanted to go out to Macedonia, because we understood that our Master had called us to announce good news to them.
And we sailed from Troas and went straight to Samothrace, and from there on the next day we came to the city Neapolis.
And from there to Philippi, which is the head ‹city› of Macedonia, and it is a colony. And we were in this city certain days.

And on the Sabbath day we went outside the gate of the city by the side of a river, because a house of prayer was seen there. And when we sat down, we were speaking with the women who were assembled there.

And a certain woman, a seller of purple, who was fearing Elohim, whose name was Lydia, from the city of Thyatira, ‹was there›. Our Master opened her heart, and she was listening to what Paulos was saying.

And she was immersed, she and the people of her house. And she was requesting of us and saying, If you are truly confident that I have believed in our Master, come stay in my house. And she urged us much.

And it happened that as we were going to the house of prayer, a certain young girl met us who had a spirit of divination, and she was making much profit for her masters by the divination she was performing.
And she was coming after Paulos and after us, and she was crying out and saying, These men are the servants of Elohim the Most High, and they are announcing to you the way of life.
And she was doing this many days. And Paulos was indignant, and he said to that spirit, I command you in the name of Y'shua the Mashiyach to come out of her. And it came out in that hour.
And when her masters saw that the hope of their trade had gone out from her, they seized Paulos and Shila, and dragged them and brought them to the marketplace.
And they brought them near to the prefects and to the chiefs of the city, and were saying: These men are troubling our city, because they are Yehudaye,
and they proclaim to us customs which it is not permitted for us to receive and to do, because we are Romans.
And a great crowd gathered against them. Then the prefects tore their clothes and commanded that they scourge them.
And when they had scourged them much, they threw them into the prison, and commanded the keeper of the prison to keep them carefully.
But he, when he received this command, brought them in and confined them in the inner part of the prison, and bound their feet in the stocks.
And in the middle of the night Paulos and Shila were praying and glorifying Elohim, and the prisoners were hearing them.
And suddenly there was a great shaking, and the foundations of the prison house were moved; and at once all the doors were opened, and the bonds of all of them were loosed.
And when the keeper of the prison house awoke and saw that the doors of the prison house were open, he took a sword and sought to kill himself, because he supposed the prisoners had fled.
And Paulos called to him with a loud voice and said to him, Do nothing bad to yourself, because we are all here.
And he lit a lamp for himself and sprang and came in trembling, and fell at the feet of Paulos and of Shila.
And he brought them outside and was saying to them, My masters, what must I do so that I may live?
And they were saying to him, Believe in our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, and you will live, you and your house.
And they spoke the word of Master YHWH with him, and with all the sons of his house.
And in that same hour of the night he took and washed them from their stripes, and at once he was immersed, he and all the sons of his house.
And he took and brought them up into his house, and set a table for them; and he rejoiced, he and the sons of his house, in the faith of Elohim.
And when it was morning, the prefects sent the rod-bearers to say to the chief of the prison: Release those men.
And when the chief of the prison house heard ‹it›, he went in and said this same word to Paulos, that the prefects have sent ‹word› that you be released. And now go out, go in peace.

Paulos said to him: They have scourged us, men who did no wrong, Romans, before the eyes of the whole world, and have thrown us into prison; and now are they secretly putting us out? No indeed: but let them come themselves and bring us out.
And the rod-bearers went and told the prefects these words that were said to them; and when they heard that they are Romans, they were afraid,
and came to them and begged them to go out and leave the city.
And when they went out from the prison, they entered the house of Lydia; and there they saw the brothers and comforted them, and departed.
And they passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia the city and came to Tesaloniqa, where there was a synagogue of the Yehudaye.
And Paulos went in to them as he was accustomed, and for three shabbats he spoke with them from the writings;
while he was explaining and showing that the Mashiyach was destined to suffer and to rise from the house of the dead, and that this is Y'shua the Mashiyach whom I announce to you.
And some of them believed and joined Paulos and Shila, and many of the Yawnaye who feared Elohim, and also known women, not a few.

And the Yehudaye were jealous and gathered to themselves evil men from the marketplace of the city and made a great mob, and they troubled the city and came and stood against the house of Jason and were seeking to bring them out from there and deliver them to the mob.

And when they did not find them there, they dragged Jason and the brothers who were there and brought them to the chiefs of the city, crying out: These are they who have troubled all the earth, and they have come here also.
And this Jason is their host, and all these stand against the commands of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Y'shua.
And the chiefs of the city and all the people were troubled when they heard these things.
And they took sureties from Jason and also from the brothers, and then they released them.
But the brothers at once in that night sent Paulos and Shila to the city of Berua, and when they came there they were entering the synagogue of the Yehudaye.

For those Yehudaye there were more noble than those Yehudaye who were in Tesaloniga, and they were hearing the word from them every day gladly, while they were examining from the writings whether these things were so.
And many of them believed, and so also of the Yawnaye many men and notable women.
And when those Yehudaye from Tesaloníqa knew that the word of Elohim was proclaimed by Paulos in the city of Beroya, they came also there and did not cease to stir up and to trouble the people.
And the brothers sent Paulos away, that he might go down to the sea. And Shila and Timotheos stayed in that city.

And those who accompanied Paulos came with him as far as the city of Athens. And when they went out from beside him, they received a letter from him to Shila and Timotheos, that they should come to him quickly.
But Paulos, while he was waiting ‹for them› in Athens, was provoked in his spirit when he saw that the whole city was full of idols.
And he was speaking in the synagogue with the Yehudaye and with those who fear Elohim, and in the marketplace with those who were assembling every day.

And also philosophers from the teaching of Epicurus and others who are called Stoics were disputing with him. And some of them were saying, What does this word-collector want? And others were saying, He proclaims foreign gods, because he was proclaiming Y'shua and his resurrection to them.
And they took him and brought him to the house of judgment that is called Arios Pagos, saying to him: We can know what this new teaching is that you proclaim.
For you sow foreign words in our hearing, and we want to know what these are.
But all the Athenians and the foreigners who come there care for nothing else but to say and to hear something new.
And when Paulos stood in Arios Pagos he said: Men, Athenians, I see that in all things you are excessive in the fear of demons.

For as I was going around and viewing the houses of your fear, I found one altar on which was written, To the hidden Elohim. Him therefore whom you fear while you do not know him, this one I announce to you.
For Elohim who made the world and all that is in it, and who is master of heaven and of earth, does not dwell in a temple made by hands.
And he is not served by human hands, and he needs nothing, because he gives life and breath to everyone.
And from one blood he made the whole world of humans, that they might dwell on the face of all the earth; and he marked off the times by his command and set the bounds of the dwelling of humans,
that they might seek Elohim and search, and from his creation find him, because he is not far from each one of us;
for in him we live and move and exist, as also some of the wise men among you have said: From him is our lineage.
People, then, whose lineage is from Elohim, we ought not to suppose that the divinity is like gold or silver or stone carved by the craft and knowledge of a human.
For the times of error Elohim has made to pass, and in this time he commands all humans that every person in every place should repent.

Because he has appointed a day in which he is about to judge all the earth in righteousness by the man whom he has designated, and he has turned every person to faith in him by raising him from the house of the dead.
And when they heard the resurrection from the house of the dead, some of them were mocking, and some of them were saying, At another time we will hear you about this.
And so Paulos went out from among them.
And some persons from them joined him and believed; one of them was Dionysius from the judges of Areopagus, and a woman whose name was Damaris, and others with them.
And when Paulos went out from Athens, he came to Corinth.

And he found there a certain Yehudi man whose name was Aqilos, who was from the region of Pontus. At that time he had come from the country of Italy, he and Prisqila his wife, because Claudius Caesar had commanded that all the Yehudaye should go out from Rome. And he drew near to them.
And because he was of their craft, he stayed with them and worked with them; for by their craft they were tentmakers.
And he was speaking in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuading the Yehudaye and the pagans.

And when Shila and Timotheos had come from Macedonia, Paulos was pressed in the word, because the Yehudaye were standing against him and blaspheming as he was testifying to them that Y'shua is the Mashiyach.
And he shook out his garments and said to them: From now on I am clean; I am going to the peoples.
And he went out from there and entered the house of a man whose name was Titus, one who feared Elohim, and his house was adjoining the synagogue.
And Krispos, the head of the synagogue, believed in our Master, he and all the children of his house. And many Qorinthians were hearing and believing in Elohim and immersing.
And Master YHWH said in a vision to Paulos: Do not fear, but speak and do not be silent.
because I am with you, and no one is able to harm you; and I have much people in this city.
And he was residing one year and six months in Qorinthos, and he was teaching them the word of Elohim.
And when Galion was proconsul of Akaya, the Yehudaye assembled together against Paulos and brought him before the judgment-seat.
saying, This man persuades the people to fear Elohim contrary to the law.

And when Paulos was seeking to open his mouth and speak, Gallio said to the Yehudaye, If it were about some wrong or fraud or hateful thing that you were accusing, O Yehudaye, I would accept you suitably.
But if they are disputes about a word and about names and about your law, you know among yourselves, for I do not want to be a judge of these matters.
And he drove them from his judgment-seat.
And all the pagans seized Sosthenes the elder of the synagogue and were beating him before the judgment-seat. And Gallio was unconcerned about these things.

And when Paulos had been there many days, he gave peace to the brothers and sailed by sea to go to Syria. And with him came Prisqla and Aqulos, when he had shaved his head at Qenkreos because a vow was vowed to him.
And they reached Ephesos, and Paulos entered the synagogue and was speaking with the Yehudaye.
And they were asking him to stay longer with them, but he was not persuaded.
As he said, It is necessary for me always to keep the coming feast in Urishlim, and if Elohim wills I will return again to you. And Aqelos and Prisqila he left in Ephesos.
And he journeyed by sea and came to Qesariya, and went up and greeted the members of the assembly, and went on to Antiokiya.
And when he had been there some days, he went out and traveled from place to place in the region of Galatia and of Phrygia, establishing all the disciples.
And a certain man named Apolos, a Yehudi whose origin was from Alexandria, who was trained in speech and skilled in the scriptures, came to Ephesos.
This one had been instructed in the way of Master YHWH and was fervent in spirit, and he was speaking and teaching fully about Y'shua, while he knew nothing except the immersion of Yochanan.
And he began to speak openly in the synagogue. And when Aqulos and Prisqila heard him, they took him to their house and fully showed him the way of Master YHWH.
And when he wanted to go to Akaya, the brothers urged him and wrote to the disciples to receive him. And when he went, he greatly helped all the believers by grace.
For he was powerfully disputing against the Yehudaye before the assembly, while showing from the writings about Y'shua that he is the Mashiyach.
And while Apolos was in Corinth, Paulos traveled through the upper regions and came to Ephesos, and he was asking the disciples whom he found there,
“Have you received the Ruach haKodesh since you believed?” They answered and said to him, “We have not even heard whether there is a Ruach haKodesh.”
He said to them, “Into what then were you immersed?” They said, “Into the immersion of Yochanan.”
Paulos said to them, “Yochanan immersed with the immersion of repentance for the people, while he was saying that they should believe in the one who is coming after him, who is Y'shua the Mashiyach.”
And when they heard these things, they were immersed in the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
And Paulos laid ‹his› hand on them, and the Ruach haKodesh came upon them, and they were speaking in various tongues and prophesying.
Now they were all twelve persons.
And Paulos entered the synagogue and was speaking openly for three months, and was persuading concerning the kingdom of Elohim.

And some of them were hardening and contending and reviling the way of Elohim before the assembly of the peoples. Then Paulos withdrew and separated the disciples from them. And every day he was speaking with them in the school of a man whose name was Tyrannus.
And this continued two years, until all who dwell in ‹Proconsular› Asia, Yehudaye and Aramaye, heard the word of Master YHWH.
And Elohim was doing very great powers by the hand of Paulos,
so that even from the clothes on his body they were bringing handkerchiefs or rags and laying them on the sick, and the diseases were leaving them, and the demons also were going out.

Also some Yehudi men who went around and adjured over demons wanted to adjure in the name of our Master Y'shua over those who had unclean spirits, saying, We adjure you in the name of Y'shua whom Paulos proclaims.
And there were seven sons of one Yehudi man, a chief priest, whose name was Seqwa, who were doing this.
And that evil demon answered and said to them, Y'shua I know, and Paulos I know, but you, who are you?
And the man in whom was the evil spirit leaped on them and overpowered them and threw them down, and naked and wounded they fled from that house.
And this became known to all the Yehudaye and Arameans who lived in Ephesos, and fear fell on them all, and the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach was exalted.
And many of those who believed came and narrated their faults and confessed what they had done.
And many sorcerers also gathered their books and brought and burned them before everyone, and they calculated their value, and the silver came to fifty thousand ‹pieces›.
And so with great power the faith of Elohim was strengthened and increased.
And when these things were completed, Paulos set in his mind to go around all Macedonia and Achaia and go to Urishlim. And he said, After I have gone there, I must also see Rome.
And he sent two men from those who were ministering to him to Macedonia, Timotheos and Erastos, but he himself stayed a time in Asia.
And there was at that time a great disturbance about the way of Elohim.
And there was there a certain silversmith whose name was Demetrios, who made silver shrines for Artemis, and he was bringing great profit to the sons of his craft.
This one gathered them, all the sons of his craft, and those who labor with them, and said to them: Men, you know that our whole trade is from this work.

And you also hear and see that not only the sons of Ephesos, but also the majority of all Asia, this Paulos has persuaded and turned aside, saying that those are not Elohim which are made by the hands of the sons of men.

And not only is this matter alone slandered and brought to nothing, but also that temple of Artemis the great goddess is accounted as nothing, and she herself, the goddess whom all Asia and all the peoples worship, is despised.
And when they heard these things they were filled with wrath, and they were crying out and saying: Great is Artemis of the Ephesians.
And the whole city was stirred up, and they ran together and went into the theatre, and they seized and led with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonian men, companions of Paulos.
And Paulos was wanting to enter the theatre, but the disciples restrained him.
And also the chiefs of Asia, because they were his friends, sent and requested of him that he not give his soul to enter the theatre.
But the crowd that were in the theatre were very confused, and some were crying out one thing and others another; for many of them did not know for what they had gathered.
But the people of the Yehudaye who were there set up from among them a Yehudaya man whose name was Alexander, and when he stood he waved his hand and wished to make a defence to the people.
And when they knew that he was a Yehudaya, they all cried out with one voice for about two hours: Great is Artamis of Aphsiya.

And the chief of the city quieted them, saying: Men of Aphsiya, for who is there among men who does not know the city of Aphsiya, that it is the temple-keeper of the great Artamis, and of her image that came down from heaven?
Therefore since no one can speak against this, it is right for you to be quiet and not do anything in haste.
For you have brought these men, when they have not robbed temples and have not reviled our goddess.
But if this Demetrius and the men of his craft have a case with anyone, look, the proconsuls are in the city; they are craftsmen—let them approach and litigate one with another.
And if it is that you seek something else, it is settled in the place given by the law for the assembly.
Because even now we stand in danger of being accused as a riot, since we cannot give an account for the gathering of this day, for we have assembled needlessly and been stirred up without a cause.
And after the tumult had subsided, Paulos called the disciples and comforted them and kissed them and went out ‹and› went to Macedonia.
And when he had gone around those regions and comforted them with many words, he came to the country of Hellas.
And he was there three months. But the Yehudaye made a plot against him when he was about to go to Syria, and he decided to return to Macedonia.

And there went out with him as far as Asia Sopatrus of the city Berua, and Aristarchus and Sequndos of Thessalonike, and Gaius of the city Derbe, and Timotheos of Lystra, and of Asia Tychicus and Trophimus.
These went ahead and waited for us at Troas.
But we went out from the city of Philipos of Macedonia after the days of unleavened bread, and sailed by sea and came to Troas in five days, and were there seven days.

And on the first day of the week, when we were assembled to break the eucharist, Paulos was speaking with them, because he was ready to depart the next day, and he prolonged his speaking until the middle of the night.
And there were many lamps of fire in the upper room where we were assembled.

And a young man named Eutykos was sitting in the window and listening, and he sank into a heavy sleep while Paulos prolonged his word, and in his sleep he fell from the third story and was taken up dead.
And Paulos went down, fell on him and embraced him, and said, Do not be agitated, because his soul is in him.
And when he had gone up, he broke bread and tasted ‹it›, and was speaking until morning rose, and then he went out to go by land.
And they brought the young man alive, and rejoiced over him greatly.
But we went down to the ship and sailed to the port of Tasus, because from there we were ready to receive Paulos; for so he had commanded us when he was going by land.
And when we had received him from Tasus, we took him on the ship and came to Mitylene.
And from there on the next day we sailed opposite the island Chios, and again on the next day we came to Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and on the next day we came to Miletus.
For it was decided for Paulos to pass by Ephesos, lest he be delayed there, because he was hurrying, if it was possible, to keep the day of Pentecost in Urishlim.
And when they came to him, he said to them: You yourselves know that from the first day I entered Asia, how I was with you the whole time,
serving Elohim with much humility and with tears and with the trials that came on me by the plottings of the Yehudaye.
And I did not shrink from anything that was profitable for your souls, as I proclaimed to you and taught in the marketplace and in houses,
while I was testifying to the Yehudaye and to the Aramaye about repentance toward Elohim and faith in our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
And now I am bound in the spirit, and I am going to Urishlim, and I do not know what will meet me there,
but that the Ruach haKodesh in every city testifies to me and says that bonds and afflictions await you.
But I do not count my soul as anything, so that I may finish my course and the ministry I received from our Master Y'shua, to testify to the good news of the grace of Elohim.
And now I know that you will see my face no more, all of you among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom of Elohim.
And because of this I testify to you this day that I am clean from the blood of all of you.
For I have not held back from making known to you all the will of Elohim.
Watch therefore over yourselves and over all the flock in which the Ruach haKodesh has established you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of Elohim which he acquired with his blood.
I know that after I go, fierce wolves will enter among you who will not spare the flock.
And even from among you yourselves men will rise up speaking twisted things, so as to turn the disciples away to go after them.
Because of this stay awake and remember that for three years I did not cease night and day, with tears admonishing each one of you.
And now I commend you to Elohim and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and to give you an inheritance with all the holy ones.
Silver or gold or clothing I have not coveted.
And you yourselves know that these hands served my needs and those who were with me.

And I have shown you everything, that thus it is right to labor and to care for those who are weak, and to remember the words of our Master Y'shua, because he said that it is more blessed for the one who gives than for the one who receives.
And when he had said these things, he knelt on his knees and prayed, and all the people with him.
And there was great weeping among them all, and they embraced him and were kissing him.
And they were especially grieved over that word he said, that they would not see his face again. And they accompanied him as far as the ship.
And we separated from them and sailed straight to the island of Qo, and the next day we came to Rodos, and from there to Patara.
And we found there a ship going to Puniqia, and we went up into it and sailed on.
And we reached as far as the island of Qupros and left it on the left and came to Surya, and from there we reached Tsur, for there the ship was to unload its cargo.
And when we found disciples there, we stayed with them seven days, and these were saying every day to Paulos by the Ruach that he should not go to Urishlim.

And after these days we went out to go on the way, and they all were escorting us, they and their wives and their children, until outside the city, and they knelt on their knees by the sea and prayed.
And we kissed one another and went up into the ship, and they returned to their houses.
And we sailed from Tsur and came to the city Akko, and we gave peace to the brothers there, and stayed with them one day.
And on the next day we went out and came to Qesarya, and we entered and stayed in the house of Philippos the proclaimer, who was one of the seven.
And he had four virgin daughters who were prophesying.
And when we had been there many days, a certain prophet came down from Yehuda, whose name was Agabus.

And he came in to us, and took the belt of Paulos’s waist, and bound his own feet and hands, and said: Thus says the Ruach haKodesh, The man who owns this belt—thus will the Yehudaye bind him in Urishlim, and they will deliver him into the hands of the peoples.
And when we heard these words, we and the sons of the place begged him not to go to Urishlim.
Then Paulos answered and said: What are you doing, weeping and crushing my heart? For I am prepared not only to be bound, but also to die in Urishlim for the name of our Master Y'shua.
And when he would not be persuaded by us, we desisted, and we said: Let the will of our Master be.
And after these days we prepared and went up to Urishlim.

And some men, disciples from Caesarea, went with us, taking with them one brother from among the earlier disciples, whose name was Mnason, and he was from Cyprus, that he might receive us in his house.
And when we came to Urishlim, the brothers received us joyfully.
And the next day we went in with Paulos to Ya'akov, when all the elders were with him.
And we gave them peace, and Paulos was relating to them one after another all that Elohim had done among the peoples by his ministry.
And when they heard ‹it› they glorified Elohim. And they said to him: You see, our brother, how many myriads there are in Yehuda who have believed, and all these are zealous for the law.

But it has been told them about you that you teach all the Yehudaye who are among the peoples to depart from Moshe, when you say that they should not circumcise their sons and should not walk in the customs of the law.
Because therefore it is heard by them that you have come here,
do what we tell you. We have four men who have vowed to purify themselves.

Take them and go, purify yourself with them, and pay the expenses for them so that they may shave their heads, and it will be known to everyone that what was said against you is false, and that you fulfill and keep the law.
But as for those from the peoples who have believed, we have written that they should keep themselves from what is sacrificed, and from fornication, and from what is strangled, and from blood.

Then Paulos took those men on the next day and was purified with them, and he went in to the temple, making known to them the completion of the days of purification until the offering was presented by each one of them.
And when the seventh day arrived, the Yehudaye from Asia saw him in the temple and stirred up all the people against him, and they laid hands on him,

crying out and saying, Men, sons of Yisrael, help! This is the man who teaches against our people in every place, and against the law, and against this place; and he has even brought Armaye into the temple and has defiled this holy place.
For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they supposed that he had gone into the temple with Paulos.
And the city was stirred up, and all the people assembled, and they seized Paulos and dragged him outside the temple; and at once the gates were shut.
And while the crowd was seeking to kill him, it was reported to the chiliarch of the cohort that the whole city was stirred up.
And at once he took centurions and many soldiers, and they ran upon them. And when they saw the chiliarch and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paulos.
And the chiliarch came near to him and seized him and ordered that they bind him with two chains, and he was asking about him who he was and what he had done.
And people from the throng were shouting against him one thing and another. And because of their shouting he could not learn what the truth was, and he ordered that they bring him to the barracks.
And when Paulos reached the stairs, the soldiers carried him because of the violence of the people.
For a great many people were coming after him and shouting and saying, Take him away.
And when he came near to entering the castle, Paulos said to the chiliarch: Will you permit me to speak with you? And he said to him: Do you know Greek?
Are you not that Egyptian who before these days stirred up and led out into the desert four thousand men, doers of evil?
Paulos said to him: I am a Yehudi man from Tarsus of Cilicia, a known city in which I was born. I ask of you, permit me to speak to the people.
And when he permitted him, Paulos stood on the stairs and waved his hand to them; and when they were quiet, he spoke with them in Hebrew and said to them:
Brothers and fathers, hear the defense that is toward you.
And when they heard that he was speaking with them in Hebrew, they were all the more quiet. And he said to them:

I am a man, a Yehudi, and I was born in Tarsus of Qiliqiya, but I was brought up in this city at the side of the feet of Gamaliel, and I was instructed perfectly in the law of our fathers, and I was zealous for Elohim, as you also all are.
And this way I persecuted even to death, while I was binding and delivering up to prison ‹both› men and women.

As the high priest bears witness about me, and all the elders, from whom I received letters to go to the brothers who are in Darmasuq, that I might bring those who were there bound to Urishlim, and they would receive a sentence of death.
And as I was going and began to draw near to Darmasuq, at midday, from under stillness, a great light from heaven flashed upon me.
And I fell on the earth, and I heard a voice that was saying to me, Sha'ul, Sha'ul, why are you persecuting me?
And I answered and said, Who are you, my Master? And he said to me, I am Y'shua the Natsraya, whom you are persecuting.
And the men who were with me saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of him who was speaking with me.
And I said, What shall I do, my Master? And our Master said to me, Rise, go to Darmasuq, and there it will be told you about everything that is commanded you to do.
And as I could not see because of the glory of that light, those who were with me took me by the hand, and I entered Darmasuq.
And a certain man, Chananya, upright in the law, as all the Yehudaye there were testifying about him.
He came to me and said to me, Shaul my brother, open your eyes. And in that very hour my eyes were opened, and I looked at him.
And he said to me, The Elohim of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Just One, and to hear the voice from his mouth.
And you will be a witness for him to all the children of men concerning all that you have seen and heard.
And now, why do you delay? Rise, be immersed, and be cleansed from your sins while you call on his name.
And I returned and came here to Urishlim, and I prayed in the temple.
And I saw him in a vision when he said to me, Make haste and go out from Urishlim, because they will not receive your testimony concerning me.
And I said, my Master, they also know that I was handing over to the house of prisoners and was beating in every synagogue those who were believing in you.

And when the blood of your witness Estefanos was being poured out, I also was standing with them and was consenting to the will of his killers, and I was keeping the clothes of those who were stoning him.
And he said to me, Go, for I am sending you far away to proclaim to the peoples.
And when they heard Paulos up to this word, they raised their voice and cried out, Let such a one be taken away from the earth, for it is not right for him to live!
And while they were shouting and throwing off their clothes and casting dust up to the sky,
the chiliarch ordered that they bring him into the fortress, and he ordered that he be examined with scourging, so that he might know for what cause they were crying out against him.
And as they were stretching him with ropes, Paulos said to the centurion who was standing over him: Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman and not condemned?
And when the centurion heard ‹it›, he approached the chiliarch and said to him: What are you doing? For this man is a Roman.
And the chiliarch approached him and said to him: Tell me, are you a Roman? And he said to him: Yes.
And the chiliarch answered and said: I acquired the Roman citizenship with a large sum of money. Paulos said to him: But I was even born in it.
And immediately those who were seeking to scourge him withdrew from him, and the chiliarch was afraid when he learned that he is a Roman, because he had bound him ‹for scourging›.

And on the next day he wanted to know truly what the accusation is that the Yehudaye were bringing against him, and he released him and commanded that the chief priests and all the assembly of their heads come, and he took Paulos and brought him down and set him among them.
And when Paulos looked on their assembly, he said: Men, my brothers; I have been led in every good conscience before Elohim up to this day.
And Chananya the priest commanded those who stood by his side to strike Paulos on his mouth.
And Paulos said to him: Elohim is ready to strike you, ‹you› whitewashed wall! And you sit judging me according to the law, while you transgress the law and command that they strike me.
And those who were standing there said to him: Do you revile the priest of Elohim?
Paulos said to them: I did not know, my brothers, that he is the priest; for it is written, You shall not curse the head of your people.

And when Paulos knew that part of the people is of the Zaduqaye and part of the Prishaye, he cried out in the assembly: Men, my brothers; I am a Prisha, son of a Prisha; and for the hope of the resurrection of the dead I am judged.
And when he said this, the Pharisees and Sadducees fell upon one another, and the people were divided.
For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor messenger, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of them.

And there was a great outcry, and some scribes from the side of the Pharisees rose up and were contending with them and saying, We find nothing evil in this man; but if a spirit or a messenger has spoken with him, what is there in this?

And when there was a great disturbance among them, the chiliarch was afraid lest they tear Paulos in pieces, and he sent Romans to come and snatch him from their midst and bring him into the fortress.
And when it was night, our Master appeared to Paulos and said to him, Be strong, because as you have testified about me in Urishlim, so you are also to testify in Rome.
And when it was morning, some men from the Yehudaye assembled and bound themselves under a curse that they would neither eat nor drink until they kill Paulos.
Now those who had established this compact by oath were more than forty men.
And they drew near to the priests and to the elders and were saying, We have bound ourselves with a curse that we will taste nothing until we kill Paulos.
And now you and the chiefs of the congregation request from the chiliarch that he bring him to you, as if you desire to examine his case truly, and we are ready to kill him before he reaches you.
And the son of Paulos’s sister heard of this plot, and he went into the barracks and informed Paulos.
And Paulos sent and called one of the centurions and said to him, Take this young man to the chiliarch, for he has something to tell him.
And the centurion took the young man and brought him in to the chiliarch and said, Paulos the prisoner called me and asked me to bring this young man to you, for he has something to tell you.
And the chiliarch took the young man by his hand and led him aside and asked him, What do you have to tell me?
And the young man said to him, The Yehudaye have plotted to ask you to bring Paulos down tomorrow to their assembly, as if they want to learn something more from him.

So do not be persuaded by them, for more than forty men from them are watching for him in ambush, and they have bound themselves under a curse that they will neither eat nor drink until they kill him, and they are ready and waiting for your promise.
And the chiliarch dismissed the young man after charging him, Let no one know that you have disclosed these things to me.
And he called two centurions and said to them, Go prepare two hundred Romans to go to Qesarya, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred right-hand shooters, to set out from the third hour of the night.
And provide also a beast so they may mount Paulos and bring him safely to Felix the governor.
And he wrote a letter and gave ‹it› to them, in which was thus:
Lysias to the excellent governor Felix, greeting.
This man the Yehudaye seized so that they might kill him, and I stood with the Romans and rescued him when I learned that he is a Roman.
And when I was seeking to know the cause for which they were accusing him, I brought him down to their assembly.
And I found that it was about questions of their law they were accusing him, and a cause worthy of bonds or of death was not with him.
And when the plot by ambush that the Yehudaye made against him was made known to me, at once I sent him to you, and I commanded his accusers to come and speak with him before you. Be well.
Then the Romans, as they had been commanded, took Paulos by night and brought him to the city of Antipatris.
And on the next day the horsemen dismissed the footmen their companions, that they might return to the camp.
And they brought him to Qesarya, and they gave the letter to the governor, and set Paulos before him.
And when he read the letter, he was asking him from which province he was. And when he learned that he was from Qiliqiya,
he said to him, I will hear you when your accusers come. And he ordered that they keep him in the praetorium of Herodes.
And after five days Chananya the high priest went down with the elders and with Tertullus the orator, and they informed the governor against Paulos.
And when he was called, Tertullus began accusing him and said, In much peace we dwell because of you, and many reforms have come to this people by your care.
And we all in every place receive your grace, excellent Felix.
But so as not to weary you with many ‹particulars›, I ask of you that you hear our humility in brief.
For we have found this man to be a corruptor and one who stirs up sedition among all the Yehudaye in the whole land, for he is the head of the teaching of the Natsraye.
And he wanted to pollute our temple. And when we seized him we wanted to judge him according to our law.
But Lysias the chiliarch came, and with much force took him away from our hands and sent him to you.
And he commanded his accusers to come to you. And you are able, when you question him, to learn from him about all these things of which we accuse him.
And the Yehudaye also contended against him, saying that these things are so.

And the governor signaled to Paulos that he should speak. And Paulos answered and said: I know that you have been a judge of this people for many years, and because of this I cheerfully make a defense for myself.
As you are able to know that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to Urishlim to worship.
And they did not find me speaking with anyone in the temple, nor gathering a crowd, either in their synagogues or in the city.
And they do not have ‹power› to prove before you the things of which they now accuse me.
But this I confess, that in this same teaching of which they speak I serve the Elohim of my fathers, believing all that is written in the law and in the prophets.
And I have hope toward Elohim, which these also themselves hope, that there is about to be a rising from the house of the dead, of the righteous and of the unjust.
Because of this I also labor that a pure conscience may always be mine before Elohim and before the sons of men.
But after many years I came to the sons of my own people to give alms and to present an offering.
And these found me in the temple while I was purifying myself, not with a throng nor with a tumult.
but some Yehudaye who came from Asia, who ought to stand with me before you and accuse ‹of› whatever they have.
Or let these here say what offense they found in me when I stood before their assembly;
except this one word that I cried out while I was standing among them: Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am judged today before you.
And Pilkas, because he knew this way fully, deferred them, saying: When the chiliarch comes, I will hear between you.
And he commanded the centurion to keep Paulos at ease, and that no one of his acquaintances should be forbidden to minister to him.
And after a few days Pilkas sent, and Dursila his wife who was a Yehuditha, and they called Paulos and heard from him concerning the faith of the Mashiyach.

And while he was speaking with them about righteousness and about holiness and about the judgment that is coming, Felix was filled with fear and said, For now go, and when I have opportunity I will send for you.
For he was hoping that a present would be given to him by Paulos; ‹and› because of this he also continually sent and brought him and spoke with him.
And when two years were fulfilled to him, another governor came into his place who was called Porcius Festus. But Felix, so that he might do a favor to the Yehudaye, left Paulos bound.
And when Festus came to Caesarea, after three days he went up to Urishlim.
And the chief priests and the heads of the Yehudaye informed him about Paulos, and they were seeking from him
as they asked him this favor, that he would send to bring him to Urishlim, while they were laying an ambush on the road to kill him.
And Festus answered that Paulos is kept in Caesarea, and I am hastening to go out.
Therefore let those among you who are able go down with us, and accuse him of every offence that is in the man.
And when he had been there eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea. And the next day he sat on the tribunal and commanded that they bring Paulos.
And when he came, the Yehudaye who had come down from Urishlim surrounded him, and they were bringing many and hard charges against him which they were not able to show.
And Paulos was making defense that he had not offended in anything, neither in the law of the Yehudaye, nor in the temple, nor in Caesar.
But Festus, because he wanted to grant a favor to the Yehudaye, said to Paulos, Do you want to go up to Urishlim and there be judged before me on these ‹things›?
Paulos answered and said, I stand here on the judgment seat of Caesar; here it is right for me to be judged. I have sinned nothing against the Yehudaye, as even you know.

And if a wrong is done by me, or anything worthy of death, I do not refuse death. But if there is nothing in me of these things of which they accuse me, no one gives me to them as a gift. I call on Caesar.
Then Festus spoke with the men of his council and said, You have called on Caesar; to Caesar you will go.
And when ‹some› days had passed, Agrippa the king and Bernice came down to Caesarea to greet Festus.
And when they had been with him ‹some› days, Festus related to the king the case of Paulos, saying: A certain man was left a prisoner by Felix.
And when I was in Urishlim, the chief priests and the elders of the Yehudaye informed me about him, and asked that I would pass judgment on him for them.

And I told them, It is not the custom of the Romans to hand a man over as a gift to be killed until his accuser comes and charges him to his face, and opportunity is given him to make a defense about what he is accused of.
And when I came here, without delay, the next day I sat on the judgment seat and commanded that the man be brought to me.
And his accusers stood up with him, and they were not able to show any evil charge against him, as I had expected.
But they had certain disputes with him about their worship, and about Y'shua, a man who had died, whom Paulos was saying is alive.
And because I was not established on the inquiry of these things, I said to Paulos, If you seek to go to Urishlim and there be judged concerning these,
But he sought to be kept for the judgment of Caesar, and I ordered that he be kept until I send him to Caesar.
And Agrippa said, I was wanting to hear this man. And Festus said, Tomorrow you will hear him.
And on another day Agrippa and Bernice came with much pomp and entered the house of judgment with the chiliarchs and the heads of the city, and Festus commanded, and Paulos came.

And Festus said, King Agrippa and all you men who are with us, concerning this man whom you see, all the people of the Yehudaye applied to me in Urishlim and here, crying out that it is no longer right for this one to live.
I for my part found that he has done nothing worthy of death. And because he asked to be kept for the judgment of Caesar, I ordered that he be sent.

And I do not know what I should write about him to Caesar. Because of this I wanted to bring him before you, and especially before you, king Agrippa, so that when his case is examined I may find what to write.
For it is not fitting, when we send a bound man, that we should not write his offense.
And Agrippa said to Paulos, You are permitted to speak on behalf of yourself. Then Paulos stretched out his hand and made defense, saying:
Concerning all that I am accused of by the Yehudaye, king Agrippa, I count myself blessed that before you today I make defense,
especially as I know that you are expert in all the controversies and the law of the Yehudaye. Because of this I ask of you that with patience you hear me.
For even those Yehudaye know, if they wish to testify, my way of life from my youth, which was mine from the beginning among my people and in Urishlim,
because from long ago they have been persuaded about me and know that in the foremost teaching of the Pharisees I lived.
And now for the hope of the promise that was made to our fathers by Elohim I stand and am judged.
To this hope the twelve tribes hope to arrive with earnest prayer by day and by night, and for this hope I am accused by the Yehudaye, king Agrippa.
Why do you judge? Is it not right that we believe that Elohim raises the dead?
For I from the first set in my mind that I would do many opposing things against the name of Y'shua the Natsraya.
This I also did in Urishlim, and many holy ones I cast into prison by the authority I received from the chief priests, and when they were being killed I took part with those who condemned them.
And in every assembly I was torturing them while I was forcing them to blaspheme the name of Y'shua, and being filled with much rage against them I also went out to other cities to persecute them.
And while I was going for this to Darmasuq with the authority and permission of the chief priests,
In the middle of the day, on the road, I saw, O king, from heaven a light brighter than the sun shining on me and on all who were with me.
And we all fell on the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me in Hebrew, Shaul, Shaul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.
And I said, Who are you, my Master? And our Master said to me, I am Y'shua the Natsraya, whom you are persecuting.
And he said to me, Stand on your feet, for this is why I have appeared to you: to appoint you a minister and a witness of what you have seen of me and of what you will see of me.
And I will deliver you from the people of the Yehudaye and from the other peoples to whom I am sending you,

to open their eyes so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the authority of Satana to Elohim, and may receive forgiveness of sins and a portion with the holy ones by the faith that is in me.
For this reason, king Agrippa, I did not stand rebelliously against the heavenly vision.

but I proclaimed from the first to those in Darmasuq and to those in Urishlim and in all the villages of Yehuda, and also to the peoples I proclaimed that they should repent and turn to Elohim and do works worthy of repentance.
And on account of these things the Yehudaye seized me in the temple and wanted to kill me.

But Elohim has helped me until this day, and I stand and testify to the small and to the great, saying nothing outside of Moshe and the prophets except those things which they said were going to happen:
‹namely,› that the Mashiyach would suffer and would be the first fruits of the rising from among the dead, and that he would proclaim light to the people and to the peoples.
And when Paulos had thus gone forth in spirit, Festus cried out with a loud voice: Paulos, you are mad! Much learning has made you mad.
Paulos said, I am not insane, excellent Festus, but I speak words of truth and uprightness.

And king Agrippa also knows especially about these things, and because of this I speak openly before him, for I do not suppose that any one of these words is hidden from him, since they were not done in secret.
Do you believe the prophets, king Agrippa? I know that you believe.
Agrippa said to him, In a little you persuade me to become a Christian.
And Paulos said, I was wishing from Elohim, in little and in much, not only you but also all who hear me today, that they would be like me, apart from these bonds.
And the king rose, and the governor, and Bernice, and those who were sitting with them.
And when they had gone out from there, they were speaking one with another and saying, This man has done nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
And Agrippa said to Festus, This man could have been released if he had not called on Caesar.

And Festus commanded concerning him that he should be sent to Caesar in Italy. And he delivered Paulos and the other prisoners with him to a certain man, a centurion from the Augustan cohort, whose name was Julius.

And when it was ‹time› to sail, we went down into a ship that was from the city of Adramyttium and was going to the region of Asia. And Aristarchus, a Macedonian from the city of Thessalonica, went up with us into the ship.
And on the next day we reached Tsidon. And the centurion treated Paulos with kindness and allowed him to go to his friends and be refreshed.
And from there we sailed, and because the winds were against us, we went around by Cyprus.
And we crossed the sea of Cilicia and of Pamphylia and reached Myra, a city of Lycia.
And there the centurion found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy, and he put us on board it.

And because the sailing was hard, after many days we scarcely reached opposite the island of Qnidus. And because the wind would not let us go straight, we sailed around Crete, ‹and came› opposite the city of Salmone.
And with difficulty, as we sailed around it, we reached a place called the Fair Havens, and near it was the city whose name is Lasa.
And we were there a long time, until even the day of the fast of the Yehudaye had passed. And it became hazardous for anyone to sail on the sea, and Paulos counselled them,
and said: Men, I see that our voyage will be with hardship and with much loss, not only of the cargo of our ship, but also of our own lives.
But the centurion listened to the pilot and to the owner of the ship more than to the words of Paulos.
