And because that harbor was not fit to winter in, many of us wanted to sail from there, and if they could reach and winter in a harbor that was in Crete and was called Phonkas, and it faced toward the south.
And when the south wind blew, and they hoped they would arrive as they desired, they were sailing around Crete.
And after a little, a storm wind came out upon us that is called Typhonic Euroclydon.
And the ship was seized and could not stand against the wind, and we gave ‹the ship› into its hand.
And when we passed a certain island that is called Quda, we could hardly hold the boat.
And when we took it up, we were girding and making the ship ready, and because we were afraid that we might fall into the Syrtis of the sea, we lowered the gear, and so we were sailing.
And when a hard storm stood upon us, the next day we threw goods into the sea.
And on the third day, with our own hands we threw away the gear of the ship.
And when the storm held on for many days, and neither sun nor moon nor stars was seen, all hope of our lives was wholly cut off.

And when no one was taking any food, then Paulos stood up among them and said: If you had listened to me, men, we would not have sailed from Crete, and we would have been spared this loss and this distress.
And now I counsel you to be without anxiety; for not one soul of you will be lost, but only the ship.
For there appeared to me this night the messenger of Elohim, whose I am and whom I serve;
and he said to me: Do not fear, Paulos; it is destined for you to stand before Caesar; and Elohim has given you as a gift all who sail with you.
Therefore, men, take heart; for I trust in Elohim that it will be so, as it was spoken with me.
But we must be cast onto a certain island.
And after fourteen days that we were wandering and being tossed in the Adriatic sea, in the middle of the night the sailors supposed that they were approaching land.
And they cast the sounding-lead and found twenty fathoms. And again they went a little farther and found fifteen fathoms.
And as we were afraid lest we should fall upon places where there are rocks, they cast four anchors from the stern of the ship, and were praying that day would come.
But the sailors sought to flee from the ship, and they lowered the boat from it into the sea, under the pretext that they were going in it to fasten the ship to the land.
And when Paulos saw ‹it›, he said to the centurion and to the soldiers: If these do not remain in the ship, you are not able to live.
Then the soldiers cut the ropes of the boat from the ship and let it go adrift.
But Paulos, until morning came, was persuading all of them to take food, when he said to them: Today it is fourteen days that from the fear you have tasted nothing.
Because of this I ask of you that you take food for the sustaining of your lives; for a hair from the head of one of you will not perish.
And when he said these things, he took bread and gave glory to Elohim before all of them, and broke ‹it› and began to eat.
And they were all encouraged, and they took nourishment.
And we were in the ship two hundred and seventy-six souls.
And when they were satisfied with food, they lightened the ship and took the wheat and threw it into the sea.

And when it was day, the sailors did not recognize what land it was, but they looked on the side of the dry land at one bay of the sea where they were thinking that if it was possible they might drive the ship.

And they cut the anchors from the ship and left them in the sea, and they loosened the bands of the rudder and hung the small sail to the wind that was blowing and were driving toward the face of the dry land.

And the ship struck in a place raised between two depths of the sea and stuck fast in it, and its forward side stood on it and was not moving, but its after side was loosened by the force of the waves.
And the soldiers wanted to kill the prisoners, so they would not swim and escape from them.
But the centurion kept them from this, because he was desiring to give life to Paulos. And those who were able to swim, he commanded them that they swim first and pass over to the land.
And the rest he made pass over on boards and on other wood of the ship. And so they all were delivered safe to the land.
And afterwards we learned that the island is called Melita.
And the barbarians who were living in it showed us many kindnesses. And they kindled a fire and called all of us to warm ourselves, because of the heavy rain and the cold that there was.
And Paulos took a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, and a viper came out of them from the heat of the fire and bit his hand.
And when the barbarians saw it hanging on his hand, they were saying, Doubtless this man is a murderer, whom, though he was delivered from the sea, justice has not allowed to live.
But Paulos shook off his hand and threw the viper into the fire, and nothing harmful happened to him.

But the barbarians were expecting that he would suddenly swell up and fall dead on the ground. And when they had waited a long time and saw that nothing harmful happened to him, they changed their words and said that he is an Elohim.
Now there were lands in that place belonging to a certain man whose name was Publius, who was the chief of the island, and he received us in his house three days cheerfully.
Now the father of Publius was sick with a fever and with pain of the bowels. And Paulos went in to him and prayed and laid his hand on him and healed him.
And when this happened, the rest also who were sick in the island were coming to him and were being healed.
And they honored us with great honors, and when we were leaving from there they supplied us.
Now we departed after three months and sailed in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island, and it had on it the sign of the Twins.
And we came to the city Sarqusa and remained there three days.
And from there we made a circuit and reached the city Regiyun. And after one day a south wind blew ‹favorably› for us, and in two days we came to Putiyalis, a city of Italiya.
And there we found brothers, and they asked us, and we stayed with them seven days, and then we went to Rhoma.

And when the brothers there heard, they went out to meet us as far as the market called Apiyus Forum and as far as the Three Taverns. And when Paulos saw them, he gave thanks to Elohim and was strengthened.
And we entered Rhoma. And the centurion allowed Paulos to stay where he wished with the soldier who was guarding him.

And after three days Paulos sent and called the leaders of the Yehudaye. And when they had gathered, he said to them: Men, my brothers, though I had in nothing stood against the people or the law of my fathers, I was delivered in bonds from Urishlim into the hand of the Romans.
And they, when they examined me, wanted to release me, because they found in me no charge of anything deserving death.
And when the Yehudaye were standing against me, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar; not as though I had anything of which to accuse the sons of my people.
For this reason I asked of you that you would come, and I might show you and relate these things to you; for it is on account of the hope of Yisrael that I am bound with this chain.
They say to him: We have received no letter about you from Yehuda, and none of the brothers who came from Urishlim have told us anything bad about you.
But we desire to hear from you what you think; for we know that this teaching is not received by anyone.

And they set a day for him, and many gathered and came to him at his lodging. And he revealed to them about the kingdom of Elohim, testifying and persuading them about Y'shua from the law of Moshe and from the prophets, from morning until evening.
And some of them were persuaded by his words, and others were not persuaded.
And they went out from him, not agreeing with one another. And Paulos said to them this word: Well did the Ruach haKodesh speak by the mouth of Eshaya the prophet against your fathers,
when he said, Go to this people and say to them, Hearing you will hear and not understand, and you will see and not discern.

For the heart of this people has grown dull, and their hearing they have made heavy, and their eyes they have closed, so they will not see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn to me, and I will forgive them.
Therefore let this be known to you, that to the peoples this redemption of Elohim has been sent; for they also hear it.
And when he said these things, the Yehudaye went out, and there was much disputing among them.
And Paulos hired a house for himself at his own cost, and stayed in it two years, and there he received all who came to him.
And he was proclaiming about the kingdom of Elohim, and he was teaching openly about our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, without hindrance.
Paulos, a servant of Y'shua the Mashiyach, called and sent, and separated to the gospel of Elohim,
which he promised beforehand through his prophets in the holy scriptures,
concerning his Son, who was born in the flesh from the seed of the house of Dawid,
and was made known as the Son of Elohim in power and by the Ruach haKodesh, who rose from the house of the dead, Y'shua the Mashiyach our Master,
by whom we received grace and a sending among all the peoples, so that they may obey the faith of his name;
among whom you also are called by Y'shua the Mashiyach;
To all who are in Rome, beloved of Elohim, called and holy: peace and grace be with you, from Elohim our Father and from our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
First I give thanks to my Elohim through Y'shua the Mashiyach for all of you, that your faith is heard of in all the world.
For Elohim is witness to me, whom I serve in spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I remember you at all times in my prayers.
And I pray that from now a way may be opened for me by the will of Elohim to come to you.
Because I long much to see you and give you a gift of the spirit by which you may be strengthened.
And together we may be comforted in the faith that is yours and mine.
But I want you to know, my brothers, that many times I have desired to come to you, and I have been hindered until now, so that I might have fruit among you also, as among the rest of the peoples.
Greeks and barbarians, the wise and the unwise: for to every person I am a debtor to proclaim ‹to him›.
And so I am eager to proclaim also to you who are in Rome.
For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of Elohim for life to all who believe in it, whether first from the Yehudaye and whether from the Aramaye.
For the righteousness of Elohim is revealed in it from faith to faith, as it is written: The righteous by faith will live.
For the wrath of Elohim is revealed from heaven against all the iniquity and wickedness of the sons of men, those who hold the truth in iniquity.
Because the knowledge of Elohim is revealed in them; for Elohim has revealed it in them.

For the hidden things of Elohim, from the foundation of the world, are seen by the intellect in the things he created, even his power and his divinity that is forever, so that they might be without excuse;
because they knew Elohim, and did not glorify him and give thanks to him as Elohim, but became empty in their thoughts, and their heart that does not understand was darkened.
And while they thought within themselves that they were wise, they became fools.

And they changed the glory of Elohim that does not corrupt into the likeness of the image of a man that corrupts, and into the likeness of birds and of four-footed creatures and of creeping things of the earth.
Because of this Elohim gave them up to the filthy lusts of their heart, to dishonor their bodies among themselves.
And they changed the truth of Elohim into a lie, and worshipped and served the created things more than the Creator of them, to whom ‹belong› glory and blessings forever and ever. Amen.
For this reason Elohim gave them over to shameful passions: for their females changed the natural use of their nature, and used what is not fitting.

And likewise also their males left the natural use of the female and burned with lust one for another, and male with male they did what is shameful, and received in themselves the recompense that was due for their error.
And as they did not determine in themselves to know Elohim, Elohim gave them over to a worthless mind, so that they would do what is not proper,
being filled with all iniquity and sexual immorality and bitterness and malice and greed and envy and murder and strife and deceit and evil schemes,
and whisperers and slanderers, haters of Elohim, insolent, proud, boastful, inventors of evil, lacking sense, not obedient to their parents,
and who have no covenant, nor affection, nor peace, and in whom there is no compassion.
These, while they know the judgment of Elohim, that he condemns to death those who practice such things, are not only doers of them, but also companions of those who do them.
Therefore there is no excuse for you, O man who judges his neighbor; for in that you judge your neighbor, you condemn yourself; for you who judge also practice the same things.
And we know that the judgment of Elohim is in truth upon those who practice these things.
But what do you think, O man who judges those who practice these things, while you yourself also practice them, that you will escape the judgment of Elohim?
Or do you presume upon the riches of his kindness and his long-suffering and the opportunity he gives you? And do you not know that the kindness of Elohim brings you to repentance?
But because of the hardness of your unrepenting heart, you are laying up for yourself a store of wrath for the day of wrath and for the revelation of the righteous judgment of Elohim,
who repays every person according to his deeds;
to those who by perseverance in good works seek glory and honor and incorruptibility, he gives them life forever;
but to those who are obstinate and do not obey the truth, but obey iniquity, he will repay them wrath and anger.
And tribulation and anguish ‹will be› to every human who does evil; to the Yehudi first, and also to the Aramean:
but glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good; to the Yehudi first, and also to the Aramean.
For there is no respect of persons with Elohim:
for those who without law have sinned will also perish without law; and those who in the law have sinned will be judged by the law,
For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before Elohim, but the doers of the law who are justified.
For if the nations who have no law, from their nature do the things of the law, those who while they had no law were a law to themselves:
and they show the work of the law written on their hearts, and their conscience testifies about them, while their thoughts accuse or else defend one another,
in the day when Elohim judges the secret ‹actions› of the sons of men, according to my gospel ‹teacheth›, by Y'shua the Mashiyach.
But if you are called a Yehudi, and rest on the law, and boast in Elohim,
and you know his will, and distinguish what is proper, because you are instructed from the law;
and you have confidence in yourself that you are a guide of the blind and a light of those who are in darkness,
and a corrector of those lacking in mind and a teacher of children, and you have the form of knowledge and of truth in the law:
You therefore who teach another, do you not teach yourself? And you who proclaim that they should not steal, do you steal?
And you who say they should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? And you who despise idols, do you plunder the house of the sanctuary?
And you who boast in the law, by that in which you transgress the law you insult Elohim.
For the name of Elohim is blasphemed among the peoples because of you, as it is written.
For circumcision is of benefit if you fulfill the law; but if you transgress the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
And if uncircumcision keeps the precepts of the law, is not that uncircumcision accounted as circumcision?
And uncircumcision that by nature fulfills the law will judge you who, with the writing and with circumcision, transgress the law.
For he is not a Yehudi who is one outwardly, nor is that circumcision which is visible in the flesh.
But he is a Yehudi who is one in what is hidden, and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit and not in the writing, whose praise is not from the sons of men but from Elohim.
What then is the superiority of the Yehudi? Or what is the advantage of circumcision?
Much, in every way. First, because the words of Elohim were entrusted ‹to them›.
For if some of them have not believed, have they by not believing nullified the faith of Elohim?
Far from it! For Elohim is true, and every man a liar, as it is written: That you may be upright in your words, and may overcome when they judge you.
But if our injustice establishes the righteousness of Elohim, what shall we say? Is Elohim unjust when he brings his wrath? I am speaking as a man.
Far from it. Otherwise how will Elohim judge the world?
But if the truth of Elohim has been furthered by my falsehood to his glory, why then am I judged as a sinner?
Or as some blaspheme against us and say that we say, Let us do evil things that good ‹results› may come? The judgment of such is reserved for justice.
What then? Do we hold a superiority? For we have before decided concerning Yehudaye and Armaye that they are all under sin.
As it is written: There is no righteous, not even one.
And there is none that understands, and none that seeks Elohim.
They have all turned aside together and become worthless, and there is none that does good, not even one.
Their throat is an open grave, and their tongues are deceitful, and the venom of asps is under their lips.
Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness;
and their feet are swift to shed blood.
Destruction and misery are in their paths:
and the way of peace they have not known:
and the fear of Elohim is not before their eyes.
Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are in the law, so that every mouth may be shut and the whole world may become guilty before Elohim.
Because by the works of the law no flesh is justified before him, for by the law sin is made known.
But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of Elohim is revealed, and the law and the prophets testify to it:
the righteousness of Elohim through the faith of Y'shua the Mashiyach, to everyone and upon everyone who believes in him, for there is no distinction;
because they have all sinned and fall short of the glory of Elohim,
and they are justified freely by grace and by the redemption that is in Y'shua the Mashiyach;
This one whom Elohim set beforehand as a covering by faith in his blood, because of our sins which we sinned from before,

in the place that Elohim gave us in the long-suffering of his spirit, for the showing of his righteousness in this time, that he might be righteous and might justify in righteousness the one who is in the faith of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
Where then is boasting? It is made void. By what law? Of works? No, but by the law of faith.
We therefore reckon that a man is justified by faith and not by the works of the law.
For is Elohim of the Yehudaye only, and not of the peoples? Yes, also of the peoples.
Because there is one Elohim who justifies circumcision by faith, and also uncircumcision by the same faith.
Do we then nullify the law by faith? Far be it. On the contrary, we establish the law.
What then do we say about Avraham the head of the fathers, that he found in the flesh?
For if Avraham was justified from works, he had ‹ground of› boasting; but not toward Elohim.
For what does the writing say? That Avraham believed Elohim, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness.
But to the one who works, the wage is not reckoned to him as of favor, but as to one who is owed.
But to him who does not work, but only believes in the one who justifies the sinner, his faith is reckoned to him for righteousness.
Just as Dawid also says of the blessedness of the man to whom Elohim reckons righteousness without works, when he says
Blessed are they whose iniquity is forgiven them, and whose sins are covered.
and blessed is the man to whom Elohim will not reckon his sin.
Is this blessedness therefore on the circumcision, or on the uncircumcision? For we say that Avraham's faith was reckoned to him for righteousness.
How then was it reckoned to him? In circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

For he received circumcision as a sign and a seal of the righteousness of his faith that was in uncircumcision, that he might be father to all who believe from uncircumcision, that it might be reckoned also to them for righteousness,
and father to the circumcision, not only to those who are of the circumcision, but also to those who walk in the steps of the faith of the uncircumcision of our father Avraham.
For the promise to Avraham and to his seed, that he would be heir of the world, was not by the law, but by the righteousness of his faith.
For if those who are of the law were heirs, faith would be empty, and the promise would be void.
For the law is a worker of wrath; for where there is no law, there is also no transgression of law.

Because of this it is by faith, which is by grace, that we are justified, so that the promise may be sure to all his seed; not only to the one who is of the law, but also to the one who is of the faith of Avraham, who is the father of us all,
as it is written: I have set you a father to a multitude of peoples; ‹namely› before Elohim, in whom you have believed, who gives life to the dead and calls those who are not as though they are.
And without hope he believed in hope that he would become a father to a multitude of peoples, as it is written: So will your seed be.
And he did not weaken in his faith when he contemplated his dead body (for he was a hundred years old) and the dead womb of Sara.
And he did not doubt at the promise of Elohim as one lacking faith, but was strengthened in faith and gave glory to Elohim;
and was assured that what Elohim had promised him he is able to fulfill.
Because of this it was accounted to him for righteousness.
And it was not for his sake alone that this was written, that his faith was accounted for righteousness;
but also for our sake, because it is to be accounted ‹so› to us also who believe in him who raised our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach from the dead.
who was delivered up on account of our sins, and rose that we might be justified.
Therefore, because we have been justified by faith, we will have peace with Elohim through our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
By whom we have been brought near by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we glory in the hope of the glory of Elohim.
And not only so, but we also glory in afflictions, because we know that affliction perfects patience in us;
and patience, proving; and proving, hope;
and hope does not put to shame, because the love of Elohim is poured out on our hearts by the Ruach haKodesh who has been given to us.
For if Mashiyach, on account of our weakness, at this time died for the ungodly:
For rarely does a person die for the wicked; though for the good someone might perhaps dare to die.
Here Elohim has shown his love toward us, that while we were still sinners, the Mashiyach died for us.
How much more, then, will we now be justified by his blood and by him be rescued from wrath?
For if when we were enemies Elohim was reconciled with us by the death of his Son, how much more, then, in his reconciliation will we live by his life?
And not only so, but we also boast in Elohim through our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
For just as through one man sin entered the world, and through sin death, and so death passed upon all the sons of men, because they all sinned:
For until the law, sin, while it was in the world, was not accounted sin, because there was no law.
But death reigned from Adam until Moshe, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of the transgression of Adam's command, who is the type of him who was to come.

But not as the offense, so also the free gift. For if because of the offense of one many died, how much more then will the grace of Elohim and his free gift because of one man Y'shua the Mashiyach abound to many?
And not as the offense of one, so also the free gift. For the judgment that was from one ‹offense› was to condemnation, but the free gift from many sins was to righteousness.

For if because of the offense of one death reigned, how much more will those who receive the abundance of the grace and of the free gift and of the righteousness reign in life by means of one, Y'shua the Mashiyach.
Therefore, as by the offense of one there was condemnation for all the sons of men, so by the righteousness of one there will be victory to life for all the sons of men.
For just as on account of the disobedience of one man many became sinners, so also on account of the obedience of one many become righteous.
And the entrance that came to the law was so that sin might increase; and where sin increased, there grace abounded.
so that as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign in righteousness to life everlasting by our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
What then shall we say? Shall we remain in sin, so that grace may abound?
Far be it! For those of us who have died to sin, how will we live in it again?
Or do you not know that those of us who were immersed into Y'shua the Mashiyach were immersed into his death?
We were buried with him by immersion into death, so that just as Y'shua the Mashiyach rose from among the dead by the glory of his Father, so we too will walk in new life.
For if we have been planted together with him in the likeness of his death, so we will also be in his rising.
For we know that our old man was crucified with him, so that the body of sin might be abolished, and we would no longer serve sin.
For he who has died ‹to it› is set free from sin.
If then we have died with the Mashiyach, we believe that we will also live with the Mashiyach.
For we know that the Mashiyach rose from among the dead and does not die again, and death has no dominion over him.
For in that he died, he died to sin once, and in that he lives, he lives to Elohim.
So you also reckon yourselves dead to sin and alive to Elohim in our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
Therefore do not let sin reign in your dead body so that you obey its lusts.

And also do not give up your members as instruments of evil to sin, but give up yourselves to Elohim, as people who have been given life from the dead; and let your members be instruments for the righteousness of Elohim.
And sin will not have dominion over you; for you are not under the law, but under grace.
What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? Far be it.
Do you not know that to whomever you give up yourselves to serve in bondage, you are his servants whom you obey; whether to sin, or whether to righteousness, that you give ear?
But thanks be to Elohim, that you were ‹once› the servants of sin but have ‹now› from the heart obeyed that form of doctrine to which you are devoted.
And when you were emancipated from sin, you became servants to righteousness.

I speak as among men, because of the weakness of your flesh. As you ‹once› prepared your members for the servitude of pollution and of iniquity, so also now prepare your members for the servitude of righteousness and of holiness.
For when you were servants of sin, you were free from righteousness.
And what fruit did you have then from that of which you are now ashamed? For its end is death.
And now that you have been freed from sin and have become servants to Elohim, you have holy fruit, and their end is life everlasting.
For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of Elohim is life everlasting in our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
Or do you not know, my brothers—for I am speaking to those who know the law—that the law has authority over a man as long as he is alive?
Just as a woman is bound by the law to her husband as long as he is alive, but if her husband dies, she is freed from the law of her husband.

But if, while her husband is alive, she joins herself to another man, she becomes an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is freed from the law, and is not an adulteress if she becomes another man’s.
And now, my brothers, you also have died to the law by the body of the Mashiyach, that you might be joined to another, ‹even› to him who rose from among the dead, that you might give fruit to Elohim.
For while we were in the flesh, the pains of sin that are by the law were at work in our members, that we might give fruit to death.
But now we are released from the law and have died to that which held us, so that we might serve from now on in the newness of the spirit and not in the oldness of the writing.
What then do we say? Is the law sin? Far from it. But I did not learn sin except by means of the law. For I would not have known desire if the law had not said, Do not desire.
And by this commandment sin found occasion and perfected in me every desire. For without the law sin was dead.
And I was alive without the law formerly; but when the commandment came, sin came alive and I died;
and the commandment of life was found by me ‹to be› to death.
For sin, by the occasion it found by means of the commandment, deceived me and by it killed me.
So then the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.

So did what is good become death to me? Far from it. But sin, so that it would be seen to be sin, perfected death in me by means of the good ‹law›; so that sin would be condemned all the more by means of the commandment.
For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am of the flesh, and sold to sin.
For what I am doing I do not know; and it is not what I want that I do, but what I hate, that I do.
And if I do what I do not want, I testify of the law that it is right.
But now it is no longer I who do this, but sin that dwells in me.
For I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh; for to want the good is easy for me, but to do it I am not able.
For I do not do the good that I want to do, but the bad that I do not want to do, that I do.
And if I do what I do not want, it is not I who do it, but sin that dwells in me.
I find therefore a law that agrees with my mind, which wants to do the good, because evil is near to me.
For I rejoice in the law of Elohim in the inner man.
But I see another law in my members that wars against the law of my mind and makes me captive to the law of sin that is in my members.
I am a miserable man! Who will rescue me from this body of death?
I thank Elohim by means of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach ‹I shall be rescued.› Now therefore I in my mind am a servant of the law of Elohim, but in my flesh I am a servant of the law of sin.
Therefore there is no condemnation for those who do not walk in the flesh in Y'shua the Mashiyach.
For the law of the spirit of life that is in Y'shua the Mashiyach has freed you from the law of sin and of death.
Because the law was weak through the weakness of the flesh, Elohim sent his Son in the likeness of flesh of sin on account of sin, that he might condemn sin in his flesh,
so that the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us who do not walk in the flesh but in the spirit.
For those who are in the flesh mind the things of the flesh, and those who are of the spirit mind the things of the spirit.
For the minding of the flesh is death, but the minding of the spirit is life and peace.
Because the mind of the flesh is enmity toward Elohim, for it does not subject itself to the law of Elohim, because it is not possible.
And those who are in the flesh are not able to please Elohim.
You, however, are not in the flesh but in the ruach, if the Ruach of Elohim truly dwells in you. But if a person does not have in him the Ruach of the Mashiyach, this one is not his.
But if the Mashiyach is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the ruach is life because of righteousness.

And if the Ruach of him who raised our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach from the house of the dead dwells in you, he who raised Y'shua the Mashiyach from the house of the dead will also give life to your dead bodies because of his Ruach that dwells in you.
Now, my brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, that we should walk in the flesh.
For if you live in the flesh, you are about to die. But if by the Ruach you put to death the practices of the body, you live.
For those who are led by the Ruach of Elohim, these are the sons of Elohim.
For you have not received a ruach of bondage again to fear, but you have received a Ruach of sonship, by which we cry, Abba, our Father.
And that Ruach testifies to our spirit that we are sons of Elohim.
And if sons, then also heirs; heirs of Elohim and sharers of the inheritance of Y'shua the Mashiyach, so that if we suffer with him, we will also be glorified with him.
For I reckon that the sufferings of this time are not equal to the glory that is about to be revealed in us.
For the whole creation is hoping and waiting for the revealing of the sons of Elohim.
For the creation was subjected to vanity, not by its own will, but because of him who subjected it, in hope
that the creation itself also will be set free from the bondage of corruption into the freedom of the glory of the sons of Elohim.
For we know that all creation groans and travails in pain until this day.
And not only they, but we also who have the first fruits of the Spirit groan within ourselves and wait for the adoption of sons and the redemption of our bodies.
Because we live in hope. But hope that is seen is not hope; for if we see it, what do we wait for?
But if we hope for what is not seen, we wait in patience.
So also the Ruach helps our weakness. For we do not know what to pray as is proper, but the Ruach prays for us with groans that are not spoken.
And he who searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the Ruach, because according to the will of Elohim he prays for the holy ones.
And we know that those who love Elohim, he helps them in everything for good, those whom he previously set to be called.
And those he knew beforehand he marked with the likeness of the image of his Son, that he would be the firstborn of many brothers.
And those whom he previously marked, he called; and those whom he called, he made righteous; and those whom he made righteous, he glorified.
What then will we say about these things? If Elohim ‹is› for us, who ‹is› against us?
And if he did not spare his Son, but delivered him up for all of us, how will he not give us all things with him?
Who will bring a charge against the chosen of Elohim? Elohim justifies.
Who condemns? The Mashiyach died and rose and is at the right hand of Elohim and intercedes for us.
Who will separate me from the love of the Mashiyach? Affliction or imprisonment or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or the sword?
As it is written: For your sake we are killed every day, and we are counted as sheep for slaughter.
But in all these things we are victorious through him who loved us.
For I am persuaded that neither death nor life nor messengers nor principalities nor powers nor things present nor things to come,
nor height nor depth nor any other created thing will be able to separate me from the love of Elohim that is in our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
I say the truth in the Mashiyach and I do not lie, and my mind bears witness for me in the Ruach haKodesh,
that I have great grief, and pain from my heart that does not cease.
For I was praying that I myself would be a ban from the Mashiyach for the sake of my brothers and my kinsmen who are in the flesh,
who are the sons of Yisrael, whose was the adoption of sons and the glory and the covenants and the law and the service in it and the promises
and the fathers, and from them the Mashiyach appeared in the flesh, who is Elohim over all, to whom be praises and blessings forever and ever. Amen.
But it is not that the word of Elohim has fallen. For not all who are from Yisrael are Yisrael.
Nor are they all children because they are of the seed of Avraham, for it was said, In Yitz'chak your seed will be called.
That is, it is not the children of the flesh who are the children of Elohim, but the children of the promise are accounted for the seed.
For the word of promise is this: At this time I will come, and there will be a son to Sara.
And not this only, but also Repqa, when she had partnership with one ‹man›, our father Yitz'chak,
before her children were born and had not done good or evil, the choice of Elohim was made known beforehand, that it might stand, not by works but by him who calls.
For it was said that the elder will be servant to the younger.
As it is written: I loved Ya'akov, and I hated Esau.
What then shall we say? Is there injustice with Elohim? Far be it.
Also to Moshe he said: I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will pity whom I pity.
So then it is not of the one who wills, nor of the one who runs, but of Elohim who has mercy.
For he said in the writing to Pharaoh: For this very thing I raised you up, that I might show my power in you, and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
So then he has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens.
And perhaps you will say: Why then does he find fault? For who has stood against his will?
But who are you, O man, that you give answer to Elohim? Does the thing formed say to the one who formed it, Why have you formed me like this?
Or does the potter not have authority over his clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honor and one for dishonor?
And if Elohim, wanting to show his wrath and make known his power, endured with much long-suffering the vessels of wrath that are completed for destruction,
and poured out his mercies on the vessels of mercy that were prepared beforehand by Elohim for glory,
even us whom he has called, not only from the Yehudaye but also from the peoples.
As also in Hoshea he says: I will call those who were not my people, my people; and her who was not pitied, I have pitied.
For it will be that in the place where they were called Not my people, there they will be called sons of the living Elohim.
But Eshaya proclaimed concerning the sons of Yisrael: If the number of the sons of Yisrael should be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of them will live.
For he has finished and cut short the matter, and Master YHWH will do it on the earth.
And as Eshaya said before: If Master YHWH of hosts had not left us a remnant, we would have been as Sodom, and we would have been like Amora.
What then shall we say? That the peoples who were not running after righteousness have attained righteousness, even the righteousness that is from faith.
But Yisrael, who was running after the law of righteousness, did not attain the law of righteousness.
Why? Because ‹they sought it› not from faith, but from the works of the law. For they stumbled at the stone of stumbling.
As it is written: See, I place in Tsiyon a stone of stumbling and a stone of offense, and whoever believes in him will not be ashamed.
My brothers, the desire of my heart and my petition to Elohim for them is that they may live.
For I bear witness about them that a zeal for Elohim is in them, but not according to knowledge.
For they have not known the righteousness of Elohim, but have sought to establish the righteousness of their own selves, and because of this they have not submitted to the righteousness of Elohim.
For the Mashiyach is the aim of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.
For Moshe writes thus of the righteousness that is by the law: The one who does these things will live by them.
But the righteousness that is by faith says thus: Do not say in your heart, Who has gone up to heaven and brought the Mashiyach down?
Or, Who goes down to the abyss of Sheol and brings up the Mashiyach from the house of the dead?
But what does it say? The word is near to you, to your mouth and to your heart: this is the word of faith that we proclaim.
And if you confess with your mouth our Master Y'shua, and believe in your heart that Elohim raised him from the house of the dead, you will live.
For the heart that believes in him is justified, and the mouth that confesses him is given life.
For the writing says: Everyone who believes in him will not be ashamed.
And in this it does not distinguish, neither for the Yehudi nor for the Aramean. For there is one Master YHWH of them all, who is rich toward everyone who calls on him.
For everyone who calls on the name of Master YHWH will live.
How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe in him of whom they have not heard? Or how will they hear without a preacher?
Or how will they preach if they are not sent? As it is written: How beautiful are the feet of those who announce peace, and of those who announce good things!
But not all of them have obeyed the proclamation of the gospel. For Eshaya said: My Master, who has believed our report?
So then faith is from the hearing of the ear, and the hearing of the ear is from the word of Elohim.
But I say: Have they not heard? And their proclamation has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
But I say, Did Yisrael not know? First Moshe says thus: I will make you jealous by a people that is not a people, and by a people that is not persuaded I will anger you.
But Esha'ya is bold and says: I was seen by those who did not seek me, and I was found by those who did not ask for me.
But to Yisrael he says: All the day I have stretched out my hands toward a people that contends and is not persuaded.
But I say: Has Elohim cast off his people? Far be it. For I also am of Yisrael, of the seed of Avraham, of the tribe of Benyamin.
Elohim has not cast off his people whom he knew from before. Or do you not know what he said in the writing of Eliyahu, when he complained to Elohim against Yisrael and said:
My Master, they have killed your prophets and have thrown down your altars, and I alone am left, and they seek my life.
And it was said to him by revelation: Look, I have left for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed their knees and have not worshipped Baal.
So also in this time a remnant is left by the election of grace.
But if by grace, it is not from works: otherwise grace is not grace. And if by works, it is not from grace: otherwise work is not work.
What then? Yisrael did not find what it was seeking. But the election found it, and the rest of them were blinded in their heart.
as it is written: Elohim gave them a spirit of stupor, and eyes that they would not see with them, and ears that they would not hear, until this very day.
And Dawid again says: Let their table become a snare before them, and their recompense a stumbling block.
Let their eyes be darkened so they will not see, and let their back be bowed down at all times.
But I say: Have they stumbled so as to fall? Far be it. Rather, by their stumbling life has come to the nations, for ‹awakening› their jealousy.
And if their stumbling was riches to the world, and their condemnation riches to the nations, how much more their fullness?
But to you Gentiles I am speaking: I who am an apostle of the Gentiles, I glorify my ministry;
if perhaps I may provoke jealousy in the children of my flesh, and give life to some of them.
For if their rejection was a reconciliation of the world, how much more then will their return be but life from among the dead?
And if the first-fruits ‹are› holy, then the lump ‹is› also: and if the root is holy, then also the branches.
And if some of the branches were broken off, and you, a wild olive, were grafted in their place, and became a partaker of the root and fatness of the olive;
do not boast over the branches. And if you boast, you do not support the root, but the root supports you.
And perhaps you will say, The branches were broken off so that I might be grafted into their place.
Well said. These were broken off because they did not believe, but you stand by faith. Do not be lifted up in your mind, but fear.
For if Elohim did not spare the branches that are from their nature, perhaps he will not spare you either.
Look therefore at the kindness and the severity of Elohim: on those who fell, severity; but on you, kindness, if you continue in that kindness; and if not, you also will be broken off.
And they, if they do not continue in their lack of faith, even they will be grafted in; for Elohim is able to graft them in again.

For if you, who are from the wild olive tree that is natural to you, were broken off and contrary to your nature were grafted into the good olive tree, how much more then may they be grafted into their natural olive tree?

For I want you to know this mystery, my brothers, so that you will not be wise in the thinking of your own selves: that a blindness of heart has in some measure come upon Yisrael until the fullness of the peoples comes in.
And then all Yisrael will live, as it is written: A deliverer will come from Tsiyon and will turn away iniquity from Ya'akov.
And then they will have the covenant that is from me, when I have forgiven them their sins.
But in the good news they are enemies for your sake, and in the election they are beloved for the fathers' sake.
For Elohim does not change in his free gift and in his calling.
For as you also were formerly not persuaded toward Elohim, and now you have obtained mercy because of their not being persuaded;
So also these have not been persuaded now to the mercy that is upon you, that mercy may also be upon them.
For Elohim has shut up every man in disobedience, that he may have mercy on every man.
O the depth of the riches and the wisdom and the knowledge of Elohim! For man has not searched out his judgments, and his ways are not tracked.
For who has known the mind of Master YHWH? Or who has been a counselor to him?
And who has first given to him, and then received from him?
Because all is from him, and all in him, and all in his hand: to him be praises and blessings forever and ever. Amen.
I beg you therefore, my brothers, by the mercies of Elohim, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to Elohim, by a rational service ‹of him›.
And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your minds, and discern what is the good and acceptable and perfect will of Elohim.

But I say by the grace that was given to me, to all of you, that you not think beyond what is proper for you to think, but think with humility, each one as Elohim has distributed to him the measure of faith.
For as we have many members in one body, and all the members do not have one function,
so also we who are many are one body in the Mashiyach, and each one of us is a member of one another.
But we have differing gifts according to the grace that was given to us. There is that of prophecy, according to the measure of his faith.
And there is that of service; he has it in his service. And there is that of a teacher; he in his teaching.
And there is that of an encourager, in his encouraging. And of one who gives, with simplicity. And of one who stands at the head, with diligence. And of one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
Do not let your love be deceitful, but be haters of what is evil and cling to what is good.
Be affectionate to your brothers and love one another. Be foremost in honoring one another.
Be diligent and not lazy. Be fervent in spirit. Be serving your Master.
Be joyful in your hope. Be patient in your afflictions. Be constant in prayer.
Be sharers in the needs of the holy ones. Be loving to strangers.
Bless those who persecute you: bless, and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep.
And what you think of yourselves, ‹think› also of your brothers. And do not think high thoughts, but cling to those who are lowly. And do not be wise in your own thinking.
And do not repay anyone evil for evil, but let it be your care to do good before all people.
And if it is possible, as far as it is from you, make peace with every person.
And do not be avengers of yourselves, my beloved, but give place to wrath. For it is written: If you do not execute judgment for yourself, I will execute your judgment, says Elohim.
And if your adversary is hungry, feed him, and if he is thirsty, give him drink. And if you do these things to him, you will heap coals of fire on his head.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Let every soul be subject to the authorities of greatness. For there is no authority that is not from Elohim, and those authorities that exist are appointed from Elohim.
So the one who stands against the authority stands against the ordinance of Elohim, and those who stand against them will receive judgment.
For judges are not a terror to good deeds, but to evil ones. Do you want, then, not to fear the authority? Do good, and you will have praise from it.
For he is a minister of Elohim to you for good. But if you do evil, fear; for he is not girded with the sword in vain. For he is a minister of Elohim and an avenger of wrath to those who do evil.
And because of this it is necessary for us to be subject, not only because of wrath, but also because of our conscience.
Because of this you also pay head-money; for they are ministers of Elohim who stand over these things.
Pay back therefore to everyone as is due to him: to whom head-money, head-money; and to whom tax, tax; and to whom fear, fear; and to whom honor, honor.
And owe nothing to anyone, except to love one another. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

For this also which it says: You will not commit adultery, and you will not kill, and you will not steal, and you will not covet; and if there is any other commandment, it is completed in this word: You will love your neighbor as yourself.
Love does no evil to his neighbor, because love is the fulfillment of the law.
And this also know, that it is the time and the hour from now on that we should wake from our sleep. For now our life has drawn nearer to us than when we believed.
The night now has passed, and the day has drawn near. Let us therefore put away from us the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light.
And let us walk in a seemly way, as in the day; not in revelry, and not in drunkenness, and not in impure beds, and not in envy and strife.
But put on our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, and do not be thoughtful for your flesh, for desires.
To the one who is feeble in the faith, reach out a hand to him. And do not be divided in your thoughts.
For there is one who believes he may eat everything, and the one who is feeble eats herbs.
And the one who eats should not despise the one who does not eat, and the one who does not eat should not judge the one who eats, for Elohim has received him.

Who are you that you judge a servant who is not yours? If he stands, he stands to his master, and if he falls, he falls to his master. But he will stand, for it is in the hand of his master to make him stand.
There is one who judges day from day, and there is one who judges all the days alike. But let each one be sure in his own mind.

The one who regards a day regards ‹it› for his master, and the one who does not regard a day, for his master he does not regard ‹it.› And the one who eats eats for his master and gives thanks to Elohim, and the one who does not eat, for his master he does not eat, and gives thanks to Elohim.
For there is no one of us who lives for himself, and there is no one who dies for himself.
Because if we live, we live to our Master, and if we die, we die to our Master. So whether we live or whether we die, we are our Master's.
For this reason the Mashiyach also died and lived and rose, that he might be Master YHWH to the dead and to the living.
But you, why do you judge your brother? Or you also, why do you despise your brother? For we are all going to stand before the judgment seat of the Mashiyach,
as it is written: As I live, says Master YHWH, to me every knee will bow, and to me every tongue will confess.
So then every one of us will give an account for himself to Elohim.
So then let us not judge one another, but rather decide this more carefully: that you do not set a stumbling-block for your brother.
For I know and am persuaded in Master YHWH Y'shua that nothing is unclean of itself; but to the one who thinks anything unclean, to him alone it is unclean.
But if because of food you grieve your brother, you are not walking in love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom the Mashiyach died.
And do not let our good be blasphemed.
For the kingdom of Elohim is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Ruach haKodesh.
For the one who in these things serves the Mashiyach is pleasing to Elohim and approved before people.
Now let us run after peace, and after the building up of one another.
And let us not, because of food, destroy the work of Elohim. For everything is, ‹indeed,› pure; but it is evil to the person who eats with stumbling.
It is good that we not eat flesh, and not drink wine, and not anything by which our brother is stumbled.
You who have faith, keep it in yourself before Elohim. Blessed is the one who does not condemn his soul in the thing he allows.
For the one who doubts and eats is condemned, because it is not in faith. For everything that is not from faith is sin.
We who are strong, then, are obligated to bear the weakness of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
But each of us should please his neighbor in what is good, for building up.
Because the Mashiyach also did not please himself; but as it is written: The insults of those who insult you fell on me.
For everything that was written of old was written for our instruction, so that by patience and by the comfort of the writings we might have hope.
And may Elohim of patience and of comfort give you to think in harmony one with another in Y'shua the Mashiyach;
so that with one mind and with one mouth you may glorify Elohim, the Father of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
Because of this, be receiving and bearing one another, just as the Mashiyach also received you, to the glory of Elohim.
Now I say that Y'shua the Mashiyach ministered to the circumcision for the truth of Elohim, so that he might confirm the promises ‹made› to the fathers;
and that the peoples might glorify Elohim for his mercies upon them, as it is written: I will confess to you among the peoples, and to your name I will sing.
And again he said: Rejoice, peoples, with his people.
And again he said: Praise Master YHWH, all you peoples; ‹and› laud him, all you nations.
And again Eshaya said: There will be a root of Yishai; and he who will arise will be a head for the peoples; and in him the peoples will hope.
Now may Elohim of hope fill you with all joy and peace in faith, that you may abound in his hope by the power of the Ruach haKodesh.
Now I am persuaded even I concerning you, my brothers, that you also are full of goodness and are complete in all knowledge, and are able also to instruct others.
Yet I have written rather boldly to you, my brothers, so as to remind you, because of the grace that was given to me from Elohim,
that I should be a minister of Y'shua the Mashiyach among the peoples and labor for the gospel of Elohim, that the offering of the peoples might be acceptable and sanctified by the Ruach haKodesh.
I have therefore a boasting in Y'shua the Mashiyach before Elohim.
For I do not presume to speak of anything ‹done› which Mashiyach has not wrought by my hands for the obedience of the peoples, in word and in deed,
by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of his Ruach of Elohim; so that from Urishlim I have made a circuit as far as Illyricum, and have fulfilled the announcement of the Mashiyach;
while I am careful not to announce where the name of the Mashiyach has been called, so that I do not build on a foreign foundation;
but as it is written: Those to whom it was not told about him will see him; and those who have not heard will be persuaded.
Because of this I have been hindered many times from coming to you.
But now, because there is no place for me in these regions, and I have longed for many years to come to you,
when I go to Spain, I hope to come and see you; and that you will accompany me there, when I have been satisfied a little from much with seeing you.
But now I am going to Urishlim to serve the holy ones.
For those in Macedonia and in Achaia have been willing that a contribution should be theirs with the poor holy ones who are in Urishlim.
They were willing because they are also debtors to them: for if the peoples have shared with them in the spirit, they are debtors to serve them also in the flesh.
When therefore I have finished this and sealed to them this fruit, I will pass by you to Spain.
But I know that when I come to you, I come in the fullness of the blessing of the good news of the Mashiyach.
But I ask of you, my brothers, by our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach and by the love of the Spirit, that you labor with me in prayer for me to Elohim.
that I may be delivered from those in Yehuda who do not obey, and that the service which I am bringing to the holy ones in Urishlim may be received well;
and that I may come to you with joy by the will of Elohim, and may be refreshed with you.
But may the Elohim of peace be with you all. Amen.
I commend to you Phoibe our sister, who is a minister of the assembly of Qenkraus:
that you may receive her in our Master as is right for the holy ones, and stand by her in every matter she asks of you, because she also has been a support to many and also to me.
Greet Prisqila and Aqlas, my fellow-workers in Y'shua the Mashiyach,
who for my life laid down their own necks; and not only I give thanks to them, but also all the assemblies of the peoples.
And greet the assembly that is in their house. Greet my beloved Epenetos, who is the firstfruits of Akaia in the Mashiyach.
Greet Maryam, who has labored much among you.
Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives, who were captives with me, and they are known among the apostles, and they were in the Mashiyach before me.
Greet Amplias, my beloved in our Master.
Greet Urbanus, a laborer with us in the Mashiyach, and my beloved Stachys.
Greet Apelles, chosen in our Master. Greet the members of the house of Aristobulus.
Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet the members of the house of Narcissus who are in our Master.
