Greet Asyncritus, and Phlegon, and Hermas, and Patrobas, and Hermes, and the brothers who are with them.
Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the holy ones who are with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the assemblies of the Mashiyach greet you.
And I beg you, my brothers, that you beware of those who cause divisions and stumblings ‹among you›, aside from the teaching which you have learned, and that you keep away from them.
For those who are such do not serve our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, but their own belly; and by pleasant words and by blessings they deceive the hearts of the simple.
But your obedience has become known to every person. I therefore rejoice in you, and I want you to be wise toward what is good, and pure toward what is evil.
But the Elohim of peace will soon crush Satana under your feet. The grace of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach be with you.
Timotheos, the laborer who is with me, and Luqiyos and Aison and Sosipatros, my kinsmen, ask for your peace.
I, Tartiyos, who wrote the letter, ask for your peace in our Master.
Gayos, who receives me and the whole assembly, asks for your peace. Aristus, the steward of the city, and Quwartos a brother, ask for your peace.
Now to him who is able to establish you in my gospel, which is proclaimed about Y'shua the Mashiyach, by the revelation of the mystery that was hidden from the times of the ages,
But it has been revealed in this time by the writings of the prophets, and by the command of the eternal Elohim it has been made known to all the peoples for the hearing of faith.
To him who alone is wise be glory through Y'shua the Mashiyach forever and ever. Amen.
The grace of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach be with all of you. Amen.
Paulos, called and an apostle of Y'shua the Mashiyach by the will of Elohim, and Sosthenes a brother;

to the assembly of Elohim that is at Corinth, to the ‹people› called and holy, who are made holy in Y'shua the Mashiyach; and to all those who call on the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach in every place, theirs and ours ‹Master›:
Grace ‹be› with you, and peace, from Elohim our Father and from our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
I thank my Elohim at all times on your behalf for the grace of Elohim that was given to you in Y'shua the Mashiyach;
that in everything you are enriched in him, in every word and in all knowledge;
as the testimony of Mashiyach was confirmed among you:
so that you are not lacking in any one of his gifts, but you are waiting for the revelation of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach
who will confirm you until the end, so that you may be without blame in the day of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach
Elohim is faithful, by whose hand you were called into the fellowship of his Son Y'shua the Mashiyach our Master

But I ask of you, my brothers, in the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, that there may be one word for all of you, and that there may not be divisions among you, but that you may be perfected in one mind and in one thought
For it has been reported to me concerning you, my brothers, from the house of Chloe, that there are contentions among you
But this I say: that there are some of you who say, I am of Paulos, and some who say, I am of Apolos, and some who say, I am of Keefa, and some who say, I am of Mashiyach
Has Mashiyach been divided? Or was Paulos crucified for you? Or were you immersed in the name of Paulos?
I thank my Elohim that I immersed none of you, except Krispos and Gaius;
so that no one may say that I immersed in my name.
I immersed also the household of Stephanas; but beyond that I do not know whether I immersed any other.
For Mashiyach did not send me to immerse, but to proclaim; not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Mashiyach be made empty.
For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing; but to us who are living it is the power of Elohim.
For it is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and I will dissipate the intelligence of the sagacious.
Where is the wise? Or where is the scribe? Or where is the disputant of this world? Has not Elohim made foolish the wisdom of this world?
For since in the wisdom of Elohim the world through wisdom did not know Elohim, Elohim was pleased through the foolishness of the proclamation to give life to those who believe.
Because the Yehudaye ask for signs, and the Aramaye seek wisdom.
But we proclaim Mashiyach crucified, ‹which is› a stumbling-block to the Yehudaye and foolishness to the Aramaye;
but to those who are called, both Yehudaye and Aramaye, Mashiyach is the power of Elohim and the wisdom of Elohim.
Because the foolishness of Elohim is wiser than the sons of men, and the feebleness of Elohim is stronger than the sons of men.
For look also at your calling, my brothers, that not many among you are wise in the flesh, and not many among you are mighty, and not many among you are of high birth.
But Elohim has chosen the foolish ones of the world to shame the wise, and he has chosen the feeble ones of the world to shame the mighty;
and he has chosen those of low birth in the world, and the despised, and those who are nothing, to bring to nothing those who are,
so that no flesh might glory before him.
And you also are of him in Y'shua the Mashiyach, who has become to us wisdom from Elohim, and righteousness and holiness and redemption.
as it is written: the one who glories, let him glory in Master YHWH.
And I, my brothers, when I came to you, did not preach to you the mystery of Elohim with magnificent speech, nor with wisdom.
And I did not set my soul among you as if I knew anything, except Y'shua the Mashiyach, and him also as crucified.
And I was with you in much fear and in trembling.
And my speech and my preaching were not with the persuasiveness of words of wisdom, but with the demonstration of the Ruach and of power,
so that your faith would not be in the wisdom of men, but in the power of Elohim.
Yet we speak wisdom among the perfect; wisdom not of this world, nor of the rulers of this world who are coming to nothing.
But we speak the wisdom of Elohim in a mystery, that which was hidden, and which Elohim predetermined before the world for our glory:
which none of the rulers of this world knew; for if they had known it, they would not have crucified the Master of glory.
But as it is written: Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and it has not risen upon the heart of a son of man, that which Elohim has prepared for those who love him.
But Elohim has revealed it to us by his Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of Elohim.
For who is the son of man who knows what is in a son of man, except the spirit of the son of man that is in him? So also, what is in Elohim no one knows, except the Spirit of Elohim.
But we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that is from Elohim, that we may know the gifts that are given to us from Elohim.
Which things we also speak; not in the teaching of the words of the wisdom of the sons of men, but in the teaching of the Spirit; and to spiritual ones we compare spiritual things.
For a man who is in the soul does not receive spiritual things, for they are foolishness to him, and he is not able to know them, because they are judged by the Spirit.
But the spiritual one judges all things, and he is judged by no one.
For who has known the mind of Master YHWH, that he may teach him? But we have the mind of the Mashiyach.
And I, my brothers, could not speak with you as with spiritual ‹persons›, but as with carnal, and as with babes in Mashiyach.
I gave you milk to drink, and I did not give you solid food, for you were not yet able; but neither now are you able.
For you are still in the flesh. For where there is among you envy and strife and division, are you not carnal, and walking in the flesh?
For when one of you says, I am of Paulos, and another says, I am of Apolos, are you not carnal?
For who is Paulos, or who is Apolos, but ministers by whose hand you believed, each one as Master YHWH gave to him?
I planted, and Apolos watered, but Elohim made it grow.
So then he who plants is nothing, nor he who waters, but Elohim who makes it grow.
Now he who plants and he who waters are one, and each receives his wage according to his labor.
For we labor with Elohim, and you are Elohim's husbandry and Elohim's building.
And according to the grace of Elohim that was given to me, I laid a foundation like a wise architect, but another builds on it. Let each one see how he builds on it.
For no one can lay another foundation besides the one that is laid, which is Y'shua the Mashiyach.
And if anyone builds on this foundation gold or silver or precious stones or wood or hay or stubble,
The work of each one is revealed, for the day reveals it, because it is revealed by fire; and the fire will test the work of each one, of what sort it is.
And he whose work that he built remains will receive his reward.
And he whose work burns will suffer loss; yet he himself will escape, but so as from fire.
Do you not know that you are the temple of Elohim, and the Spirit of Elohim dwells in you?
And whoever ruins the temple of Elohim, Elohim will ruin him; for the temple of Elohim is holy, which ‹temple› you are.
Let no one deceive himself. Whoever among you thinks he is wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may be wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with Elohim: for it is written, He catches the wise in their craftiness.
And again: Master YHWH knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are empty.
Because of this, let no one boast in humans: for everything is yours;
whether Paulos or Apolos or Keefa or the world or life or death or things present or things to come; everything is yours;
and you are of Mashiyach, and Mashiyach is of Elohim.
So let us be accounted by you as ministers of Mashiyach and stewards of the mysteries of Elohim.
Here then it is required in stewards that a man be found faithful.
But this is a small thing to me that I am judged by you or by any son of man. But neither do I judge myself.
For I am not conscious in myself of anything ‹flagrant›, yet I am not justified by this, for my judge is Master YHWH.

Therefore do not judge before the time ‹or› until Master YHWH comes, who will light up the hidden things of darkness and reveal the thoughts of ‹men's› hearts, and then each one will have ‹due› praise from Elohim.

These things, my brothers, I have applied to the person of myself and of Apolos for your sakes, that in us you may learn not to think ‹of men› above what is written, and that no one may exalt himself over his companion because of any person.
For who explores you? Or what do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as if you did not receive it?
Already you are full, and you have become rich, and without us you have reigned as kings! And I wish you had reigned, that we also might reign with you.
For I suppose that Elohim has set us the apostles last, as appointed to death, that we have become a spectacle to the world and to messengers and to the sons of men.
We are fools because of Mashiyach, but you are wise in Mashiyach. We are weak, and you are strong. You are praised, and we are despised.
Until this hour we hunger and thirst and are naked and are beaten and have no permanent home.
And we toil, working with our hands: they revile us, and we bless; they persecute us, and we endure.
They revile us and we entreat them; we are like the filth of the world and the scrapings of everyone up to now.
I do not write these things as shaming you, but as beloved children I admonish.
For if you have ten thousand tutors in Mashiyach, yet not many fathers; for in Y'shua the Mashiyach I begot you through the good news.
I ask of you therefore that you imitate me.
Because of this I sent Timotheos to you, who is my beloved son and faithful in Master YHWH, that he may remind you of my ways in Mashiyach, as I teach in all the assemblies.
Now some of you are puffed up as though I would not ‹dare› come to you.
But if Master YHWH wills, I will come to you quickly, and I will know not the word of those who exalt themselves, but their power.
For the kingdom of Elohim is not in word, but in power.
How do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and with a meek spirit?
It is reported that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not even named among the pagans, that a son takes his father's wife.
And you are puffed up, and have not rather sat down in mourning, so that the one who has done this deed might be removed from among you.
For I, though distant from you in body yet near to you in spirit, have already judged as if present the one who has done this.
that you all assemble in the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, and I with you in spirit, with the power of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach,
and deliver this one to Satana for the destruction of his body, so that in spirit he may have life in the day of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?
Clean out from among you the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened. For our passover is Mashiyach, who was slain for us.
Because of this let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of wickedness and of bitterness, but with the leaven of purity and of holiness.
I wrote to you in the letter not to mix with fornicators.
Yet I am not speaking of the fornicators of this world, or of the greedy, or of the rapacious, or of idol-worshippers—otherwise you would be obliged to go out from the world.

But this is what I wrote to you, that you not mix if anyone is called a brother and is a fornicator, or greedy, or an idol-worshipper, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or rapacious—with one who is such, not even to eat bread.
For what is it to me to judge those outside? You judge those who are inside.
But those outside, Elohim judges; and remove the wicked one from among you.
Does any one of you dare, when he has a case with his brother, to go to judgment before the unjust and not before the holy ones?
Or do you not know that the holy ones will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you not fit to judge the smallest cases?
Do you not know that we judge messengers? How much more the things of this world?
But if you have a case about worldly things, seat for yourselves those who are despised in the assembly!
I say this to your shame. Is it so, that there is not even one wise man among you who can decide fairly between a brother and his brother?
But a brother goes to judgment with his brother, and that before those who do not believe!
Already then you have condemned yourselves, that you have lawsuits one with another. For why do you not rather suffer wrong? And why are you not rather defrauded?
But you yourselves do wrong, and you defraud even your brothers.

Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of Elohim? Do not be deceived: neither fornicators, nor idol-worshippers, nor adulterers, nor the corrupt, nor those who lie with males,
nor oppressors, nor thieves, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners—these will not inherit the kingdom of Elohim.
And these things were in some of you: but you were washed, and you were sanctified, and you were made righteous, in the name of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach and by the Ruach of our Elohim.
Everything is permitted to me, but not everything is profitable to me. Everything is permitted to me, but no one ‹of them› will have dominion over me.
Food is for the belly, and the belly is for food; but Elohim will bring both of them to nothing. But the body is not for whoredom, but for our Master, and our Master for the body.
And Elohim has raised our Master, and he will raise us by his power.
Do you not know that your bodies are members of the Mashiyach? Shall one take the members of the Mashiyach and make them members of a harlot? Far be it.
Or do you not know that whoever joins himself to a harlot is one body ‹with her›? For it is said, The two of them shall be one body.
But he who joins himself to our Master is with him one spirit.
Flee from whoredom. Every ‹other› sin that a man commits is outside his body; but he who commits whoredom sins against his own body.
Or do you not know that your body is the temple of the Ruach haKodesh who dwells in you, whom you received from Elohim? And you are not your own.
For you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify Elohim with your body and with your spirit, which are Elohim's.
And concerning those things that you wrote to me, it is good for a man not to approach a woman.
But because of whoredom, let a man hold his wife, and let a woman hold her husband.
Let the man pay to his wife the love that is due; so also she the woman to her husband.
The woman is not authorized over her body, but her husband; so also the man is not authorized over his body, but his wife.

Do not therefore deprive one another, except when you both consent for a time that you may devote yourselves to fasting and prayer; and return again to the same matter, so that Satana may not tempt you because of the desire of your body.
But this I say as to the weak, not from a commandment.
For I desire that all people would be like me in purity. But each person is given a gift from Elohim; there is one like this, and there is one like that.
And I say to those who have no wives, and to widows, that it is advantageous for them if they remain as I am.
But if they cannot endure ‹it›, let them marry: for it is more profitable to take a wife than to burn with desire.
And to those who have wives I command—not I, but my Master—that a wife not separate from her husband.
And if she separates, let her remain without a husband, or be reconciled to her husband; and let a man not put away his wife.
And to the rest I say—I, not my Master—that if there is a brother who has a wife who does not believe, and she is willing to dwell with him, let him not put her away.
And a woman who has a husband who does not believe, and he is willing to dwell with her, let her not leave her husband.

For the man who does not believe is sanctified by the believing wife, and the wife who does not believe is sanctified by the believing man; and if not, their children are unclean; but now they are clean.
But if the one who does not believe separates, let him separate. A brother or a sister is not enslaved in these things. Elohim has called us to peace.
For what do you know, wife, whether you will give life to your husband? Or you, man, do you know whether you will give life to your wife?
But each one as Master YHWH has distributed to him, and each one as Elohim has called him, so let him walk. And so I also command to all the churches.
If a man was called while circumcised, let him not turn back to uncircumcision. And if he was called in uncircumcision, let him not be circumcised.
For circumcision is nothing, and neither is uncircumcision, but the keeping of the commandments of Elohim.
Let every person remain in the calling in which he was called.
If you were called as a servant, let it not trouble you. But even if you are able to be made free, choose for yourself to serve.
For he who was called as a servant in our Master is a freedman of Elohim. In the same way, he who was called as a free man is a servant of the Mashiyach.
You were bought with a price; do not become servants of men.
Let every one, my brothers, remain with Elohim in whatever ‹state› he was called.
And concerning virginity, I have no commandment from Elohim; but I give counsel as a man who has obtained mercy from Elohim to be a believer.
And I think this is good because of the necessity of the time, that it is advantageous for a person to remain as he is.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek a release. Are you free from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
And if you take a wife, you do not sin. And if a virgin is given to a husband, she does not sin. But those who are such will have trouble in the body; but I spare you.
And this I say, my brothers, that the time from now on is shortened, so that those who have wives should be as if they had none;
and those who weep, as if they did not weep; and those who rejoice, as if they did not rejoice; and those who buy, as if they did not possess;
and those who make use of this world, not beyond the just use: for the fashion of this world is passing away.
Because of this I want you to be without care. For he who has no wife thinks on the things of his master, how he may please his master.
And he who has a wife is anxious about the world, how he may please his wife.

But there is a difference also between a wife and a virgin. She who has not been to a man thinks on her master, that she may be holy in her body and in her spirit. And she who has a husband thinks of the world, how she may please her husband.
But this I say for your own help. I am not casting a snare on you, but that you may be constant toward your master in a beautiful fashion, while you are not thinking on the world.

But if anyone thinks he is put to shame regarding his virgin ‹daughter› because her time has passed and he has not given her to a husband, ‹and› it is fitting that he give her, let him do as he wills; he does not sin; let her marry.
But he who has truly decided in his mind, and nothing compels him, and he has authority over his will, and has so judged in his heart to keep his virgin ‹daughter›, does well.
So then he who gives his virgin ‹daughter› does well, and he who does not give his virgin ‹daughter› does even better.
A wife, as long as her husband lives, is bound by the law; but if her husband falls asleep ‹in death›, she is free to be to whom she wills, ‹yet› only in our Master.
But she is happier if she remains so, according to my own mind; and I think that I also have the Ruach of Elohim in me.
Now concerning sacrifices to idols, we know that in all of us there is knowledge; and knowledge puffs up, but love builds.
But if anyone thinks that he knows something, he does not yet know anything as he ought to know ‹it›.
But if anyone loves Elohim, this one is known by him.
Therefore concerning the eating of the sacrifices of idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no other Elohim except one.
For even if there are those called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, as there are many gods and many masters,
yet for us there is one Elohim, the Father, from whom are all things, and we in him; and one Master YHWH, Y'shua the Mashiyach, by whom are all things, and we also by him.
But there is not ‹this› knowledge in every person; for there are some who until now in their conscience eat ‹it› as sacrificed to idols; and because their conscience is weak, it is defiled.
But food does not bring us near to Elohim; for if we eat, we do not abound; and if we do not eat, we are not in want.
See then that this authority of yours does not become a stumbling-block to the weak.
For if someone sees you who have knowledge reclining in an idol house, will not his conscience, because he is weak, be strengthened to eat what is sacrificed?
And by your knowledge he who is weak, for whom Mashiyach died, will perish.
And if you sin like this against your brothers and wound their weak consciences, you sin against Mashiyach.
Because of this, if food is a stumbling-block to my brother, I will forever eat no flesh, so that I do not cause my brother to stumble.
Am I not a free man? Or am I not an apostle? Or have I not seen Y'shua the Mashiyach our Master? Or have you not been my work in my Master?
And if to others I have not been an apostle, yet to you I am; and you are the seal of my apostleship.
And ‹my› defense to those who judge me is this:
Do we not have authority to eat and to drink?
Or do we not have authority to take around a sister as a wife, just as the rest of the apostles, and as the brothers of our Master, and as Keefa?
Or only I and Bar-Naba, do we not have authority not to work?
Who is it that serves in war at his own expense? Or who is it that plants a vineyard and does not eat from its fruits? Or who is it that tends a flock and does not eat from the milk of his flock?
Do I say these things as a man? See, the law also says these things.
For it is written in the law of Moshe: You shall not muzzle the ox that is threshing. Is Elohim concerned about oxen?
But it is clear that he said it for our sake. And indeed it was written for our sake, because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the one who threshes in hope of the crop.
If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it a great thing if we reap bodily things from you?

And if others have authority over you, do we not have it still more? Yet we have not used this authority, but we endure everything so that we might not hinder the announcement of the Mashiyach in anything.
Do you not know that those who serve in the house of holiness are sustained from the house of holiness, and those who serve at the altar share with the altar?
In this way also our Master has commanded that those who proclaim his good news should live from his good news.
But I have used none of these things, and I have not written this so that it would be so for me; for it is better for me to die than that anyone should empty my boasting.
For while I proclaim, I have no ‹ground of› boasting, because necessity is laid on me, and woe to me if I do not proclaim.
For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward; but if not of my own will, a stewardship is entrusted to me.
What then is my reward? ‹It is,› that when I proclaim, I make the good news of the Mashiyach without cost, and do not use the authority given me in the good news.
For though I am free from all of them, I have subjected myself to every person, that I might gain many.
And with the Yehudaye I was as a Yehudaya, that I might gain the Yehudaye; and with those under the law I was as under the law, that I might gain those who are under the law;
and to those who have no law I was as without law, ‹though I am not without law to Elohim, but in the law of the Mashiyach›, that I might gain those who are without law.
I was with the weak as weak, that I might gain the weak. I became all things to every person, that I might give life to every one.
And this I do, that I may be a partner in the announcement.
Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all run, but one receives the victory? Run so that you may attain.
But every person who does the contest holds his mind from everything. And these run that they may take a crown that perishes; but we, one that does not perish.
I therefore thus run, not as upon something that is not known; and thus I struggle, not as one who beats the air.
But I subdue my body and make it subject, lest somehow when I have proclaimed to others, I myself should be rejected.
But I want you to know, my brothers, that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all of them passed through the sea;
and all of them were immersed by Moshe in the cloud and in the sea;
and all of them ate one food of the spirit;
and all of them drank one drink of the spirit; for they were drinking from the rock of the spirit that was coming with them, and that rock was Mashiyach.
But Elohim was not pleased with many of them, for they fell in the wilderness.
Now these things were a type for us, that we should not desire evil things as they desired.
And neither should we be servants of idols, as also some of them served, as it is written: The people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.
And neither should we commit whoredom, as some of them committed whoredom, and there fell in one day twenty-three thousand.
And let us not test the Mashiyach, as some of them tested, and the serpents destroyed them.
And neither murmur, as some of them murmured, and they perished by the hands of the destroyer.
But all these things that happened to them were for types, and they were written for our admonition, on whom the ends of the ages have come.
Therefore let him who thinks he stands beware that he does not fall.

No trial has come upon you except what is of the sons of men. But Elohim is faithful, who will not let you be tried beyond what you are able, but will make a way out for your trial so that you may be able to endure.
Because of this, my beloved, flee from the service of idols.
I speak as to the wise; you judge what I say.
The cup of thanksgiving that we bless, is it not a communion of the blood of the Mashiyach? And the bread that we break, is it not a communion of the body of the Mashiyach?
As that bread is one, so we all are one body; for we all take from that one bread.
Look at Yisrael who are in the flesh; are not those who eat the sacrifices sharers of the altar?
What then am I saying? That an idol is anything? Or that a sacrifice of idols is anything? No.
But what the pagans sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to Elohim. And I do not want you to be partners with demons.
You cannot drink the cup of our Master and the cup of demons, and you cannot share in the table of our Master and in the table of demons.
Or are we provoking our Master to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
Everything is allowed to me, but not everything is helpful. Everything is allowed to me, but not everything builds up.
Let no one seek his own, but each one also that of his neighbor.
Everything that is sold in the meat-market, eat without inquiry because of conscience.
for the earth is Master YHWH's, in its fullness.
And if someone from the pagans invites you, and you want to go, eat everything that is set before you, without inquiry because of conscience.
But if someone says to you, This is of a sacrifice, do not eat, because of him who told you, and because of conscience.
But conscience, I say, is not yours, but his who told ‹you›. For why is my freedom judged by another's conscience?
If I partake by grace, why am I reviled for that for which I give thanks?
If therefore you eat, or if you drink, or if you do anything, do all things for the glory of Elohim.
Be without offense to the Yehudaye, and to the Aramaye, and to the assembly of Elohim:
even as I also, in everything, please every person; and I do not seek what is profitable to me, but what is profitable to many, that they may live.
Imitate me, just as I also ‹imitate› Mashiyach.
But I praise you, my brothers, that in everything you remember me, and that you hold the commandments as I delivered ‹them› to you.
But I want you to know that the head of every man is Mashiyach, and the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Mashiyach is Elohim.
Every man who prays or prophesies while covering his head dishonors his head.
And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for she is equal with her whose head is shaved.
For if a woman is not covered, let her also be shorn. But if it is shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaved, let her be covered.
For a man ought not to cover his head, because he is the likeness and glory of Elohim; but the woman is the glory of the man.
For the man is not from the woman, but the woman from the man.
For neither was the man created for the woman, but the woman for the man.
For this reason a woman ought to have on her head ‹the mark of› authority, because of the messengers.
Nevertheless, the man is not without the woman, nor the woman without the man, in our Master.
For as the woman ‹was› from the man, so also the man is by the woman; and everything is from Elohim.
Judge among yourselves for yourselves: is it becoming for a woman, when her head is uncovered, to pray to Elohim?
Does not even nature itself teach you that a man, when his hair grows long, it is a disgrace to him?
But a woman, when she lets her hair grow long, it is a glory to her, because her hair is given to her in place of a covering.
But if anyone is contentious about these things, we have no such custom, nor ‹has› the church of Elohim.
But this that I am commanding, I am not praising you, because you have not come together for the better, but have come down for the worse.
For first, when you assemble in the church, I hear that there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.
For there are also to be contentions among you, so that those who are approved among you may be known.
When therefore you come together, you eat and drink not as is proper for the day of our Master.
But each one eats his own supper beforehand, and one is hungry and another is drunk.
Do you not have houses in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the assembly of Elohim and shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you.
For I received from our Master that which I delivered to you, that our Master Y'shua on the night he was betrayed took bread,
and blessed and broke ‹it› and said, "Take, eat; this is my body which is broken for your sakes. Do this in remembrance of me."
So after they had supper, he also gave the cup and said: This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this whenever you drink ‹it›, for my remembrance.
For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you commemorate the death of our Master until his coming.
Whoever therefore eats of the bread of Master YHWH and drinks of his cup and is not worthy of it is guilty of the blood of Master YHWH and of his body.
For this reason a person should examine himself, and then eat of this bread and drink of this cup.
For whoever eats and drinks of it while not worthy eats and drinks condemnation on himself, not discerning the body of Master YHWH.
For this reason many among you are weak and sick, and many sleep.
For if we were judging ourselves, we would not be judged.
But when we are judged by our Master, we are chastened, that we may not be condemned with the world.
So then, my brothers, when you assemble to eat, wait for one another.
But let him who is hungry eat in his house, that you may not assemble for condemnation. And as for the rest, I will give you directions when I come.
Now concerning the spirituals, my brothers, I want you to know,
that you were pagans, and you were being led away without distinction after idols that have no voice.

Because of this I make known to you that there is no one who speaks by the Ruach of Elohim and says that Y'shua is accursed, and no one is able to say that Master YHWH is Y'shua except by the Ruach haKodesh.
Now there are diversities of gifts, but the Ruach is one.
And there are diversities of ministries, but Master YHWH is one.
And there are diversities of powers, but Elohim is one, who works all in everyone.
And to each one is given a manifestation of the Spirit, that it may help him.
There is one to whom is given by the Spirit a word of wisdom, and to another a word of knowledge by the same Spirit,
to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by the same Spirit,
and to another powers, and to another prophecy, and to another discernment of spirits, and to another ‹divers› kinds of tongues, and to another interpretation of tongues.
But all these the one Spirit works, and distributes to each one as it wills.
For as the body is one and has many members in it, and all the members of the body, though they are many, are one body, so also is the Mashiyach.
For we also, all of us, were immersed by one spirit into one body, whether Yehudaye or Aramaye, whether slaves or freeborn, and all of us drank one spirit.
For the body also is not one member, but many.
For if the foot says, Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body, is it on that account not of the body?
And if the ear says, Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body, is it on that account not of the body?
For if the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? And if it were all hearing, how would it smell?
But now Elohim has placed each one of the members in the body just as he willed.
But if they were all one member, where would the body be?
But now the members are many, yet one is the body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, You are not needed by me; nor can the head say to the feet, You are not needed by me.
But rather those members that are thought to be weak, on them is the need.
And those that we think are shameful in the body, on these we heap more abundant honor; and those that are uncomely, we make more abundant form for them.
But those members that are in us that are honorable have no need of honor; for Elohim has mixed the body and given more abundant honor to the member that is small.
so that there would be no division in the body, but that all the members equally would care one for another;
so that when one member is in pain, all of them suffer; and if one member is glorified, all the members are glorified.
Now you are the body of Mashiyach, and members in your place.

For Elohim has placed in his assembly first apostles, after them prophets, after them teachers, after them workers of powers, after them gifts of healings, and helpers, and leaders, and ‹various› kinds of tongues.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all workers of powers?
Do all have the gifts of healings? Do all speak with tongues? Or do all interpret?
But if you are zealous for the greater gifts, I show you again a better way.
If I speak in every tongue of the sons of men and of messengers, and love is not in me, I have become brass that resounds or a cymbal that gives a sound.
And if ‹the gift of› prophecy is in me, and I know all the mysteries and all knowledge, and if all faith is in me so that I move mountains, and love is not in me, I am nothing.
And if I feed out all I have to the poor, and if I hand over my body to be burned, and love is not in me, I gain nothing.
Love is long in spirit and kind; love does not envy; love is not agitated and is not puffed up;
and does not act in a shameful way, and does not seek its own, and is not provoked, and does not think evil;
does not rejoice in injustice, but rejoices in the truth;
It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
Love never falls. For prophecies will be abolished, and tongues will be silenced, and knowledge will be abolished.
For we know a little from much, and we prophesy a little from much.
But when completeness comes, then that which is little will be abolished.
When I was a child, I spoke as a child, and I reasoned as a child, and I thought as a child; but when I became a man, I abolished these things of childhood.
Now we see as in a mirror in a riddle; but then face to face. Now I know a little from much; but then I will know as I am known.
For these three are abiding: faith and hope and love; but the greatest of them is love.
Pursue love, and be zealous for the gifts of the Spirit, but especially that you may prophesy.
For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to people but to Elohim, for no one hears anything he speaks, yet in the spirit he speaks a mystery.
But he who prophesies speaks to people edification and encouragement and comfort.
He who speaks in a tongue builds up himself, and he who prophesies builds up the church.

Now I want you all to speak in tongues, but especially that you prophesy; for greater is he who prophesies than he who speaks in a tongue, unless he interprets; but if he interprets, he builds up the church.
And now, my brothers, if I come to you and speak with you in a tongue, what do I profit you, unless I speak with you either by revelation or by knowledge or by prophecy or by teaching?
For even things that have no life in them and give a sound, whether a flute or a harp, if they make no distinction between one tone and its companion, how is what is played or what is struck known?
And if a horn sounds a sound that is not distinct, who will get ready for battle?
So also you, if you speak a word in a tongue and it is not interpreted, how will what you are saying be known? You will have been to yourselves like one who speaks into the air.
For look, there are many kinds of tongues in the world, and there is not one of them without a sound.
And if I do not know the force of the sound, I am a barbarian to the one who speaks, and the one who speaks is also a barbarian to me.
So also you, because you are zealous for the gifts of the Spirit, seek to abound for the building up of the assembly.
And he who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit is praying, but my understanding is without fruit.
What then will I do? I will pray with my spirit, and I will pray also with my understanding; and I will sing with my spirit, and I will sing also with my understanding.
And if not, if you bless in the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say Amen on your thanksgiving, because he does not know what you are saying?
For you bless well, but your companion is not built up.
I thank Elohim that I speak in a tongue more than all of you.
But in the church I desire to speak five words with my understanding, so that I may also teach others, more than a myriad of words in a tongue.
My brothers, do not be children in your thoughts; but to evil things be infants, and in your thoughts be complete.
In the law it is written: With a foreign speech and with another tongue I will speak with this people; and even so they will not hear me, says Master YHWH.
Therefore tongues are set for a sign, not to the believers, but to those who do not believe. But prophecy is not for those who do not believe, but for those who believe.
If therefore the whole church assembles and they all speak in tongues, and unlearned ones or those who do not believe come in, will they not say that these people are mad?
But if all of you are prophesying, and an unlearned one or one who does not believe comes in among you, he is examined by all of you and is convicted by all of you.
and the secrets of his heart are revealed ‹to him›, and then he falls on his face and worships Elohim and says, Truly Elohim is in you.

I say therefore ‹to you›, my brothers, that when you assemble, whoever of you has a psalm, let him speak, and whoever has a teaching, and whoever has a revelation, and whoever has a tongue, and whoever has an interpretation. Let them all be for building up.
And if anyone speaks in a tongue, let two speak, and at most three, and let them speak one by one, and let one interpret.
And if there is no one who interprets, let him who speaks in a tongue be silent in the assembly, and let him speak to himself and to Elohim.
But prophets, let two or three speak, and let the rest discern.
And if it is revealed to another who is sitting, let the first be silent.
For you can all prophesy one by one, so that everyone may learn, and everyone be comforted.
For the spirit of the prophets is subject to the prophets.
Because Elohim is not ‹the author› of tumult, but of peace, as in all the churches of the holy ones.
Let your women be silent in the church: for it is not permitted them to speak, but to be subject, as also the law says.
And if they wish to learn anything, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for women to speak in the church.
Or did the word of Elohim go out from you? Or did it reach only to you?
And if anyone among you thinks that he is a prophet, or that he is of the spirit, let him know these things that I write to you, that they are the commandments of our Master.
But if anyone does not know, let him not know.
Therefore, my brothers, be zealous to prophesy, and do not forbid to speak in tongues.
But let everything be done with decency and in order.
And I make known to you, my brothers, the gospel which I preached to you, and which you received, and in which you stand,
and by which you have life. By what word I preached to you, if you remember, unless you believed in vain.
For I delivered to you from the first, as I received, that Mashiyach died on account of our sins, as it is written:
and that he was buried and rose on the third day, as it is written:
and that he was seen by Keefa, and after him by the twelve:
and after that, he was seen by more than five hundred brothers at once, many of whom are standing until now, and some of them have slept.
And after these he was seen by Ya'akov, and after him by all the apostles.
But last of them all, as to one untimely born, he was seen also by me.
For I am the least of the apostles, and I am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of Elohim.
But by the grace of Elohim I am what I am, and his grace that was in me was not empty; but I labored more than all of them—not I, but his grace that was with me.
Whether I then or they, so we proclaim, and so you believed.
But if Mashiyach is proclaimed that he rose from the house of the dead, how is it that there are some among you who say there is no life of the dead?
And if there is no giving of life to the dead, Mashiyach also has not risen.
And if Mashiyach has not risen, our preaching is empty, and your faith also is empty.
And we too are found false witnesses of Elohim, for we have testified of Elohim that he raised Mashiyach, when he did not raise him.
For if the dead do not rise, Mashiyach also has not risen.
And if Mashiyach has not risen, your faith is empty, and you are still in your sins.
And also those who have fallen asleep in Mashiyach have perished.
And if in this life only we hope in the Mashiyach, we are more miserable than all the sons of men.
But now Mashiyach has risen from among the dead, and has become the first-fruits of those who sleep.
And as by a man came death, so also by a man comes the life of the dead.
For as in Adam all the sons of men die, so also in the Mashiyach all live.
each one in his order; Mashiyach was the first-fruits; afterwards those who are of Mashiyach, at his coming.
And then will be the end, when he delivers the kingdom to Elohim the Father, when he has abolished every ruler and every authority and every power.
For he is going to reign until he puts all his enemies under his feet.
And the last enemy, death, is abolished.
For he has subjected all under his feet. But when it says that everything is subjected to him, it is known that he is excepted who subjected all to him.
And when all is subjected to him, then the Son himself will be subjected to him who subjected all to him, so that Elohim will be all in all.
Otherwise, what will they do who are immersed for the dead, if the dead do not rise? Why are they immersed for the dead?
And why also do we stand in peril every hour?
I swear by your boasting, my brothers, which I have in our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, that I die every day.
If as among men I was thrown to wild beasts at Ephesos, what did I gain? If the dead do not rise, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Do not be deceived; evil talk corrupts good minds.
Awaken your hearts righteously and do not sin, for there are people in whom there is no knowledge of Elohim; I say this to your shame.
Someone among you will say, How do the dead rise, and with what body do they come?
Fool! The seed that you sow does not live unless it dies.
And what you sow, you do not sow the body that is to be, but the naked grain of wheat or of barley or of the rest of the seeds.
But Elohim gives it a body as he wills, and to each one of the seeds a body of its nature.
But not every body is the same, for another is the body of a son of man, and another of a beast, and another of a bird, and another of a fish.
And there are heavenly bodies and there are earthly bodies, but another is the glory of the heavenly ‹bodies› and another of the earthly.
And another is the glory of the sun, and another the glory of the moon, and another the glory of the stars, and a star exceeds a star in glory.
So also the life of the dead: they are sown in corruption, they rise without corruption.
They are sown in dishonor, they rise in glory. They are sown in weakness, they rise in power.
It is sown a soulish body, it rises a spiritual body. For there is a body of the soul, and there is a body of the spirit.
So also it is written: Adam the first man became a living soul; and the last Adam ‹became› a life-giving spirit.
But the spiritual was not first, but the soulish, and then the spiritual.
The first man is of dust from the earth; the second man is Master YHWH from heaven.
As is the one of dust, so also are those of dust; and as is the one from heaven, so also are the heavenly.
And as we have worn the likeness of him who is from the dust, so we will wear the likeness of him who is from heaven.
But this I say, my brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of heaven, and corruption does not inherit incorruption.
I tell you a mystery: we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
in a moment, as in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet, when it sounds, and the dead will rise without corruption, and we will be changed.
For this which is corruptible is ready to put on incorruption, and this which dies to put on immortality.
And when this which is corruptible puts on incorruption, and this which dies puts on immortality, then will take place the word that is written: Death is swallowed up in victory.
Where is your sting, death? Or where is your victory, Sheol?
But the sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks to Elohim who gives us the victory through our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
So then, my brothers and my beloved, be steadfast and do not be shaken, but be abounding at all times in the work of Master YHWH, knowing that your labor is not empty in Master YHWH.
Now concerning the collection for the holy ones, as I directed the assemblies of Galatia, so you also do.
On every first day of the week, each one of you is to set aside and keep at his house whatever comes into his hands, so that collections will not be made when I come.
And when I come, those whom you select I will send with letters to carry your gift to Urishlim.
But if it is fitting that I also go, they will go with me.
But I will come to you when I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.
And perhaps I will also stay with you, or spend the winter with you, so that you may accompany me to the place where I am going.
For I do not want to see you now as one passing on the way; for I hope to remain a time with you, if my Master permits me.
But I am remaining in Ephesos until Pentecost.
For a great door has been opened to me that is full of work, and the opposers are many.
But if Timotheos comes to you, see that he is without fear among you; for he does the work of Master YHWH, like me.
Therefore let no one despise him, but send him on in peace so that he may come to me; for I am waiting for him with the brothers.
But concerning Apolos my brother, I asked him much that he would come to you with the brothers, and it was not at all his will to come to you now; but when he has opportunity, he will come to you.
Be awake and stand firm in the faith; act like men, be strong.
And let all your affairs be in love.
But I ask of you, my brothers, concerning the household of Stephanas, because you know that they are the first-fruits of Achaia, and they have set their soul to the service of the holy ones;
that you also be subject to those who are such, and to everyone who labors with us and helps.
But I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas and of Fortunatus and of Achaicus, for they have filled what you lacked toward me.
For they have refreshed my spirit and yours; therefore acknowledge those who are such.
All the assemblies that are in Asia greet you. Aqlus and Prisqila, with the assembly in their house, greet you much in our Master.
All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
The greeting is in the handwriting of me, Paulos.
Whoever does not love our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, let him be accursed. Our Master comes.
The grace of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach be with you.
And my love be with you all, in Mashiyach Y'shua.
Paulos, an apostle of Y'shua the Mashiyach by the will of Elohim, and Timotheos a brother, to the assembly of Elohim that is in Qorinthos, and to all the holy ones that are in all Achaia.
Grace be with you, and peace, from Elohim our Father and from our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
Blessed is Elohim, the Father of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, the Father of mercies and Elohim of all comfort,
who comforts us in all our afflictions, so that we also may be able to comfort those who are in every affliction with the comfort with which we are comforted by Elohim.
For as the sufferings of the Mashiyach abound in us, so also our comfort abounds through the Mashiyach.

And if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and for your life that we are afflicted; and if we are comforted, it is so that you may be comforted, and that there may be in you an eagerness to endure those sufferings which we also suffer.
And our hope concerning you is firm, for we know that if you share in the sufferings, you also share in the consolation.
But we want you to know, our brothers, about the affliction that came upon us in Asia, that we were afflicted exceedingly beyond our strength, so that our life was near to being destroyed.
And we passed a sentence of death upon ourselves, that we might not have confidence in ourselves, but in Elohim who raises the dead;
who rescued us from near death, and again we hope that he will rescue us,
by the help of your prayers on our behalf, so that his gift toward us may be a favor done for the sake of many, and many may give thanks to him on our behalf.

For our boasting is this, the testimony of our mind, that in simplicity and in purity and by the grace of Elohim we have conducted ourselves in the world, and not in the wisdom of the flesh, and especially toward you.
We are not writing other things to you, but those that you know and also acknowledge. And I am confident that you will acknowledge them to the end.
as you have also acknowledged in part that we are your boasting, just as you also are ours, in the day of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
And in this confidence I was wanting beforehand to come to you, that you might receive grace a second time;
and pass by you into Macedonia, and again come to you from Macedonia, and ‹so› you would accompany me to Yehuda.
When therefore I purposed this, did I purpose it as one who is hasty? Or are the things I purpose of the flesh, so that there should be in them Yes, yes, and No, no?
Elohim is faithful, that our word to you was not Yes and No.
For the Son of Elohim, Y'shua the Mashiyach, who was preached to you by us, ‹namely,› by me, by Silwanus, and by Timotheos, was not Yes and No; but it was Yes in him.
For all the promises of Elohim in him, the Mashiyach, are Yes; for which cause, we through him give ‹our› Amen, to the glory of Elohim.
Now it is Elohim who establishes us, with you, in the Mashiyach, and has anointed us,
and has sealed us, and has given the earnest of his Ruach in our hearts.
Moreover, I call Elohim for a witness on my soul, that it was in order to spare you that I did not come to Corinth.
Not that we are masters over your faith, but we are helpers of your joy; for it is by faith you stand.
And I decided this in myself, that I would not come to you again in sadness.
For if I make you sad, who will make me joyful, except the one whom I made sad?
And I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I come those who ought to make me joyful would not make me sad. But I am confident concerning all of you, that my joy is that of all of you.
And from great affliction and from anguish of heart I wrote these things to you with many tears, not so that you would be sad, but so that you would know the abundant love I have toward you.
But if someone has caused sadness, he has not caused sadness to me ‹only›, but in a little measure to all of you, so that the word may not weigh heavily on you.
And this rebuke from the many is enough for this one.
so that, on the other hand, you should forgive him and console him, lest he who is such be swallowed up with excessive grief.
Because of this I ask you to confirm your love toward him.
For it was for this also that I wrote ‹to you›, that I might know by trial whether you are obedient in everything.
And whom you forgive, I also ‹forgive›: for what I forgave to anyone, for your sakes I forgave it in the face of the Mashiyach;
lest Satana overreach us; for we know his devices.
Moreover, when I came to Troas in the good news of the Mashiyach, and a door was opened to me by Master YHWH,
There was no rest for me in my spirit, because I did not find Titus my brother; but I took leave of them and went out to Macedonia.
But thanks be to Elohim, who at every time makes a triumph for us in the Mashiyach, and reveals by us the fragrance of his knowledge in every place.
For we are a sweet fragrance in the Mashiyach to Elohim, among those who live and among those who perish:
to those, a fragrance of death to death, and to those, a fragrance of life to life. And who is equal to these things?
For we are not like the rest who dilute the words of Elohim, but as in truth and as from Elohim, before Elohim we speak in the Mashiyach.
Do we begin again from the start to show you who we are? Or do we need, like others, that letters of recommendation be written to you about us, or that you write ‹and› recommend about us?
You are our letter, written on our hearts, and known and read by everyone.
For you know that you are a letter of the Mashiyach ministered by us, written not with ink but by the Ruach of the living Elohim, not on tablets of stone but on the tablets of the heart of flesh.
And such confidence we have through the Mashiyach toward Elohim.
Not that we are sufficient to think anything as from ourselves, but our power is from Elohim,
who has made us fit to be ministers of the new covenant, not of the writing but of the Ruach; for the writing kills, but the Ruach gives life.
Now if the ministry of death in writing was engraved on stones and was in glory, so that the sons of Yisrael could not look on the face of Moshe because of the glory of his face which was abolished;
how then will the ministry of the Spirit not be still more in glory?
For if the ministry of condemnation had glory, how much more will the ministry of righteousness excel in glory?
For that which was glorified is not even glorified in comparison with this excelling glory.
For if that which is abolished was in glory, much more will that which remains be in glory.
Because we have this hope, therefore we act all the more with open face.
and are not like Moshe, who threw a veil over his face, so that the sons of Yisrael would not look on the end of that which is abolished.

But they were blinded in their understanding; for until this day, when the old covenant is read, that same veil stands upon them; and it is not revealed ‹to them› that it is abolished in the Mashiyach.
And until this day, when Moshe is read, a veil is thrown upon their heart.
But when any of them turns to Master YHWH, the veil is taken from him.
Now Master YHWH is the Spirit. And where the Spirit of Master YHWH is, there is freedom.
But we all, with uncovered faces, see the glory of Master YHWH as in a mirror, and are transformed into that same likeness, from glory to glory, as from Master YHWH the Spirit.
Therefore we do not grow weary in this ministry that we hold, according to the mercies that have been upon us.

But we have renounced the concealments of shame, and we do not walk in craftiness, and we do not handle the word of Elohim deceitfully; but by the manifestation of the truth we exhibit ourselves to all the minds of the children of men before Elohim.

to those whose minds the Elohim of this world has blinded, because they do not believe, so that the light of the gospel of the glory of the Mashiyach (who is the likeness of Elohim) might not dawn upon them.
For it is not ourselves that we proclaim, but the Mashiyach Y'shua our Master; and as for ourselves, that we are your servants for the sake of Y'shua.

Because Elohim is he who said that light should dawn from darkness; he has dawned in our hearts, that we might be enlightened with the knowledge of the glory of Elohim in the face of Y'shua the Mashiyach.
But we have this treasure in vessels of clay, so that the greatness of the power may be from Elohim and not from us.
For in everything we are oppressed, but not choked; we are harassed, but we are not condemned;
we are persecuted, but not forsaken; we are cast down, but we do not perish.
At all times we carry the dying of Y'shua in our body, so that the life of Y'shua also may be revealed in our body.
For if we who live are handed over to death for the sake of Y'shua, so also the life of Y'shua will be revealed in this body of ours that dies.
So now death is at work in us, and life in you.
And we also therefore have the same spirit of faith, as it is written: I believed, because of this I also spoke; we believe, because of this we also speak.
and we know that he who gave life to our Master Y'shua will also give life to us through Y'shua, and will bring us near with you to himself.
For everything is for your sake, so that when grace is made to abound through many, thanksgiving may abound to the glory of Elohim.
Because of this we do not grow weary; for even if our outer man is being corrupted, yet the one from within ‹man› is being renewed day by day.
For the affliction of this time, while very small and light, prepares for us a great glory without end, forever and ever.
as we do not look at these that are seen, but at these that are not seen; for those that are seen are of time, but those that are not seen are forever.
For we know that if our house on earth—this of the body—is dissolved, yet we have a building from Elohim, a house not made with hands, eternal in heaven.
For on this also we groan and long to put on our house that is from heaven:
if indeed when we have put it on we will not be found naked.
For while we are now in this house we groan from its weight, and we do not desire to strip it off, but to put on over it, so that its mortality may be swallowed up in life.
And the one who prepares us for this is Elohim, he who has given us the earnest of his Ruach.
Therefore we know and are persuaded that as long as we dwell in the body we are away from our Master;
for we walk by faith and not by sight.
Therefore we are confident and desire to be away from the body and to be with our Master.
And we strive that whether we are away or whether we are at home, we may be pleasing to him.
For we are all ready to stand before the judgment seat of the Mashiyach, that each one may be repaid in his body ‹for› what was done by him, whether good or whether evil.
Therefore because we know the fear of our Master, we persuade men; but to Elohim we are revealed; and I hope also that we are revealed to your minds.
We are not again praising ourselves to you, but we give you occasion to boast in us toward those who boast in appearance and not in heart.
For if we are out of our minds, it is for Elohim; and if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
For the love of the Mashiyach constrains us to reason this: that one died for every person; therefore every person has died.
And he died for every person, so that those who live should not live for themselves, but for him who died for them and rose.
And from now on we know no person after the body; and if we have known the Mashiyach after the body, yet from now we know ‹him› no more.
Therefore everyone who is in the Mashiyach is a new creation; the old things have passed away.
And everything has become new from Elohim, who reconciled us to himself in the Mashiyach and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
For Elohim was in the Mashiyach, who reconciled the world with his majesty, and did not reckon to them their sins; and he placed in us the word of reconciliation.
We are therefore ambassadors for the Mashiyach, and it is as if Elohim is beseeching you by us. On behalf of the Mashiyach, therefore, we beseech ‹you›, be reconciled to Elohim.
For he who did not know sin, on your account he made him sin, that we might become in him the righteousness of Elohim.
And as helpers we beg of you that the grace of Elohim which you have received may not be empty in you.
For he has said, In an accepted time I answered you, and in the day of life I helped you. Now is the accepted time, and now is the day of life!
Give no one an occasion of stumbling in anything, that there may be no blemish on our ministry.
But in everything we show ourselves to be ministers of Elohim, in much endurance, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses,
in scourgings, in imprisonments, in tumults, in toil, in watchings, in fastings;
in purity, in knowledge, in long-suffering, in kindness, in Ruach haKodesh, in love without hypocrisy,
by the word of truth, by the power of Elohim, by the armor of righteousness on the right and on the left;
in glory and in disgrace, in praise and in blame; as deceivers and true;
as unknown and known; as dying, and look, we live; as being disciplined and not dying;
as grieving and always rejoicing; as poor and enriching many; as having nothing and holding all things.
Our mouth is open toward you, Corinthians, and our heart is wide.
You are not restricted in us, but you are restricted in your own bowels.
I speak as to ‹my› children: repay me my due that is toward you, and expand your love toward me.
And do not be yoke-fellows with those who do not believe. For what fellowship is there for righteousness with iniquity? Or what mixing is there for light with darkness?
Or what peace is there for Mashiyach with Satana? Or what portion is there for one who believes with one who does not believe?

Or what agreement is there for the temple of Elohim with demons? But you are the temple of the living Elohim, as it is said: I will dwell in them and walk in them, and I will be their Elohim, and they will be a people for me.
Because of this, go out from among them and be separated from them, says Master YHWH, and do not come near the unclean, and I will receive you;
and I will be a father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me, says Master YHWH who holds all.
Therefore, since we have these promises, my beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit, and let us work holiness in the fear of Elohim.
Make room for us, brothers; we have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have defrauded no one.
I do not say ‹this› to condemn you; for I said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live.
I have great boldness toward you, and I have much boasting in you; I am filled with comfort, and I overflow with joy in all my afflictions.
For even when we came to Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were afflicted in everything; outside were fights, and inside were fears.
But Elohim, who comforts the lowly, comforted us by the coming of Titus.

And not only by his coming, but also by the rest with which he was refreshed by you. For he told us of your love toward us, and of your grief, and of your zeal on our behalf; and when I heard it, great joy was mine.
And even if I made you sad by the letter, I do not regret it, even if I did regret it; for I see that that letter, even if for a time it made you sad,
yet it produced great joy for me, not because you were made sad, but because your sadness brought you to repentance; for you were made sad according to Elohim, so that you would lack nothing from us.
For sadness on account of Elohim works a turning of the soul that is not reversed, and a turning to life; but the sadness of the world works death.

For look, this same thing, that you were distressed on account of Elohim, how much diligence it worked in you, and defense, and anger, and fear, and love, and zeal, and vengeance! And in everything you showed yourselves that you are ‹now› pure in this matter.

And it will be ‹seen› that I wrote to you, not for the sake of him who did the wrong, nor for the sake of him who received the wrong, ‹only,› but that your diligence toward us might be made known before Elohim.
Because of this we were comforted; and with our comfort we rejoiced all the more in the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed with you all.
so that I was not ashamed in anything I had boasted to him about you; but as we spoke everything in truth with you, so also our boasting toward Titus was found in truth.
and his compassions also increased all the more toward you, as he remembers the obedience of you all, how you received him with fear and trembling.
I rejoice that in everything I am confident concerning you.
And we make known to you, brothers, the grace of Elohim that was given in the assembly of Macedonia.
that in the great testing of their affliction, abundance was to their joy, and the depth of their poverty abounded in the riches of their simplicity.
For I testify that according to their strength, and beyond their strength, by the will of their soul,
they sought from us with much entreaty that they might share in the grace of the ministry to the holy ones.
And not ‹only› as we had hoped, but they first gave themselves to our Master and also to us by the will of Elohim.
so that we asked Titus that as he had begun, so he would complete in you also this grace.
But as you abound in everything—in faith and in word and in knowledge and in all diligence and in our love toward you—so also abound in this grace.
I am not commanding you, but by the diligence of your companions I am testing the truth of your love.
For you know the grace of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, that for your sake he became poor when he was rich, so that you by his poverty might become rich.
And I give counsel to you in this, which helps you, because from last year you began not only to will but also to do.
But now complete in the deed what you willed, so that as you had readiness to will, so you may complete it in the deed from what you have.
For if the willingness is there, it is accepted according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
For it is not that there should be relief for others and pressure for you;
but that there may be equality at this time, and that your abundance may be ‹a supply› for their lack, that their abundance also may be ‹a supply› for your lack, that there may be equality.
As it is written, He who took much had nothing left over, and he who took little was not lacking.
But thanks to Elohim, who put this diligence for you into the heart of Titus.
For he received our request, and because he was very diligent, of his own will he went out to you.
And we sent with him our brother, whose praise in the gospel is in all the churches;
so that he also was chosen by the churches to go out with us in this grace that is ministered by us to the glory of Elohim himself and to our own encouragement.
And we are careful in this, that no one should put blame on us in this abundance that is ministered by us.
For we take care for what is beautiful, not only before Elohim, but also before the sons of men.
And we sent with them also our brother, the one who has been proved by us at all times in many things as he is diligent; but now he is more diligent in the great confidence that is upon you.
If therefore Titus, he is my partner and helper among you; and if our other brothers, they are apostles of the churches of the glory of the Mashiyach.
Therefore show to them, before the face of all the churches, the demonstration of your love and of our boasting that is in you.
Now concerning the service of the holy ones, it is superfluous for me if I write to you.
for I know the readiness of your mind, and because of this I boasted of you to the Macedonians, that Achaia has been ready since last year, and your zeal has stirred up many.
Yet I have sent the brothers, so that our boasting with which we boasted of you in this matter would not be empty, that as I said, you would be ready;
so that if the Macedonians come with me and find you not ready, we—not to say you—would be put to shame in that boasting with which we boasted.

Because of this it seemed good to me to urge these brothers to go ahead to you and prepare beforehand that blessing of which you were informed from before, so that it would be ready, thus as a blessing and not as greed.
And this ‹I say›: whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows in blessing will also reap in blessing.
Every person as he has in his mind, not as from sadness or as from compulsion, for Elohim loves a cheerful giver.
But it is in the hand of Elohim to make all grace abound in you, so that in every time and in everything you may have what is enough for you, and may abound in every good work.
As it is written: He scattered and gave to the poor, and his righteousness stands forever.
Now he who gives seed to the sower and bread for food will give and multiply your seed and increase the fruits of your righteousness,
so that in everything you may be enriched in all liberality, which through us completes thanksgiving to Elohim.
Because the service of this ministry not only fills up the lack of the holy ones, but also abounds through many thanksgivings to Elohim.

Because of the proof of this service they glorify Elohim that you have subjected yourselves to the confession of the good news of the Mashiyach, and that you have shared in your simplicity with them and with everyone.
And they offer prayer for you with much love because of the abundance of the grace of Elohim that is upon you.
Thanks then to Elohim for his gift that cannot be spoken.
Now I, Paulos, ask you by the mildness and the meekness of the Mashiyach, that although in face I am meek toward you, yet when I am far I am confident toward you.
Yet I ask of you that I may not, when I come, be forced by the confidence that is mine to be bold, as I reckon it, toward those who think of us that we walk as in the flesh.
For although we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh.
For the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but of the power of Elohim, and by it we cast down rebellious fortresses.
And we tear down reasonings and every high thing that is raised up against the knowledge of Elohim, and we take captive every thought to the obedience of the Mashiyach.
And we are ready to execute vengeance on those who do not obey, when your obedience is fulfilled.
You look on outward appearances. If anyone is confident in himself that he is of the Mashiyach, let him know from himself that as he is of the Mashiyach, so also are we.
For if I should also boast somewhat more in the authority that our Master has given me, I am not ashamed, because he gave it to us for your building up, and not for your tearing down.
But I forbear, so that I may not be thought as one who terrifies you with my letters.
For there are some who say, ‹His› letters are weighty and strong, but the presence of his body is weak, and his speech is contemptible.
But let the one who says so consider this, that as we are in the word of our letters when we are far away, so also we are in deed when we are near.
For we do not dare to reckon or compare ourselves with those who boast themselves. But they, because they compare themselves with themselves, are not wise.
But we do not boast beyond our measure, but within the measure of the limit that Elohim allotted to us, that we should reach even as far as you.
For we are not stretching ourselves as if we do not reach you; for we have reached as far as you in the good news of the Mashiyach.
And we do not boast beyond our measure in the labor of others; but we have hope that when your faith grows, we will be magnified among you according to our measure and will abound,
even to proclaim beyond you, not to boast in another’s measure in things already prepared.

For it is not the one who praises himself who is approved, but the one whom Master YHWH praises.
I wish you would bear with me a little, that I may speak foolishly: but you do indeed bear with me.

For if he who comes to you proclaims another Y'shua whom we have not proclaimed, or you receive another spirit which you have not received, or another gospel which you have not accepted, you might well put up with it.
For I reckon that I am in nothing inferior to those legates who excel.
For though I am unskilled in speech, yet not in knowledge; but in everything we have been made known among you.

And other churches I stripped and I took pay ‹of them› for your service.
