one who is without blame, who is the husband of one wife, and has believing children who are not accused of dissipation and are not rebellious.

For an elder is bound to be without blame, as the steward of Elohim, and not be self-willed, and not be hot-tempered, and not be excessive over wine, and not have a hand swift to strike, and not be a lover of filthy gain.
But he should be a lover of strangers, and a lover of good ‹deeds›, and be sober, and be upright, and be pure, and restraining his soul from lusts;
and careful over the teaching of the word of faith, so that he may be able also to encourage with his healthy teaching, and to rebuke those who contend.
For there are many who are not submissive, and their words are empty, and they lead astray the minds of people, especially those who are from the circumcision.
Those whose mouths ought to be stopped: for they ruin many houses, and teach what is not right, for the sake of filthy gain.
One of them, a prophet of their own, said, The sons of Crete are always liars, evil beasts, idle bellies.
And this testimony is true. Because of this, rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,
and not throw themselves into Yehudi fables and into the precepts of men who hate the truth.
For everything is pure to the pure; but to those who are defiled and do not believe, nothing is pure, but their mind and their conscience are defiled.
And they profess that they know Elohim, but in their works they deny him; and they are hateful and disobedient and rejected for every good work.
But you speak what is fitting for healthy teaching.
And teach that the older men be watchful in their minds, and be sober, and be pure, and be sound in the faith and in love and in patience.
And also the older women likewise, that they be in a manner fitting for the fear of Elohim, and not be slanderers, and not be enslaved to much wine, and be teachers of good things,
and make the younger women modest, that they love their husbands and their children,
and be sober and holy, and take good care of their households, and be subject to their husbands, so that no one may blaspheme the word of Elohim.
And likewise urge the younger men to be sober.
In everything show yourself a pattern in all good works, and in your teaching let your word be healthy,
that is sober and not corrupt, and let no one despise it, so that he who stands against us may be ashamed when he cannot say anything hateful against us.
Servants should submit to their masters in everything and please them and not be contradictory
and not be thieves, but show their good faithfulness in everything so that they may adorn in everything the teaching of Elohim our Life-Giver.
For the grace of Elohim that gives life to all has been revealed to all the sons of men.
and it teaches us to deny ungodliness and the lusts of the world, and to live in this world in sobriety and in uprightness and in the fear of Elohim,
while we look for the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of the great Elohim and our Life-Giver Y'shua the Mashiyach;
who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a new people who are zealous in good works.
Speak these things and exhort and correct with all authority, and let no one despise you.
And keep reminding them to submit to rulers and authorities and to obey, and to be ready for every good work;
and to speak evil of no one, and not to be quarrelsome, but to be gentle, and in everything to show their kindness toward all people.
For we also were once without sense and disobedient and going astray, and enslaved to various desires, and living in evil and envy, and were hateful and also hating one another.
But when the kindness and compassion of Elohim our Life-Giver was revealed,
not by works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his own mercy he gave us life by the washing of the new birth and by the renewal of the Ruach haKodesh,
which he poured out on us richly through Y'shua the Mashiyach our Life-Giver;
so that by his grace we may be justified and become heirs in the hope of life forever.

The word is faithful, and in these things I want you also to confirm them, so that those who have believed in Elohim may be careful to practice good works. These are good and profitable to the children of men.
But stay away from foolish questions and from stories of genealogies and from contentions and from disputes of the scribes, for there is no profit in them and they are empty.
From a heretical man, after you have admonished him once and twice, stay away.
And know that one who is like this is perverse and sinful and condemned in himself.
When I send Artima to you or Tukikos, be diligent to come to me at Nikopolis, for there I have set in my mind to spend the winter.
As for Zenas the scribe and Apolos, take care to send them on their way well, so that nothing is lacking for them.
And let those who are ours also learn to be workers of good deeds for the needs that press, so that they may not be without fruit.
All who are with me greet you. Greet all who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
Paulos, a prisoner of Y'shua the Mashiyach, and Timotheos the brother, to Philimon the beloved and our fellow laborer,
and to Apphia our beloved, and to Arkippos our fellow laborer, and to the assembly that is in your house.
Grace be with you, and peace, from Elohim our Father and from our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
I give thanks to my Elohim at all times, and I remember you in my prayers,
since I heard of your faith and of the love you have toward our Master Y'shua and toward all the holy ones,
that the fellowship of your faith may yield fruit in works and in the knowledge of every good thing that is yours in Y'shua the Mashiyach.
For we have much joy and consolation, because by your love the mercies of the holy ones have been refreshed.
Therefore I have much boldness in the Mashiyach to enjoin on you the things that are right.
But for love’s sake I rather beseech you, I Paulos who am aged as you know, and now also a prisoner of Y'shua the Mashiyach.
And I beseech you for my son, whom I begot in my bonds, Onesimos,
who formerly was of no use to you, but now is very useful both to you and to me.
And I have sent him to you. But you receive him as my own begotten.
For I was wanting to keep him with me, that he might serve me in your place in the bonds of the gospel.
But without your counsel I did not want to do anything, so that your good would not be as by compulsion, but by your will.
Perhaps also for this reason he was separated for a time, that you might keep him forever,
no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother to me, how much more to you, both in the flesh and in our Master.
If then you are a partner with me, receive him as me.
And if he has wronged you in anything, or owes, charge this to me.
I, Paulos, have written ‹it› with my own hand. I will repay—not to say to you that you even owe me your own self.
Yes, my brother, let me be refreshed by you in our Master. Refresh my bowels in the Mashiyach.
Because I am confident that you will listen to me, I have written to you, and I know that you will do more than I say.
And at the same time also prepare a lodging for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be given to you.
Epaphras, a fellow captive with me in Y'shua the Mashiyach, greets you,
and Marqos and Aristarkos and Dema and Luqa, my helpers.
The grace of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach be with your spirit. Amen.
In all ways and in all forms Elohim spoke with our fathers by the prophets from of old.
And in these last days he has spoken with us by his Son, whom he has set as heir of all things, and by him he made the worlds.

who is the radiance of his glory and the image of his being, and holds all by the power of his word; and he in his person made a purification of our sins and sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.
And he is altogether greater than the messengers, as he has also inherited a name more excellent than theirs.
For to which of the messengers did Elohim ever say, You are my Son; today I have begotten you? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he will be to me a Son?
And again, when he brings the firstborn into the world, he says: Let all the messengers of Elohim worship him.
But of the messengers he says this: Who makes his messengers a wind, and his ministers a flaming fire.
But of the Son he says: Your throne, O Elohim, is forever and ever; a straight scepter is the scepter of your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore Elohim, your Elohim, has anointed you with the oil of gladness more than your companions.
And again, You from the beginning laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will pass away, but you remain; and they all like a garment will wear out;
and like a cloak you will fold them up. They will be changed; but you are as you are, and your years will not end.
And to which of the messengers did he ever say: Sit at my right hand, until I place your enemies a footstool under your feet?
Are they not all spirits of ministration, who are sent into ministration on account of those who are to inherit life?
Because of this we are bound to be more careful about what we have heard, so that we do not fall.
For if the word that was spoken by the hand of messengers was confirmed, and everyone who heard it and transgressed it received a just recompense,
how will we escape if we neglect those things which are our life, which began to be spoken by our Master, and were confirmed to us by those who heard from him,
while Elohim testified concerning them with signs and wonders and with various powers and with distributions of the Ruach haKodesh that were given according to his will?
For it was not to messengers that he subjected the world to come, of which we speak.
But as the writing testifies and says: What is man, that you remember him? and the son of man, that you attend to him?
You have made him a little lower than the messengers; glory and honor you have put on his head, and you have given him authority over the works of your hands.
And all things you have subjected under his feet. And in that he subjected all things to him, he left nothing that is not subjected. But now we do not yet see that all things are subjected to him.

But we see him who was made a little lower than the messengers—that is Y'shua—because of the suffering of his death, and glory and honor are placed on his head; for Elohim, in his grace, tasted death for everyone.
For it was fitting for him, by whom are all things and for whom are all things, and ‹who› brings many sons to glory, to perfect the prince of their life through suffering.
For he who makes holy and those who are made holy are all from one. For this reason he is not ashamed to call them his brothers,
when he says, I will announce your name to my brothers, and in the midst of the assembly I will praise you.
And again, I will be trusting on him. And again, Look, I and the children that Elohim gave to me.
For because the children shared in flesh and blood, he also in that same likeness shared in these, that by his death he might bring to nothing him who holds the authority of death, who is Satana,
and set free those who, through fear of death, were all their lives subject to bondage.
For death did not have authority over messengers, but it had authority over the seed of Avraham.

Because of this it was right that in every thing he be made like his brothers, that he might be merciful and a high priest faithful in the things of Elohim, and make propitiation for the sins of the people.
For in that he himself suffered and was tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.
Therefore, my holy brothers, who are called with a calling from heaven, look at this apostle and high priest of our confession, Y'shua the Mashiyach:
who is faithful to him who made him, as Moshe in all his house.
For the glory of this one is much greater than that of Moshe, just as the honor of the builder of a house is greater than that of the house.
For every house is built by someone, but he who built all is Elohim.
And Moshe, as a servant, was faithful in all the house, for a testimony of those things that were to be spoken by his hand:
but the Mashiyach as the Son ‹is› over his house; and we are his house, if we hold fast to the end the confidence and the boasting of his hope.
Because the Ruach haKodesh has said: Today, if you hear his voice,
do not harden your hearts to provoke him, like the provocators, and like the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested me, and proved, ‹and› saw my works forty years.
Because of this I was disgusted with that generation, and said: This is a people whose heart wanders, and they have not known my ways:
so that I swore in my wrath that they will not enter into my rest.
Watch out, therefore, my brothers, lest there be in any of you an evil heart that does not believe, and you depart from the living Elohim.
But examine yourselves all the days, until the day that is called today, so that no one of you is hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
For we have become partakers with the Mashiyach if from the beginning until the end we hold firmly to this confidence.
as it is said, Today if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts to provoke him.
For who are those who heard and provoked him? Was it not all these who went out from Mitsrayin by the hand of Moshe?
And with whom was he disgusted forty years, but with those who sinned, and whose bones fell in the wilderness?
And to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, but to those who did not believe?
And we see that they could not enter because they did not believe.
Therefore let us fear, lest while the promise of entering into his rest stands firm, anyone among you should be found falling short of entering.
For we also have had the announcement, just as they did; but the word they heard did not profit them, because it was not mixed with faith in those who heard it.
But we who have believed enter into the rest, as he said: As I swore in my wrath, They will not enter into my rest—for the works of Elohim were from the foundation of the world.
As he said of the sabbath, Elohim rested on the seventh day from all his works.
And here again he said, They will not enter into my rest.
Therefore, since there was a place for some to enter into it, and those who first received the announcement did not enter because they were not persuaded:
Again he sets another day a long time afterwards, as it is written above, that Dawid said, Today if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.
For if Y'shua son of Nun had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterwards of another day.
Therefore a sabbath remains for the people of Elohim.
For the one who has entered into his rest has also rested from his works, as Elohim did from his own.
Let us therefore strive to enter into that rest, so that we do not fall in the likeness of those who did not obey.

For the word of Elohim is living and all-efficient and sharper than a two-edged sword, and enters even to the separation of soul and spirit and of joints and marrow and bones, and judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
And there is no creature that is hidden from before him; but everything is naked and open before his eyes, to whom we give account.
Since then we have a great High Priest, Y'shua the Mashiyach, the Son of Elohim, who has gone up into the heavens, let us hold fast to his confession.
For we do not have a high priest who cannot feel with our weakness, but ‹one› who was tested in everything like us, aside from sin.
Let us therefore draw near with openness to the throne of his grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace for help in the time of affliction.
For every high priest who is from among men is established for men over the things of Elohim, that he may present offerings and sacrifices for sin.
who can humble himself and feel with those who do not know and who err, because he also is clothed with weakness.
And because of this he is obligated, as for the people, so also for himself, to present an offering for his sins.
And no one takes the honor for himself, but he who is called by Elohim, as Aharon ‹was›.
So also the Mashiyach did not glorify himself to become high priest, but he ‹appointed him› who said to him, You are my Son; today I have begotten you.
As he also said in another place: You are a priest forever in the likeness of Malki-Zedek.
Also when he was clothed in flesh, he offered prayer and entreaty with strong crying and with tears to him who was able to give him life from death; and he was heard.
And though he was a Son, from the fear and the sufferings he endured he learned obedience.
And thus he was perfected and became the cause of life forever to all who obey him.
And he was named by Elohim high priest in the likeness of Malkizedeq.
Now concerning this Malkizedeq, there is much word for us to say, and it is hard to explain, because you have become weak in your hearing.

For you ought to be teachers, because time has been yours in the teaching. But now again you need to learn what the first writings are of the beginning of the words of Elohim, and you have become needing milk and not solid food.
But everyone whose food is milk is not skilled in the word of righteousness, because he is a child.
But solid food is for the mature, who because they are trained have their senses exercised to distinguish good and evil.
Because of this let us leave the beginning of the word of the Mashiyach and let us come to perfection. Or will you again lay another foundation for repentance from dead works and for faith in Elohim,
and for the teaching of immersion and of the laying on of a hand and of the resurrection from the dead and of the eternal judgment?
We will do this if Master YHWH permits.
But those who once went down to immersion and tasted the gift from heaven and received the Ruach haKodesh
and tasted the good word of Elohim and the power of the world to come
who again sin cannot a second time be renewed to repentance, and a second time crucify and insult the Son of Elohim.
For the earth that drinks the rain that comes upon it many times, and brings forth the herb useful to those for whom it is cultivated, receives blessing from Elohim.
But if it puts forth thorns and briers, it is rejected and not far from a curse, but its end is a burning.
But we are persuaded concerning you, my brothers, of the things that are better and near to life, even though we speak this way.
For Elohim is not unjust to forget your works and your love that you have shown in his name, in that you have ministered to the holy ones and do minister.
But we desire that each one of you show this same diligence toward the full assurance of your hope until the end,
and that you not grow weary, but be imitators of those who by faith and by patience of spirit became heirs of the promise.
For when Elohim promised Avraham, because there was none greater than himself by whom he could swear, he swore by himself,
and said, Blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.
And so he was patient and received the promise.
For people swear by one greater than themselves, and in every dispute that happens among them the sure end of it is by an oath.
Therefore Elohim, being more willing to show the heirs of the promise that his promise does not change, bound it with an oath,
so that by two things that do not change, in which Elohim cannot lie, we who have fled for refuge in him might have great comfort and hold fast the hope promised to us.
which is to us as an anchor that holds our soul so that it does not sway, and it enters into that within the veil,
where Y'shua has previously entered for us, and has become a priest forever after the likeness of Melkizedeq.
Now this Melkizedeq is king of Shalem, priest of Elohim the Most High, and he met Avraham when he returned from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him.
And to him Avraham set apart a tenth from all that was with him. Now his name is interpreted king of righteousness, and again ‹he is called› king of Shalem, that is king of peace.

Of whom neither his father nor his mother are written in the genealogies, nor the beginning of his days nor the end of his life, but in the likeness of the Son of Elohim his priesthood continues forever.
See then how great this one is, to whom Avraham the head of the fathers gave a tenth of the firstfruits.

For those from the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a commandment of the law to take tithes from the people, those from their brothers, though they also came out from the loins of Avraham.
But this one who is not written in their genealogy took tithes from Avraham and blessed him who received the promise.
But without dispute, the lesser is blessed by the one who is greater than him.
And here men who die receive tithes; but there, he of whom the writing testifies that he lives.
And as one may say, through Avraham even Levi who receives tithes was himself tithed.
For he was still in the loins of his father when Melkizedeq met him.

If therefore perfection had been through the priesthood of the Levites, in which the law was set for the people, why was another priest needed to arise in the likeness of Melkizedeq? Yet it says he would be in the likeness of Aharon.
But as there was a change in the priesthood, so there was a change also in the law.
For he of whom these things were said was born of another tribe, from which no one ever served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Master rose from Yehuda, from a tribe of which Moshe said nothing concerning priesthood.
And it is still more evident from this, that he says another priest arises in the likeness of Malkizedeq,
who was not according to the law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of a life that cannot be dissolved.
For he testifies of him: You are a priest forever in the likeness of Malkizedeq.
But the change that came to the former commandment was because of its weakness and because there was no profit in it.
For the law perfected nothing; but in its place a hope came in that is better than it, by which we draw near to Elohim.
And he confirmed it to us by an oath.
For they became priests without an oath; but this one by an oath, as he said to him by Dawid: Master YHWH has sworn and will not lie, You are a priest forever in the likeness of Malki-Zedek.
By all this is that better covenant of which Y'shua became the sponsor.
And they were many priests, because they were dying and were not permitted to continue.
But this one, because he remains forever, his priesthood does not pass away.
and he is able to give life forever to those who come near to Elohim by his hand; for he lives at all times and sends up prayer for them.
For a priest like this was also fitting for us; one pure, without evil and without stain; one separated from sins, and exalted higher than the heavens;
and who has no need every day, like the ‹Aaronic› high priests, first to offer sacrifices for his own sins and then for the people; for this he did once, by offering up himself.
For the law appoints weak men as priests; but the word of the oath, which was after the law ‹appoints› the Son perfected forever.
Now the sum of all of them is that we have a high priest who sits at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven:
And he is the minister of the holy place and of the true tabernacle, which Elohim pitched, and not man.
For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; therefore it was right that this one also should have something to offer.
And if he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, because there are priests ‹there› who offer gifts according to the law:

‹namely› those who minister to the likeness and shadow of the things in heaven, as it was said to Moshe when he was making the tabernacle, See and make everything according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.
But now Y'shua the Mashiyach has received a ministry better than that, just as the covenant of which he is made the mediator is also better and is given with better promises than the former.
For if the first ‹covenant› had been without fault, there would have been no place for this second ‹one›.
For he finds fault with them and says: The days are coming, says Master YHWH, when I will complete with the house of the house of Yisrael and with the house of the house of Yehuda a new covenant,

not like that covenant which I gave to their fathers in the day that I took them by their hand and brought them out from the land of Mitsrayin; because they did not continue in my covenant, I also rejected them, says Master YHWH.

But this is the covenant that I will give to the house of the house of Yisrael after those days, says Master YHWH: I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts, and I will be to them Elohim and they will be to me a people.
And no one will teach his fellow-citizen or his brother and say, Know Master YHWH, because they will all know me, from their little one to their elder.
And I will forgive them their iniquity, and their sins I will remember no more.
In that he said a New ‹Covenant›, he has made the first old; and that which is old and aged is near to dissolution.
Now, in the first ‹covenant› there were ordinances of ministration, and a worldly sanctuary.
For the first tabernacle that was made had in it the lampstand and the table and the bread of the presence, and it was called the Sanctuary.
But the inner tabernacle, which was within the second veil, was called the Holy of Holies.

And there was in it the golden censer and the ark of the covenant, overlaid all over with gold; and in it were the golden pot that had the manna, and the rod of Aharon that sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant;
and above it the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. But it is not time to speak particularly of each of these things that were so arranged.
And into the outer tabernacle the priests at all times were entering and fulfilling their ministration.
But into the tabernacle that is inside from it, once a year only, the high priest was entering with the blood that he was offering for his soul and for the sins of the people.
And by this the Ruach haKodesh was making known that the way of the holy ‹places› was not yet revealed, so long as there was a standing for the first tabernacle.
And this was a parable for that time in which offerings and sacrifices were being offered that were not able to perfect the conscience of him who was offering them:
but only in food and in drink and in immersions of various kinds, which are ordinances of the flesh that are set until the time of the correction.
But the Mashiyach who came was high priest of the good things that he wrought, and he entered into the great and perfect tabernacle that was not made with hands and was not of these created things.
And he did not enter with the blood of goats and of calves, but with the blood of his soul he entered once into the sanctuary and obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and of calves and the ashes of a heifer was sprinkled on those who were defiled and sanctifies them for the purification of their flesh,

how much more then will the blood of the Mashiyach, who by the Spirit that is forever offered his life without blemish to Elohim, cleanse our conscience from dead works so that we may serve the living Elohim?

For this reason he became the mediator of a new covenant, that by his death he might be redemption for those who transgressed the first covenant, so that those who are called might receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
For where there is a covenant, the death of him who made it is shown.
For it is confirmed only over the dead ‹person›, because while the one who made it is alive it has no use.
Therefore not even the first ‹covenant› was confirmed without blood.

For when the whole commandment was commanded by Moshe to all the people in the law, Moshe took the blood of a heifer and water with scarlet wool and hyssop and sprinkled it on the book and on all the people,
and said to them, This is the blood of the covenant that was commanded to you from Elohim.
Also on the tabernacle and on all the vessels of the service he sprinkled from that blood.
Because everything is purified with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
For it is necessary that these things that are likenesses of the heavenly ones be purified with these, but the heavenly ones themselves with sacrifices better than these.
For the Mashiyach did not enter a holy house made with hands, which is a likeness of the true ‹one›, but into heaven itself, to appear before the face of Elohim for us.
Neither ‹was it necessary› that he offer himself many times, as the high priest entered every year into the sanctuary with blood not his own:
otherwise he would have had to suffer many times from the beginning of the world; but now, at the end of the world, he has once offered himself in his sacrifice to abolish sin.
And just as it is appointed for men that they die once, and after their death comes the judgment,
so also the Mashiyach was offered once, and in his person he sacrificed the sins of many; and a second time, without sins, he will appear for the life of those who wait for him.

For the law had a shadow in it of the good things that are coming; it was not the substance of the things themselves. Because of this, while those same sacrifices were offered every year, they could never perfect those who offer them.
For if they had perfected them, they would long ago have ceased from their offerings, because their conscience would no longer trouble those who were once purified concerning sins.
But in those sacrifices they remember their sins every year.
For the blood of bulls and of goats cannot purify sins.
Because of this, when he entered the world, he said: In sacrifices and offerings you have not desired, but a body you have clothed me with.
And burnt offerings for sins you have not asked.
Then I said, Look, I come; it is written of me in the head of the book that I will do your will, Elohim.
From above he said, Sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings for sins you did not desire, those that were offered according to the law;
and after that he said, Look, I come to do your will, Elohim. By this he abolished the first, that he might establish the second.
For by this his will we are made holy through the offering of the body of Y'shua the Mashiyach once.
For every high priest who stood and ministered daily offered those same sacrifices again and again, which were never able to cleanse away sins.
But this ‹Priest› offered one sacrifice for sins, and sat down forever at the right hand of Elohim;
and from then on he waits until his foes are placed as a footstool under his feet.
For by one offering he has perfected forever those who are sanctified by him.
And the Ruach haKodesh also testifies to us, saying:
This is the covenant that I will give them after those days, says Master YHWH: I will put my law in their minds, and on their hearts I will write it;
and their iniquity and their sins I will not remember against them.
But where there is forgiveness of sins, an offering for sin is not required.
We have therefore, my brothers, openness of face in the entrance of the house of holiness by the blood of Y'shua
and a way of life that he has newly made for us now through the veil, that is his flesh.
And we have a great priest over the house of Elohim.
Let us draw near therefore with a true heart and with the confidence of faith, our hearts being sprinkled and cleansed from an evil conscience, and our body washed with pure water.
And let us hold firm in the confession of our hope and not waver, for he is faithful who promised us.
And let us look on one another for the stirring of love and of good works.
And let us not forsake our assemblies, as is the custom of some, but entreat one another all the more as you see that day drawing near.
For if a man sins willfully after he has received knowledge of the truth, there is no longer a sacrifice that may be offered for sins,
but a fearful judgment is ready, and the zeal of fire that consumes the adversaries.
For if he who transgressed the law of Moshe died without mercies at the mouth of two or three witnesses,

how much more do you think will he receive a worse punishment who has trampled the Son of Elohim and has accounted the blood of his covenant, by which he was sanctified, as ‹that› of all men, and has insulted the Ruach of grace?
We know him who has said, Retribution is mine, and I will repay; and again, Master YHWH will judge his people.
It is a great terror to fall into the hands of the living Elohim.
Remember therefore the former days, those in which you received immersion, and you endured a great contest of sufferings with reproach and with affliction;
and you were a spectacle, and also you shared with people who endured these things:
and it grieved you for those who were bound, and you endured the plundering of your goods with joy, because you know that you have a possession in heaven that is better and does not pass away.
Therefore do not cast away your boldness of face which you have, which has a great reward ready for it.
For patience is needed for you, that you may do the will of Elohim and receive the promise.
Because it is a little time, and very small, that he who is coming will come, and will not delay.
But the just one will live by my faith; and if he draws back, my soul is not pleased in him.
But we are not of the drawing back that leads to destruction, but of the faith that gains us our soul.
Now faith is the persuasion of the things that are in hope, as if they were in act; and ‹it is› the manifestation of the things that are not seen.
And by this there was testimony concerning the elders.
For by faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of Elohim, and these things that are seen came to be from those that are not seen.

By faith Habeel offered to Elohim a better sacrifice than that of Qayin, and because of it there was testimony concerning him that he is righteous, and Elohim testified to his offering; and because of it, even though he is dead, he still speaks.

By faith Chanokh was translated, and he did not taste death; and he was not found, because Elohim had translated him: for before he translated him, there was testimony concerning him that he pleased Elohim.
But without faith no one is able to please Elohim. For the one who draws near to Elohim must believe that he exists, and that he is a rewarder of those who seek him.

By faith Noach, when it was spoken with him about those things that are not seen, feared and made himself an ark for the life of the sons of his house, by which he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that is by faith.
By faith Avraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to that place which he was about to receive for an inheritance, and he went out when he did not know where he was going.
By faith he became a sojourner in the land that was promised to him as in a foreign land, and he dwelt in tents with Yitz'chak and Ya'akov, the heirs with him of the same promise.
For he was looking for the city that has foundations, whose craftsman and maker is Elohim.
By faith also Sarah, who was barren, received power to receive seed, and outside the time of her years she gave birth, because she was sure that he is faithful who promised her.
Therefore from one who was worn out in old age many were born, like the stars in the heavens and like the sand on the shore of the sea that has no number.
In faith all these died, and they did not receive their promise, but they saw it from afar and rejoiced in it, and they confessed that they are strangers and sojourners on the earth.
Now those who say these things show that they seek their city.
And if they had been seeking that city from which they went out, there was time for them to return again and go to it.
But now it is known that they longed for a better ‹city› than that, ‹namely,› for that which is in heaven. Therefore Elohim is not ashamed to be called their Elohim, for he prepared a city for them.
In faith Avraham, in his trial, offered up Yitz'chak, and he brought his only one up onto the altar, him whom he had received by the promise.
For it had been said to him, In Yitz'chak seed will be called for you.
And he reasoned in himself that it was possible in the hands of Elohim even to raise ‹him› from the dead, and because of this in a similitude ‹of a resurrection› he was given to him.
By faith in what was to come, Yitz'chak blessed Ya'akov and Esau.
By faith, when he was dying, Ya'akov blessed each one of the sons of Yosip, and bowed on the top of his staff.
By faith Yosip, when he was dying, remembered the departure of the sons of Yisrael, and gave charge concerning his bones.
By faith the parents of Moshe hid him when he was born for three months, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the command of the king.
By faith Moshe, when he became a man, refused to be called the son of the daughter of Pharaoh.
And he chose to be in affliction with the people of Elohim, and not to take pleasure in sin for a short time.
And he considered the riches of the reproach of the Mashiyach better than the treasures of Mitsrayin, for he looked to the repayment of the reward.
By faith he left Mitsrayin and did not fear the wrath of the king, and he endured as one who sees Elohim who is not seen.
By faith he made the pesach and the sprinkling of blood, that he who was destroying the firstborn might not approach them.
By faith they crossed the sea of Suf as on dry land, and in it the Mitsraye were swallowed when they dared to enter it.
By faith the walls of Airikhu fell after they had been circled seven days.
By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with those who did not obey, for she received the spies in peace.
And what more shall I say? For the time is too short for me to tell of Gid'on and of Baraq and of Shimshon and of Naftach and of Dawid and of Shmuel and of the rest of the prophets,
who by faith conquered kingdoms and worked righteousness and received promises and shut the mouths of lions,
and quenched the force of fire and were delivered from the mouth of the sword and were strengthened from sickness and became mighty in battle and overthrew the camps of the enemies,
and gave to women their children from the resurrection of the dead. And others died under tortures and did not look to be delivered, that a better resurrection might be theirs;
and others went through mockings and scourgings; others were handed over to bonds and to imprisonment.
Others were stoned, others were sawn, others died by the mouth of the sword, others went about clothed in skins of sheep and of goats, and were in need, and oppressed, and tormented.
people of whom the world was not worthy, and they were like wanderers in the wilderness and in the mountains and in caves and in the holes of the earth.
And all these, on whom there was testimony in their faith, did not receive the promise,
because Elohim had looked beforehand on our help, so that without us they would not be perfected.

Therefore we also, who have all these witnesses surrounding us like a cloud, cast from us every weight and also the sin that is always prepared for us, and with endurance let us run this contest that is set for us.

And let us look to Y'shua, who was the head and the completer of our faith, who for the joy that was his endured the cross and despised the shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of Elohim.
Look therefore how much he endured from those sinners who were adversaries of their own soul, so that you may not grow weary and your soul may not become remiss.
You have not yet come as far as blood in the contest against sin.
And you have forgotten the instruction that speaks to you as to sons: My son, do not disregard the discipline of Master YHWH, and do not let your soul faint when you are rebuked by him.
For whom Master YHWH loves he disciplines, and he scourges the sons in whom he is pleased.
Therefore endure the discipline, because Elohim is dealing with you as with sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline?
But if you are without the discipline with which everyone is disciplined, you have become strangers and not sons.
And if our fathers of the flesh disciplined us and we held them in awe, how much more then ought we to be subject to the Father of spirits and live?
For they disciplined us for a short time as they wished, but Elohim for our help, that we may share in his holiness.
Now all discipline in its time is not counted as joy but as grief; yet afterward it gives the fruit of peace and of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
Because of this, strengthen your slack hands and your tottering knees.
And make straight paths for your feet, so that the limb that is lame may not be wrenched, but may be healed.
Pursue peace with every person, and holiness, without which no one will see our Master.
And be careful, lest anyone be found among you lacking the grace of Elohim; or lest a root of bitterness spring up and trouble you, and by it many be defiled.
or lest anyone be found among you a fornicator, or reckless like Esau, who for one meal sold his birthright.
For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no place for repentance, though he sought it with tears.
For you have not come to the fire that burned and was tangible ‹mount›; nor to the darkness and the gloom and the storm;
nor to the sound of the horn and the voice of words, which those who heard it begged that it would not be spoken with them any more;
for they were not able to endure what was commanded, that even if a beast approached the mountain it would be stoned.
And so fearful was the sight that Moshe said, I am afraid and I tremble.
But you have drawn near to the mountain of Tsiyon and to the city of the living Elohim, to Urishlim that is in heaven, and to the assembly of myriads of messengers;
and to the congregation of the firstborn who are written in heaven, and to Elohim the Judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous who are perfected;
and to Y'shua the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the sprinkling of his blood that speaks better than that of Habeel.

Watch out, therefore, lest you refuse ‹to hear› him who speaks with you. For if those did not escape who refused ‹to hear› him who spoke with them on the earth, how much more ‹shall› we ‹not›, if we refuse ‹to hear› him who speaks with us from heaven?
Whose voice shook the earth; but now he has promised and said, Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also heaven.
And this that he says, Once more, shows the changing of those things that are shaken, because they are made, so that those that are not shaken may remain.
Therefore, since we have received a kingdom that is not shaken, let us hold the grace by which we may serve and please Elohim with reverence and fear.
For our Elohim is a consuming fire.
Let love of the brothers remain among you.
And do not forget kindness to strangers; for by this some have been worthy, while not aware, to receive messengers.
Remember those who are bound as if you yourselves are bound with them; remember those who are afflicted as people clothed in flesh.
Marriage is honorable in all, and their bed is pure; but fornicators and adulterers Elohim will judge.
Let not your mind love money, but let what you have be enough for you. For Master YHWH has said, I will not leave you, and I will not loosen my hands from you.
And we have ‹it› to say confidently, My Master is my helper; I will not fear. What can a son of man do to me?
Be remembering your guides, those who spoke the word of Elohim with you; look into the outcome of their conduct, and imitate their faith.
Y'shua the Mashiyach is the same yesterday and today and forever.
Do not be led away by strange and changing teachings. For it is good that we strengthen our hearts by grace, and not by foods, because those who walked in them were not helped.
We have an altar from which those who minister in the tabernacle have no right to eat.
For the flesh of those animals whose blood the high priest brings into the sanctuary for sins is burned outside the camp.
For this reason Y'shua also, that he might sanctify his people with his blood, suffered outside the city.
So let us also go out to him outside the camp, bearing his reproach.
for we have no lasting city here, but we look for the one that is to come.
And through him let us offer up a sacrifice of praise at all times to Elohim, which is the fruit of lips that confess his name.
And do not forget compassion and sharing with the poor, for with such sacrifices a person pleases Elohim.

Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls as those who will give account, that they may do this with joy and not with groaning, for that would not be profitable for you.
Pray for us, for we are confident that we have a good conscience, that in everything we desire to conduct ourselves well.
Especially I ask of you that you do this, so that I may return to you quickly.
Now may Elohim of peace, who brought up from the house of the dead the great Shepherd of the flock by the blood of the everlasting covenant, who is Y'shua the Mashiyach our Master,
complete you in every good work so that you may do his will, and may he work in us what is pleasing before him through Y'shua the Mashiyach, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Now I ask of you, my brothers, that you bear with the word of exhortation, because it is in few ‹words› that I have written to you.
Know that our brother Timotheos is set free, and if he comes soon, I will see you with him.
Greet all your leaders and all the holy ones. All those from Italy greet you.
Grace be with you all. Amen.
Ya'akov, a servant of Elohim and of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, to the twelve tribes scattered among the peoples: peace.
Let it be all joy to you, my brothers, when you enter into many and various trials.
For you know that the trial of ‹your› faith makes you possess patience.
And let patience have its perfect work, so that you may be complete and perfect, and may lack nothing.
And if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask ‹it› of Elohim, who gives to all freely and does not reproach; and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith, not hesitating: for he who hesitates is like the waves of the sea that the wind agitates.
And let not that man expect to receive anything from Master YHWH,
who is divided in his mind and unstable in all his ways.
But let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation,
and the rich in his humiliation, because like the flower of the grass he passes away.
For the sun rises with its heat and dries up the grass, and its flower falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes: so also the rich man withers in his ways.
Blessed is the man who endures testing, so that when he is proven he will receive the crown of life, which Elohim has promised to those who love him.
Let no one say when he is tempted, I am tempted of Elohim: for Elohim is not tempted with evils, and he tempts no one.
But every person is tempted by his own desire, and he desires and is drawn away.
And this ‹his› desire conceives and brings forth sin; and sin, when it is mature, brings forth death.
Do not err, my beloved brothers.
Every good and perfect gift comes down from above, from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change, not even the shadow of turning.
He willed and gave birth to us by the word of truth, that we might be the firstfruits of his creatures.
And you, my beloved brothers, let every one of you be swift to hear and slow to speak and slow to anger:
for the anger of a man does not work the righteousness of Elohim.
Because of this, remove from you all impurity and the abundance of wickedness, and with meekness receive the word that is planted in our nature, which is able to give life to your souls.
But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, and do not deceive your souls.
For if a man is a hearer of the word and not a doer of it, he is like one who sees his face in a mirror:
for he sees himself and passes on and forgets what he was like.
But everyone who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues in it is not a hearer of a hearing that is forgotten, but a doer of the deed, and this one will be blessed in his doing.
And if anyone thinks that he serves Elohim and does not hold his tongue, but deceives his heart, this one's service is empty.
For the pure and holy service before Elohim the Father is this: to visit the orphans and widows in their affliction, and that a person keep his soul unspotted from the world.
My brothers, do not hold the faith of the glory of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach with respect of persons.
For if a man comes into your assembly with a gold ring or with fine clothes, and a poor man comes in with filthy clothes;
and you look on the one who is wearing fine clothes and say to him, You sit here in a good place, and to the poor man you say, You stand over there, or sit here before the footstool of my feet;
have you not divided among yourselves and become judges of evil thoughts?
Hear, my beloved brothers: has not Elohim chosen the poor of the world, rich in faith, to be heirs of the kingdom that Elohim has promised to those who love him?
But you have despised the poor man. Do not the rich exalt themselves over you and drag you to the house of judgment?
Do they not blaspheme the good name that is called upon you?
And if in this you fulfill the law of Elohim, as it is written, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you do well.
But if you show favoritism, you commit sin, and you are convicted by the law as transgressors of the law.
For whoever keeps the whole law, and yet fails in one ‹precept›, is guilty of the whole law.
For he who said, You shall not commit adultery, also said, You shall not kill. If then you do not commit adultery, but you kill, you have become a transgressor of the law.
So speak and so act as people who are to be judged by the law of liberty.
For judgment without mercy is on him who has not done mercy. You are raised by mercy above judgment.
What is the use, my brothers, if a man says, I have faith, and he has no works? Can his faith give him life?
And if a brother or sister are naked and lacking the food of the day,
and one of you says to them, Go in peace, be warm and be filled, and you do not give them what the body needs, what is the use?
So also faith without works is dead by itself.
For a man says to you, You have faith, and I have works. Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith from my works.
You believe that Elohim is one; you do well; the demons also believe and tremble.
Do you want to know, O weak man, that faith without works is dead?
Was not our father Avraham justified by works when he offered Yitz'chak his son on the altar?
You see that his faith aided his works, and by the works his faith was made complete.
And the writing was fulfilled that says, Avraham believed in Elohim, and it was counted to him as righteousness, and he was called the friend of Elohim.
You see that a man is justified by works and not by faith alone.
So also Rahab the harlot, was she not justified by works when she received the spies and sent them out by another way?
As the body without the spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.
Do not let many be teachers among you, my brothers, but know that we are liable to a greater judgment.
For we all stumble in many things. Everyone who does not stumble in word is a perfect man who is able to bring even his whole body into subjection.
Look, we put bits into the mouths of horses so that they will be subject to us, and we turn about their whole body.
Also strong ships, when hard winds drive them, are turned about by a small piece of wood to the place the will of the one who steers looks.
So also the tongue is a small member, and it exalts itself. Also a little fire kindles a large forest.

And the tongue is a fire, and the world of sin is like a forest. And this tongue, while it is among our members, stains the whole body and sets on fire the course of our generations that run like a wheel, and it itself is set on fire.
For all natures of beasts and of birds and of creeping things of the sea and of the dry land are subjected to the nature of humankind.
But the tongue no one has been able to tame: this evil that is not restrained, full of the poison of death.
With it we bless Master YHWH and Father, and with it we curse human beings who are made in the likeness of Elohim.
And from it, from the mouth, go out blessing and curse. It is not right, my brothers, that these things should be done so.
Can sweet waters and bitter go out from one spring?
Or can a fig tree, my brothers, make olives, or a vine figs? So also salt waters cannot be made sweet.
Who among you is wise and instructed? Let him show his works by good conduct, with meek wisdom.
But if bitter envy is in you, or contention in your hearts, do not exalt yourselves against the truth and lie.
For this wisdom does not come down from above, but is earthly, from the thoughts of the soul, and from demons.
For where envy and contention are, there is also disorder and every evil thing.
But the wisdom that is from above is pure and full of peace and meek and submissive and full of mercy and good fruits, and without partiality, and it does not take faces.
And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
From where are there among you wars and fights? Is it not from the lusts that war in your members?
You lust and you do not have, and you kill and you envy and nothing comes into your hands, and you fight and make war and you do not have because you do not ask.
You ask and you do not receive, because you ask wickedly so that you may feed your lusts.
Adulterers, do you not know that the love of this world is enmity with Elohim? Whoever therefore chooses to be a friend of this world becomes an enemy of Elohim.
Or do you think in vain that the scripture says, The spirit that dwells in us lusts with envy?
But our Master has given us greater grace. Because of this he says, Elohim humbles the proud and gives grace to the humble.
Subject yourselves therefore to Elohim, and stand against Satana, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to Elohim, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners; sanctify your hearts, you who are divided in soul.
Humble yourselves and mourn, and let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into grief.
Humble yourselves before Master YHWH, and he will exalt you.

Do not speak against one another, my brothers; for he who speaks against his brother, or judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. And if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but its judge.
There is one Law-giver and Judge, who can give life and ‹can› destroy; but who are you that you judge your neighbor?
But what then shall we say also of those who say, Today or tomorrow we will go to such and such a city, and we will work there one year, and we will trade and make a profit?
And they do not know what will be tomorrow: for what are they, our lives, but a vapor that is seen a little while, and then vanishes and is gone?
Instead they should say, If Master YHWH wills and we live, we will do this or that.
They boast in their arrogance. All boasting like this is evil.
And whoever knows the good and does not do it, to him it is sin.
O rich ones, wail and weep over the miseries that are coming upon you.
For your wealth is spoiled and putrid, and your garments are eaten by moths.
And your gold and your silver have rusted, and their rust is becoming a testimony against you, and it will eat your flesh. You have heaped up fire for yourselves for the last days.
The wages of the laborers who reaped your lands, which you wrongfully withheld, cry out, and the cry of the reapers has entered the ears of Master YHWH of Sabaoth.
For you have lived in pleasure on the earth and revelled, and you have fattened your bodies as for a day of slaughter.
You have condemned and killed the just, and he did not stand against you.

But you, my brothers, lengthen your spirit until the coming of Master YHWH, like the farmer who waits for the precious fruits of his ground and lengthens his spirit over them until he receives the early and the latter rain.
So also you, lengthen your spirit and strengthen your hearts, for the coming of our Master has drawn near.
Do not groan one against another, my brothers, so that you will not be judged; for look, the judge stands before the door.
Take for yourselves the example of the prophets, my brothers, of lengthening of spirit in your afflictions, those who spoke in the name of Master YHWH.

For look, we give blessing to those who have endured. You have heard of the endurance of Iyov, and you have seen the end that Master YHWH made for him, because Master YHWH is merciful and compassionate.
But before everything, my brothers, do not be swearing, neither by heaven nor by earth nor by any other oath, but let your word be yes, yes, and no, no, so that you will not fall under judgment.
And if anyone among you is in affliction, let him pray; and if he is joyful, let him sing psalms.
And if he is sick, let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of our Master.
And the prayer of faith heals the one who is sick, and our Master raises him up; and if sins have been done by him, they are forgiven him.
Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that you may be healed; for great is the power of the prayer that a righteous one prays.
Eliyahu also was a man of feelings like us, and he prayed that rain would not come down on the earth, and it did not come down for three years and six months.
And again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth gave its fruits.
My brothers, if anyone among you errs from the way of truth, and someone turns him back from his error,
let him know that he who turns the sinner from the error of his way will give life to his soul from death, and will cover a multitude of his sins.
Petros, an apostle of Y'shua the Mashiyach, to the chosen and sojourners who are scattered in Pontus and in Galatia and in Cappadocia and in Asia and in Bithynia,
who were chosen by the foreknowledge of Elohim the Father, in the holiness of the Ruach, to obedience and to the sprinkling of the blood of Y'shua the Mashiyach: grace and peace be multiplied to you.
Blessed is Elohim the Father of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach, who in his great mercy has begotten us anew by the resurrection of Y'shua the Mashiyach to the hope of life,
and to an inheritance that does not corrupt and is not defiled and does not fade, which is prepared for you in heaven,
while you are kept by the power of Elohim and by faith for the life that is prepared to be revealed in the last time,
in which you will rejoice forever, even if in this little time you are pressed by the various trials that come upon you;
so that the proving of your faith may be seen as more excellent than gold that is tried by fire, to glory and honor and praise at the revealing of Y'shua the Mashiyach
whom you have not seen, and you love him, and in his faith you rejoice with joy that is glorious and cannot be spoken
that you may receive the reward of your faith, the life of your souls
that life ‹namely› which the prophets searched into, when they prophesied about the grace that was going to be given to you
and they searched into what time the Ruach of Mashiyach that dwelt in them was showing and testifying, of the sufferings coming to Mashiyach and his glory after them

and it was revealed to them ‹in regard to› all they were searching, that not for themselves were they inquiring, but for us they were prophesying the things that are now revealed to you by those who announced good news to you by the Ruach haKodesh sent from heaven, things into which messengers also long to look
Because of this, gird up the loins of your minds, and be fully awake, and hope for the joy that is coming to you at the revelation of our Master Y'shua the Mashiyach.
as obedient children, and do not share again in your former lusts, those you lusted after when without knowledge.
But be holy in all your ways of life, as he is holy who called you.
Because it is written: Be holy, just as I also am holy.
And if you call on the Father, before whom there is no taking of faces, and who judges each one according to his works, walk in fear during this time of your sojourning,
knowing that you were not redeemed with perishable silver or with gold from your empty works that you received from your fathers;
but with the precious blood of the Lamb in whom there is no spot and no blemish, who is the Mashiyach:
who was previously set apart for this from before the foundation of the world, and was revealed in the last of the times for your sakes;
who through him have believed in Elohim, who raised him from the house of the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and your hope would be on Elohim,
when your souls have been made holy by obedience to the truth, and you are full of love without respect of persons, so that you love one another from a pure and perfect heart;
like people born again from the start, not from seed that perishes but from that which does not perish, by the living word of Elohim that stands forever.
Because all flesh is grass, and all its beauty is like the flower of the field. The grass dries up and the flower withers;
but the word of our Elohim stands forever: and this is the word that was announced to you.
Therefore put away from yourselves all wickedness and all deceit and hypocrisy and envy and slander.
And be like newborn infants and long for the word as for the pure and spiritual milk, that by it you may grow up to life,
if you have tasted and seen that Master YHWH is good,
to whom you are coming, who is a living stone rejected by the sons of men, but chosen and precious with Elohim.
And you also, as living stones, are being built and become a spiritual temple and holy priests to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable before Elohim through Y'shua the Mashiyach.
For it is said in the writing, Look, I am laying in Tsiyon a chosen and precious stone, the head of the corner, and whoever believes in him will not be ashamed.
So to you who believe this honor is given; but to those who are not persuaded,
he is a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense. And they stumble on it because they are not persuaded by the word, to which they are appointed.
But you are a chosen race, a priesthood for the kingdom, a holy people, a redeemed assembly, that you may declare the praises of him who called you from darkness to his excellent light:
who once were not counted a people, but now are the people of Elohim; and also there were ‹once› no mercies on you, but now mercies are poured out on you.
My beloved, I beg you as strangers and sojourners: keep yourselves from all the lusts of the body, these that make war against the soul.
And let your ways be beautiful before all the sons of men, so that those who speak evil words against you may see your good works and praise Elohim in the day of visitation.
And be submissive to all the sons of men because of Elohim, to the king because of their authority;
and to judges, because they are sent from him for the punishment of wrongdoers and for the praise of those who do good.
For this is the will of Elohim, that by your good works you may shut the mouth of the foolish who do not know Elohim:
as free men, and not as men who make their freedom a cover for their wickedness, but as the servants of Elohim.

who will give account to Elohim, who is ready to judge the dead and the living.
